title: Quality Inspector - 1st shift - M-F - 7am-4pm
description:
The Quality Inspector is responsible for performing moderately complex dimensional inspection of standard parts, units, or materials to ensure conformance with specifications utilizing various measuring and testing equipment. This includes quality inspections for incoming inspections, in process inspections and final inspections.
Job responsibilities

Perform process audits per defined control plans and react to non-conformances.
Use various gauging devices to measure, inspect, and test product to ensure conformance with engineering drawing specifications and other material/finished good standards.
Document inspection results using quality software, Excel, or SharePoint.
Analyze inspection results with product stakeholders and follow non-conformance procedures for product containment and disposition.
Participate in problem solving teams.
Keep work area in a clean and orderly condition, complying with established 6S standards.
Perform other duties as required within the nature and level of work.

Job Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent and one (1) year of related work experience are required.
Must be able to read, write, speak and understand basic English.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint) and quality control software.
Excellent time‐management, attention to detail, and multi‐tasking skills in a fast‐paced environment.
Ability to problem‐solve and make decisions per work instructions and documents.
Ability to communicate with team members through verbal and written form.
Ability to demonstrate basic math skills and use/test measuring equipment including, but not limited to, micrometers, calipers, dial indicators, gauges, Rockwell hardness tester, optical comparator and templates, torque testing machine, gauge pins and blocks, and metallurgical equipment such as wet saws, grinders, and sample mounting equipment.

Physical Demand Requirements
DISCLAIMER: This position may include exposure to radio frequencies that may be dangerous to individuals with a pacemaker, consult with your doctor.Occasionally required to stand, walk or sit; use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs; balance; stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl; talk or hear; taste or smell. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move objects up to 35 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

title: Planner
description:
Department: Operations

Reports to: Director, Project Controls

Location: On-site

Who We Are

CoVolt Power is a leading utility-scale EPC (Engineering, Procurement & Construction) company specializing in the design and delivery of solar, battery energy storage (BESS), and high-voltage infrastructure. Since its founding in 2005, the company has built a reputation for de-risking project delivery and providing creative, integrated solutions that span the power and digital infrastructure sectors.

Consistently ranked as a top-tier EPC, CoVolt Power leverages a mission-driven approach to safety and quality, delivering thousands of megawatts in renewable assets that support a more resilient and sustainable energy future for developers, utilities, independent power producers (IPPs), and data center operators across North America.

The Role

We are currently searching for a very experienced, ambitious EPC Planner for Utility-Scale Solar Energy Projects.​ We are looking for leaders with a proven track record.​

Key Responsibilities

  • Responsible for the overall Plan of the Project.
    • Understand current productivities, resources, and equipment to have a daily, weekly, 3 week and 90-Day lookahead needs of materials, people, equipment, Documents, Permits and other resources.
    • Constantly monitor quantities and productivities for forecasting purposes.
    • Actively participate in the cost/revenue forecast of the project based on the updated plan.
    • Anticipate barriers such as weather or equipment delays to reroute or increase resources to keep the project on track.
    • Actively monitor all activities to understand the critical path and anticipate potential obstacles.
  • Systemic Approach: Keep a long-term look ahead of all activities by having a Systemic approach towards the overall completion of the project:
      • Civil and mechanical sequence to prevent erosion.
      • Mechanical and electrical sequence to minimize simultaneous operations in the same area.
      • Mechanical sequence to ensure piles are ahead of trackers and trackers are ahead of panels so there are no stoppages in work.
      • Electrical sequence aligned with Mechanical Completion dates.
      • Commissioning Plan, Substantial Completion Contractual requirements, and Electrical sequence aligned.
      • Testing requirements, SWI approvals, and Testing methodologies times included in overall schedule.
  • Personnel Planning:
    • Work closely with the recruitment team to understand their lead times and have craft properly recruited, drug tested and safety trained when needed.
    • Understand the productivity of the existing team and work with Project Managers and Field Operations Managers to adjust if needed to meet the required plan.
    • Plan the personnel reductions at the tail end of the scopes in alignment with the plan and equipment plan.
  • Materials Planning:
    • Work closely with the Procurement Team to understand logistics and planned arrival dates of deliveries to ensure these are aligned with the personnel, equipment, and production needs.
  • Subcontractor planning:
    • Work closely with the Procurement Team to ensure subcontractor mobilization dates are aligned with plan and site needs.
    • Ensure subcontractor progress is being met to minimize potential Change Orders.
  • Construction sequence:
    • Constantly evaluate the Construction sequence on the different areas and blocks to maximize the utilization of people and equipment based on preceding activities completed.
  • Equipment Utilization:
    • Based on the plan anticipate equipment needs.
    • Work with the Fleet Superintendent to identify required dates based on local or regional lead times from equipment vendors.
    • Monitor the ratio of Equipment Operators/type of equipment to anticipate people need.
  • Energization:
    • Clearly understands the Client’s Financing priorities and needs to align as best as possible the energization plan to meet their requirements.
    • Work backwards to align the Mechanical Completion and Construction sequence to be aligned with the energization plan.
  • Forecasting:
    • Work with the Project Management and Project Controls Team to validate the forecasts based on the past average productions and future plan. Educate the PMs, schedulers, and APMs on how to challenge and validate forecasts, by using historical data and anticipating barriers.
  • Alternate Plans:
    • Based on the overall plan, have options to pivot when obstacles arrive “Pilot’s alternate route”.
  • Documentation and Permitting:
    • Understand the need for documents that can prevent the project from progressing:
      • Local permits.
      • DOT permits and RUAs (Road Use Agreements).
      • Mechanical Completion contractual checklist of requirements.
      • Standard Work Instruction (SWI) approvals.
      • Job Book progress and plan in coordination with the Quality and Commissioning Teams.

  • Work with and train the schedulers.
  • Deputize for Project Director when absent.
  • Provide project analytics and KPIs for month-end project financial reporting (earned value, SPI, milestone progress, etc.).
  • Enforce project team compliance to maintain schedule integrity.
  • Communicate risk and opportunities based on analysis of the schedule.

Required Skills, Qualifications & Experience

  • Strong work ethic and desire to learn and grow professionally.
  • 10 years’ experience in EPC construction; utility-scale solar experience a plus.
  • Experience working with owner representatives and subcontractors involved with the project.
  • Excellent organization, communication, and time management skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a team environment with co-workers, service providers, and customers.
  • Ability to think strategically and synthesize information from multiple sources.
  • Proficient in resources and cost-loaded scheduling.
  • Advanced proficiency in the use of Primavera P6 scheduling systems.
  • Advanced proficiency in basic Microsoft 365 products (Power BI a plus).

Education:

  • A degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or a related quantitative major a plus.
  • 10+ years of experience in a role as an EPC Planner or Project Manager
  • PMP or AACEI Scheduling certifications a plus.

Additional Information

  • Position is site based with rotations.

If an unauthorized bot joins the meeting, our team will ask for it to be removed before beginning the interview. Thank you for your cooperation!

title: Group Lead (Packing) - 1st Shift
description:
Group Leader

OMG Inc. is a leading manufacturer of fastening products and technologies for the commercial roofing and construction industries worldwide. Headquartered in western Massachusetts, OMG is an equal-opportunity employer prioritizing the safety of our employees and customers. The company values integrity, teamwork, diversity, trust, respect, commitment, and a passion for excellence. OMG is a global company operating manufacturing facilities in Massachusetts, Illinois, and Minnesota.

Position Overview

OMG currently operates in two Divisions: OMG Roofing Products and FastenMaster®. OMG Roofing Products is a leading global manufacturer and supplier of value-added components for the commercial roofing industry. The FastenMaster Division manufactures and markets innovative, premium quality wood-to-wood fasteners that are engineered to enable professional contractors to complete building projects safer, faster, and easier. Our managers and supervisors use Group Leaders to help coordinate production and manage team members in their work area. Group Leaders encourage teamwork and collaboration and drive production goals. Their priorities are safety, quality, continuous improvement, and employee development. This key position requires strong communication, problem-solving, and time management skills, the ability to work effectively with people and technical expertise in the specific work to be performed.

Position Responsibilities

  • Promote Safety as the Number One priority of all OMG employees.
  • Conduct regular safety meetings with the work group.
  • Lead by example by following and supporting OMG policies.
  • Build strong working relationships and encourage teamwork and collaboration.
  • Communicate in a manner that is respectful and results in mutual understanding.
  • Take ownership of issues in your work area and work proactively to solve issues (especially those related to safety and quality).
  • Promote continuous Lean activity and follow through.
  • Confidently make changes that will improve the work area’s performance and move simple issues or problems forward.
  • Demonstrate the use of good judgment when making decisions.
  • Schedule daily work and direct team members to achieve safety, production, quality, and continuous improvement goals.
  • Demonstrate technical, functional, and job-specific knowledge required for assignments in the work area.
  • Assist with production needs as necessary, including equipment setup and troubleshooting.
  • Support performance management process by contributing to the review process, disciplinary actions, and providing documentation related to performance.
  • Challenge standard approaches and find improved processes to get work done.
  • Communicate with manager or supervisor regularly on team performance against goals and individual contributor progress, immediately elevating specific issues or concerns.
  • Perform other tasks as assigned.

title: Collections Specialist
description:
Company Description

Palmetto is a consumer energy platform that provides homeowners with a single destination to discover, purchase, finance, install, monitor and manage home energy products and services. By offering one integrated platform across solar, battery storage, HVAC, heat pumps and more, Palmetto helps homeowners make home energy more affordable, reliable and accessible. Today Palmetto serves hundreds of thousands of homeowners, across 30+ states, building the operating infrastructure for the consumer energy transition, one home at a time.

Our employees are our most valuable resource. We foster a promote-from-within culture that prioritizes talent development, career growth, and purpose-driven work. Palmetto offers a comprehensive benefits package—including unlimited PTO, medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid parental leave, retirement plans, and more—so you can have it all both personally and professionally. Palmetto prioritizes people, planet, and profit—backed by a culture that values collaboration, impact, and balance. Join us in building a brighter, cleaner world.

Department Description

Palmetto Home is a branch of Palmetto focused on the democratization of the renewable energy and HVAC industries. We provide homeowners with financial products to benefit from solar power, energy storage systems, and home efficiency through advanced heating and cooling technologies. We empower solar and HVAC sales professionals and installation companies with access to our proprietary platform, financing, customer management system, and milestone quality control system. Our #1 focus is a phenomenal experience for our customers and partners, evidenced in our growing financial product adoption.

Location

This position will be based remotely in the Philippines.

Summary of Role

The Collections Specialist is responsible for managing a portfolio of past-due accounts, conducting outbound collection calls/emails/texts, and working directly with customers to resolve outstanding balances.
This role requires strong communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to balance firmness with empathy — all while delivering a positive customer experience and supporting the company's overall financial health. If you're a clear communicator, a natural problem-solver, and someone who stays composed under pressure, this role is a great fit for you!

About You:

  • Passionate about problem solving, and you excel at finding solutions to unstructured issues while achieving success in a structured environment.
  • You love to innovate. A "no" or a difficult conversation is simply an opportunity to get creative and find a resolution that works for both the customer and the business!
  • You can tackle the macro and micro — staying focused on the individual customer in front of you while keeping an eye on your own performance metrics and the broader financial health of the business.

Strategic & Tactical

  • Make outbound collection calls to customers regarding past-due accounts with goal of 100 per day.
  • Negotiate payment arrangements and resolve delinquent accounts in accordance with company policy and applicable regulations.
  • Accurately document call outcomes, payment commitments, and account notes in the CRM.
  • De-escalate and professionally handle frustrated, upset, or difficult customers.
  • Educate customers on account status, balances, and available payment options.
  • Meet or exceed daily, weekly, and monthly call volume and collection targets.
  • Follow all applicable federal, state, and company collection laws and guidelines (e.g., FDCPA where applicable).
  • Identify accounts that may require escalation to a supervisor or alternate resolution path.
  • Maintain a professional, courteous, and customer-focused approach on every call

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; some college coursework preferred.
  • Prior experience in collections, call center, or customer service roles required.
  • Fluent in English, both verbal and written, with clear and professional phone communication skills.
  • Strong negotiation and conflict-resolution skills.
  • Ability to remain calm, patient, and solution-oriented with escalated or difficult customers.
  • Comfortable working in a high-volume, fast-paced call environment.
  • Basic computer proficiency, including data entry and navigating CRM or collections software.
  • Strong attention to detail and accurate record-keeping.
  • Positive attitude, reliability, and a genuine customer-first mindset.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills.
  • Knowledge of construction or solar industry preferred.
  • Preferred Skills
    • Bilingual abilities a plus (English & Spanish).
    • Familiarity with collections-related regulations and compliance requirements.
    • Previous experience with outbound dialer systems.

Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Palmetto embraces diversity and is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. Employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law.

title: Safe Place Healing Hearts Program Coordinator
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

The overall aim of the Safe Place Healing Hearts (SPHH) Program is to enhance the safety of victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, dating violence, and stalking within Choctaw, McCurtain and Pushmataha Counties. The Program Coordinator will assist the Director with all aspects of the program, in an effort to build the capacity of these communities to ensure the safety of and enhance services for all victims of sexual assault, domestic/dating violence and stalking. This is a Safety Sensitive position.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  1. Assist the Program Director with the design, planning, implementation, and coordination of the SPHH Program.
  2. Provide direct services to victims in the program (i.e. emotional support, advocacy, emergency and long-term assistance, coordination of referrals, follow-up services) as appropriate.
  3. Conduct an intake assessment with victim clients and assess all needs; develop support and assistance goals based on identified needs.
  4. Provide trauma-informed outreach, advocacy, and crisis intervention for victims as needed.
  5. Maintain victim safety and confidentiality as a top priority when conducting all program activities, complying with confidentiality and privacy requirements for the Violence Against Women Act.
  6. Conduct safety planning with victim clients and provide comprehensive case management, to include provision of resources and referrals as appropriate for immediate and follow-up services.
  7. Based on identified needs, work to address immediate victim health and safety concerns through the Victim Assistance Fund and provision of Victim Support Kits.
  8. Assist with ordering, stocking, documentation, and inventory tracking of Victim Support Kits.
  9. Assist with coordination, documentation, and reporting of Victim Assistance Fund expenditures.
  10. Assist in the building of referral networks among service providers.
  11. Work in cooperation with area law enforcement agencies, District Attorney's Office, victim and other service providers/community agencies to appropriately respond to victim needs, including sharing information and coordinating activities; hold monthly meetings to facilitate work.
  12. Assist in the development, coordination, and facilitation of victim support groups.
  13. Maintain regular, long-term contact with victim clients (up to at least one year); assess client outcomes, stability, and safety through follow-up surveys.
  14. Assist the Program Director in developing client and partner pre/post-surveys as well as other program measurement tools; distribute/collect surveys and assessments, input data, and assist with analysis.
  15. Assist with provision of multidisciplinary training, technical assistance, and materials for partners and professionals who impact victims of sexual assault, domestic/dating violence, and stalking.
  16. Work with the SPHH Planning and Implementation Team to determine topics, design, and coordinate and conduct trainings for partners and victim service providers.
  17. Work with each program partner to complete an organizational community safety assessment.
  18. Work with program partners to develop materials for community distribution to raise awareness and work towards prevention of sexual assault, domestic/dating violence, and stalking crimes.
  19. Develop community awareness education/prevention presentations; assist with program events.
  20. Coordinate, participate in, and work to further build the County Sexual Assault Response Teams (SARTs), Coordinated Community Response Teams (CCRTs), and Multidisciplinary Teams (MDTs); provide program activity reports at monthly SART/CCRT and MDT meetings for each service county.
  21. Attend all program trainings, including grant-mandated training as assigned.
  22. Maintain accurate, current statistical records and case management files for each victim client.
  23. Assist the Program Director with program reporting; maintain required performance reporting data as directed.
  24. Travel required.
  25. Perform other duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RELATIONSHIP:

The SPHH Program Coordinator reports to the Victim and Youth Program Director and performs no staff supervision.

OUALIFICATIONS:

  1. Must submit to and pass a background screening.
  2. Degree or equivalent work experience in criminal justice, social services, or related field is preferred.
  3. Experience in developing and delivering training and/or technical assistance is preferred.
  4. Ability to communicate with and empower victims of crime; knowledge and understanding of families in crisis is preferred.
  5. Possess strong communication and organizational skills, and the ability to work independently.
  6. Must be able to work collaboratively as a team player as well as lead coalitions or large groups.
  7. Must have a valid driver license, valid auto insurance and have own vehicle.

MENTAL AND PHYSICAL DEMANDS/ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS:

  1. Ability to communicate effectively; verbally and written, and maintain emotional control under stress.
  2. Constantly must be able to sit/stand in a stationary position 50% of the time.
  3. Frequently must be able to move about inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, etc.
  4. Frequently must operate a computer and other office productive machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine, and computer printer.
  5. Frequently must communicate with staff and others who have inquiries about the program. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.
  6. Occasionally must move/carry items weighing up to 30 pounds or more.

title: Electrical Engineering Intern | Summer 2027
description:
DLR Group is an integrated design firm with a promise to elevate the human experience through design. This fuels the work we do around the world and inspires our mission to improve the lives of our clients, our communities, and our planet. If this sparks your interest, you’re in the right place.

DLR Group’s Los Angeles studio has an opening for an Electrical Engineering Summer Intern.

  • Los Angeles, CA

We have multiple positions and locations available; please refer to all openings posted and apply to the locations that are most suitable for your living situation during the course of your internship. This is not a remote position.

About EPX at DLR Group

As an intern at DLR Group, you’ll be part of our Emerging Professional Experience (EPX) Program, designed to give you a meaningful introduction to life within an integrated design firm and a strong foundation for your career in the AEC industry.

Each person at DLR Group has a design voice, and EPX gives you opportunities to develop and share yours. Through hands-on project work, mentorship, and learning experiences, you’ll gain exposure to the people, disciplines, and ideas that shape the built environment. You may participate in design discussions, project meetings, site visits, business development efforts, office activities, and other experiences that broaden your understanding of the design profession.

The program combines three core components: mentorship, project work, and weekly learning sessions. Topics may include design culture, sustainability, design technology, communication, marketing and business development, project and resource management, research, equity, career development, and more. Along the way, you’ll hear from leaders and integrated designers across DLR Group and build connections with fellow emerging professionals.

Position Summary

As an Electrical Engineering Intern at DLR Group, you will be an important part of our integrated design team, contributing to the design of electrical systems for buildings of various types, sizes, and complexities. Working alongside electrical engineers and professionals across architecture, engineering, interiors, and other disciplines, you will gain hands-on experience with the design process from early concepts and system development through documentation and construction administration.

Our Summer Internship Program is a paid, full-time opportunity running May 18 through August 6, 2027, and interns are expected to participate for the duration of the program. This is an opportunity to apply what you’ve learned in the classroom, build your technical and professional skills, and contribute your perspective to design solutions that support our brand promise of Elevating the Human Experience through design.

What you will do

Each person at DLR Group has a design voice, and EPX gives you opportunities to develop and share yours. title: Program Therapist
description:
Position Summary

The Part-Time OPTS Program Therapist provides clinical care to adult and geriatric psychiatric patients. Responsibilities include facilitating therapeutic groups and individual sessions, completing psychological assessments, serving as a patient case manager, and collaborating with the multidisciplinary treatment team.

The Program Therapist provides patient-centered care while maintaining professional boundaries, sound clinical judgment, and compliance with established policies and treatment plans.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Conduct individual and group therapy sessions.
  • Complete psychological assessments, evaluations, and clinical documentation.
  • Develop, maintain, and update individualized treatment plans.
  • Serve as case manager for assigned patients.
  • Participate in treatment planning and multidisciplinary team meetings.
  • Monitor patient progress and document treatment outcomes.
  • Assist with crisis intervention and patient de-escalation.
  • Coordinate care with patients, families, physicians, staff, and community resources.
  • Participate in quality improvement activities.
  • Maintain accurate, timely, and legally compliant documentation.
  • Maintain patient confidentiality and professional standards.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Master's degree or higher in Psychology, Marriage and Family Therapy, Social Work, Counseling, Counseling Psychology, or a related mental health field.
  • Current California professional license, as applicable.
  • Minimum 1 year of experience working with adult psychiatric populations.
  • Strong clinical, communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
  • Strong assessment, documentation, and crisis intervention skills.
  • Current CPR and MAB/PART certification, or ability to obtain within the probationary period.
  • Must meet hospital credentialing requirements, as applicable.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Knowledge of psychiatric treatment and behavioral health practices.
  • Ability to facilitate individual and group therapy.
  • Strong clinical judgment and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to establish therapeutic and professional relationships.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • Ability to remain calm and effective during crisis situations.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with physicians, nurses, social workers, therapists, and other healthcare professionals.

Physical & Work Environment

The Program Therapist works in a behavioral health/psychiatric care environment and may interact directly with patients for extended periods. The position may require responding to behavioral or psychiatric emergencies and assisting with patient de-escalation in accordance with hospital policies and procedures.

title: Senior Specialist Warranty, Fleet Maintenance
description:
About Carvana

At Carvana, we sell cars, but we’re not salespeople. Since 2013, we’ve been making it our mission to change the way people buy cars. We saw a huge problem with how much it can suck to buy a car the traditional way, so we committed ourselves to tackling one of the largest, yet-to-be-disrupted markets in the world – the $1T per year U.S. car market (yes, that’s $Trillion with a “T”).

With the ability to search thousands of vehicles from our expansive inventory, to high-resolution 360° photographs of our vehicles’ interior and exterior, to real-time financing and the ability to complete contracts without visiting the back room of a dealership, we provide a seamless, online car buying experience for consumers that can be completed from their desktop or mobile device. All our vehicles are inspected and reconditioned based on our 150-point certification checklist and come with a 7-day return policy. We also operate our own logistics network to deliver cars to customers as soon as the next day, as well as offer customer pick-up at our state-of-the-art Car Vending Machine locations (yes, you read that right). By putting customer satisfaction at the core of our business, we’ve built a no-pressure, no-haggle online car buying experience that saves our customers time and money.

For more information on Carvana, take a look at our company introduction video.

About the team and position

The Sr. Specialist Warranty is responsible for the oversight, administration, and optimization of all warranty claims and recovery processes for a large-scale Class 8, Class 6, and Class 5 tractor and trailer fleet. This includes managing relationships with OEMs (e.g., Freightliner, Isuzu, Cummins), ensuring shop compliance with filing procedures, and identifying "hidden" recovery opportunities like policy adjustments and campaigns.

The Sr. Specialist Warranty is an individual contributor role based at Tempe headquarters, reporting directly to the Associate Director Vendor and Asset Operations. This role will work a traditional Monday - Friday business hours schedule (typically 8-5).

What you’ll be doing

  • Claim Lifecycle Management: Oversee the submission, tracking, and reconciliation of all warranty claims to ensure maximum recovery of parts and labor costs.
  • OEM & Dealer Relations: Act as the primary point of contact for manufacturers and dealerships; negotiate "policy" or "goodwill" coverage for failures occurring just outside of standard warranty terms.
  • Compliance & Auditing: Perform regular audits of internal repair orders to ensure technicians and service writers are documenting "three Cs" (Complaint, Cause, and Correction) required for successful filings.
  • Data Analysis: Monitor failure trends across the fleet to identify recurring component issues. Provide data to the Procurement team to influence future equipment specifications.
  • Financial Reporting: Track monthly recovery targets and provide leadership with visibility into "dollars-per-unit" recovered and pending credits.
  • Campaign & Recall Tracking: Monitor completion rates for safety recalls and manufacturer service bulletins across multiple regions/terminals.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: 3+ years in heavy-duty trucking maintenance, specifically focused on Class 8, Class 6, and Class 5 equipment.
  • Technical Knowledge: Deep understanding of VMRS (Vehicle Maintenance Reporting Standards) codes and major OEM portal systems (e.g., Daimler, Cummins QuickServe, etc.).
  • Communication: Ability to bridge the gap between "grease-under-the-fingernails" shop operations and corporate financial reporting.

What you should have

  • Working knowledge of the transportation and mechanical repair industry
  • Warranty processing experience
  • Proficient in G Suite (Gmail, Google Docs, Google Sheets, etc.), Excel (SQL is a plus), and has experience building forecast models and analyzing complex data sets to make impact high-impact business decisions

What we’ll offer in return

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits
  • 401K with company match
  • A multitude of perks including student loan payments, discounts on vehicles, benefits for your pets, and much more
  • A great wellness program to keep you healthy and happy both physically and mentally
  • Access to opportunities to expand your skillset and share your knowledge with others across the organization
  • A company culture of promotions from within, with a start-up atmosphere allowing for varied and rapid career development
  • A seat in one of the fastest-growing companies in the country

Other requirements

To be able to do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you.

  • Must be able to read, write, speak and understand English
  • Ability to work a flexible work schedule
  • Sees the ‘big picture’ with the ability to get it done (task oriented)
  • High energy and the ability to multitask and prioritize effectively
  • Strong interpersonal skills creating the ability to influence Operating units across the Carvana Network

Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

title: Overnight Shelter Attendant
description:
Department: Homeless Services

Job Title: Overnight Shelter Attendant - Third Shift

Reports to: Shelter Lead or Homeless Services Director

The Organization:

Homeward Bound is the leading nonprofit organization in Buncombe County focused on preventing and ending homelessness using the best-practice Prioritizing Home model. We work collaboratively with community partners and have a proven track record of helping individuals and families achieve housing stability. Since 2006, Homeward Bound has moved more than 2,615 people off the streets, out of cars, camps, and shelters, and into permanent housing.

Position:

The Overnight Shelter Staff provides essential overnight coverage, security, and support to guests at Homeward Bound’s cold-weather and severe-weather shelters. In this role, you will ensure the safety, dignity, and comfort of all guests, fostering a welcoming and compassionate environment throughout the night.

This position is critical during Buncombe County’s Code Purple and other emergency weather operations. Code Purple is activated when temperatures are forecasted at 32°F (0°C) or below, prompting shelters to open additional beds and provide emergency services, including transportation via ART buses. During these events, Overnight Shelter Staff work closely with city, county, and community partners to provide safe refuge and support to individuals experiencing homelessness.

Location: AHOPE Day Shelter - 19 N Ann Street, Asheville NC 28801

Schedule and Compensation:

This is a non-exempt, hourly PRN position paid at $24.15 an hour. Not benefit eligible

Typical hours: Third
Shifts often rotate and may be scheduled up to 48 hours in advance depending on weather conditions.

Education/Experience Requirements:

  • High school diploma or GED required

  • Minimum 2+ years working with populations experiencing poverty, homelessness, or with a social service background preferred

  • Familiarity with behavioral health, mental health, or substance use challenges preferred

  • Completion of essential training (e.g., de-escalation, bloodborne pathogens, etc.)

  • Strong communication and customer service skills

  • Basic computer literacy for reporting and scheduling tools

  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs, stand for long periods, and remain alert overnight

  • Must be able to arrive at shifts in all weather conditions.

Responsibilities:

  • Welcome and check in guests; perform brief health screenings and review shelter rules

  • Maintain a secure, calm atmosphere throughout overnight hours

  • Patrol sleeping areas, restrooms, and common spaces regularly

  • Control access to entrances and exits, locking doors securely

  • Coordinate with the Code Purple Shelter Coordinator and other team members

  • Manage refreshments, coffee, snacks, and maintain cleanliness in kitchen and common areas

  • Prevent and respond appropriately to incidents, rule violations, or disturbances

  • Write incident and shift reports each morning and communicate issues promptly

  • Gently wake guests in the morning and oversee their departure

  • Clean and sanitize the facility, preparing bedding and supplies for the next shift

  • Support clients in maintaining housing stability and independent living skills as appropriate

  • Perform other duties as assigned to support Homeward Bound’s mission of ending homelessness

Our Values:

We believe in the absolute value and worth of every single human being.
 We believe that housing is a basic human right, integral to self-worth and dignity.
 We believe that homelessness is a solvable problem.

Mission:

To prevent and end homelessness in our community through permanent housing and support.

title: Engineering & Regulatory Technician
description:
The Opportunity

jade owls operating LLC is a rapidly growing, integrated oil and gas company built on integrity, grit, and cash flow. Since 2022, we’ve grown more than 70x and currently operate 14,000 BOE/d across Northeast Wyoming and Oklahoma.

This role sits at the intersection of engineering, operations, and compliance, ensuring that wells are permitted, drilled, completed, produced, and plugged in full compliance with state, tribal, and federal requirements, while providing the asset team with accurate well data, regulatory requirements and associated deadlines, and technical support.

The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, organized, comfortable managing deadlines across multiple agencies, and able to communicate effectively with regulators, field personnel, and engineers.

Responsibilities — What You'll Do

Regulatory Permitting and Compliance

  • Prepare, file, and track drilling permits, completion reports, recompletions, workovers, transfers of operator, and plugging and abandonment filings with the Oklahoma Corporation Commission (OCC) Oil and Gas Conservation Division, Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission (WOGCC), and Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA).
  • Prepare and submit federal filings for wells on federal and tribal minerals, including Applications for Permit to Drill (APDs), sundry notices, and well completion reports through the Bureau of Land Management's electronic systems.
  • Support spacing, pooling, increased density, and location exception applications in Oklahoma, and spacing/unit and exception location matters in Wyoming, in coordination with land and legal staff.
  • Maintain a regulatory calendar tracking permit expiration, reporting deadlines, testing requirements, bonding obligations, and agency correspondence.
  • Respond to agency inquiries, notices of violation, and audits in a timely and professional manner.

Engineering Support

  • Maintain accurate well files, wellbore diagrams, directional surveys, and completion records in the company's database and document management system.
  • Gather and organize data for engineering evaluations, including production decline analysis, AFE preparation, reserves updates, and workover candidate reviews.
  • Assist asset team with well test data, pressure data, and mechanical integrity test (MIT) records.
  • Support drilling, completion, and plugging operations by coordinating regulatory notices (e.g., spud, casing, cementing, and plugging notifications) with field personnel.
  • Generate maps, reports, and summaries for asset teams.

Communication and Coordination

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for regulatory agencies.
  • Communicate regulatory requirements and deadlines to field staff and management.
  • Stay current on rule changes and agency guidance in Oklahoma, Wyoming, and at the federal level, and help update internal procedures accordingly.

Qualifications — What We're Looking For

Required

  • Associate's or bachelor's degree in petroleum technology, engineering technology, geology, environmental science, or a related field, OR equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 3+ years of experience in upstream oil and gas regulatory, engineering technician, or production support roles.
  • Working knowledge of state oil and gas regulatory processes; direct experience with OCC and/or WOGCC filings strongly preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and Outlook; ability to learn industry software quickly.

Preferred

  • Experience with BLM federal permitting and reporting.
  • Experience with well data and engineering software.
  • Understanding of drilling, completion, and production operations terminology and practices.
  • Experience with GIS or mapping tools.

Work Environment

  • Remote work-from-home position
  • Occasional travel to field locations and agency offices required
  • Fields visits include
    • Working in ambient temperatures of -40°F to 100°F
    • Work in all weather conditions including rain, snow, mud, etc.
    • Exposure to hazardous facilities including moving equipment and H2S environments.

Compensation & Benefits

  • 100% employer paid medical, vision, and dental premiums for applicable plans
  • 401(k) Retirement Plan with generous match
  • Paid Time Off and Company Holidays
  • Potential RSU awards, subject to plan terms, performance, and company discretion
  • Career growth with potential for future advancement

Additional Terms

The Historic Architect / Historic Preservation Lead is responsible for advancing the firm’s historic preservation practice, providing technical leadership, and ensuring the responsible stewardship of historic resources. title: Corrections Specialist 4 -CN93 - CCD
location: King County - Seattle - S. Seattle, WA
description:
Description




Correction Specialist 4
Everett Field Office - 8625 Evergreen Way, Everett, WA
Full Time/Perm/WFSE
Salary Range: $7,066 - $9,506 Monthly

The mission of the Department of Corrections is to improve public safety by positively changing lives.

Join a dedicated team committed to reducing recidivism, promoting successful community reintegration, and enhancing public safety through evidence-based treatment and assessment.

This permanent position provides therapeutic services within the Sex Offense Treatment and Assessment Programs. As a Corrections Specialist 4, you will play a critical role in supporting individuals as they transition from incarceration back into the community. Through evidence-based assessment and the provision of sex offense specific treatment, you will help reduce the risk of reoffending while encouraging positive behavioral change and long-term success.

In this role, you will:
1. Conduct sex offense-specific risk assessments and guide individualized treatment planning and treatment delivery.
2. Facilitate evidence-based cognitive behavioral therapy in both individual and group settings.
3. Provide compassionate, professional clinical services to clients on your assigned caseload while promoting accountability and lasting behavioral change.
4. Prepare timely and accurate clinical documentation, reports, and other required program materials.
5. Collaborate with internal staff and criminal justice partners to coordinate services, monitor client progress, and support community safety.

To be considered for this position, please attach the following to your online application:
  • Cover Letter
  • Resume
  • 3 Professional References

Application assessment will be ongoing, and the hiring authority reserves the right to offer the position at any time during the recruitment process. It is to the applicant's advantage to apply as early as possible.

"This recruitment could be used to fill multiple permanent or non-permanent positions."

Duties


As a Correction Specialist 4, some of your duties will include:

Assess client treatment needs and risk in order to provide evidence-based sex offense treatment to adult men and women in both group and individual settings. Facilitate behavioral change in clients, present client information to committees related to client planning, risk management issues and transition. Complete documentation to include agency approved risk assessment, initial treatment plans, group and individual progress notes and a comprehensive treatment summary for external distribution. Additionally, some clients may require treatment summary addendums and/or additional documentation. Meet with client support persons and outside stakeholders to educate and answer questions.

  • Conduct group and individual therapy following the approved program guidelines.
  • Complete all required documentation in a timely and complete manner.
  • Complete all required risk assessments (currently Stable-2007 and Acute-2007).
  • Make contact with and response promptly in communications with client support persons and stakeholders.

Participate in required team meets, unit meetings, trainings, and clinical and administrative supervision. Collaborate with Community Corrections Officers and Supervisors to address risk and assist in developing protective factors for clients. Work with Mental Health providers, community members, and external stakeholders regarding sex offense specific risk and transition.

  • Attend and participate in meetings as required.
  • Coordinate and facilitate meetings with internal and external stakeholders as necessary.
  • Travel to Quarterly Community SOTAP team meetings.
  • Share and educate stakeholders regarding releasing clients and their specific criminogenic needs and dynamic risk obtaining appropriate Release of Information documentation as necessary.

Work directly with guardian and victim advocates concerning the management of those with sexually related offenses. Serve as an active member in the client transition process by identifying risk and developing supervision strategies. Provide deposition and testimony as legally required. Provide education, training, and workshops to the DOC and external agencies as necessary.

  • Meet and collaborate with prison clinical and custody staff and community supervising staff regarding client transition, management, and release.
  • Provide testimony when requested via subpoena.
  • Provide educational opportunities for the DOC and external sources regarding sex offense specific issues related to treatment, assessment, and transition.

Facilitate Community Transition groups.

  • Coordinate with prison staff for the delivery of Community Transition group for clients prior to discharge.
  • Coordinate with external stakeholders to schedule participation in CT group meetings as needed.
  • Complete appropriate documentation on client participation in CT group in preparation for release.

Perform other duties as assigned by the Community Program Clinical Manager.

  • As assigned.

Qualifications


Required Qualifications:

Two year of experience providing structured individual and/or group psychotherapy guided by a treatment plan to juvenile or adult populations which includes six (6) months of work experience providing structured therapy in a group setting.
OR
Three years of mental/behavioral health experience with a minimum of six months of providing psychotherapy in a group setting guided by a treatment plan.
OR
One (1) year of experience conducting structured group therapy in a sex offense specific program utilizing cognitive behavioral interventions.
AND
Obtain/maintain Washington State Agency Affiliated Counselor credential per RCW 18.19.030 within 30 days of hire.
Experience may be paid or unpaid.
Additional clarification: work experience in mental health and/or therapy to “groups” is identified as, “group experience where responsibilities have included mental health treatment and/or therapy planning, mental health program implementation and/or direct delivery of mental health services.

Preferred/Desired Qualifications:

A master’s degree or bachelor’s degree in psychology, social work, marriage and family therapy, or counseling.

Supplemental Information

title: Ophthalmic Scribe
description:
Florida Vision Institute seeks a motivated, patient-focused, and team-oriented Ophthalmic Scribe to join our multi-specialty ophthalmology practice in Stuart, Florida. Enjoy excellent work hours, enjoy time off on major holidays, a comprehensive benefits package, a supportive team environment, and clear career advancement opportunities.

This is your opportunity to join one of the areas most recognized leaders in ophthalmology and optometry. Florida Vision Institute is a multi-subspecialty eye care practice composed of fellowship-trained board-certified ophthalmologists in every sub-specialty of ophthalmology. Our goal is to provide each patient with the latest in comprehensive eye care in an efficient, patient-friendly private practice environment.

We are committed to customer service and making every interaction extraordinary while inspiring the complete confidence of our patients. Our employees contribute directly to the growth and success of our practices and take pride in being a member of our team. We strongly believe that the way our patients and customers are treated by our employees is as important as the services provided by the doctor.

All of us at Florida Vision Institute are committed to inclusion and diversity. We believe today more than ever; it isn’t speaking the words, but starts with a culture of service, caring and listening and we would thoroughly enjoy meeting with you and discussing our employment opportunities.

As an Ophthalmic Scribe you will provide accurate documentation and summarization of the examination and recommendations, while maintaining patient flow and communication regarding appointment status.

Responsibilities

  • Make introductions and establish rapport with patients
  • Initiate patient evaluation, documenting the chief complaint, history of present illness, review of systems, and all pertinent ocular findings accurately and in accordance with compliance guidelines
  • Accurately and thoroughly document medical visits and procedures as they are being performed by the physician, and other procedures
  • Communicates with patients regarding follow-up care, surgeries, procedures, changes in schedule, signs and symptoms, surgery schedules
  • Maintains and cleans all ophthalmic equipment being used
  • Ability to document and apply correct ICD-10 and CPT Codes
  • Able to manage multiple projects simultaneously, with strong attention to detail.
  • Effectively navigate NextGen software or applicable EHR
  • Complete requests for prescription refills as authorized by physician, with full documentation in patient chart
  • Educate patients regarding administration of medications
  • Check temperature of medical refrigerator daily
  • Maintain and conduct inventory of medications and supplies
  • Assist with maintenance of clinical examination equipment
  • Clean surgical instruments in preparation for sterile processing
  • Inspect instruments periodically for damage, send for repair, and request a replacement, as necessary
  • Open and close exam lanes daily, ensuring equipment is wiped down in an appropriate manner and as per office procedures, battery powered instruments are seated properly in re-charge wells, slit lamps and projectors are switched off under covers
  • Follow all safety procedures as per guidelines
  • Prioritize building and maintaining a positive relationship with doctors and clinical colleagues
  • Executes duties of position in a professional and courteous manner
  • Handles sensitive information in a confidential manner
  • Perform other tasks and duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • High School diploma or equivalent required.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to communicate clearly and effectively with patients, staff, managers, and doctors.
  • Basic computer literacy required.
  • Highly energetic with a positive attitude.
  • Must be willing to travel to other offices occasionally to meet the demands of business.
  • Must be able to walk and stand for eight hours.
  • Must be able to type or write legibly in a dimly lit setting.
  • Certified Ophthalmic Assistant (COA) or Certified Ophthalmic Technician (COT) preferred not required
  • Certified Ophthalmic Scribe (OSC) preferred not required/Ability to obtain certification within one year of employment
  • Two years as medical scribe preferred
  • Knowledge of ophthalmology billing/coding strongly preferred

In Turn We Will Provide

  • Benefits to full-time team members that include comprehensive medical, dental and optical coverage, 401K and short and long term disability
  • Company paid life insurance
  • Paid holidays and generous paid time off
  • Paid parking where applicable
  • Team oriented working environment where you are heard and respected
  • Clear career ladder opportunities

title: Senior IT Systems Engineer
description:
Nature of Work

This is advanced technical work in the design, implementation, administration, security, and maintenance of the City's enterprise information technology infrastructure. This position serves as a senior technical resource within the Technical Services Branch and provides high-level engineering support across networking, servers, virtualization, operating systems, telecommunications, and cybersecurity. The position operates with substantial independence and judgment but does not supervise personnel. Job related duties require a Bachelor’s Degree in IT, Computer Science or related field with five years of experience. Job performance is evaluated by the Information Technology Director through review of the quality and quantity of work, ability to perform assigned job duties and follow daily instructions and physical capacity to perform the job.

Illustrative Examples of Work

  • Design, implement, and maintain enterprise server infrastructure (Windows Server and
  • Linux environments).
  • Administer virtualization platforms including VMware, Hyper-V, or equivalent systems.
  • Configure and troubleshoot advanced networking components including routing,
  • switching, VLANs, VPNs, firewalls, NAT, and ACLs.
  • Manage TCP/IP-based services including DNS, DHCP, and network performance
  • optimization.
  • Support and engineer VoIP systems, SIP trunking, QoS, and telecommunications
  • integrations.
  • Administer and secure Windows, macOS, and Linux endpoints and servers.
  • Implement cybersecurity controls aligned with NIST, CIS, or comparable frameworks.
  • Manage backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity systems.
  • Perform scripting and automation using tools such as PowerShell and Bash.
  • Serve as escalation point for complex technical issues and major system incidents.
  • Assist in long-range infrastructure planning and technology roadmap development.
  • Maintain documentation of systems architecture, configurations, and procedures.

Necessary Requirements of Work

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, or related field, or equivalent experience. Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in systems administration, networking, or infrastructure engineering; Industry certifications such as CCNA, CCNP, Security+, RHCSA, VMware, or equivalent preferred; experience in municipal or public-sector IT environments preferred; good decision making and interpersonal skills; ability to accurately deal with detailed information; ability to multi-task and organize; or any equivalent combination of education and/or experience to provide the following knowledge, abilities and skills:

  • Thorough knowledge of computer systems hardware and software maintenance, trouble shooting and networking; systems design, networking and computer operating systems.
  • Thorough knowledge of hardware and software associated with the operations of a local area networking.
  • Thorough knowledge of basic and virtual machine security and virtualization
  • Thorough knowledge of modern office procedures, methods, techniques and equipment.
  • Thorough knowledge of the operations, characteristics and requirements of computer configurations.
  • Thorough knowledge of Information System Technology; computers, peripheral, devices, cabling and telecommunications equipment.
  • Thorough knowledge of network and computer security practice; midrange systems servers, PC’s and printers.
  • Thorough knowledge of Windows Server operating systems, Virtual machines and Linux; word processing, MacOS, spreadsheets, database, website and desktop publishing techniques.
  • Thorough knowledge of active directory, group policy, TCP/IP, routers and firewall capabilities including the limitations, characteristics and uses of computer and records information systems.
  • Thorough knowledge of methods and techniques used to maintain and repair computer equipment
  • Thorough knowledge of the hazards of the work and necessary safety precautions.
  • Considerable knowledge of the functions and operations of the City Administrative Department, City Information Technology Department, City Council and all other City Departments.
  • Ability to organize and perform work in an effective and efficient manner and consistently meet all established deadlines and requirements.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
  • Ability to analyze and resolve complex infrastructure and security issues.
  • Ability to interact in a professional and courteous manner with co-workers, elected officials, vendors, etc.
  • Ability to make timely and appropriate decisions in response to situations encountered on the job.
  • Ability to remain current on emerging and new technical advances in the information technology industry.
  • Ability to consistently follow oral and written instructions.
  • Ability to perform the physically demanding aspects of the job in a variety of weather conditions.
  • Ability to climb water tanks and communication towers without fear of heights while following all safety protocols.
  • Strong documentation and communication skills.
  • Skill in the use of hand tools and diagnostic equipment utilized to diagnose, install, repair and maintain information system components.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift moderately heavy equipment up to 50 pounds occasionally.
  • Ability to use small hand tools, including those battery/electrically operated, requiring manual dexterity.
  • Ability to climb ladders to extended lengths/heights
  • Work requires reaching, repetitive motions, pushing and pulling walking, standing, carrying objects, operation of vehicle, operation of keyboard, bending, kneeling and crouching.
  • Work may be performed indoors with extended periods of sitting and extended periods of use of a computer keyboard, inside equipment rooms, or performed outdoors with extended periods of activity depending in current projects.
  • Tasks are occasionally performed with exposure to adverse environmental conditions with possible exposure to dust, dirt, fumes, lint, electrical shock-installation, etc.

Necessary Special Requirements

  • Possession of a valid Tennessee driver’s license and the ability to be insured at standard vehicle liability rates

title: Research and Development Food Scientist
description:
About the Role:

This role will be based at our Charleville site and will report to the R&D Ingredients Lead. We are seeking an ambitious and technically strong R&D Scientist to join our Dairy & Nutritional Ingredients R&D team. This position will focus on the fundamental development, optimization and scale-up of innovative dairy and nutritional ingredients. The successful candidate will possess deep expertise in food chemistry, ingredient functionality, dairy processing and membrane filtration technologies including MF, UF, NF, RO and diafiltration. Dynamic, self-driven and capable of working on your own initiative is a key attribute for this role. Ability to function as part of a multi-disciplinary team (sales, business development, long term R&D, operations, supply chain, quality, regulatory and customers) is also important.

What will I be doing?

  • Develop new dairy and nutritional ingredients.
  • Design and execute laboratory, pilot-scale and manufacturing trials.
  • Provide technical leadership in membrane filtration and separation technologies.
  • Support technology transfer from laboratory to pilot scale and commercial manufacture.
  • Manage innovation projects from concept through to pilot scale.
  • Collaborate with Operations, Quality, Regulatory, Commercial and Supply Chain teams.
  • Prepare technical reports, specifications and stakeholder presentations.
  • Monitor industry trends, consumer insights, and emerging technologies to identify innovation opportunities.

What do I need to be successful?

At Kinisla, we understand that people have very different career trajectories and experiences. In order to be successful in this role we would be looking for the right competencies and aptitudes as well as your proven track record of success in a similar role and environment.

These include:

  • Bachelor’s, Master’s or PhD in Food Science, Dairy Science, Food Chemistry, Chemical Engineering or related discipline.
  • 3–5 years of industrial R&D experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in ingredient development and commercialization.
  • Strong understanding of food chemistry, dairy chemistry, proteins, carbohydrates and ingredient functionality.
  • Deep understanding of key dairy unit operations and process scale-up.
  • Excellent analytical, project management and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Project management and organisational skills
  • Excellent problem-solving, project management, and communication skills.
  • Strong Innovation mindset.

Technical Expertise Required:

  • Membrane filtration technologies including MF, UF, NF, RO and Diafiltration.
  • Dairy processing operations and process optimisation.
  • Ingredient functionality.
  • Protein, lipid and carbohydrate fractionation.
  • Experimental design.
  • Pilot plant and manufacturing trial execution.
  • Competence in key analytical methods (e.g., chromatography).

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience with nutritional and functional ingredient development.
  • Knowledge of physicochemical properties of dairy proteins.
  • Competency in Optiva and other formulation, recipe management, specification management and PLM systems.
  • Knowledge of process modelling, data analysis and process optimisation.
  • Track record of successful commercialization of innovative ingredient solutions.

Personal Attributes:

  • Scientifically curious and innovation focused.
  • Capable of translating scientific understanding into commercial opportunities.
  • Self-motivated individual with strong attention to detail.
  • Strong communicator who can work effectively within multidisciplinary teams.

What will I get in return?

At Kinisla, we believe in giving talented, curious people the opportunity to make a difference. We work as a team, searching for the best ways to inspire and lead the evolution of dairy food and nutrition. We are a community of innovators, working across disciplines to solve global food challenges with a fresh approach. We want you to achieve whatever you put your mind to.

We also offer:

  • 25 days annual leave (excluding bank holidays).
  • Matched pension scheme up to 10% Employer Contribution.
  • Benefits platform offering discounts and cashback on major retailers.
  • Employee Assistance Policy.

About Kinisla

Kinisla is a vertically integrated farm-to-fork business with a very substantial consumer foods presence and a leading nutritional and dairy ingredients division, delivering high-quality dairy solutions with a focus on sustainability and innovation. From partnering with local family farms to producing world-class dairy products, we ensure every step of our value chain reflects our commitment to excellence.

With over 50 years’ experience in milk processing, dairy and nutritional technology advancement, and product innovation, we are a key stakeholder in the global food industry and creators of a strong portfolio of market leading dairy brands including Cheestrings, Charleville and Coleraine Cheese, Dairygold, Golden Cow and our new SMUG range. Our from food, for food culture and deep-rooted connection to our 2,800 milk suppliers differentiates our business and offers captivating opportunities for our customers and consumers.

Our dairy comes from some of the world’s richest grazing land and is produced by a network of Irish family farms that have one of the lowest carbon footprints in the world. Through a combination of expertise, innovation, and sustainability, Kinisla is proud to shape the future of dairy while meeting the diverse needs of our farmers, customers, and communities.

Headquartered in Tralee, Co. Kerry, we operate multiple manufacturing facilities in the southwest of Ireland, including Listowel, Charleville, Newmarket, and Farranfore. Additionally, we manage 28 Farm & Home stores throughout the region, ensuring comprehensive coverage and service. In Northern Ireland and the United Kingdom, our presence extends to key locations in Portadown, Coleraine, and Ossett.

Globally, Kinisla employs over 1,700 dedicated professionals across Ireland, Northern Ireland, the UK, USA, Netherlands, Spain, Germany, and China. In 2024, we achieved a turnover of approximately €1.3 billion, reflecting our commitment to excellence and growth.

Get in touch today!

At Kinisla, we benefit from the knowledge of our colleagues who bring a diverse range of cultures, backgrounds, lifestyles and experiences. One team fostering an inclusive culture that, above all, inspires food and nourishes life. One culture where everyone brings their unique perspectives and experiences to help make us better, together. We are committed to nurturing an environment of positivity and inclusiveness, where everyone can be at their best, both personally and professionally.

Our recruitment, selection and assessment process are based on the skills and competencies of the specific roles and based entirely on merit. We are committed to and value Diversity and Inclusion in all recruitment processes within Kinisla and do not discriminate based on gender, race, class, economic status, ethnic background, sexual orientation, age, political beliefs, veteran status, marital status or any other protected characteristic.

Additionally, we will not consider or agree to payment of any recruiter fee under these circumstances. This also applies to CVs or candidate profiles sent directly to any Kinisla Hiring Managers.

title: Vice President of IT Operations
description:
About Monet Bank

Monet Bank is pioneering the future of banking and money movement — faster, more efficient, and built for the modern financial ecosystem.

At our core, we believe Monet Bank is an essential bridge to the next generation of banking and payments infrastructure. As a profitable, well-capitalized Texas state-chartered bank and FDIC-Insured — backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. Government — Monet combines the strength and stability of traditional banking with forward-thinking financial technology innovation.

If you are motivated by building secure, intentional, and future-ready banking infrastructure, we invite you to explore opportunities with Monet Bank.

About the Role

We're a small, fast-moving bank, and our cloud environment is core to everything we build. As a Senior Cloud Architect, you'll own our AWS environment end to end — designing it, running it, securing it, and setting the standards we grow into. This is a hands-on role with real autonomy and unusually direct impact: you won't be one architect among many, you'll be our cloud function. If you like the pace of a startup but want the substance of building resilient, compliant infrastructure for a regulated bank, this is that role.

What You'll Own

  • The design, operation, and security of Monet's entire AWS environment.
  • The migration and modernization path for key workloads to the cloud.
  • The automation, resilience, and cost standards the rest of the team builds against.

Core Responsibilities (Essential duties include, but are not limited to):

Architecture & delivery

  • Design and operate scalable, secure, cost-effective AWS architectures across compute, storage, data, and networking.
  • Lead cloud migration and modernization with minimal disruption to the business.

Automation & operations

  • Drive Infrastructure-as-Code and CI/CD so provisioning is consistent, repeatable, and auditable.
  • Own monitoring, capacity planning, disaster recovery, and cost optimization; design backup and multi-region failover strategies.
  • Maintain clear architecture documentation and data-flow diagrams for operations and audit.

Security & compliance

  • Define and enforce cloud security standards (network design, encryption, and identity & access management) aligned to banking regulations.
  • Partner with Security and Risk to keep the architecture compliant by design.

Collaboration

  • Work directly across a small, cross-functional team, and help establish engineering standards as the team grows.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies and manage key cloud vendor relationships.

AI Platform Administration

As a secondary responsibility, administer Monet's AI platforms (Claude / ChatGPT): user provisioning and access controls, SSO/identity integration, and usage guidelines and security guardrails for responsible, compliant AI use in a regulated environment. This is a smaller, well-scoped part of the role alongside your core cloud work.

Required Qualifications:

  • 8-10 years in IT (at least 5 years in cloud architecture or infrastructure roles) with strong, hands-on cloud experience, including demonstrated AWS delivery.
  • Deep AWS expertise across compute, storage, networking, and databases.
  • Hands-on with Infrastructure-as-Code and CI/CD.
  • Strong cloud network and security design: VPC, encryption, and identity and access management.
  • Comfortable operating with autonomy in a small, fast-paced environment and wearing multiple hats.
  • Bachelor's degree in a related field is required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • AWS certification (Solutions Architect – Professional).
  • Edge security/CDN and observability tooling.
  • Experience administering or governing enterprise AI platforms (e.g., OpenAI/ChatGPT).
  • Financial services or other regulated-industry experience.

Benefits options include:

  • Medical, dental and vision coverage
  • 401K with company match
  • 10 paid holidays
  • Accrue up to 17 vacation/sick days per year in your first year on a pro rata basis
  • Applicant may be eligible for annual discretionary bonus

No relocation assistance provided.

If you are looking to be a part of a winning team and meet the above requirements, we look forward to hearing from you.

description:

Bonhams is a global auction house with an 18th century heritage poised for transformative change. Our global operations are based in London, Paris, New York, Los Angeles and Hong Kong where we sell in over 60 categories, including motor cars, paintings, jewelry, and entertainment memorabilia.


Bonhams is an Equal Opportunity Employer. As part of our commitment to fight for equality, we work to ensure a fair and consistent interview process. We celebrate diversity and we are committed to an inclusive work environment.

About the Role

The Sale Coordinator is an integral role in the expert departments, supporting the Specialists in the successful delivery of auctions as well as the day to day running of both departments.

About the Departments

Bonhams Handbags & Fashion is a global destination for exceptional handbags, accessories, ready-to-wear and haute couture from houses including Hermès, Chanel, Louis Vuitton and Dior. Our sales celebrate craftsmanship, provenance and rarity, treating fashion as art and cultural heritage as well as luxury.


Bonhams Watch auctions offer vintage and modern timepieces from makers including Patek Philippe, Rolex, Omega, Audemars Piguet, Cartier and George Daniels. We are distinguished by our international team of specialists, white-glove care for every piece, and a global client base.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities

  • You will be the experienced user of Auctioneer 3, Bonhams’ bespoke Auction Management System and primary business tool for both departments.
  • You will be responsible for managing clients and their property throughout both departments’ sale cycles, including receipting property into A3, generating and issuing consignment contracts, requesting and uploading client details and payment management.
  • For both departments you will be the primary contact for a range of external stakeholders ranging from our clients to restorers and suppliers, escalating to your Specialists when required.
  • You will help co-ordinate the movement of property throughout the sale cycles, working with regional offices, Shipping, Operations & Photography to ensure efficient and compliant stock transfer.
  • You will work with Client Services, Operations and Shipping to support clients with after sale enquiries, including the resolution of payments and arranging shipping quotes for both purchased and unsold lots.

  • As an important part of both
    departments, you will also support on many day to day auction activities and ensure the departments have all it needs to run smoothly and effectively. Tasks will include responding to client enquiries pre and post sale,
    bidding and event management.
  • Assist with company-wide sale day activities such as clerking and phone bidding as needed.

In addition to the tasks and responsibilities listed, you may be required to perform other duties as assigned by your Manager. This is an in-person position and the expectation is to be in the office for all working hours.

Key Skills & Attributes

  • Strong time management and organizational ability
  • Excellent communication in all modes with both internal and external stakeholders
  • Ability to manage workflow and priorities in a fast-moving environment

What We Offer

In addition to an active and progressive work environment, Bonhams offers a competitive benefits package to encourage work/life balance, including:

  • 20 days
    paid time off (PTO)

  • 16 weeks fully paid parental leave (after one year) and flexible work arrangements
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company contribution (after one year)
  • Life insurance with AD&D
  • Short- and long-term disability
  • Tuition reimbursement (after six months)
  • Commuter benefits (transit and parking)
  • Employee assistance program (EAP)
  • Professional development: free online training and expansive content library
  • Employee resource groups: social club, diversity committee, mentorship program
  • Sponsored socials: annual summer and holiday parties, monthly birthday treats, weekly breakfast


Bonhams participates in E-Verify.

Applicants who best match the position needs will be contacted.

$20.00 -25.00 Hourly, depending on experience.
