title: Manager or Director of IT Operations
description:
Position Title: Manager/Director of IT Operations
Location: Huntsville, AL / Onsite
Reports To: Chief Information and Digital Officer

Position Summary

The Manager/Director of IT Operations is Rural Metro Fire’s designated Information Security Officer and owns cybersecurity, enterprise infrastructure (network, server, cloud, and endpoint), identity and access management, business continuity and disaster recovery, and IT service management for a distributed, 24/7 public safety organization. The role governs the managed service provider (MSP) that delivers the security operations center (SOC), IT Helpdesk, and project-level engineering support, retaining ownership of strategy, standards, risk, and outcomes while holding the MSP accountable for contracted services.

This role does not administer business or public safety applications (e.g., CAD, RMS, ERP, and SaaS business systems); those remain with their designated application owners and administrators. As Security Officer, it sets and enforces the security requirements those systems must meet and provides the secure infrastructure, oversight, and escalation support they depend on.

Title and level (Manager or Director) will be determined by the selected candidate’s experience and scope of prior leadership.

Essential Functions

  • MSP Oversight, Service Management, and Team Leadership
    • Own the MSP relationship for SOC, Helpdesk, and project support: govern scope, SLAs, escalation paths, and performance against the master services agreement; lead operational and quarterly business reviews.
    • Own IT service management processes (incident, problem, change, request, asset) across internal and MSP-delivered services; establish KPIs and reporting; ensure Helpdesk quality for a distributed, 24/7 workforce.
    • Define and maintain the MSP/internal division of responsibilities (RACI), escalation paths, and after-hours coverage.
    • Lead and develop internal IT operations staff assigned to the role; partner with, but do not administer on behalf of, business and public safety application owners
  • Cybersecurity and Risk Management
    • Serve as the company’s Information Security Officer: accountable to executive leadership for security posture, with authority to set security requirements for all systems and data, and primary point of contact for auditors, regulators, cyber insurance carriers, and law enforcement.
    • Own the cybersecurity program—strategy, policies, standards, and risk decisions aligned to NIST CSF/CIS Controls—and direct the MSP-provided SOC that executes monitoring, detection, vulnerability and patch management, and endpoint and email security; set requirements and SLAs and hold the MSP accountable for results.
    • Own identity and access governance (Entra ID/Active Directory, MFA, conditional access, privileged access, access reviews) and serve as incident commander for security events, coordinating response with the MSP SOC, cyber insurance carrier, and legal partners.
    • Understand and apply CMMC and NIST standards and lead assessment readiness; ensure compliance with HIPAA (where applicable), PCI DSS, and cyber insurance requirements, and manage security awareness training and vendor security risk.
  • Infrastructure, Cloud, and Network Operations
    • Own the architecture, lifecycle, and operation of networks (LAN/WAN, Wi-Fi, firewalls), servers and virtualization, storage, backup, and cloud platforms (Microsoft 365, Azure).
    • Ensure high availability, redundancy, and performance for mission-critical systems at headquarters, fire stations, dispatch, and remote sites.
    • Lead backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity planning and testing with defined recovery time and recovery point objectives.
    • Standardize the endpoint lifecycle (Intune/MDM) for office, station, and field devices; drive modernization, automation, and cost optimization.
  • Field Operations Technology Modernization (Station Alerting, Radio, and CAD Infrastructure)
    • Support modernizing field operations technology, including station alerting systems, radio and dispatch communications, mobile data/MDT connectivity, and the network, server, and integration platforms that CAD and related systems run on.
    • Design and deliver resilient, redundant connectivity and infrastructure for fire stations and apparatus (primary and backup WAN, cellular/LTE and FirstNet, Wi-Fi, power protection) so alerting, radio, and CAD services remain available during outages.
    • Lead evaluation, selection, and implementation of station alerting platforms and radio system upgrades (e.g., IP-based alerting, radio-over-IP, console and gateway integrations) in partnership with operations leadership, dispatch, and vendors.
    • Coordinate maintenance windows, change control, and disaster recovery testing for dispatch-critical infrastructure with operations leadership and vendors.

  • Vendor, Budget, Projects, and Governance
    • Develop and manage the IT operations budget, procurement, licensing, and contracts; negotiate MSP agreements, statements of work, and renewals.
    • Lead infrastructure and security projects, directing MSP project resources and ensuring scope, quality, security, and documentation standards are met.
    • Develop and enforce IT policies (acceptable use, access control, data protection, retention, change management); report security posture, risk, and project status to executive leadership.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Seven or more years of progressive IT experience, including three or more years leading IT operations, infrastructure, or security teams (Director level: ten or more years, including five or more years of leadership).
  • Experience building or maturing a cybersecurity program, including framework alignment, vulnerability management, identity and access management, and incident response.
  • Working knowledge of CMMC and NIST standards, with the ability to interpret controls and assess gaps.
  • Microsoft ecosystem experience: Windows Server, Active Directory, Entra ID, Microsoft 365, Azure, Intune, and Defender.
  • Strong networking and backup/disaster recovery knowledge.
  • ITSM/ITIL experience and vendor, contract, and budget management.
  • Excellent communication skills, including translating technical risk into business terms for executives.

Preferred

  • Experience managing an MSP or MSSP in a co-managed model, including SLA governance, service reviews, and contract management.
  • CISSP, CISM, CompTIA Security+, CCNA/CCNP, Microsoft Azure/Microsoft 365 security, or ITIL certifications.
  • CMMC credentials (CCP, CCA, or Registered Practitioner) or experience leading a CMMC Level assessment and remediation program.
  • Experience overseeing an outsourced SOC or MDR service; familiarity with SIEM, zero-trust architecture, and security automation.
  • Experience in a 24/7, multi-site public safety or other mission-critical environment; familiarity with HIPAA and PCI DSS.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Sets strategic direction for security and infrastructure while remaining hands-on when needed.
  • Exercises security authority over systems administered by others without taking over their administration.
  • Calm, decisive leadership during incidents and outages; risk-based prioritization of work and investments.
  • Drives outcomes through both direct authority and MSP contractual governance.
  • Communicates clearly with executives, operational leaders, field personnel, and technical staff; handles sensitive information with discretion.

Position Conditions

title: Certified Peer Specialist (CPS) - Temporary Observation Unit (TOU) - Adult CSU
description:
View Point Health

Job Title: CPS - Certified Peer Specialist

Job Code: SST012/Client Support Worker 3

Shift: Full-Time (40 hours per week on average)

Job Hours: 12pm - 8:30pm (Evenings)

Base Location: Lawrenceville, GA.

Division/Department/Program: Temporary Observation Unit (TOU) - Adult CSU

View Point Health is a state agency of Georgia that provides assessment, group counseling, medication management, recovery and crisis stabilization services for behavioral health and developmental disabilities.

The View Point Health Acute Services has three Crisis Stabilization Programs.

Our Adult unit is located in Lawrenceville, Georgia. We serve adult clients with psychiatric crisis intervention and stabilization services as well as substance use disorders.

Our Adolescent unit is located in Decatur, Georgia. We serve adolescent clients (14-17) with psychiatric crisis intervention and stabilization services as well as substance use disorder.

Our Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) unit is located in Conyers, Georgia. We serve adolescent clients (10-14) on the Autism Spectrum with severe and challenging behaviors with psychiatric crisis intervention and stabilization services.

A Crisis Stabilization Unit (CSU) operates 24 hours/7 days a week (including weekends and holidays) to provide a safe, structured and locked environment for clients experiencing a mental health or addictions crisis. The services are like residential treatment but provide a higher level of care due to the acuity of the clients who are in crisis. Our units operate much like a psychiatric hospital. A client’s stay with us is to help ensure he/she is stable from the prompting event of their crisis prior to discharge. Clients do not leave the facility during their stay with us. The Temporary Observation Unit (TOU) is located onsite in the same building as the CSU. It also operates 24/7 and is a locked environment for clients who may be experiencing a mental health or addictions crisis. This unit is reserved for the observation and assessment of a client to determine level of care needs in a 23 hour or less time period. During time on TOU a client may or may not be on an involuntary status and will be assessed by a nurse, physician, and clinician. A paraprofessional and CPS may also provide services during this time to assess the clients’ overall needs and level of care. At the end of their stay in TOU the treatment team must determine if the client necessitates CSU or inpatient services or if they are safe for discharge into a lower level of care such as ACT, ICM, or general outpatient services.

Our goal for Acute Services is to provide person-centered care and utilize a trauma-informed approach to our client and throughout their treatment experience with us.

Currently at our Adult Unit, we are looking for a Certified Peer Specialist to join our team working the Temporary Observation Unit. This position is on-site and does not accommodate a remote schedule or working from home.

Duties & Responsibilities:

The Certified Peer Specialist (CPS) will work to build connections with adult clientele placed in the Temporary Observation Unit. The CPS will assist in needs identifications, solution brainstorming and self-advocacy. CPS are tasked with providing meaningful resources that support the client to increase wellness and resilience and assist with transition back to the community when cleared for discharge. The CPS will assist/partner with the multi-disciplinary team, in developing responsive and flexible resources, while cooperatively working to ensure smooth transitions to other levels of care.

Specific responsibilities include:

  • Complete initial billable activity (MH Peer Supports-Individual H0038 U4/U5 U6) with each client in the TOU during shift (maximum 6 individuals). Sessions must be a minimum of 30 minutes (2 units) with each client that is able to participate and should not exceed 2 hours (8 units).
  • Complete any follow up billable activities to clients that were previously met with in TOU in the last 23 hours (Psychosocial Rehabilitation Individual H2017 HE U5 U6 OR Case Management T1016 U5 U6). Sessions must be a minimum of 15 minutes (1 unit) with each client that is able to participate and should not exceed 2 hours (8 units) for PSRI or 3 hours (12 units) for CM.
  • May complete Family Training W/Out Client (H2014 HS U5 U6) or Family Training W/Client (H2014 HR U5 U6). Clients should have family training sessions documented whenever clinically warranted based on criteria. Session must be a minimum of 15 minutes (1 unit) and no longer than 3.5 hours (14 units).
  • Billable sessions include the following:

o Share lived experience one-on -one to provide support to clients

o Engage and build professional supportive relationships with clients

o Assist clients with selecting appropriate services to suit their recovery goals

o Empower clients to advocate for themselves through effective modeling

o Refer clients to community-based resources, support, and opportunities

o Identify goals for recovery

o WRAP planning

o Suicide prevention education and skills

o Assist client in identifying triggers and coping tools

o Intervene when client is exhibiting crisis behaviors and assist with de-escalation

  • Complete all documentation within 24 hours of service, and adhere to all documentation guidelines and service definitions for interventions in order for services to appropriately be billed.
  • Act as an intermediary with clinical mental health staff by advocating for recovery-based interventions
  • Complete handoff report for treatment team.
  • Meet daily billing goals of 4.5 hours (18 units or 360 units per month). Communicate with supervisors when unable to complete due to census or other reasons.
  • Support in completion of authorization requests for TOU.
  • Address all failed claims/activities and daily review of Carelogic alerts.
  • Comply with all Viewpoint Health company policies specific to the employee manual and additional site-specific guidelines.
  • Rotation of evening and weekend coverage of TOU.
  • Support with CSU clients as needed/assigned
  • Perform any other tasks or duties as assigned by supervisor

Minimum Qualifications:

High school diploma/GED and three (3) years of job-related experience in a social services-related position; or one (1) year of experience at the lower-level Social Services Tech 2 (SST011) or equivalent position.

Note:

  • Certified Peer Specialist (CPS) Certification lived experience.
  • Ability to work weekends, evenings, or holidays when scheduled

Preferred qualifications:

  • Previous work experience as a CPS - Certified Peer Specialist
  • Previous work experience in a crisis stabilization setting or IFI/ACT team experience.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a helping profession

Requirements/Competencies:

  • Must be able to lift 20 pounds.
  • Requires long periods of sitting/standing.
  • Must be able to respond quickly to sounds.
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit, move about, hear and speak.
  • Must be able to pass physical requirements of MANDT training (i.e. - standing from knees without using hands, regular transitions from knees to standing, and perform holds).
  • Must be able to restrain an individual over 100 pounds.
  • Candidates for selection must pass a criminal background check (including fingerprinting).
  • Must pass a pre-employment drug screen and subject to random drug screens.

Note: Some positions may require a valid driver's license.

Benefits (for qualified employees):

  • State Health Benefits Package (medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability, long-term care, legal services, flexible spending accounts)
  • Paid New Hire Training
  • Company contributes additional 7.5% of salary to 401(a) Retirement Plan
  • No employee deduction for Social Security
  • Additional benefits such as legal services, Employee Assistance Program and discounted tickets to attractions, shopping, technology, and travel
  • Supervision, training, and continuing education opportunities available

title: Security Engineer, Business Continuity & Risk
location: Bay Area, CA, United States of America
description:
Block is one company built from many blocks, all united by the same purpose of economic empowerment. The blocks that form our foundational teams — People, Finance, Counsel, Hardware, Information Security, Platform Infrastructure Engineering, and more — provide support and guidance at the corporate level. They work across business groups and around the globe, spanning time zones and disciplines to develop inclusive People policies, forecast finances, give legal counsel, safeguard systems, nurture new initiatives, and more. Every challenge creates possibilities, and we need different perspectives to see them all. Bring yours to Block.

The Role

Square Financial Services, Inc. (SFS) is Block’s bank. We opened in March 2021 and provide lending and FDIC-insured deposit products to individuals and small businesses on a nationwide basis.

SFS Risk Management is scaling vendor security, third party risk, and business continuity through innovation. Our Risk team designs and promotes the frameworks, standards, and oversight that elevates security considerations among our vendors, simplifies our regulatory obligations, and ensures resilience in our business operations. The team also operates the agent-first platforms that turn those frameworks into running systems.

Most of governance is a data problem. The risk, control, and asset information needed to answer "are we secure and compliant?" is dispersed across dozens of systems: Security Engineers treat that as an engineering problem. You'll build the data pipelines, integrations, and agentic AI workflows that turn manual governance processes into products that run continuously, produce measurable results, and hold up to audit end to end.

You Will

  • Own and operationalize a SFS third-party risk management and business continuity program program.
  • Define the technical approach for ambiguous, cross-team problem spaces. This is an early-stage program, and you will frame problems as often as you solve them.
  • Build and operate the pipelines and integrations that aggregate, normalize, and join risk, control, and asset signals from systems of record across Block and SFS, including source control, the service registry, identity, ticketing, and data platforms.
  • Translate standards and compliance requirements into policy-as-code: enforceable, testable rules that run continuously. For example, "every production service has an accountable owner" becomes a versioned, tested check instead of a quarterly spreadsheet.
  • Design agentic AI workflows that pair LLM reasoning with deterministic, auditable decision layers for evidence analysis, control monitoring, classification, and assessment.
  • Automate evidence collection and continuous control monitoring to replace point-in-time audit preparation.
  • Partner with Security, Procurement, Resilience and Engineering teams to find the manual processes most worth turning into a product.
  • Contribute to technical design discussions, evaluating the security and reliability properties of the platform itself.

You Have

  • Third-party risk management and business continuity experience.
  • 4+ years building production software in backend, platform, data, or software engineering
  • Multi-year ownership of a production system, including on-call, SLOs, and the maintenance work that starts after launch
  • Proficiency with at least one of Python, Kotlin, Java, or Go, and comfort reading unfamiliar codebases
  • Hands-on experience building with LLMs (prompting, tool use, agents, or LLM-backed features) and opinions about where model judgment belongs and where it doesn't. Judgment matters more here than volume
  • Experience with integration patterns: REST APIs, webhooks, authentication flows, event-driven architectures
  • Experience pulling, normalizing, and joining data from multiple imperfect sources, and handling the edge cases gracefully
  • Experience defining technical direction where the problem was ambiguous, and carrying it across team boundaries
  • Attention to detail balanced with pragmatism about risk-based prioritization
  • Curiosity, persistence, and comfort operating with minimal structure in an early-stage program

Nice to have:

  • Working knowledge of a security or compliance framework such as PCI DSS, SOX, SOC 2, ISO 27001, or NIST. Prior GRC experience is not required; we can teach the governance side
  • Production-scale LLM or agentic systems experience

You Know

Ideal candidates will have familiarity with some of the technologies in our environment:

  • Languages & Frameworks: Python, Java, Kotlin, Go
  • AI: LLM APIs (we build on Claude), agent frameworks and tool-use patterns such as Model Context Protocol, eval harnesses
  • APIs & Data: HTTP, JSON, gRPC, Protocol Buffers, SQL, Snowflake
  • Infrastructure: AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD (Buildkite), event-driven architecture

title: Grants Specialist VI
description:
Department Information

This recruitment may be used to fill multiple vacancies

Opt in below to receive text message updates on CDHS recruiting events!

CDHSCareers

Description of Job

This position is designated as hybrid with 3 days in office per week.

Please note: These working arrangements are subject to change.


This position is located within the Behavioral Health Administration (BHA) which is responsible for policy development, service provision and coordination, program monitoring and evaluation, and administrative oversight for the public behavioral health system.

Located within the Behavioral Health Administration work unit, pursuant to House Bill (HB) 21-1097. HB21-1097 provides that a Behavioral Health Administration (BHA) was created to be a single state entity. It was initially established under CDHS as of July 1, 2022, and provides administrative and “back-of-the-house” support as long as the BHA remains under CDHS’ purview. The BHA is a permanent entity that is responsible for leading and promoting the state’s behavioral health priorities and efforts across agencies, creating shared goals, improving collaboration, and driving accountability and transparency. The BHA provides oversight and coordinate service standards across the hundreds of behavioral health programs that currently exist under multiple state agencies and the Judicial Branch. The BHA also works to ensure the recommendations that resulted from the work of the Behavioral Health Task Force (BHTF) and multiple ancillary projects evolving out of the work of the BHTF are honored and implemented, to ensure and meet our vision of having a comprehensive, equitable, effective continuum of behavioral health services that meets the needs of all Coloradans. The Behavioral Health Administration (BHA) is responsible for policy development, service provision and coordination, program monitoring and evaluation, and administrative oversight for the public behavioral health system. BHA funds, supports and monitors numerous mental health and substance abuse community programs and providers, and reviews and designates the State’s 27-65 providers and licenses substance use disorder service providers. BHA executes the State’s federal responsibilities as the State Mental Health Authority and the State Substance Abuse Authority for the purposes of administering federal mental health and substance abuse block grant funds.


Job Duties:

Grant Oversight:

  • Directs the agency’s formal grant vetting process including grant application intake forms and decision workflows to enforce strategic alignment, thorough upfront project/budget planning, and evaluate organizational risk before submitting grant applications.

  • Leads proposal development, writing assignments, narrative editing, logic model development, and budget architecture for dollar grant applications.

  • Provides technical assistance to program directors to translate complex federal Notice of Funding Opportunities (NOFOs) into executable project plans.

  • Monitor the federal register and other sources of information about discretionary grant opportunities and emerging potential funding opportunities, determining fit with the Office strategic plan and summarizing viable alternatives for leadership review.

  • Tracks grant application statuses, Notices of Award (NOAs), budgets, submission documents, and reporting deadlines.

  • Establishes agency-wide protocols, standard operating procedures (SOPs), desk manuals, and workflow priorities while continually monitors team performance.

  • Lead the preparation of letters of support/commitment and maintains bolierplate agency descriptions for grant proposals.

  • Maintain boilerplate language that describes the Department, Office, and Divisions to be used in grant applications.
    Complete all State, Departmental and Office clearance documents to ensure that submissions are cleared completely prior to submission.

  • Applies a rigorous "Go/No-Go" evaluation matrix to assess project feasibility, capacity constraints, budget requirements, and strategic fit.

  • Manages post-award transition frameworks upon receipt of new NOAs to prepare programmatic leads for implementation.

Audit Compliance & Systemic Governance:

  • Leads BHA’s agency-wide contract monitoring framework, establishing standardized tools and risk assessment protocols.

  • Serves as the central lead for external state and federal audits (e.g., Office of the State Auditor SUPTRS Single Audit).

  • Coordinates cross-divisional compliance data gathering and prepares final audit packages for executive leadership.

  • Establishes standardized grant and contract closeout procedures to ensure adherence to audit and retention requirements.

  • Designs and delivers staff training on grant compliance, subrecipient monitoring, and federal/state regulations (e.g., 2 CFR Part 200).

  • Maintains the central library of BHA grant/contract policies, SOPs, and internal control documentation.

Supervision:

  • Supervises a team of 6 FTE staff directly or through lower-tier management.

  • Handles recruitment, hiring, onboarding, workload prioritization, and performance evaluations.

  • Provides regular coaching, identifies professional development needs, and resolves employee performance or grievance issues.

Other Duties as assigned:
The needs of this position are highly dependent upon the federal and other grant funding landscape and evolves based on funding needs to support BHA funding diversity.

Experience Only:

Nine (9) years of relevant experience in an occupation related to the work assigned to this position

OR

A combination of related education and/or relevant experience in an occupation related to the work assigned equal to nine (9) years.

title: Senior Embedded Software Engineer – RFIO / RF Systems Integration
description:
We’re looking for humble geniuses who believe engineering can turn the impossible into reality—and who are driven to design, build, and test solutions that matter for some of the world’s most trusted companies. If you want to do meaningful work with a diverse team that believes in shared wins, continuous learning, and engineering a brighter future, this is the place for you.

We are seeking an experienced Embedded Software Engineer to develop and integrate software that controls, calibrates, and interfaces with RF transmit/receive systems. This hands-on role combines C/C++, Python, RF hardware, FPGA/firmware, and laboratory testing to characterize system performance, develop calibration and compensation techniques, and troubleshoot complex hardware/software issues.

Location: Phoenix, Arizona. On-site preferred, 3+ days/week

Citizenship: U.S. Person

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain RFIO software interfacing embedded software/FPGA with RF subsystem hardware.
  • Develop C/C++ software to configure, control, monitor, and characterize RF and mixed-signal devices.
  • Implement multi-channel transmitter control, including phase alignment, beamforming, power/gain leveling, and programmable RF components.
  • Develop receiver calibration and compensation techniques for gain, phase, sensitivity, temperature, and other RF variations.
  • Integrate RF hardware with FPGA/firmware, embedded software, and system-level components.
  • Interpret device datasheets and develop low-level register/configuration interfaces.
  • Develop Python test and automation for laboratory equipment, RF testing, data collection, and analysis.
  • Perform hands-on laboratory integration, characterization, measurement, troubleshooting, and debugging.
  • Diagnose cross-domain issues involving software, FPGA/firmware, RF, and hardware.
  • Work across RF, FPGA, hardware, systems, and software teams to resolve technical issues.
  • Follow disciplined software processes for requirements, traceability, verification, validation, configuration management, and documentation.

Required Qualifications

  • 5–15 years of relevant engineering experience in embedded software and hardware/software integration.
  • Strong C and C++ development skills.
  • Experience developing embedded or FPGA-facing software interfacing directly with RF or mixed-signal hardware.
  • Practical understanding of RF transmit/receive signal chains, including phase, gain, synchronization, power leveling, sensitivity, calibration, and temperature compensation.
  • Experience configuring hardware through low-level interfaces and device registers and interpreting component datasheets.
  • Strong Python skills for test automation, instrumentation, data collection, and engineering analysis.
  • Experience debugging issues across software, FPGA/firmware, and hardware.
  • Hands-on experience with oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, and RF/electronic test equipment.
  • Strong mathematical and analytical skills related to calibration, signal behavior, and system characterization.
  • Ability to independently troubleshoot and drive root-cause resolution in a laboratory environment.
  • Experience with requirements, traceability, verification, and validation processes.
  • Experience with multi-channel RF systems, phased arrays, beamforming, radar, communications, electronic warfare, or similar RF-intensive systems.
  • Familiarity with DO-178B/C or comparable requirements-based software development and verification.
  • Must meet U.S. Person requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience developing multi-channel RF calibration algorithms.
  • Experience characterizing RF performance across temperature or other environmental conditions.
  • Experience automating RF laboratory equipment using Python.
  • Experience with SPI, I²C, UART, GPIO, or similar device-control interfaces.
  • Familiarity with FPGA-based architectures and software-to-FPGA interfaces.
  • Aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability embedded product experience.
  • Experience supporting formal integration, verification, qualification, or certification activities.

title: Clinical Director
description:
Position Overview: Provides direct oversight of the facility Clinical Department. Manages the hiring, supervision, and evaluation of staff. Directs the implementation and management of clinical programs and initiatives. Provides clinical oversight of the daily operations of the facility, including the assessment, psychosocial treatment, and discharge of patients. Provides crisis response and support throughout the facility. With the support of RCA's corporate clinical team, develops, plans, and implements strategies for program continuation and growth. Provides clinical training to staff and interns.

Specific Responsibilities:

Directly oversees Clinical Supervisors (if applicable), Clinical Coordinator(s), Manager of Case Management, Primary Therapists, Case Managers, and Group Facilitators and/or Counselors including hiring, training, performance evaluation and coaching, and disciplinary action (in cooperation with Human Resources Business Partners). Supports the day-to-day operation of the facility by overseeing and participating in assessment, active treatment via individual and group psychotherapy, discharge planning, and milieu management (in cooperation with the Director of Nursing and RSS Supervisor). Ensures adequate clinical staff to provide patient care services while maintaining adherence to regulatory requirements and FTE budgets. Drives Clinical Quality KPIs including progressions to Outpatient, aftercare planning, and census management through the Clinical and Case Management staff. Ensures active treatment 7 days a week by developing, implementing, and maintaining accountability to the program schedule. Ensure all clinical documentation is completed accurately and in a timely manner, maintaining compliance with regulatory, accreditation, and organizational requirements across the department. Meets patient needs by working with the clinical team to reduce barriers to treatment, address patient concerns which could lead to a discharge against advice. Provides clinical supervision to staff with a focus on trauma-informed and family-oriented care in adherence with the care model core principles Regularly engages in in-vivo supervision/observation of group psychotherapy to evaluate and improve the skills of Primary Therapists and Group Facilitators. Alongside the Medical Director and Director of Nursing, serves as a primary clinical leader by facilitating clinical meetings, providing clinical consultation to all staff, and modeling appropriate clinical decision-making. Represents their facility and RCA in the community (e.g., referral sources, aftercare providers, community organizations) with the utmost professionalism. Provides crisis management in the facility while acting as a leader and modeling appropriate patient-focused de-escalation skills. Assists with the planning and facility-level implementation of enterprise-wide clinical initiatives. title: Mental Health Worker - Cape CBHC CCS (Saturday & Sunday 11pm-7am)
description:
Bay Cove Human Services’ mission is to partner with people to overcome challenges and realize personal potential. Bay Cove pursues this mission by providing individualized and compassionate services to people facing the challenges associated with developmental disabilities, mental illness, substance use disorders, and homelessness at more than 175 program sites throughout Greater Boston and Southeastern Massachusetts.
Job Summary: The CCS Mental Health Worker (MHW) provides direct services to adults in crisis at the CCS. The Mental Health Worker will carry a case load based on daily census and will provide direct care supports including admission, treatment planning, running groups, case management, and discharge. The Mental Health Worker ensures safety of all clients through provision of as needed 1:1 supervision, conducting and documenting checks, proactively addressing escalating behaviors. The MHW also provides for operation of the CCS in terms of meal set-up and clean-up; room maintenance; keeping the unit clean; and doing laundry. This is a non-exempt position. The Mental Health Worker supports coordination with the Cape Cod Community Behavioral Health Center (CBHC), helping clients understand available services and supporting warm handoffs and follow-up after crisis stabilization.
Essential Functions of Position:

Completes and documents admissions, treatment plans, client daily documentation, and discharge summaries in accordance with BCHS, DMH and applicable payer and regulatory standards.

Ensure that the unit follows the daily schedule of program activities, client meetings, and groups. Oversight of therapeutic groups as leader, co-leader, and observer.

Ensures for the cleanliness and upkeep of the unit, assists in meal preparation and cleanup, completes bed set up and gathers linens.

Maintains effective working relationships with insurers, DMH, local community resources, and treatment/rehabilitation programs throughout the Cape Cod community.

Participation in daily rounds with multidisciplinary team and follows up on identified issues for the unit and for the individual clients.

Ensures that safety protocols are routinely reviewed and followed consistently by all staff (such as emergency systems; identification and remedy of facility safety hazards; security systems; lock up of sharps and any potential toxins; hazardous waste management; checks protocols, checking vitals protocols, etc).

Support referrals and warm handoffs to Cape Cod CBHC outpatient, urgent, crisis, care coordination, peer, and recovery-support services under the direction of the clinical team.

Complete timely documentation in eHana and communicate information needed for CCS/CBHC admission, discharge, follow-up, and continuity-of-care workflows.

Participate in CCS/CBHC training, team consultation, and quality-improvement activities as assigned.

Performs all other duties and projects as assigned by supervisor.

Requirements for the position:
Schedule/shift: Saturday & Sunday 11pm-7am

Full-time, part-time/per-diem schedule for each opening.

Minimally 3 years’ experience working in a mental health setting.

Excellent writing and oral communication skills.

Demonstrated skills in working as an effective team player in a fast-paced unit

Ability to work collaboratively as a member of multi-disciplinary and cross-functional teams.

Demonstrated ability to work in a pressured situation and maintain clarity, focus, judgment, and compassion

Ability to provide leadership

Ability to identify problems and initiate solutions to problems

Ability to work with people in crisis in a hopeful and compassionate manner and model this for others

Ability to work independently

Physical Requirements

Must be able to lift 20 pounds and complete cleaning and laundry

title: Police Administrator (*Non-Classified)
location: Magnolia Police Station - 10540 Magnolia Ave. Riverside, CA
description:
The Position




The City of Riverside is accepting applications for the position of Police Administrator (*Non-Classified) to fill one (1) vacancy in the Police Department. The eligibility list established may be used to fill the current and/or upcoming vacancies within this classification. This position is posted continuously and will remain open for applications until the posting is closed, which may occur without prior notice at any time after October 8, 2026.

As a civilian member of the police executive team, directs the activities, through managers, of the following units within the Police Department: Accounting, Payroll, Police Technology, Fleet Services, Grants Management, and Facilities Management. Under management direction, manages and coordinates diverse and complex administrative services for the Police Department.

This is a civilian management classification that works as a member of the police executive team. The Police Administrator class is distinguished by the law enforcement services and level of difficulty and complexity of duties, the supervision of professional staff, and the breadth of managerial responsibility for a command (division) within the police department. This class is characterized by the responsibility to develop, manage, and coordinate the policies, programs, and financial operations of the police department. Incumbents exercise significant decision-making authority. Direct supervision is exercised over professional, technical and/or support staff. An incumbent may represent the Department Head before the City Council, City Manager, community groups, other City staff, and the public.

*Positions designated as Non-Classified are exempt from the classified service. The incumbent shall be appointed "at-will" and serve at the pleasure of the City Manager.

For positions indicating a salary range from 1N – 2X, the top 15% of the pay range cannot be offered upon hire or upon an employee promotion.

Work Performed

Duties may include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Plan, organize and direct the work of management, professional, technical and support employees in the Administrative Services Division, which may include, but are not limited to, Accounting, Payroll, Police Technology, Fleet Services, Grants Management, and Facilities Management.
  • Maintain asset forfeiture records in accounts separate from General Fund in order to accurately track income/expenditures.
  • Adhere to non-supplantation guidelines.
  • Keep Chief of Police or designee advised of financial implications of purchases made with
  • Assure all reporting requirements are timely met and correctly submitted.
  • Assist the department director in establishing and implementing organizational policies and procedures for department operations; monitor effectiveness of policies and procedures, and make revisions or recommendations for improvement as appropriate.
  • Direct and coordinate the fiscal and analytical operations of the department, which may include, but are not limited to, the functions of budgeting, fiscal control, accounting, purchasing, position control, grant preparation, administration and analysis, contract administration, fleet services, facilities management and capital improvements.
  • Conduct or direct complex studies pertaining to a variety of administrative and operational problems; determine actions appropriate for improvements; advise department director on findings and methods of effective solution; prepare written reports and make presentations to various City groups and officials.
  • Direct the preparation of technical and administrative reports.
  • Monitor financial reporting systems including monthly financial statements, comparison of actual revenues and expenditures to budget categories, monthly management reports on current financial status, and project activity status.
  • Maintain and supervise a system of internal accounting control and segregation of duties.
  • Supervise the preparation of the departmental budget; review, analyze and compile budgets of various programs and divisions; provide expenditure projections to Finance as requested; explain needs and provide justifications for items; review and decide on expenditure requests and budget variances; provide updates to Command Staff for effective expenditure control.
  • Oversee departmental computer operations; assist in identification and recommendation of computer software and hardware needs, acquisition/installation, application design and implementation; and computer operation and maintenance.
  • Prepare or supervise the preparation of and review grant proposals for various programs and projects of the department; interface with governmental agencies regarding requirements for obtaining funds and monitoring procedures; present proposals to various boards and commissions in order to gain approval for programs and projects.
  • Manage and direct personnel actions; define and resolve complex work problems; establish work standards and operational objectives in assigned area of responsibility.
  • Coordinate all audits related to departmental or program operation and services; explain procedures to auditors and serve as reference for questions.
  • Review, interpret, and analyze new and proposed legislation; determine effect of legislation on operations and programs of the organization served; advise superiors of findings; take appropriate action in order to ensure compliance with existing rules and regulations; propose legislation on own initiative or upon request.
  • Provide technical administrative support to City or departmental management, committees, or other personnel as assigned. Participate in the selection of professional, para-professional, technical, and support personnel; establish work standards; supervise, train and evaluate personnel.
  • Meet with other City departments, agencies, committees, community groups and public officials to coordinate and implement various projects and programs.
  • May represent the Department Head in administrative services matters in the Department Head's absence.

Knowledge of:

  • Federal, State and local asset forfeiture laws, including monitoring of proper expenditures in accordance with asset forfeiture laws and guidelines.
  • Applicable federal, state and local laws, rules and policies regarding local government operations.
  • Principles of management, administration and budgetary systems and procedures.
  • Methods and practices of modern police administration.
  • Research methods and techniques, statistical and work measurements, and standards development and implementation, and report presentation.
  • Personal computer operation and applications including work processing, database and spreadsheet.


Ability to:

  • Analyze and supervise the systematic compilation of technical and statistical data and prepare complex reports.
  • Plan, organize, supervise, and evaluate the work of professional, technical and support personnel.
  • Properly interpret and make decisions in accordance with laws, rules and policies.
  • Supervise and conduct analytical studies and prepare analytical reports of both policy and administrative matters.
  • Analyze organizational and administrative problems; recommend and adopt an effective course of action.
  • Present ideas, concepts and recommendations clearly and concisely in oral, written and chart form.
  • Establish and maintain effective and cooperative working relationships with staff, City officials and representatives of other governmental agencies, community leaders and the general public.
  • Coordinate activities with other divisions and City departments.
  • Operate personal computer and applicable software programs.

Qualifications

Education and Experience:

Education: The equivalent of a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with major work in public or business administration or a closely related field.

Experience: At least five years of professional administrative experience in local government. A master's degree may substitute for one year of the required experience.

Highly Desired Qualifications:
  • Strong knowledge of budget development, administration, and financial management principles and procedures.
  • Demonstrated experience monitoring expenditures to ensure compliance with asset forfeiture laws, regulations, and applicable guidelines.
  • Professional experience working within a law enforcement agency or related public safety environment.
  • Experience in local, state and federal grant oversite.

Selection Process

1) Completed Employment Application

FOR GENERAL INFORMATION ON COMPLETING YOUR ON-LINE APPLICATION, CLICK HERE: (Application Guide).

The Maintenance Technician is responsible for the repair, upkeep, and preventive maintenance of hotel facilities, guest rooms, and equipment. This role ensures that all building systems operate safely and efficiently, supporting a comfortable, well-maintained environment that enhances the guest experience.

The technician performs hands-on maintenance work and responds quickly to service requests to minimize downtime and guest disruption. This position operates in a fast-paced hotel environment requiring strong technical skills, attention to detail, and a guest-focused service mindset.

title: AV Technician
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

AV TECHNICIAN

SpaceX is seeking an AV (Audio/Visual) Technician to deliver exceptional support for conferences and events across the organization. As a key member of our team, you will work closely with our AV Administrators to master the use of AV equipment and systems, ensuring seamless experiences in our expanding network of conference rooms and event spaces.

In this role, you will be responsible for providing ongoing support for daily technical issues, maintenance, and general upkeep of all AV hardware and systems. You will also play a critical role in supporting live events, meetings, and hybrid/remote gatherings. To succeed, you must be a motivated, organized, and results-driven individual with excellent listening skills and strong oral and written communication abilities.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Support AV/VC solutions locally and globally to support in-region teams.
  • Support events around the SpaceX office from an audio/visual standpoint, and occasional out-of-hours event support.
  • Respond promptly to requests for technical support via email, ticketing, and chat as needed.
  • Responsible for troubleshooting hardware and applications, providing technical support, and problem solving.
  • Exhibit a high level of professionalism and are passionate about providing outstanding customer service.
  • Document the status of issues and provide updates to management, team, and end users.
  • Maintain standard operating procedures, best practices, and customer service guidelines.
  • Create documentation for AV troubleshooting and configuration for team members and end users.
  • Participate in onboarding and training team members.
  • Drive quality and adherence to best practices within the team.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate.
  • 1+ years of professional experience in AV support.
  • Professional experience in live audio and video production or video conferencing solutions and support.
  • Professional experience with Mac or Windows OS.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Familiarity with one or more of the following: Q-SYS, Logitech, Biamp, Extron, Shure.
  • Experience supporting Microsoft Teams or video conferencing technologies.
  • Experience with line drawings, signal flow, AV concepts.
  • Knowledge and ability to terminate various audio and data connections.
  • Cabling experience including pulling and terminating.
  • Construction or mechanical background.
  • Knowledge of layer 1 network technology.
  • Customer service, problem-solving, and teamwork abilities.
  • Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Q-SYS, CTS, Crestron DM, or similar certifications.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be willing to work all shifts, overtime, and/or weekends as needed.

title: Senior Archer GRC Administrator
description:
Tharros supports the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) with cybersecurity services across its Intelligence Enterprise.

In support of this mission, we have an immediate opportunity for a Senior Archer GRC Administrator. In this role you will configure, operate, and maintain the RSA Archer governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform that supports DHS security authorization and risk management. You will own the platform from server and database through the security controls catalog, workflows, and leadership dashboards, and train users across the enterprise. This position is on-site in a Government SCIF in Washington, DC.

Duties include but not limited to:

  • Configure, operate, and maintain the Archer GRC software toolset.
  • Install vendor patches; test and install updated versions of the GRC software.
  • Maintain the GRC server platform and manage the GRC database.
  • Configure, populate, and maintain the Security Controls Catalog (DHS 4300C, NIST SP 800-53, CNSSI 1253, IC overlays).
  • Tailor the tool for new use cases as requested by the Government.
  • Develop compliance dashboards for CSD leadership and system owners.
  • Set up and manage user accounts; train Government and contractor users within 3 business days of request.
  • Develop and maintain GRC SOPs and training documentation.
  • BS degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Information Systems, or Computer Science OR minimum of 10 years' experience in IT or cybersecurity.
  • Minimum of 7 years' IT or cybersecurity experience, including hands-on RSA Archer administration.
  • Active TS/SCI clearance and U.S. citizenship; willingness to undergo a DHS counterintelligence-scope polygraph.
  • Knowledge of RSA Archer architecture, application builder, workflow, data feeds, and reporting.
  • Knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 and CNSSI 1253 security control structures.
  • Knowledge of the Risk Management Framework (RMF) authorization workflow.
  • Skill in configuring GRC applications, workflows, and dashboards.
  • Skill in patching and upgrading enterprise applications.
  • Ability to train users of varying technical backgrounds.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite to include Teams or similar workplace chat and videoconferencing tools.
  • Excellent written and oral communications skills.

Desired

  • RSA Archer Certified Administrator or another professional GRC certification.
  • SQL Server administration experience.

title: Systems Analyst
description:
When you work with Clarke, you are working with an industry leader! Headquarters located in Cincinnati, with around 60 locations across the country, we are looking for a Systems Analyst to join our I.T. team! The Systems Analyst is responsible for the administration, support, security, and continuous improvement of the organization's technology environment. This role works closely with business stakeholders and IT team members to support Microsoft 365 services, virtualization platforms, endpoint management, identity and access management, cybersecurity initiatives, and business-critical applications.

The Systems Analyst applies technical expertise, analytical skills, and a strong customer service focus to identify, troubleshoot, and resolve technology issues while helping implement strategic technology solutions that support business objectives. Infrastructure & Systems Management

  • Administer and support VMware virtual infrastructure and associated systems.
  • Monitor server and infrastructure performance and take proactive measures to ensure reliability and availability.

  • Support enterprise storage, backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity solutions.
  • Networking concepts including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPN, and firewall technologies.
  • PowerShell scripting and automation.
  • Maintain technical documentation, diagrams, standards, and procedures.
  • Collaborate with IT team members to identify opportunities for process and technology improvements.
  • Participate in technology projects, infrastructure upgrades, and business initiatives.
  • Perform root cause analysis and implement long-term solutions to recurring issues.
  • Active Directory and Windows Server Support.
  • Management & Deployment of Certificates.

Citrix & Business Applications

  • Administer and support Citrix environments that deliver critical business applications.
  • Troubleshoot application performance and user access issues.
  • Collaborate with vendors and internal stakeholders to support enterprise software solutions.
  • Assist with application upgrades, testing, and deployment activities.
  • Experience with NetScaler management and troubleshooting

Endpoint Management & Security

  • Manage device deployment, configuration, compliance, and security through Microsoft Intune and SCCM.
  • Support endpoint protection initiatives using Microsoft Defender technologies.
  • Monitor and investigate security alerts and assist with incident response activities.
  • Implement security best practices, hardening standards, and vulnerability remediation efforts.
  • Participate in cybersecurity awareness and risk reduction initiatives.
  • Knowledge in Application Whitelisting for the enterprise.

Microsoft 365 Administration

  • Administer and support Microsoft 365 services including:
    • Microsoft Entra ID
    • Microsoft Intune
    • Microsoft Defender
    • Microsoft Purview
    • Exchange Online
    • Microsoft Teams
    • SharePoint Online
    • OneDrive for Business
  • Manage user provisioning, licensing, access controls, group membership, and identity governance.
  • Assist with the implementation and maintenance of Microsoft security and compliance solutions.
  • Support data protection, retention, governance, and compliance initiatives.

Si tienes experiencia en ensamblaje, manufactura, construcción, producción o en el uso de herramientas eléctricas, nos gustaría conocerte.

  • Revisar los productos terminados para garantizar su calidad y precisión.
  • Mantener el área de trabajo limpia y organizada.
  • Seguir las normas de seguridad y los procedimientos de la empresa.
  • Trabajar con el equipo para cumplir con los objetivos diarios de producción.
  • Ayudar con otras tareas de producción según sea necesario.

Lo que buscamos

  • Diploma de escuela secundaria o equivalente, preferido.
  • Capacidad para levantar 50 libras repetidamente durante turnos de 8 horas o más.
  • Capacidad para leer y utilizar una cinta métrica con precisión, incluyendo medidas de hasta 1/16 de pulgada.
  • Disponibilidad para trabajar horas extras cuando sea necesario.
  • Capacidad para trabajar en un almacén sin control de temperatura.
  • Capacidad para leer y comprender inglés básico.

Large area, heavy bodywork (including Bondo repair)

  • Mid-Level Prepper (min 3-5 years professional experience): perform bodywork on multiple panels, including heavy plastic welding, minor metal pulling, roof and rocker panel repair, stud welding, and large area heavy bodywork (including Bondo repair)

  • Must be at least 18 years of age and possess a valid driver’s license. Some positions may be subject to an Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check
  • An ability to work in a fast-paced, ever-changing production environment while sometimes being exposed to excessive weather conditions (heat/cold)
  • Use of safety equipment that may include but not limited to face shield or goggles, non-slip shoes, gloves, mask, and other protective garments and equipment

At Carvana, we sell cars but we aren’t car salesmen. Our promise is simple: we won’t sell a car to a customer that we wouldn’t sell to our own Mom. Period.

To make sure our cars are in first-rate condition, we’ve built multiple vehicle Reconditioning Centers around the country, where our cars are inspected, perfected, and photographed before reaching the Carvana website.

title: Data Engineer
description:
Als Data Engineer bij Zonneplan werk je aan iets dat de hele organisatie raakt. Je bouwt en verbetert het centrale dataplatform, maakt data veilig beschikbaar voor alle teams en legt de technische basis voor een nieuw ML-platform. Dat betekent: pipelines die betrouwbaar draaien, datakwaliteit die teams kunnen vertrouwen en selfservice-oplossingen waarmee collega's zelf aan de slag kunnen.


Dien uw cv en eventuele aanvullende vereiste informatie in nadat u deze omschrijving heeft gelezen, door op de sollicitatieknop te klikken.

Je ziet direct wat jouw werk oplevert wanneer dataverzoeken sneller worden afgehandeld en teams autonomer met data werken. Je werkt vanuit Team Infra en schakelt dagelijks met engineering, Trading & Optimization, GenAI en andere developmentteams. Denk aan een terugkerend dataverzoek dat je samen vertaalt naar een duurzame selfservice-oplossing, of een dataset die je veilig ontsluit zodat het GenAI-team er zelfstandig dashboards mee kan bouwen.

Agentic Engineering is een vast onderdeel van hoe we werken: je krijgt een Claude Code Max 20x-licentie (of equivalent) tot je beschikking en we moedigen actief aan om AI in te zetten bij alles wat je doet. De lijnen zijn kort, de impact breed. Zo help je Zonneplan datagedreven en AI-gedreven te werken, en dat versnelt plan Zero: betere data betekent snellere beslissingen en slimmere energiesystemen. Je werkt 32-40 uur per week met een salaris tussen €3.500 en €5.000 bruto per maand.

Jouw impact bij Zonneplan Jij bouwt en verbetert het dataplatform. Je ontwikkelt datapipelines en datamodellen die de hele organisatie van betrouwbare data voorzien. Je monitort wat er draait, signaleert problemen vroeg en lost ze op voordat ze impact hebben op dashboards, analyses of ML-toepassingen. Jij maakt data veilig en breed beschikbaar.

Je richt toegangscontroles en datakwaliteitschecks in zodat teams zelfstandig en verantwoord met data kunnen werken. Je vertaalt dataverzoeken vanuit de organisatie naar structurele oplossingen en verkort daarmee de doorlooptijd flink. Jij legt de basis voor het ML-platform. Je bouwt de technische fundamenten waarop toekomstige machine learning-toepassingen kunnen draaien. Je werkt daarbij nauw samen met andere developers om te zorgen dat het platform aansluit op wat zij nodig hebben, van modeltraining tot serving.

Jij werkt AI-gedreven en verbetert continu. Agentic Engineering is geen experiment, het is hoe we werken. Je zet tools zoals Claude Code in bij ontwikkeling, testen, documentatie en monitoring. Terugkerend werk automatiseer je en je deelt wat je leert actief met je team. Dit neem jij mee Je hebt minimaal 1 tot 2 jaar ervaring als Data Engineer en bent breed inzetbaar op het vakgebied. Je beheerst SQL en hebt ervaring met datamodellering en het bouwen en beheren van betrouwbare datapipelines.

Je denkt kritisch over datakwaliteit, betrouwbaarheid en veiligheid, en neemt daar eigenaarschap over. Je maakt technische onderwerpen begrijpelijk voor niet-technische collega's en werkt graag samen met andere teams om gebruikersbehoeften te vertalen naar oplossingen. Je signaleert verbeterkansen en pakt ze op zonder dat iemand je erom vraagt. AI zet je dagelijks in om sneller en slimmer te werken. Ervaring met tools uit onze stack zoals Dagster, Snowflake, Postgres, Kafka, dbt, dlthub, Airbyte, Kubernetes of AWS is mooi meegenomen.

Je hoeft niet alles te kennen, maar nieuwe tooling maak je snel eigen. Heb je eerder gewerkt aan data mesh of self-service analytics? Dan is dat een echte pre. Je snapt dan hoe je teams in staat stelt zelfstandig met data te werken zonder in te leveren op kwaliteit of veiligheid. Dit krijg je van ons Een salaris tussen €3.500 en €5.000 bruto per maand, afhankelijk van je ervaring en kennis. 25 vakantiedagen (met de mogelijkheid om er meer bij te kopen) en reiskostenvergoeding.

Een persoonlijk keuzebudget voor sport, boodschappen of iets anders dat bij je past. Vanaf dag één investeren we in jouw groei met de Zonneplan Academie, sterke tooling (waaronder een Claude Code Max 20x-licentie) en ruimte om te blijven leren. Het groeipad loopt van medior Data Engineer naar senior Data Engineer en op termijn naar Tech Lead Data. Een werksfeer waarin je snel schakelt met engineers, data-specialisten en productteams.

Je werkt in een team dat het fundament onder alles legt wat Zonneplan bouwt, en dat merk je in de waardering en de breedte van je impact. Samen bouwen aan de energie van morgen Bij Zonneplan werken we aan één duidelijk doel: een Nederland zonder fossiele energie. Wij noemen dat plan Zero. title: Onboard Infrastructure Engineer
description:
Company Introduction

At Bot Auto, we are revolutionizing the transportation of goods with our cutting-edge autonomous trucks, enhancing the quality of life for communities around the globe. With the agility of a start-up and the wisdom of seasoned experts, Bot Auto boasts a team that has achieved numerous world-firsts and unparalleled innovations. United by a shared vision, we create miracles and propel the future of transportation. Join us and transform your dreams into reality.

About the Role

We are looking for an Onboard Infrastructure Engineer to join our Autonomous Driving team. In this role, you will be responsible for developing and maintaining the onboard infrastructure that supports autonomous vehicle systems, ensuring reliable communication, data management, and system integration.

You would work on critical infrastructure projects for autonomous driving systems, such as implementing middleware/ROS core functionalities, conducting optimizations to reduce latency and improving system determinism. You will play a critical role in designing and optimizing the architecture that handles real-time data from sensors and computing hardware. This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of hardware, software, and real-world autonomous driving technology.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and implement onboard infrastructure modules (sensor driver, health management) to support real-time autonomous driving applications, ensuring computing efficiency, and SW reliability in resource demanding environments.
  • Monitor system performance and implement tools for diagnostics, logging, and recovery to ensure stable vehicle operations.
  • Optimize the deployment of autonomous driving software to embedded systems and onboard computing platforms.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree with 5+ years of experience, or a Master’s degree with 2+ years of experience, in Computer Science or a related field.
  • A strong willingness to develop computationally efficient code with consistently low runtime variance
  • Proficiency in C/C++ programming
  • Write robust, reliable codes

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experiences in Sensor SW development
  • Experience with ROS (Robot Operating System), or similar middleware for robotics and autonomous systems.
  • 3+ years of experience in onboard infrastructure, embedded systems, or systems engineering.
  • Experience with autonomous driving technologies or similar high-performance computing systems
  • Experience with RTOS (Real-time Operating System)
  • Experience with Nvidia Drive Products (Orin/Thor)

title: IT Security Operations Specialist
description:
Tharros supports the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) with cybersecurity services across its Intelligence Enterprise. In support of this mission, we have an immediate opportunity for an IT Security Operations Specialist.

In this role you will run day-to-day IT security programs inside DHS SCIFs, including SCI incident reporting, privileged user tracking, removable media management, equipment entry/exit and decommissioning, and IT security training and outreach. This position is on-site in a Government SCIF in Washington, DC.

Duties include but not limited to:

  • Identify, record, and report SCI IT security incidents in the GRC tool and to the DHS Enterprise SOC and IC Security Coordination Center.
  • Maintain the privileged user database; issue annual training memos and 30/60/90-day compliance reminders.
  • Administer the Removable Media Program in accordance with ICS 500-18, including training, waivers, Rules of Behavior, and tracking.
  • Inspect IT equipment entering and exiting SCIFs; review pre-procurement and PED request forms.
  • Coordinate sanitization and decommissioning in accordance with DHS 4300C and NSA/CSS Policy Manual 9-12.
  • Manage daily operations of the SCIF compliance oversight program (ICOP) and ISCR/ISSO designations.
  • Develop and update annual SCI IT security awareness, removable media, and privileged user training; deliver classroom sessions.
  • Produce IT security tips, newsletters, surveys, and briefings for non-technical audiences.
  • BS degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Information Systems, or Computer Science OR minimum of 6 years' experience in IT or security operations.
  • Minimum of 3 years' experience in IT security operations, SCIF compliance, or security program administration.
  • Active TS/SCI clearance and U.S. citizenship; willingness to undergo a DHS counterintelligence-scope polygraph.
  • Knowledge of ICS 500-18 removable media requirements.
  • Knowledge of SCIF IT equipment entry/exit, sanitization, and decommissioning procedures.
  • Knowledge of security incident reporting and handling processes.
  • Skill in maintaining compliance databases and producing metrics reports.
  • Skill in developing training materials and briefing non-technical audiences.
  • Ability to manage multiple recurring compliance programs and deadlines.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite to include Teams or similar workplace chat and videoconferencing tools.
  • Excellent written and oral communications skills.

Desired

  • Experience with NSA/CSS media sanitization procedures.
  • LMS administration or instructional design experience.
  • COMSEC familiarity to serve as a backup for two-person integrity.
  • CompTIA Security+ certification.

title: Staff Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
Staff Foward Deployed Manufacturing Engineer

Summary

The Staff Foward Deployed Manufacturing Engineer leads the deployment, ramp-up, and scaling of advanced manufacturing systems across multiple Deterrence Defense production facilities. This role owns critical manufacturing processes and equipment strategy at the program level, directing commissioning activities and driving cross-site standardization to ensure systems operate safely, efficiently, and reliably. The engineer serves as a technical leader for cross-functional engineering and operations teams — mentoring junior engineers and guiding project teams — to solve complex electromechanical and process challenges in fast-paced, high-throughput production environments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead development, installation, and ramp-up of advanced manufacturing equipment and automated systems across multiple sites or programs.
  • Own performance, reliability, and safety of assigned production equipment and serve as the escalation point for complex technical issues.
  • Direct root-cause analysis across mechanical, electrical, controls, and process domains, and guide others through structured problem-solving.
  • Drive equipment and process performance improvements through data-driven experimentation and continuous improvement, setting standards adopted across sites.
  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior and mid-level manufacturing engineers; may lead or coordinate cross-functional project teams.
  • Develop specifications, work instructions, operating procedures, and maintenance documentation, and review/approve documentation produced by others.
  • Partner with internal stakeholders, program leadership, and suppliers to define requirements, lead equipment readiness reviews, and validate equipment.
  • Support process controls, PLC/HMI interactions, automation troubleshooting, and system bring-up.
  • Ensure equipment meets all ergonomic, safety, and regulatory standards across all facilities it's deployed to.
  • Identify critical spare parts and lead preventive and predictive maintenance strategy across multiple lines or sites.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, or related engineering field.
  • 7+ years of experience in high-volume or high-precision manufacturing environments, including experience supporting or leading equipment deployment across multiple lines, programs, or facilities.
  • Strong understanding of core engineering principles applied to production systems, with demonstrated ability to apply them at scale.
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex electromechanical equipment and lead others through technical problem-solving.
  • Experience mentoring or informally leading other engineers or technicians.
  • Ability to travel between facilities and supplier locations as required.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with cycle time modeling, bottleneck identification, and throughput optimization.
  • Proficiency with DOE, SPC, Cp/Cpk analysis, Gage R&R, and real-time data monitoring.
  • Understanding of OEE tracking, yield analysis, and defect reduction methods.
  • Familiarity with PLCs, HMIs, SCADA, safety circuits, and automation debugging.
  • Knowledge of servo systems, pneumatics, vacuum systems, and motion tuning.
  • Experience leading FAT/SAT, commissioning, validation, and equipment acceptance.

title: Sourcing Engineer, ABCD, VR
description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Lead teams in identification of risks/hazards relative to new product designs, processes, suppliers, and applications.
  • Assist the mechanical category manager & Legal teams in negotiating and executing optimal contract terms with key new suppliers.
  • Participate in the supplier selection process and ensure supplier selections are based on sound selection criteria for new product introduction activities to select the right supplier for the part, considering long term fit and total cost of ownership.
  • Participate in periodic business reviews with key suppliers to review supplier performance on new product programs
  • Own the development and maintenance of the approved manufacturer’s list.

  • BS in Mechanical Engineering, Supply Chain or related field.
  • Minimum of three (3) years of experience in supply chain, technical sourcing, and/or engineering.

  • Experience with a high mix/low volume procurement environment is preferred.
  • Ability to work on multiple cross functional projects simultaneously.
  • Ability to develop strong relationships with key stakeholders to drive proper rigor in supplier selection process.
  • Self-motivation and ability to work in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to manage rapid changes typical during the NPI development process.

  • Strong proficiency in Google/Microsoft Office software packages.
  • Excellent communicator, ability to lead in an environment of in-direct control.
  • Communicates effectively in a dynamic, multidisciplinary team environment to meet internal and external customer demands.
  • Excellent analytic and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to lead and influence change in the face of complexity and ambiguity.
  • Proficient with managing and understanding cross-cultural business practices, especially within Asia.
  • Located or willing to relocate to Scottsdale, AZ.
  • Ability to influence without authority, create win/win situations, and produce results.
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, product specifications, procedures and standard.

  • Discretionary paid time off

  • Emotional & Mental Wellness support

Gorilla Logic is looking for a Senior Platform / DevOps Engineer with strong hands-on experience in Kubernetes, Terraform, and Python to join our team and support a production platform running complex, highly available workloads. In this role, you will take ownership of day-to-day platform operations, deployments, infrastructure automation, reliability, and production support.

The ideal candidate is comfortable challenging decisions when necessary, protecting engineering standards, and making thoughtful trade-offs rather than sacrificing long-term quality for short-term speed.


What you'll do

  • Manage application deployments, upgrades, configuration changes, and complex deployment lifecycles.

  • Support Kubernetes scaling and autoscaling strategies for production workloads.
  • Collaborate closely with development and platform teams to identify and resolve infrastructure and deployment challenges.
  • Participate in technical decisions and proactively identify risks, reliability concerns, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Maintain high engineering and quality standards, providing technical pushback when necessary to ensure reliable and maintainable solutions.
  • Take ownership of platform initiatives and drive issues through resolution with minimal supervision.


Required Qualifications


  • Strong hands-on experience managing Kubernetes in production environments.
  • Experience with Kubernetes deployments, scaling, troubleshooting, and operational management.
  • Hands-on experience with Terraform for provisioning and managing cloud infrastructure.
  • Ability to read and write Python for scripting, automation, troubleshooting, and platform tooling.
  • Experience with AWS cloud infrastructure, ideally including EKS or similar managed Kubernetes environments.
  • Experience with GitOps practices and deployment tools such as Argo CD.
  • Experience managing complex application deployment and upgrade lifecycles.
  • Proven experience troubleshooting, triaging, and supporting production incidents.
  • Strong understanding of infrastructure reliability, scalability, and operational best practices.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to independently investigate complex production issues.
  • Strong sense of ownership and accountability, with the ability to operate effectively with limited supervision.
  • Quality-first mindset with the judgment to balance delivery speed, reliability, and long-term maintainability.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.


Preferred Qualifications


  • Experience with Helm and Kubernetes package/deployment management.
  • Familiarity with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers.
  • Experience supporting GPU-based workloads or ML inference platforms.
  • Familiarity with NVIDIA Triton Inference Server.
  • Experience with Chainguard, distroless container images, Trivy, or container vulnerability reduction.
  • Experience implementing or improving Kubernetes autoscaling solutions.
  • Familiarity with streaming or messaging platforms such as Apache Kafka or similar technologies.
  • Experience with Elasticsearch or ArangoDB.
  • Experience troubleshooting complex service-to-service networking.
  • Exposure to OpenShift, IL5, FedRAMP, or similarly constrained environments.
  • Familiarity with AI/ML or agentic AI development environments.
