title: Senior Cybersecurity Engineer
description:
Tharros is seeking a Senior Cybersecurity Engineer to support a DHS cybersecurity program in the National Capital Region.

This role will provide senior technical direction across cybersecurity engineering, cloud security, DevSecOps, AI/ML security, Zero Trust, security tooling, and technical architecture. The ideal candidate is a hands-on technical leader who can translate complex cybersecurity requirements into scalable, secure, and executable engineering solutions across cloud, on-premise, classified, and unclassified environments.
Responsibilities:
  • Provide senior technical direction across cybersecurity engineering, cloud security, DevSecOps, AI/ML security, and Zero Trust activities.
  • Work with enterprise architects, system architects, developers, and security teams to integrate cybersecurity requirements into reusable technical architectures and engineering practices.
  • Assess and recommend scalable, resilient cloud architectures that incorporate cybersecurity and safeguarding requirements.
  • Support cybersecurity tool configuration, maintenance, integration, and improvement across enterprise environments.
  • Support STIG implementation, vulnerability scanning, secure configuration, and security tool maintenance.
  • Identify opportunities to apply automation, emerging technologies, and process improvements to improve cybersecurity engineering delivery.
  • Develop repeatable security processes for cloud and AI capabilities.
  • Support technical remediation and assessment activities, including engineering support for Assessment and Authorization efforts.
  • Recommend, configure, operate, and maintain approved cybersecurity tools and applications.
  • Support Zero Trust maturity efforts, including capability gap analysis, implementation recommendations, roadmap development, and dashboard integration.
  • Integrate security into DevSecOps pipelines, including automation scripts, security testing, configuration validation, and continuous monitoring support.
  • Assess DevSecOps tool configurations, identify gaps, and recommend improvements.
  • Develop and apply tools and scripts to automate security requirements, STIG implementation, and configuration validation.
  • Support near real-time dashboards and reporting that improve visibility into security testing, vulnerabilities, compliance status, and cyber risk.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams throughout requirements, design, implementation, testing, delivery, and enhancement of secure IT solutions.
  • Support migration of IT services to cloud environments by identifying security requirements, risks, and technical issues.
  • Apply secure coding, security testing, static analysis, fuzzing, and threat modeling practices.
  • Active TS/SCI
  • 10+ years of cybersecurity engineering experience on projects of similar size and complexity.
  • AWS certification.
  • CISSP certification.
  • Scrum certification or demonstrated Scrum practices experience.
  • Experience with Federal, DHS, or Intelligence Community cybersecurity architectures, standards, and technologies.
  • Experience with cybersecurity engineering, cloud engineering, DevSecOps, AI/ML security, and Zero Trust.
  • Experience translating cybersecurity requirements into technical plans and engineering solutions.
  • Experience with security tools, secure configuration, vulnerability scanning, STIGs, cloud security, and DevSecOps automation.
  • Strong technical communication skills, including the ability to brief technical concepts and recommendations to stakeholders.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Prior DHS, Intelligence Community, CISO office, classified cloud, TS/SCI engineering, or national security cybersecurity experience.
  • Certifications or experience with additional cloud platforms, including Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, or Microsoft 365.
  • Experience with GRC platforms, ACAS, Nessus, SCAP, SonarQube, GitLab, Splunk, Tanium, Tenable, or related Federal cybersecurity tools.
  • Experience with RMF, A&A, continuous monitoring, Zero Trust dashboards, DevSecOps pipeline security, cloud security architecture, and secure automation.
  • Experience supporting classified, hybrid cloud, cross-domain, or secure mission environments.
  • Experience developing dashboards, technical metrics, or executive-ready reporting for cyber risk, vulnerability posture, Zero Trust maturity, or security testing status.

title: Tree Climber

description:
Tree Climber

What We Offer·

  • Benefits: Health and dental insurance, paid time off, 401(k) Savings Plan, and Flexible Spending Plan

title: Assistant Director, Office of Animal Care & Institutional Biosafety
description: Position Summary This position assists in the management of regulatory guidance for and support to the Animal Care Committee (ACC) and the Institutional Biosafety Committee (IBC). This includes review of animal use recombinant/ synthetic DNA and infectious agent research protocols and modifications; making regulatory determinations; shepherding the documents through the review steps; and assisting with other committee business, as necessary. Advises researchers/Principal Investigators on regulatory requirements and institutional policies and procedures. This position also serves as a liaison to UIC veterinary staff and UIC Environmental Health Safety staff. title: Sr. Infrastructure Engineer - SATX
description:
Company Profile
With over 80 years of innovation, JCB is the world’s largest privately owned manufacturer of construction and agricultural equipment. Operating 23 manufacturing facilities across four continents—including the United States, the United Kingdom, India, and Brazil—JCB produces a diverse portfolio of more than 300 products. These include telescopic handlers, backhoe loaders, excavators, wheel loaders, compact excavators, skid steer loaders, compact track loaders, access aerial work platforms, rough terrain forklifts, and tractors.

At the heart of JCB’s success are its people. As a family-owned business, we are accountable to our customers—not shareholders—which gives us the flexibility to focus on long-term innovation and delivering real value. This independence allows us to continuously develop advanced technologies and integrate them into equipment designed to perform in the toughest environments while maximizing customer productivity.

At JCB, we stand behind our products—and our name—with pride and commitment to quality.

Position Purpose
The Senior Infrastructure Engineer is responsible for the administration, support, optimization, and continuous improvement of JCB's IT infrastructure environment. This role serves as a technical expert across multiple infrastructure disciplines, ensuring the reliability, security, performance, and scalability of critical systems while supporting strategic business initiatives and providing advanced technical leadership.

Position Type
Full Time, FLSA Exempt

Location
13210 Palo Alto Rd., San Antonio, TX 78224

Benefits and Other Compensation
JCB offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance; 401 (k) retirement plan; paid time off and paid holidays.

Application Process
Applications will be accepted through Careers | JCB Careers | JCB Jobs | JCB or via LinkedIn. The anticipated application window will close on October 15, 2026.

Major Tasks, Responsibilities & Key Accountabilities

Administer and support Microsoft Windows Server and Linux/Unix operating systems.
Manage Microsoft Active Directory environments, including Group Policy administration.
Administer and maintain virtualized infrastructure platforms, including VMware and Hyper-V.
Configure, manage, and support enterprise storage solutions and disk storage environments.
Administer and manage backup and disaster recovery solutions, ensuring data integrity and business continuity.
Monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize infrastructure performance across servers, storage, networking, and cloud environments.
Provide technical leadership and infrastructure expertise for business and IT projects.
Support and maintain network infrastructure, including Cisco Meraki network administration.
Create, maintain, and update infrastructure architecture documentation, diagrams, standards, and operating procedures.
Provide Tier III support for critical incidents, including participation in on-call support rotations and after-hours escalations.
Coordinate with third-party vendors to ensure service and support expectations are met.
Support MDF/IDF environments, including racking, stacking, hardware installations, inventory management, and environmental monitoring.
Other duties as assigned

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Minimum 10 years of experience supporting enterprise IT infrastructure environments.
Minimum 10 years of experience managing data center, MDF/IDF, and infrastructure hardware environments.
Advanced experience with Microsoft Windows Server administration.
Advanced experience supporting virtualization technologies such as VMware and Hyper-V.
Strong understanding of networking, storage, backup, and disaster recovery technologies.
Must pass any drug screens, background checks, and any pre-employment tests, which will be conducted in accordance with applicable law.

Preferred Qualifications

Technical certifications in Microsoft, VMware, Azure, AWS, Cisco, NetApp, or related infrastructure technologies.
Experience managing enterprise cloud platforms including Microsoft Azure and/or AWS.
Experience supporting SAP infrastructure environments.
Experience with Cohesity, Rubrik, or similar appliance-based backup technologies.
Experience administering Cisco Call Manager, Cisco WebEx, or VoIP technologies.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities & Competencies

Expert-level proficiency in three or more of the following areas:

Windows Server Operating Systems
Linux/Unix Operating Systems
Azure and AWS Cloud Technologies
Enterprise Networking (LAN/WAN/Wireless)
Storage Technologies (NetApp preferred)
Microsoft 365 Administration
Backup and Disaster Recovery Technologies
SAP Infrastructure Support
VoIP Systems Administration

Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
Ability to work in a high-stress environment.
Detail-oriented and able to work independently.
Collaborative approach to resolving issues impacting various groups across the enterprise.
Ability to understand processes (system and non-system), troubleshoot, develop, and recommend solutions.
Enjoy working in a dynamic environment and be a self-motivated team player.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office products, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and Microsoft Project.

Job Conditions

Both office environment and occasionally manufacturing/factory environment.
Subject to noise and temperature changes.

Physical Requirements
The physical demands described here are representative of those required of an employee to perform the essential functions of this job successfully. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to:

Remain stationary, operate hands to finger, handle, or feel, reach with hands and arms, and talk or hear.
The employee is occasionally required to stand and move and/or walk.
The employee must frequently move and/or transport up to 10 pounds.
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

Equal Opportunity Employer
JCB is an equal employment opportunity (EEO) employer in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. JCB complies with applicable state and local laws governing non-discrimination in employment at every location where the company has facilities. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability statute, or any other characteristic protected under federal, state, and local laws.
EEO EMPLOYER/VET/DISABLED.

JCB complies with federal and state disability laws and makes reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees with disabilities. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact the JCB Human Resources team at hrsupport@jcb.com.

JCB Inc. is not currently hiring individuals for this position who now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status; however, as a global company, JCB offers many job opportunities outside of the U.S., which can be found through our website at https://www.jcb.com/en-gb/about/careers.

JOB SUMMARY:
Under direct supervision, assists in overseeing school age programs, operations, and staff of one or more assigned sites for children over four (4) years of age. Performs duties of school age staff.

  • Regular attendance at Employer's place of business and/or during particular hours, as assigned, is an essential function of this position. Employee must comply with and follow YWCA’s attendance policy at all times, unless a reasonable accommodation is requested and granted, as required by law.

  • Assists in supervision of day-to-day programs, operations, facility, staff, participants, business and record keeping for assigned site(s) for children age four (4) or older to ensure the safety and the physical, cognitive, social and emotional development of each child in a nurturing and appropriate environment.

  • Assists in training new and tenured assigned employees to ensure compliance with standards, resolution of deficiencies identified in monitoring, and the improvement of overall program quality and staff development.

  • Routinely performs duties of assigned staff or assigned site as needed or to fill or ensure qualified child/staff ratio, spending a minimum of 30% of time role modeling tasks.

  • Under supervision of Director, is accountable for record keeping, accounts, budgets and regulatory compliance with Texas Department of Family and Protective Services (TDFPS) standards and other appropriate government laws, regulations, and contractual agreements.

  • Ensures nutrition of children enrolled through direct supervision of kitchen staff, food management and compliance with USDA standards.

  • Ensures enrollment by assisting Director with continued marketing of program(s).

  • Monitors, detects and reports abuse or neglect according to Texas Family Code and TDFPS Minimum Standards.

  • Participates in and cooperates with investigations into parent, participant or staff complaints, grievances, charges, claims and hearings as requested.

  • Assists in selection and purchase appropriate materials and equipment and reporting transfer/disposal of equipment and needed repairs to supervisor.

  • Maintains regular communications with supervisor to discuss progress, issues, and concerns.

  • Conducts and attends training and meetings as required, including participation annually required hours of training per TDFPS minimum standards.

  • Interprets YWCA purpose, imperative and mission to staff and public.

  • Follows all YWCA policies and procedures, including safety procedures, at all times.

  • Responsible for all equipment, supplies, documents and materials related to job.

  • Communicates all problems and questions to supervisor.

  • Complies with all federal, state, and local regulations.

  • Communicates with all levels of staff and public as appropriate to the job.

YWCA SUMMER CAMP ONLY:
– Provides full-time care at YWCA outdoor summer camp.
– Works closely in-ratio with activity leaders to carry out summer camp schedule of activities.
– Reports to director school age (activities and staffing) during summer camp.

JOB QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Must meet TDPRS minimum standard director qualifications which includes graduation from high school or equivalent, plus one of the following:

a. Associate applied sciences degree in child development, or related degree with six (6) college credit hours in child development and six (6) college credit hours in business management and two (2) years’ experience in a licensed childcare facility; or

b. Child Development Associate (CDA) credential with six (6) college credit hours in business management and two (2) years’ experience in a licensed childcare facility; or

c. Sixty (60) college credit hours with at least nine (9) credit hours in child development or early childhood education, or the equivalent and six (6) credit hours in business management and two (2) years’ experience in a licensed childcare facility; or

d. A day care administrator’s credential issued by professional organization or educational institution that is recognized by the Licensing Division based on published criteria and two (2) years of experience in a licensed childcare facility; or

e. Three (3) years’ experience in a licensed childcare facility and nine (9) credit hours in childcare, child development or early childhood education and nine (9) credit hours in business management from an accredited college or university. Five (5) continuing education units (CEUs) may be substituted for each three (3) credit hours; or

f. A bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with twelve (12) credit hours of child development or early childhood education, six (6) credit hours of business management and one (1) year of experience in a licensed childcare facility.

  • Two (2) years of related childcare experience required.

  • Previous supervisory experience required; or any equivalent combination of experience and training that provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities.

  • Must be at least 18 years of age.

  • Love of children, patience, stamina and flexibility required.

  • Must be able to work other than regular scheduled hours.

  • Must be able to cope with emergencies, adept at mediating/resolving disputes and problem-solving.

  • Must be a self-starter, have creative energy, and be enthusiastic.

  • Must be well organized and be able to handle multiple priorities.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, as well as listening skills, required.

  • Excellent interpersonal skills required, with ability to interact at all levels.

  • Must be able to work under pressure with constant interruptions.

  • Must be able to work independently and autonomously as required.

  • Must be able to make sound judgments, have excellent decision-making skills, and possess strong conflict resolution skills.

  • Bilingual capabilities in English/Spanish preferred.

  • Must be familiar with operation of personal computer and data entry.

  • Must have access to vehicle and possess valid driver's license and sufficient liability insurance.

  • Must acquire CPR, First Aid, DFPS background check, FBI fingerprint and food handling certifications prior to start of employment. Must maintain these certifications throughout employment.

  • If you have lived out of state in the past five years you are required to submit for criminal history and child abuse/neglect check for the different states you have resided in.

  • Must supply physician statement of current negative TB test and freedom from communicable diseases.

ANTICIPATED BENEFITS:
YWCA Membership and Program Discounts
Basic Life Insurance, Retirement
Medical, Dental, and Vision

title: IT System Administrator 2 - Juneau / Anchorage (PCN 068536)
description:
Job Description

Come join the State of Alaska!

This job class uses Competency Based minimum qualifications (MQs). Please read the

Competency Based MQ instructions below to learn more.

The Department of Family & Community Services is recruiting for IT System

Administrator 2 in Anchorage/Juneau!

This position is open to Alaska Residents only.
Please check our residency definition to determine if you qualify.


What You Will Be Doing:

  • Supervise and mentor Site Support staff (Systems Administrators I), providing technical guidance, workload coordination, and performance support to ensure consistent, high-quality service delivery.
  • Oversee site-level server, Active Directory, GPO, networking, and workstation support activities, ensuring adherence to standards and validating the quality of work performed by the team.
  • Plan, assign, and manage site support projects—including server upgrades, GPO deployments, network improvements, and operational initiatives—while monitoring progress and removing obstacles.
  • Provide advanced troubleshooting for escalated issues across file/print services, Active Directory, GPOs, WAN/Ethernet/Wi-Fi networks, and entry-level datacenter components, guiding staff through resolution.
  • Coordinate with management and cross-functional teams to improve processes, develop documentation, and ensure alignment between site operations, datacenter standards, and organizational goals.

Mission and Values/Culture:
The mission of the Department of Family and Community Services (DFCS) is "To provide support, safety, and personal well-being for vulnerable Alaskans.”

The Network Services (NS) of DFCS works as a team with the Customer Service section of IT, Business Applications (BA), Project Management Office (PMO), and the Department Security Office (DSO) to keep the department technologically operational and secure

Benefits of Joining Our Team:

We are a dynamic, diverse, high performing team where no two days are the same. You will have the ability to use your technical expertise to serve some of the greatest teams of people in Alaska who are dedicated to keeping all Alaskans healthy and safe.

As a State of Alaska employer, we offer competitive wages, generous medical, vision, and dental benefits, personal leave, 12 paid holidays per year, and great retirement benefits

The Working Environment You Can Expect:

This is an in-office position located in Anchorage. The office is in the Frontier Building, located in midtown Anchorage. This office has been recently renovated and offers a vibrant setting. We are a dynamic enterprise development environment. This team is a diverse, highly technical, and collaborative group which embraces, implements, and supports the latest technologies to provide the best operational capabilities and resources to DFCS

Who We Are Looking For:

We are interested in candidates who possess some or all of the following position specific competencies:

  • Customer Service: Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services
  • Technical Expertise: Effectively applies technical knowledge to solve a range of problems; develops technical solutions to new or highly complex problems that cannot be solved using existing methods or approaches; is sought out as an expert to provide advice or solutions in the technical area.
  • Technical Problem Solving: Troubleshoots, diagnoses, analyzes, and identifies system malfunctions to determine the source and cause of the problem.

To view the general description and example of duties for the position please go to the following link: https://www.governmentjobs.com/careers/alaska/classspecs/1845288keywords=it%20system%20administrator&pagetype=classSpecifications

If you can imagine yourself in this role, we encourage you to apply!

Minimum Qualifications

Competency Based Minimum Qualifications Instructions
This job class uses competency based minimum qualifications. Please ensure your application (through work history, volunteer experience (duties summary), training, education, licenses, certifications, etc.) supports how you have gained the knowledge, skills, abilities, and behaviors (competencies) and that you possess the minimum required competencies for the job class.

Competency Description
The competency description(s) listed below have been designed to promote a common understanding of the essential elements of the job class. They highlight the more general and customary knowledge, skills, abilities (KSAs), tasks, and behaviors used to describe the competency. They typically list expectations, as opposed to specific tasks, and are to be used only as parameters and guidelines. A competency’s description is not intended to exclusively define every KSA, task, and behavior needed to successfully meet the competency, but rather to provide the manager/agency with a broad reference of options as to how an applicant can meet the job expectation.

Any combination of education and/or experience that provides the applicant with competencies in

  • Hardware: Knowledge of specifications, uses, and types of computer or computer-related equipment.
  • Infrastructure Design: Knowledge of the architecture and typology of software, hardware, and networks, including LANS, WANS, and telecommunications systems, their components and associated protocols and standards, and how they operate and integrate with one another and with associated controlling software.
  • Operating Systems: Knowledge of computer network, desktop, and mainframe operating systems and their applications.
  • Systems Integration: Knowledge of the principles, methods, and procedures for installing, integrating, and optimizing information systems components.
  • Systems Testing and Evaluation: Knowledge of principles, methods, and tools for analyzing and developing systems testing and evaluation procedures and technical characteristics of IT systems, including identifying critical operational issues.

Equivalent to those typically gained by:

Training in computer science, information technology, system administration, or a similar field and professional experience in database, network, or system administration.

Special Note:

“Competencies” means a combination of interrelated knowledge, skills, abilities, and behaviors that enable a person to act effectively in a job or situation.

“Typically gained by” means the prevalent, usual method of gaining the competencies expected for entry into the job.

“Training” means the process of acquiring knowledge and skills through instruction. It includes instruction through formal and informal methods (such as classroom, on-line, self-study, and on-the-job), from accredited and unaccredited sources, and long-duration (such as a post-secondary degree) and short-duration (such as a seminar) programs.

“Professional experience” means work that is creative, analytical, evaluative, and interpretive; requires a range and depth of specialized knowledge of the profession's principles, concepts, theories, and practices; and is performed with the power or right to decide or act according to one's own judgment.

“Progressively responsible” means indicating growth and/or advancement in complexity, difficulty, or level of responsibility.

Additional Required Information

At the time of the interview, please provide the following:

  • Copy of academic transcripts with your application if you will be using education to meet the minimum qualifications and/or competencies desired for the position. (Unofficial are acceptable but must include the institution name/URL on the transcripts). Please provide them at the time of the interview if they are not included in your application.
  • A list of three (3) professional* references including daytime telephone numbers and email address; at least two (2) of these must be from a current or former supervisor.

*Professional is defined as a supervisor or an individual who has direct knowledge of your work performance.


Supplemental Questions

For your application to be evaluated you must answer the Supplemental Questions.

The State of Alaska (SOA) uses four levels of proficiency to measure and describe an applicant's level of competence in applying certain behaviors, knowledge, skills, and abilities to accomplish a specific task. The proficiency levels are Mastery, Fluency, Literacy, and Discovery. You will need to rate your proficiency for each competency listed in the supplemental questions.

You must also complete the “References” section in the application. In the reference section please provide contact details for a minimum of three (3) individuals who can attest to your work performance, technical skills, and job competencies, in which one (1) of the three (3) references must be a current or former direct supervisor.


Please read the below information carefully. This applies to your application submission.

NOTE: Attaching a resume or curriculum vitae is not an alternative to filling out the application in its entirety. Noting "see resume or CV" or any similar response on any portion of your application may lead to a determination your application is incomplete and removal from consideration for this job posting.

EDUCATION
To verify education being used to meet the required minimum qualifications, you must fill in the Education section of the application. If you have not obtained a degree, please indicate the number of units completed. Copies of transcripts are required to verify educational credentials being used to meet the minimum qualifications for a position and are required with each application. (Unofficial are okay, please ensure that the institution/URL name is listed on the transcripts). Transcripts can be attached at the time of application, provided at the time of interview or if not provided, transcripts will be required prior to appointment.

SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS FOR FOREIGN EDUCATION
Education completed in foreign colleges or universities may be used to meet the above requirements, if applicable. If utilizing this education you must show that the education credentials have been submitted to a private organization that specializes in interpretation of foreign educational credentials and that such education has been deemed to be at least equivalent to that gained in conventional U.S. education programs; or an accredited U.S. state university reports the other institution as one whose transcript is given full value, or full value is given in subject areas applicable to the curricula at the state university. It is your responsibility to provide such evidence when applying. Omission of required documentation listed will result in an incomplete application and you will not receive further consideration.

WORK EXPERIENCE
When using work experience not already documented in your application, please provide the employer's name, your job title, dates of employment, and whether full-or part-time. Applications will be reviewed to determine if the responses are supported, and minimum qualifications are clearly met. Work experience needed to meet the minimum qualifications must be documented in the application. If the application does not support minimum qualifications, the applicant may not advance to the interview and selection phase of the recruitment. A resume will not be used to determine that minimum qualifications have been met for the position in which you are applying.

If you are currently or previously been appointed to a flexibly staffed position, please ensure your work experience within a flexibly staffed position indicates the actual dates employed at each level. Ensure your time and any subsequent flex promotion(s) are documented as a separate position. This is required as there are minimum qualifications that require experience at a particular level in which the lower level may not be considered. If this information is not accurately reflected in your application this may cause the processing of your application for consideration to be delayed.

LEGAL EMPLOYMENT
The State’s online recruitment system, Workplace Alaska, requires applicants to certify that they have a legal right to accept employment in the United States. It is the responsibility of the employee to maintain the appropriate documentation to accept or continue legal employment. The State of Alaska does not function in the role as an employer sponsor.


NOTE: The State of Alaska does not provide VISA Employer sponsorships.

RECRUITMENT SCOPE: This position is open to Alaska Residents.

description:
OnTrac is hiring a Customer Experience Senior Coordinator!

Are you eager to join a dynamic and expanding company where you can both learn and make a meaningful impact? If you possess a strong sense of empathy, enjoy assisting others, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and excel at problem-solving, we encourage you to apply today to connect with a recruiter!

Founded in 1986, OnTrac has evolved into the leading provider of same-day and next-day delivery services in the U.S. for premier e-commerce and product-supply businesses, including five of the largest retailers in the U.S.

Location: Hybrid Any HUB in Network OH Dayton, NJ Swedesboro, NJ Groveport, IL Romeoville, Orlando FL, Fort Mill SC, TN Lebanon, CA Fremont, CA Fontana, CA Los Angeles, NV Reno, NV Henderson, TX Desoto

Compensation: The expected starting base pay range for this position is $32.31 - $40.38, with full potential base salary range over a successful candidate’s tenure in the position of $32.31 - $48.46. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, internal equity, and other job-related factors.
Employment Logistics:
The Customer Experience Senior Coordinator supports the day-to-day execution of OnTrac’s Customer Control Tower within a 24/7 operating model. This individual contributor independently handles complex operational issues, supports reporting and data-quality activities, and helps ensure consistent execution of escalation and white-glove processes. This role does not own a customer portfolio and has no direct reports. The Senior Coordinator provides experienced operational support across customers, shifts, and business needs, serves as an escalation resource for Coordinators, and assists leadership with performance reporting, MBR/QBR preparation, and process improvement.

Unpacking the Benefits:

Employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package which may include:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Life and short- and long-term disability coverage
401(k) retirement savings plan with company match
Flex vacation in states other than CA, CO, IL, MA, MT, and NE, with accruals up to 96 hours for first year of employment with tenure-based increases up to 160 hours
Two (2) floating holidays per year
Paid sick leave*
Six (6) paid company holidays
Two (2) weeks paid pregnancy disability leave, four (4) weeks paid parental bonding leave
Additional wellness and employee assistance programs

Benefits eligibility and offerings are subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable plans and company policies.

The Must-Haves:

High school diploma or equivalent; Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience preferred
3+ years of experience in customer operations, logistics, transportation, customer service, supply chain, reporting, or a related field
Experience managing escalations, service issues, incident response, or time-sensitive operational requests
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Outlook, Teams, and other business or reporting applications
Ability to work evenings, weekends, overnight shifts, holidays, or on-call schedules as business needs require
Experience in parcel, transportation, logistics, supply chain, command center, or Control Tower operations preferred
Experience validating operational reports, researching performance issues, or using dashboards and metrics to support decisions preferred
Experience assisting with MBRs, QBRs, customer reviews, or executive-level performance materials preferred
​​It is the responsibility of every position to understand and adhere to the security guidelines outlined in OnTrac’s Acceptable Use policy and to conduct their activities accordingly.​

Your Mission in Motion:
A summary of key responsibilities for the role is outlined below. Additional duties may be assigned as needed to support business objectives.

Control Tower execution & escalation management: Independently monitor, assess, document, and coordinate customer and operational escalations; evaluate severity, urgency, and business impact; engage the appropriate teams or leaders; and provide accurate updates through resolution.
Incident response & Coordinator support: Serve as an escalation resource for Coordinators when issues require additional judgment, cross-functional coordination, or leadership visibility; support incident response during service disruptions, peak periods, and other high-volume or high-risk events.
Reporting quality & operational insights: Review recurring customer and operational reports for accuracy, completeness, and timely delivery; investigate discrepancies, data anomalies, and service-performance questions; coordinate corrections or escalations; and maintain audit logs and supporting records.
Performance reporting & process improvement: Support daily, weekly, and monthly reporting on escalations, service trends, customer issues, and operational performance; identify recurring patterns and summarize findings for Consultants and leadership to support root-cause analysis and process improvement.
Customer reporting & business reviews: Prepare customer-facing reports, performance updates, operational summaries, and resolution recaps; assist with MBR/QBR preparation, including data validation, issue research, trend identification, performance summaries, and presentation support.
Customer support & white-glove execution: Support customer calls, operational reviews, ad hoc information requests, manual reporting, and customer-specific operational needs without owning a portfolio; execute white-glove monitoring, conduct shipment research, identify emerging risks, and initiate escalation when service commitments are at risk.
Cross-functional coordination & issue resolution: Partner with Operations, Field Operations, Transportation, Linehaul, Network Planning, Quality, Customer Success, and other teams to resolve issues and close action items; communicate systemic risks and recurring issues with clear supporting context.
Team enablement & process consistency: Guide Coordinators on procedures, reporting, documentation, and escalation handling; support onboarding, peer training, and knowledge sharing; contribute to updates to SOPs, escalation workflows, reporting processes, and quality-control practices; and help maintain consistent execution across shifts.

Paving your way to your success:

You communicate clearly in writing and verbally, summarizing issues, impacts, actions, and outcomes for customers and internal stakeholders.
You demonstrate strong attention to detail, organization, and follow-through across escalations, reports, and documentation.
You make sound decisions, prioritize competing work, and remain effective in a fast-paced, high-visibility environment.
You coach peers, support onboarding, and serve as a trusted subject matter resource when needed.
You effectively support enterprise, strategic, and high-risk customer accounts without direct portfolio ownership.

title: Senior Product Engineer
description:
Open the Door to Your Future with Clopay Corporation & CornellCookson

At Clopay Corporation, we are more than just North America’s largest residential and commercial garage door manufacturer—we are a powerhouse of innovation, safety, and design. Through our premier brands, we lead the industry in providing groundbreaking high-performance closure solutions for both the places people call home and the spaces where the world does business.

Headquartered in Mason, Ohio, and operating state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities in Troy, Ohio, Russia, Ohio, Mountaintop, Pennsylvania, and Goodyear, Arizona, we are a proud American-owned company and a wholly owned subsidiary of Griffon Corporation. Our reach extends across 55+ distribution centers and thousands of retail locations in the U.S. and Canada ensuring that we deliver the right door for every opening – from homes to businesses and beyond. By joining our team, you become part of a legacy that blends the residential elegance of Clopay, known as "America’s Favorite Garage Doors," with the industrial strength and 180-year heritage of our rolling brands, Cornell and Cookson. Together, we secure everything from family garages to the world's most iconic stadiums and skyscrapers.

We currently have an opening for a Senior Product Engineer in our Mason, Ohio location.

Summary:

Design, plan, test, communicate, and implement product engineering projects. Concentrate on the current product line, including specification maintenance, product design improvements, product approval, customer technical support, special applications, product education, and shop floor information.

Responsibilities/Principal Duties:

  • Resolve product related issues, including product design, feature enhancements, value engineering, installation, and applications. Works closely with Marketing, Sales, Production, Quality, and Manufacturing Engineering, and purchasing.
  • Implement strategic, multiple-plant, assigned product engineering projects via the engineering change process procedure. Completes other product engineering projects as assigned. Lead design engineer on projects with capital expenditures of over $1,000,000.
  • Initiate and implement product improvement and cost reduction ideas.
  • Implement product changes and specification changes in a timely manner in conjunction with other functional areas throughout Clopay. Troubleshoot production problems directly related to engineering specifications and bills of material.
  • Create detailed engineering analysis based on testing, experience, scientific theory, and engineering principles for use in the design and application of the product line or new product line extensions.
  • Communicate product specifications and product changes to internal customers and help in communications to external customers. Use the Engineering Release/Notice procedure as the primary tool in accomplishing this task and direct communications with external customers as required.
  • Train and educate various internal and external customers on product offerings and product specifications. Internal customers include production, marketing, and sales. External customers include customers, consumers, and regulatory agencies (governmental, legal).
  • Responsible for developing product cost and capital expenditure data as required.
  • Travel as required to customers, manufacturing plants, vendors, and to provide other company representation.
  • Assist sales representatives or customers in understanding their product requirements, installation methods, and their proper applications. Makes suggestions on available alternatives if possible.



Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • Collaborative technical supervision.
  • (If assigned): Engineering Co-ops: extensive supervision; CAD Operators: moderate supervision.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering or Engineering Technology.
  • Professional Engineer (P.E.) license preferred.
  • Engineer with minimum eight years’ experience in the garage door industry or ten years of other product engineering experience, with exposure to various types of manufacturing processes.
  • Heavily involved in product design and specifications.
  • Must be able to use common computer packages, including 3-D CAD, spreadsheet, word processing, and capital expenditure programs.



Why Choose a Career with Us?

We don't just manufacture doors; we engineer the "front door" of the American dream and the security of global commerce. At Clopay, we believe our strength lies in our people. From our design engineers to our manufacturing associates and delivery drivers, every member of the team plays a vital role in our success.

Our team members thrive because we prioritize:

  • Unrivaled Scale: Work for a market leader with a massive manufacturing footprint and a reputation for excellence that spans nearly two centuries.
  • A Culture of "What’s Next": We invest heavily in automation, sustainable materials, and smart-home integration to stay ahead of the curve.
  • Commitment to People: As a Griffon Corporation company, we provide the stability of a large organization with the tight-knit, collaborative feel of a specialized craft team.
  • A Legacy of Expertise: Join our "Pioneer Club"—a group of over 440 employees who have been with us for 20 years or more. We offer the stability of a market leader and a place where you can truly grow a lifelong career.
  • Commitment to Innovation: We aren’t just keeping up with industry trends; we’re setting them. Whether it’s our exclusive WINDCODE® technology or our award-winning designs, we provide the tools for you to do your best work.
  • Community Focused: Our success is linked to the well-being of our neighbors and communities. Through our partnership with Habitat for Humanity, Clopay employees help provide homes and security to families in the communities where we live and work.

title: Principal Activation & Engagement Lead
description:
This role is an essential part of our Public Affairs & Access (PAA) organization, specifically within Channel & Contract Management - Activation & Capabilities Enablement (ACE). PAA is dedicated to delivering impact through a fully integrated public affairs function that leverages our capabilities and world-class brand to ensure eligible patients gain access to life-saving medicines. As a member of this ACE team, you will have the opportunity to collaborate closely with key stakeholders across brand teams, commercial functions, operations, and Learning & Skill Development (L&SD). In this role, you will lead complex change initiatives, coach teams, and implement new capabilities to ensure seamless alignment across our commercial strategies.

### **The Opportunity**

As a **Principal Activation & Engagement Lead**, you will serve as the domain expert and strategic change agent driving complex operational transformations to transition brand teams to future-state PAA practices. In this role, you will design and execute targeted change initiatives, onboard brand teams, and partner with L&SD and cross-functional teams to build custom capabilities, streamline processes, and deliver tailored training. By mobilizing a champion network, holding regular office hours, and monitoring engagement health, you will coach teams through critical capability shifts, proactively address knowledge gaps, and ensure seamless, long-term adoption across the organization. Key responsibilities include:

- **Drive End-to-End Change Management:** Lead teams through current-to-future state transitions, ensuring seamless adoption of new PAA strategies, practices, and operational processes.
- **Deliver Tailored Training & Capability Building:** Partner with Learning & Skill Development (L&SD) to design and deliver comprehensive, bespoke PAA training programs addressing both foundational knowledge and advanced practices.
- **Lead Champion Networks & Direct Coaching:** Lead champion teams, actively onboard individual brands into PAA practices, and hold regular office hours to address knowledge gaps and provide direct support.
- **Optimize Operational Workflows:** Collaborate with Operations and the PAA Enablement & Process Lead to identify, revise, or overhaul inefficient processes and represent best practices across PAA workstreams.
- **Partner Across Functions:** Align with cross-functional partners to co-identify, build, and scale shared capabilities and platforms that can be leveraged across the PAA organization.
- **Measure & Report Engagement Health:** Document and report on the overall health of PAA engagement, track change adoption metrics, and proactively escalate challenges or risks.
- **Facilitate Special Projects & Workshops:** Lead and support high-impact initiatives, including large-group presentations, interactive workshops, and cross-brand alignment sessions.

### **Who You Are**

- **Education:** Bachelor’s degree required; an MBA or related graduate-level degree is a plus.
- **Commercial Experience:** Minimum of 8 years total professional experience, including at least 6 years of commercial experience in sales, market access, or customer insights (preferably within the managed care, pharmaceutical, or biotech industries).
- **Strategic Ownership & Execution:** Proven experience with sole ownership of commercial tactics, including the ability to articulate business problems, craft end-to-end strategies, and own content development from strategy through execution.
- **Change Leadership & Enterprise Mindset:** Demonstrated ability to lead complex change management initiatives, flex and thrive in an ambiguous environment undergoing transformation, and think with an enterprise-wide perspective.
- **Cross-Functional Collaboration & Coaching:** Strong interpersonal, leadership, and communication skills with a proven track record of building partnerships, coaching teams, and elevating the capabilities of others.
- **Business Acumen & Project Management:** Highly proficient in project planning, budgeting, oversight, and vendor management, with strong critical thinking skills and the ability to drive high-value business and customer outcomes.

title: Contract Planner
location: Long Beach, California, United States; Torrance, California, United States
description:
Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies.

Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.

Purpose

The Program Planner works closely with Program Managers (PMs), engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain teams to build and maintain program schedules from the proposal stage through part release and delivery. The role ensures that design, release, and supply-chain activities are synchronized to achieve program success.

As Divergent scales across multiple material systems and multiple factories, this role also builds the planning processes that make that scale repeatable. The Program Planner develops and documents standard approaches for planning programs that span more than one material technology and more than one production site — including the inter-factory logistics, material movement, and hand-off points that connect them.

The ideal candidate is self-motivated, detail-oriented, hands-on, and able to respond quickly in a fast-moving environment. We value leadership skills and those who conduct all activities with the highest integrity.

The Role

  • Partner with PMO and engineering during the proposal phase to develop detailed schedules (including design and release milestones). Continuously update the schedule as design progresses and communicate changes to all stakeholders.
  • Monitor real-time progress against the schedule, flag variances, and work with engineering leads to implement corrective actions that keep part release on-time.
  • Build and maintain multi-material program plans that account for the differing lead times, qualification paths, and process maturity of each material system, and sequence work so that the governing material constraint drives the schedule rather than surprising it late.
  • Develop the planning processes for programs that build across multiple factories — defining how scope is allocated between sites, how schedules stay synchronized, and how capacity, tooling, and material are balanced across the network.
  • Plan the inter-factory logistics that connect multi-site programs, including material and sub-assembly movement, transit and customs lead times, packaging and containerization needs, and buffer and inventory placement between sites. Partner with logistics and supply chain to build these into the program schedule rather than treating them as downstream assumptions.
  • Define and document the hand-off points and data requirements between sites and material streams (routings, work-center definitions, traveler and revision control) so that a part released at one factory can be planned and built at another without rework.
  • Maintain and/or collaborate with data teams for the development of tools necessary to professionally report out on status and health of relevant programs, including visibility that rolls up across materials, sites, and logistics lanes.
  • Participate in Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) meetings to ensure demand, supply, and production plans are synchronized across sales, engineering, and manufacturing — and across sites as the factory network grows.
  • Identify gaps in the scheduling or supply-chain processes, propose enhancements, and apply lessons-learned to future programs. Codify what works into repeatable, documented planning standards that scale to new materials, new factories, and new programs.
  • Other duties as required to achieve 99% on-time delivery.

Basic Qualifications

  • Ability to lawfully access information and technology that is subject to US export controls
  • A proven, progressing track record in planning, operations, manufacturing, supply chain management, or consulting
  • Experience building and maintaining integrated program schedules with defined milestones, dependencies, and critical path
  • Exposure to planning or coordinating work across more than one production site, process, or material system, including the movement of material between them
  • Experience using Microsoft Office
  • Solid interpersonal skills, motivated self-starter who can manage personal workload and execution to tight schedule

Preferred Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience in a start-up, consulting, or similar high-growth, fast-paced, rapidly changing environment
  • Direct experience planning multi-site or multi-factory manufacturing programs, including inter-site logistics, transit and customs lead times, and buffer strategy
  • Experience across more than one manufacturing process family (for example additive, casting, machining, composites, extrusion, or joining) and an understanding of how their lead times and qualification paths differ
  • Experience writing, rolling out, and driving adoption of new planning or supply-chain processes and work instructions — not only executing existing ones
  • Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems and project scheduling tools (for example Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or Primavera)
  • Collaborated successfully in a team environment to ensure cross-functional requirements are met
  • Advanced Excel skills; comfort with data and visualization tools (SQL, Power BI, Tableau) a plus
  • Strong communication (verbal and written) and organizational skills

Work Environment

This role is based on-site and works across the engineering, production, and warehouse areas of the facility, with periodic travel to other Divergent sites and to supplier or logistics partner locations as the factory network expands. The environment is fast-paced and cross-functional, with regular exposure to an active manufacturing floor where personal protective equipment is required.

title: Senior Software Product Designer
description:
About Formlabs:

Do you want to change how the world creates?

At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before.

We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us.

Your Impact:

The Formlabs Design Team is looking for a Senior Software Product Designer to shape the UX/UI design and development of user experience and interfaces across our embedded, desktop, and web products. As a member of the team, you will collaborate across creative and engineering disciplines, prototype at varying levels of fidelity, and contribute to creating products and user experiences that empower our customers to achieve their goals.

If you’re deeply technical and excited to ship products that ship products, we’d love to hear from you.

What You’ll Do:

  • Deeply understand the needs of Formlabs customers, translating their insights into innovative features.
  • Collaborate closely with engineering to refine designs and bring them to life, driving features from low-fidelity wireframes to pixel-perfect prototypes and all the way through to public release—where your work has a tangible impact on our customers and their creations.
  • Partner with product managers to ideate, define, and validate early-stage concepts for new features that deliver significant business value and exceptional user experiences.
  • Conduct in-depth research by collecting, analyzing, and synthesizing product usage data, creating high-fidelity prototypes, and validating assumptions with usability studies to uncover insights that inform customer-focused, strategic design decisions.
  • Conduct regular audits of the end-to-end user experience across our ecosystem and propose impactful initiatives to leadership.
  • Help design, grow, and maintain robust and scalable design systems that ensure consistency and efficiency across all products.

About You:

  • Have a proven track record of working on complex, technical products, ideally with experience spanning desktop, web, mobile, or embedded interfaces.
  • Bring a clear understanding of human-computer interaction principles, executing them effectively and communicating design intentions clearly to collaborators.
  • Demonstrate a strong and diverse portfolio that includes early-stage ideation, user research, and pixel-perfect designs.
  • Have deep expertise with design tools such as Figma and Adobe Creative Suite.
  • Thrive in a collaborative environment, where you can take and give constructive feedback in a culture where the best ideas win.
  • Leverage a technical background, with experience working closely with product and engineering teams.
  • Prior experience designing software for physical products and/or have a background in industrial design.

Bonus Skills:

  • An interest in 3D printing, CAD, embedded software, and/or related technologies.
  • Computer Science background or coding experience.
  • Experience with Qt, QML, or OpenGL.

Our Benefits & Perks:

  • Robust equity program to build future wealth through RSUs
  • Comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
  • 401K matching and access to financial advisors
  • Generous paid Parental Leave (up to 16 weeks)
  • Tenure-based paid Sabbatical Leave (up to 6 weeks)
  • Flexible Out of Office Plan – Take time when you need it
  • Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits
  • Healthy on-site lunches, snacks, beverages, & treats
  • Regular sponsored professional development opportunities
  • Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community
  • And of course… unlimited 3D prints

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing.

Our Candidate AI Guidelines are available here. Please give them a read.

Compensation

Every Formlabs employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. You’ll have the opportunity to share financially in the value we create together, with a shared incentive to build a business that succeeds over the long term. Equity will be a significant portion of your total compensation, and will increase over time in proportion to your impact. The base pay will be determined by your skills, qualifications, experience, location, and expected impact on the organization.

$135,000—$180,000 USD

title: Collections Analyst
description:
The Trade Desk is a global technology company and the world’s leading independent platform for digital advertising, with over 3,000 employees across more than 30 offices. Our technology helps advertisers reach the right audiences across the open internet — from streaming TV and podcasts to mobile apps, news, and more.

Advertising powers the content people love. By making it more transparent, effective, and responsible, we help support trusted journalism, quality entertainment, and creators worldwide. The world’s brands and agencies rely on us to reach their customers and grow their businesses responsibly.

The scale of our platform brings unique technical challenges — from processing massive datasets in real time to building systems that operate reliably on a global scale. When you work here, your impact is worldwide. We welcome diverse perspectives, encourage curiosity, and build teams that learn from one another. If you’re driven to solve meaningful challenges, we’d love to meet you.

What we do:

The Collections Analyst supports the Global Credit & Collections organization with a focus on invoice dispute analysis and resolution, global automated collections portfolio administration, process improvement, automation, and reporting. This role analyzes dispute trends and root causes, partners across the CAO organization, Business Team, and global regions to drive resolution, and administers the global automated collections portfolio of approximately 600 lower-value, lower-risk accounts. The role also supports process improvements and automation within the GetPaid Collections Module, including the evaluation of AI tools, and provides reporting and analytical support to the management team.

What you'll do:

Dispute Management and Root Cause Analysis

  • Analyze invoice disputes to identify trends, root causes, and opportunities to reduce recurring issues.
  • Partner with departments across the CAO organization and Business Team to research and resolve Order to Cash (O2C) disputes.
  • Monitor dispute activity and provide insights to help prevent recurring billing and collection issues.
  • Support escalations and resolution of complex or recurring disputes as needed.
  • Identify trends and opportunities to improve customer experience and reduce barriers to timely payment.

Global Automated Collections Portfolio

  • Administer and support the global automated collections portfolio (Auto Desk) of approximately 600 lower-value, lower-risk customer accounts.
  • Oversee accounts managed through FIS GetPaid's automated collections process, including automated statements, payment reminders, and follow-up communications.
  • Monitor account activity and intervene when customer issues, disputes, or other situations require human attention.
  • Serve as a global liaison across all three regions for the automated collections portfolio.
  • Identify opportunities to improve and expand automation within the portfolio.

Process Improvement and Automation

  • Identify and drive process improvements and efficiencies within the GetPaid Collections Module, including Automated Collections.
  • Evaluate opportunities to leverage automation and AI to improve collections, dispute management, and email management.
  • Explore and support the use of tools such as Claude and GetPaid capabilities, including Carla 2.0 and Carla Pro.
  • Partner with C&C leadership and relevant teams to implement and sustain process improvements.

Reporting and Management Support

  • Analyze dispute, collections, and automated collections data to provide reporting, insights, and trend analysis that support Credit & Collections management and drive performance improvements.
  • Support ad hoc reporting and analytical requests as assigned.

Who you are:

  • Degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, or related field, or equivalent work experience.
  • Experience in accounts receivable, collections, dispute management, invoice research, or related financial operations.
  • Strong analytical and root cause analysis skills.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across departments and regions.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office applications.
  • Experience with the FIS GetPaid Collections Module or similar collections, AR, or dispute management systems.
  • Experience supporting global or multi-region account portfolios.
  • Experience with process improvement, automation, or systems optimization.
  • Familiarity with AI or automation tools used in collections, AR, or email management.

title: Management Analyst 5 (MA5/CQCT)
description:
Description

Management Analyst 5

This is a full-time permanent, remote position. Employees may occasionally be asked to attend an in-person meeting or event based on business needs.


The Opportunity

This position will serve as the subject matter expert and lead analyst for the 340b program. They will analyze issues and processes related to creating and administering the 340b reporting program, provide regular consultation to legislators and HCA staff, develop strategies on completing and implementing data reviews and validation, and conduct research on best practices being developed by industry, government partners, and other states for similar programs. This position will regularly formulate recommendations for the 340B reports, for the legislature, and coordinate closely with the PDAB and DPT programs on the implementation of strategic and long-term planning activities projected over the next few years.


Key Responsibilities Include:

  • Serve as the subject matter expert and lead analyst for the 340B program providing expert-level analyses on complex issues related to drug affordability.
  • Analyze issues and processes related to the creation and administration of the 340B program, ensuring effective implementation of board directives.
  • Provide regular consultation to board members and Health Care Authority (HCA) staff including leg staff, pharmacy team, data team, legal, and senior leadership to facilitate informed decision-making.
  • Conduct research on industry best practices, governmental strategies, and initiatives from other states to inform board actions and policy development.
  • Develop and implement strategies for conducting complex data reviews, ensuring alignment with best practices and regulatory requirements.
  • Coordinate closely with PDAB, DPT, and data teams on the implementation of strategic and long-term planning activities and projecting initiatives including developing methodologies for data collection, fee collection, development of reports, and analyzing 340B data per the legislation.
  • Engage in business and organizational planning, including developing annual budgets, writing policy papers related to fee collection, data reports, data usage, and assessing technology needs for data management, development of dashboards, and public surveys.
  • Engage in business and organizational planning, including developing budgets, writing policy papers, and assessing technology needs for data management.
  • Oversee all GSR contract management services from start to finish for board members, partners, and transcription services done


Why You’ll Love This Role:

This position offers a rare combination of high-level state policy influence, groundbreaking legal and healthcare strategy, and career-defining ownership over a brand-new program. Instead of just maintaining an existing system, the person in this role will help write the blueprint for how Washington State manages drug pricing transparency.


What You Bring:

The ideal candidate thrives on turning complex data and emerging legislation into actionable state policy. As a natural strategist, you will bring the rare ability to translate intricate data reviews into clear, high-level guidance for legislators, executive leadership, and diverse HCA teams. You are not looking to just maintain an existing system; you are excited to roll up your sleeves, collaborate across programs!


Required Qualifications

Experience may have been gained through paid or unpaid activities. Please ensure any relevant experience defined below is outlined in your cover letter, resume, and application.

  • Expert-Level Strategic Analysis - Demonstrated ability to lead highly complex, unprecedented, sensitive, or enterprise-level analyses requiring advanced judgment, integration of multiple information sources, and consideration of significant organizational impacts.
  • Strategic Problem Solving and Executive Decision Support-Demonstrated ability to evaluate high-risk or organization-wide issues, anticipate short- and long-term consequences, develop strategic alternatives, and provide authoritative recommendations to executive or senior leadership.
  • Enterprise Process and Organizational Improvement- Demonstrated ability to lead major evaluations of programs, organizational structures, business processes, or service-delivery models and develop comprehensive solutions having broad or long-term organizational impact.
  • Strategic Policy and Impact Analysis- Demonstrated ability to evaluate complex or emerging laws, rules, policies, standards, and strategic initiatives and advise leadership regarding organizational implications, risks, implementation strategies, and necessary changes.
  • Major Project and Initiative Leadership- Demonstrated ability to lead highly complex, cross-functional, or enterprise-wide projects and initiatives involving significant organizational risk, executive visibility, competing priorities, and substantial stakeholder interests.
  • Executive Consultation and Communication- Demonstrated ability to serve as a subject-matter expert and trusted advisor to senior or executive leadership by translating highly complex information into clear strategic options, implications, risks, and recommendations.
  • Strategic Leadership and Organizational Influence- Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional analytical efforts, influence organizational direction, facilitate resolution of complex or competing interests, mentor or guide professional staff, and establish analytical approaches or best practices.
  • The ability to take action to learn and grow.
  • The ability to take action to meet the needs of others.


Preferred Qualifications

While these are not required, having them may help you stand out as an applicant.

  • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, public administration, law, public health, health administration, or a related field and five (5) years of demonstrated experience in two (2) or more of the following areas: Conducting research, analyzing policies, laws, rules, or regulations, conducting business analysis and developing requirements, Leading business projects, Managing business operations, Business policy development, Supervising.

  • Demonstrated experience with 340B programs or in analyzing and managing programs within the pharmaceutical industry, drug manufacturing, consulting, public health systems, government policy development, or the health care industry.

About the Clinical Quality and Care Transformation Division (CQCT):

The Clinical Quality and Care Transformation Division (CQCT) is responsible for designing and implementing clinical policy; conducting oversight and monitoring of all clinically related programs; and communicating with stakeholders, providers, plans, and delivery system partners on clinical activities and issues. Clinical policy and operations include leading the state in care transformation and supporting HCA programs. The Prescription Drug Program’s vision is to provide access to affordable, evidence-based medication by designing and delivering high quality, evidence-based pharmacy programs through collaborative and innovative prescription drug purchasing strategies. Our goal is to empower each other to provide exceptional services to our customers.


The Washington State Health Care Authority:

Better Health. Better Care. A Healthier Washington

At HCA, we work to ensure people across Washington have access to high-quality health care. As the state’s largest health care purchaser, we serve nearly 3 million Washington residents through Apple Health (Medicaid), public and school employee benefits, and behavioral health programs. Together we’re building a stronger Washington.

More than a benefits package:

We want our employees to have the support, flexibility, and benefits they need to do their best work and build a career that works for their life. As a Washington State HCA employee, you’ll have access to a comprehensive benefits package that supports your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance. Our benefits are designed to support you today while helping you plan for the future. Learn more about why HCA by visiting the Voices of HCA and the "Who we are" section of our website.


Your total compensation is more than your paycheck:

  • Remote work and flexible schedules
  • Medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance
  • Paid vacation, sick leave, and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid Family and Medical Leave (PMFL)
  • Retirement options to plan for the future
  • Training and professional development opportunities
  • Employee wellness programs
  • Learn more about Washington State Employee Benefits


Working Conditions

Work Location and Schedule:

This is a full-time 40-hour-per-week REMOTE position. Our standard business hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., with alternative work schedules considered based on business needs and supervisor approval. In this role you will regularly collaborate with colleagues, Agency leaders, state and federal partners, and other external partners or customers. Occasional travel may be required for meetings, training, or other business needs. All employees are required to report to our Olympia office on their first and final day of employment.

Supplemental Information

The Health Care Authority is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating a workplace where employees are respected, included, and supported in bringing their experiences, perspectives, and ideas to work.

Our commitment to inclusion is reflected in how we work together and serve the people of Washington. HCA also supports five voluntary employee led Employee Resources Groups (ERGs), which create opportunities for connection, community, learning, and professional growth.

Application Directions:

To be considered, you must complete the online application in full and submit all required materials. Incomplete applications or applications missing required materials will not be considered. When completing your application, please include the following required materials:

  • Cover letter: describing your qualifications for this specific position

title: ANALISTA DE LABORATÓRIO PL
description:
A ALD Bioenergia busca profissional para atuar como Analista de Laboratório PL, sendo responsável pela realização e interpretação de análises físico-químicas de matérias-primas, produtos, coprodutos, utilidades e processos produtivos, assegurando a confiabilidade dos resultados e o atendimento aos padrões de qualidade, segurança e boas práticas laboratoriais.

Principais responsabilidades

  • Realizar análises físico-químicas de milho, mosto, fermentação, etanol, DDGS, óleo bruto de milho e demais produtos e intermediários;
  • Executar e interpretar análises de água industrial, caldeira, torre de resfriamento, osmose, ETE e potabilidade;
  • Realizar análises de granulometria, micotoxinas, contraprovas e demais ensaios laboratoriais;
  • Acompanhar os resultados das análises relacionadas ao processo produtivo, identificando tendências e possíveis desvios;
  • Realizar coleta, preparação, identificação e acondicionamento de amostras, garantindo sua rastreabilidade;
  • Preparar e controlar soluções, reagentes, padrões e materiais utilizados nas análises;
  • Executar e acompanhar calibrações e verificações dos equipamentos laboratoriais;
  • Registrar, revisar e lançar resultados analíticos em sistemas ERP e de gestão;
  • Avaliar resultados fora de especificação e comunicar possíveis desvios à liderança e áreas envolvidas;
  • Apoiar investigações de desvios de processo e a melhoria dos métodos e procedimentos laboratoriais;
  • Orientar Analistas de Laboratório Júnior quanto à execução das análises e boas práticas laboratoriais;
  • Contribuir para a melhoria contínua dos processos, redução de erros analíticos e aumento da confiabilidade dos resultados.

Requisitos

  • Curso Técnico em Química ou graduação completa/cursando em Química, Biomedicina, Biologia, Engenharia de Produção ou áreas correlatas;
  • Conhecimento em análises físico-químicas;
  • Conhecimento em Boas Práticas de Laboratório (BPL);
  • Conhecimento em Pacote Office;
  • Conhecimento em sistemas ERP e sistemas de gestão laboratorial.

Diferenciais

  • Experiência com análises laboratoriais em etanol de milho;
  • Conhecimento em análises de águas industriais, destilaria, moagem, secagem e óleo;
  • Conhecimento nos equipamentos HPLC, densímetro, pHmetro, condutivímetro, NIR e espectrofotômetro;
  • Senso crítico na avaliação e interpretação dos resultados;
  • Boa capacidade de trabalho em equipe;
  • Vivência em processos industriais e acompanhamento de produção.
