title: Vice President, Portfolio Chemistry
description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

The Vice President, Portfolio Chemistry will report to the Senior Vice President, Medicinal Chemistry and Screening Sciences, and lead Revolution Medicines' multidisciplinary Portfolio Chemistry organization, with responsibility for Medicinal Chemistry and chemistry leadership across the discovery portfolio. This executive will provide strategic and scientific leadership for the advancement of oncology programs from validated hit series through development candidate nomination.

Working at the intersection of chemistry, biology, structural sciences, computational chemistry, and translational research, the VP will be accountable for portfolio chemistry outcomes and delivery of high-quality development candidates while driving operational excellence, scientific innovation, and organizational performance across the portfolio. In this role, VP of Portfolio Chemistry will integrate modern medicinal chemistry strategies, with AI-enabled drug discovery and predictive analytics tools.

Working closely with the Vice President, Early Discovery Chemistry, this leader will ensure seamless transition of differentiated chemical matter into lead optimization while maintaining clear accountability for candidate delivery.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Partner with Research leadership to define and execute a long-term strategy for expanding the portfolio through advancement of novel small-molecule therapeutics.

  • Develop and execute the chemistry strategy supporting advancement of Revolution Medicines' discovery portfolio from hit validation through development candidate nomination.

  • Partner with the VP, Early Discovery Chemistry to establish clear criteria and ensure effective transitions from hit identification/validation into portfolio medicinal chemistry.

  • Drive integration of chemistry with computational chemistry, digital drug discovery, AI/ML technologies, and data science capabilities across discovery workflows.

  • Lead organizational planning, internal and external resource allocation (CRO management), talent strategy, and capability development across multiple functions.

  • Partner with Research Leadership to prioritize resources and maximize portfolio value.

  • Drive alignment across Research functions to support a dynamic portfolio of discovery and development-stage programs.

  • Vision, strategy, leadership: Partner with Research Leadership to translate portfolio strategy into differentiated chemistry programs and ensure effective advancement of the highest-value opportunities. Establish and maintain exceptional chemistry project leadership across the portfolio, developing capable project leaders.

  • Innovation: Champion predictive analytics, AI/ML methodologies, and computational approaches that increase throughput and accelerate DMTA cycles.

  • Management excellence: Manage a high-performing group, sustain productivity through strategic hiring, mentoring, and support for individual career growth. Be accountable for an annual budget.

  • Cross-functional collaboration: Position the MedChem function as a bridge across Research, enabling bench-to-bedside insights. Serve as a visible leader representing Revolution Medicines’ scientific excellence internally and externally.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

  • Ph.D. in Organic Chemistry.

  • Minimum 16+ years of industrial drug discovery experience with extensive medicinal chemistry leadership.

  • Demonstrated success advancing multiple programs from hit validation through development candidate nomination and ideally IND-enabling studies.

  • Proven leadership of multidisciplinary chemistry organizations supporting multiple concurrent discovery programs.

  • Deep expertise in medicinal chemistry, structure-based drug design, optimization strategies, and candidate selection.

  • Experience integrating computational chemistry, AI/ML technologies, and digital drug discovery into medicinal chemistry workflows.

  • Strong experience managing external collaborations, CROs, and strategic partnerships.

  • Outstanding leadership, communication, and organizational development skills.

  • Demonstrated ability to build, lead, and foster a collaborative culture on interdisciplinary teams.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience in oncology drug discovery.

  • Experience of successful IND filings and clinical candidate delivery.

  • Record of scientific publications, patents, and invited presentations.

  • Experience with alternative modality, ex. molecular glue and ADC drug discovery.

title: GIS Specialist I
description:
Geographic Information System (GIS) Specialist

HELP CONNECT ARIZONA. BUILD THE FUTURE OF BROADBAND.

At Wecom Fiber, we're helping bridge the digital divide across Arizona by building and maintaining the communications infrastructure that powers homes, businesses, schools, and communities. As our next Senior Manager of Field Operations Support, you'll play a key leadership role in scaling operations, improving performance, and helping shape the future of a rapidly growing telecommunications organization.

WHY WECOM?

At Wecom, we believe exceptional people deserve more than a paycheck.

We're building a workplace where employees can grow their careers, make an impact, and help shape the future of telecommunications across Arizona. Our employees are helping connect communities, expand broadband access, and bring meaningful technology infrastructure to underserved areas throughout the state.

GIS SPECIALIST

Reports to: Manager of Engineering

Location: Phoenix, AZ

Position Summary:

The GIS Specialist at Wecom Fiber plays a critical role in supporting geographic information system (GIS) activities, fiber network records management, spatial data analysis, and mapping functions across the full lifecycle of FTTH network infrastructure — from planning and design through construction and ongoing operations. This role is the primary steward of accurate, complete, and current network asset data in Wecom Fiber’s GIS and fiber inventory systems.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Collect, analyze, and manage spatial data using GIS software (ArcGIS, QGIS, IQGeo, Vetro FiberMap, or similar) to support FTTH network planning, asset management, and project mapping.
  • Create and maintain accurate fiber network maps, strand counts, splice diagrams, and spatial databases to support engineering design, construction execution, and executive decision-making.
  • Build, maintain, and continuously improve fiber network records in the company’s GIS system of record (e.g., IQGeo, Vetro, 3-GIS), ensuring data structure, plan hygiene, and nomenclature standards are consistently applied across all markets.
  • Perform QA/QC on GIS and OSP engineering data — including fiber cable, conduit, splice points, equipment locations, and passings — to ensure accuracy, completeness, and conformance to company data standards and NEC requirements.
  • Collaborate closely with OSP engineers, construction project managers, field technicians, and network operations teams to integrate GIS data throughout the network build lifecycle, from high-level design (HLD) through final as-built records.
  • Review and incorporate construction as-builts and civil engineering prints into GIS inventory systems, accurately recording fiber routes, conduit paths, splice closures, equipment locations, and all OSP assets to reflect field-installed conditions.
  • Prepare and maintain GIS maps, facility redlines, and positive response data to support 811 utility locate requests and ensure Wecom Fiber’s underground infrastructure is properly represented in one-call notification systems.
  • Upload and maintain current facility data in the 811-notification system, keeping Wecom Fiber’s infrastructure coverage accurate and compliant with state one-call requirements.
  • Support serviceability analysis by maintaining accurate address-level passings data, enabling the commercial team to verify serviceable locations and market footprint.
  • Interpret and process aerial and underground fiber design plans, OSP design maps, and CAD drawings in coordination with engineering and permitting teams.
  • Assist in developing GIS automation workflows and process improvements to scale data quality as the fiber network expands into new markets.

Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; an Associate or Bachelor’s degree in Geography, GIS, Geomatics, Telecommunications, or a related field is strongly preferred.
  • 1–3 years of experience in GIS analysis, spatial data management, or fiber/telecom network records, with preference for candidates who have worked in a telecommunications or utility environment.
  • Proficiency in GIS platforms such as ArcGIS (Desktop/Pro/Online), QGIS, and/or fiber-specific inventory tools such as IQGeo (Network Manager), Vetro FiberMap, 3-GIS, or OSPInsight.

title: Structural Engineering Intern | Summer 2027
description:

About EPX at DLR Group

As an intern at DLR Group, you’ll be part of our Emerging Professional Experience (EPX) Program, designed to give you a meaningful introduction to life within an integrated design firm and a strong foundation for your career in the AEC industry.

Each person at DLR Group has a design voice, and EPX gives you opportunities to develop and share yours. Through hands-on project work, mentorship, and learning experiences, you’ll gain exposure to the people, disciplines, and ideas that shape the built environment. You may participate in design discussions, project meetings, site visits, business development efforts, office activities, and other experiences that broaden your understanding of the design profession.

The program combines three core components: mentorship, project work, and weekly learning sessions. Topics may include design culture, sustainability, design technology, communication, marketing and business development, project and resource management, research, equity, career development, and more. Along the way, you’ll hear from leaders and integrated designers across DLR Group and build connections with fellow emerging professionals.

Position Summary

As a Structural Engineering Intern at DLR Group, you will be an important part of our integrated design team, contributing to the design of structural systems for buildings of various types, sizes, and complexities. Working alongside structural engineers and professionals across architecture, engineering, interiors, and other disciplines, you will gain hands-on experience with the design process from early concepts and system development through documentation and construction administration.

Our Summer Internship Program is a paid, full-time opportunity running May 18 through August 6, 2027, and interns are expected to participate for the duration of the program. This is an opportunity to apply what you’ve learned in the classroom, build your technical and professional skills, and contribute your perspective to design solutions that support our brand promise of Elevating the Human Experience through design.

What you will do

  • Work with a licensed engineer designing structural systems for new construction and/or building renovation projects
  • Attend design team meetings with a structural engineer and observe the coordination that occurs among the team members of a multi-disciplinary design team
  • Assist a structural engineer with the design and development of construction documents primarily using Revit
  • Visit an active construction site (contingent on the status of local construction projects)
  • Coordinate structural design requirements with architecture and other disciplines

Required Qualifications:

  • Completed at least one year at an ABET-accredited Structural Engineering, Civil Engineering, or Architectural Engineering program
  • Experience or interest in BIM (e.g. Autodesk Revit MEP) workflow

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam
  • Interest in architectural building design
  • A third-year student in an accredited engineering program

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future.

#LI-

DLR Group is an integrated design firm delivering architecture, engineering, interiors, planning, and building optimization for new builds, renovations, and adaptive reuse projects.

We are 100% employee-owned: every employee is literally invested in our clients’ success. At the core of our firm are interdisciplinary teams engaged in every step of project lifecycles. Our teams champion true collaboration, open information sharing, shared risk and reward, value-based decision making, and proficient use of technology to deliver exceptional design. We are pursuing the goals of the 2030 Challenge, the ME2040, and the SE2050, and are an initial signatory of the China Accord and the AIA 2030 Commitment.

Through our values – commitment, creativity, environmental stewardship, fun, integrity, ownership, sharing, teamwork – we elevate the human experience through design, together.

DLR Group follows a four-day in-office work model, with employees having the flexibility to work somewhere other than the office on Fridays.

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action/M/F/Veteran/Disabled employer.

title: Demand Planner / SIOP
description:
L3Harris is dedicated to recruiting and developing high-performing talent who are passionate about what they do. Our employees are unified in a shared dedication to our customers’ mission and quest for professional growth. L3Harris provides an inclusive, engaging environment designed to empower employees and promote work-life success. Fundamental to our culture is an unwavering focus on values, dedication to our communities, and commitment to excellence in everything we do.

L3Harris is the Trusted Disruptor in defense tech. With customers’ mission-critical needs always in mind, our employees deliver end-to-end technology solutions connecting the space, air, land, sea and cyber domains in the interest of national security.

**Job Title: Sr Spec., Production Planning (Demand Planner / SIOP)**

**Job Code: 45171**

**Job Location:** **Anaheim, CA (On-Site)**

**Schedule: 9/80 Regular** (Employees work 9 out of every 14 days – totaling 80 hours worked – and have every other Friday off)

**Job Description:**

As a Demand Planner for L3Harris, you will play a critical role in supporting the Sales, Inventory, and Operations Planning (SIOP) process across one or more manufacturing sites. Your primary responsibility will be to serve as the main point of contact for gathering and tracking demand data from various sources to be used in decision-making for future planning processes. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to consolidate demand information, including firm Sales Orders and speculative demand such as New Business, Follow On, Customer Options, Repair and Return MRO, and Engineering IRAD, while developing forecasts for commercial contracts and customers. Your role will be instrumental in creating a comprehensive demand plan that spans the next 18-24 rolling months, ensuring alignment between demand and supply plans across the organization. This role will be critical in the execution of the monthly demand reviews, as the data collected, presented, and agreed to will feed the overall SIOP cadence and cycle.

**Essential Functions:**

- Act as the primary liaison between multiple sites and cross-functional teams to gather, consolidate, and analyze demand data.
- Collect and interpret demand inputs including Sales Orders, customer forecasts, market trends, and historical sales data.
- Develop and maintain an accurate 18–24‑month demand plan incorporating internal and external factors.
- Monitor demand changes and proactively identify risks, opportunities, and required adjustments.
- Prepare for and lead SIOP meetings, ensuring demand plans align with business priorities, market conditions, and operational capabilities.
- Communicate demand forecasts and insights to stakeholders, providing recommendations for inventory and production planning.
- Collaborate with Business Development, PMO, and Engineering to understand customer requirements, market dynamics, and upcoming opportunities.
- Create and maintain reports and metrics that track demand planning, forecasting, and SIOP objectives.
- Drive continuous improvement to enhance accuracy, efficiency, and effectiveness of demand planning processes across multiple sites.
- Lead and influence stakeholders without direct authority to drive alignment.
- Adapt to changing business needs and adopt new tools/technologies to improve demand planning.
- Manage multiple priorities effectively in a fast-paced environment.
- Flexibility to travel occasionally to various sites, 10% approx..

**Qualifications:**

- Bachelor’s degree and 6+ years of related experience; Master’s degree and 4+ years; or 10+ years of relevant experience in lieu of a degree.
- Minimum 4 years of experience in planning, operations, manufacturing, or supply chain.
- At least 2 years of demand planning experience, preferably within aerospace & defense and supporting multiple sites.
- 4+ years working with SIOP processes and principles.
- Minimum 4 years of experience with ERP systems (specifically Deltek Costpoint) in demand and inventory management.

title: Sr. Director, Total Rewards
description:
About Array Marketing

For over 40 years, Array Marketing has been a global leader in retail displays and in-store merchandising solutions. With more than 1,800 employees worldwide, we partner with leading brands including Sephora, L’Oréal, Coty, PUIG, Amazon, and many others to design, engineer, manufacture, and deliver bespoke retail environments that bring their brands to life.



No two projects are the same. Combining award-winning design, engineering expertise, skilled craftsmanship, and state-of-the-art manufacturing technologies, we create highly customized solutions that help the world’s leading brands stand out where it matters most - in store.


Our success is built on the way we work as One Team fostering open communication, collaboration, and a shared commitment to excellence. We strive to be Better Every Day by continuously learning, improving, and taking initiative. We also Have Fun, creating a positive, engaging workplace where people enjoy what they do and celebrate wins together.



We’re looking for curious, open-minded problem-solvers who enjoy tackling complex challenges, thinking critically, and collaborating across disciplines. If you’re ready to make an impact while helping shape the future of retail, we’d love to hear from you.


Who we need


The Sr. Director, Total Rewards is responsible for designing, governing, and continuously improving the organization’s global compensation philosophy, benefits, job architecture, HRIS, payroll, mobility activities, and people-related integration work arising from mergers and acquisitions. Based in Canada, this role provides leadership to a small team and practical execution across regions, ensuring total rewards, HR systems, payroll, and mobility programs are market-competitive, internally equitable, legally compliant, financially sustainable, operationally effective, and aligned with the company’s culture, employee value proposition, and growth agenda.

As our new Sr. Director, Total Rewards, you will handle:


Global Total Rewards Strategy

  • Monitor and lead a global total rewards strategy that supports business growth, talent attraction, retention, performance, and internal equity.
  • Establish global rewards principles while enabling regional flexibility to reflect local market, legislative, and cultural requirements.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to the CHRO, executive leaders, Finance, Legal, and regional HR teams on compensation, benefits, incentives, and rewards governance.
  • Monitor external market trends, regulatory changes, pay transparency requirements, and evolving employee expectations, ensuring the team’s work under this role’s leadership keeps programs competitive and compliant.
  • Provide total rewards leadership and due diligence support for mergers, acquisitions, integrations, new business development and divestitures, including assessment of compensation, benefits, payroll, HRIS, mobility, and related people-cost implications.


Compensation, Job Architecture, and Pay Equity

  • Lead the design, implementation, and ongoing governance of global job architecture, job evaluation, levelling, salary structures, and pay ranges.
  • Oversee annual compensation planning processes, including merit, bonus, incentive, and executive compensation support, ensuring alignment with performance, affordability, and market competitiveness.
  • Build and maintain a consistent market pricing and benchmarking methodology using reputable survey data and internal analytics.
  • Partner with HR and business leaders to ensure new and evolving roles are evaluated objectively and assigned appropriate levels, grades, and compensation ranges.
  • Develop and apply clear compensation guidelines to support consistent, equitable, and defensible salary decisions based on job level, market data, internal equity, performance, budget affordability, and approved governance processes.
  • Lead pay equity, internal equity, and pay transparency analysis and reporting, including compliance with Canadian requirements and emerging global pay transparency obligations.


Benefits, Wellbeing & Perquisites

  • Provide strategic oversight of benefits and wellbeing programs, ensuring offerings are competitive, compliant, cost-effective, and aligned with workforce needs.
  • Lead benefits reviews, vendor evaluations, renewal processes, employee feedback analysis, and recommendations for plan design changes.
  • Design, govern, and periodically review global perquisites, allowances, and executive or role-based programs to ensure they are market-relevant, equitable, compliant, cost-managed, and aligned with total rewards principles.
  • Establish clear eligibility, approval, documentation, tax, payroll, and communication processes for global perquisites, partnering with Finance, Legal, Payroll, regional HR, and external advisors as needed.
  • Oversee pension, retirement, and legacy benefits programs, ensuring appropriate governance, compliance, vendor management, employee communication, risk monitoring, and alignment with current total rewards strategy.
  • Collaborate with Payroll, Finance, Legal, brokers, consultants, HRIS partners, mobility advisors, and HR leaders to manage rewards-related risk, cost, communication, compliance, and employee experience.


Governance, Analytics, and HRIS

  • Develop global policies, frameworks, tools, and approval processes for compensation, benefits, allowances, incentives, job changes, HRIS, and related total rewards activities.
  • Provide oversight of HRIS strategy, governance, data integrity, reporting, workflows, and system optimization to support scalable global HR operations and decision-making.
  • Assess and identify economies of scale across global programs, external vendors, platforms, and service providers, recommending opportunities to consolidate, standardize, or optimize solutions where appropriate.
  • Evaluate global system opportunities that improve scalability, data integrity, reporting, automation, employee experience, and operational efficiency across total rewards, HRIS, payroll, time and attendance, benefits, and mobility processes.
  • Use data, analytics, and dashboards to assess compensation competitiveness, benefits utilization, pay equity, turnover risk, program effectiveness, HR data quality, and overall rewards performance.
  • Define, track, and report on global total rewards, HRIS, payroll, and mobility KPIs through dashboards, scorecards, and regular reporting cycles that provide visibility to trends, risks, service levels, compliance status, and program outcomes.
  • Prepare and deliver regular global reporting for the CHRO, executive leaders, Finance, Legal, and regional HR teams to support data-driven decisions, governance reviews, and continuous improvement priorities.
  • Establish governance and periodic review processes for temporary staff, contractor, and agency worker payments to confirm appropriate approvals, rate accuracy, invoice alignment, classification, tax treatment, and compliance with applicable employment, payroll, procurement, and legislative requirements.
  • Prepare executive-ready materials, business cases, and recommendations for leadership decision-making.


Payroll Oversight

  • Provide oversight of payroll governance and controls, while the Payroll team executes day-to-day payroll activities with Finance, HR, and external providers to ensure accurate, timely, compliant payroll across applicable jurisdictions.
  • Oversee payroll audit and reconciliation requirements, while the Payroll team performs regular audits and reconciliations, including statutory remittances, deductions, taxable benefits, pension or retirement contributions, and employer-paid taxes.
  • Provide oversight and guidance for year-end payroll activities, while the Payroll team executes annual reporting, tax slips or equivalent filings, payroll balancing, audit support, and issue resolution.
  • Maintain sufficient payroll administration knowledge to step in on a temporary basis during Payroll team absences, supporting critical payroll processing, issue resolution, and continuity as needed.
  • Provide oversight of time and attendance governance, systems, controls, and reporting, while the Payroll team and applicable functional owners execute day-to-day processes to support accurate pay, compliance, scheduling inputs, leave tracking, and workforce data integrity.
  • Oversee controls for temporary staff and agency worker payments, including periodic checks of approved rates, hours, invoices, payroll or vendor payments, worker classification, and compliance with local employment, tax, and regulatory requirements.
  • Set expectations for payroll best practices, while the Payroll team executes clear calendars, documented controls, compliance reviews, vendor monitoring, data privacy requirements, and continuous improvement activities.


Mobility

  • Develop and implement a global mobility program with clear principles, eligibility criteria, relocation and assignment support, approval pathways, cost ownership, compliance requirements, and employee experience standards.
  • Provide oversight of mobility activities, including cross-border work arrangements, relocation, assignments, allowances, immigration coordination, tax considerations, and local employment requirements.
  • Establish mobility frameworks, documentation, and governance to support consistent, compliant, and employee-focused decision-making.
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, Payroll, Tax, HRIS partners, mobility advisors, external vendors, and regional HR teams to manage mobility-related needed activities, risk, cost, communication, and evolving workforce needs.


Leadership and Partnership

  • Lead, coach, and develop total rewards team members and/or support of matrixed regional contributors, building capability, consistency, and accountability.
  • Partner closely with regional HR teams to balance global standards with local execution requirements.
  • Influence senior leaders through clear, data-driven recommendations and practical solutions.
  • Communicate total rewards programs in a way that builds leader capability, employee understanding, and trust in rewards decisions.


Key Competencies:


  • Strategic and commercial mindset: Connects rewards strategy to business priorities, financial discipline, and talent outcomes.
  • Analytical decision-making: Uses data, market intelligence, and internal equity insights to develop clear recommendations.
  • Global perspective: Applies consistent principles while adapting programs to local market and legal requirements.
  • Influence and communication: Builds trust with executives, leaders, HR partners, and employees through clear, practical communication.
  • Governance and risk management: Establishes disciplined processes that support fairness, compliance, and defensible decision-making.
  • Operational excellence: Strengthens HRIS, payroll, mobility, and rewards processes through disciplined governance, clear controls, continuous improvement, and stakeholder partnership.
  • Change leadership: Leads rewards transformation, program implementation, and leader education with clarity and credibility.
  • M&A leadership: Applies structured due diligence, integration planning, and change leadership to support effective people-related outcomes during mergers, acquisitions, and organizational transactions.


You have:


  • 8+ years of Total Rewards Senior Leadership experience with significant depth of knowledge in total rewards, job architecture, pay equity, HR systems, and payroll.
  • Experience leading total rewards programs across multiple countries or regions, preferably within a global or multi-site organization.
  • Strong knowledge of Canadian compensation, benefits, employment standards, pay equity, and related legislative requirements; competency in U.S., Mexico, Europe, and APAC rewards practices is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience designing salary structures, incentive plans, job evaluation frameworks, market benchmarking processes, and compensation governance.
  • Experience overseeing HRIS, payroll governance, time and attendance, and global mobility programs and working closely with functional owners to ensure integrated, compliant, and effective HR operations.
  • Experience establishing governance, controls, and compliance review processes for temporary staff, contractor, agency worker, and related contingent workforce payments.
  • Experience developing KPIs, dashboards, scorecards, and global reporting routines that translate HR and rewards data into actionable insights for senior leadership.
  • Experience assessing economies of scale across global programs, vendors, platforms, and HR systems, with the ability to recommend consolidation, standardization, automation, or optimization opportunities.
  • Experience overseeing pension, retirement, and legacy benefits programs, including governance, compliance, vendor relationships, communications, and risk management.
  • Experience partnering with Finance, Legal, Payroll, HRIS, and Mobility, brokers, consultants, external vendors, and senior business leaders.
  • Experience leading or supporting mergers and acquisitions from a total rewards and HR operations perspective, including due diligence, integration planning, harmonization of programs, employee transition considerations, and post-close governance.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Finance, or a related field; CCP, CEBS, GRP, CHRP/CHRL, or equivalent certification is preferred.

Working Conditions:


  • Based in Canada (with some global oversight across multiple regions and time zones).
  • At least 3 days in office - Scarborough.
  • Minimal domestic and international travel may be required to support regional TR teams, leadership meetings, vendor reviews, or major program implementation – up to 10%.


Compensation:


The salary range for this role is $160,000 - $185,000. Compensation is thoughtfully determined based on your experience, skill set, and alignment with our internal compensation framework. We're always happy to answer questions about compensation through the hiring process.


Apply now.


Diversity, equity and inclusion are a critical component of life at Array Marketing and we are committed to making these values an integral part of our culture. We encourage applications from all qualified applicants, including women, persons with disabilities, Black, Indigenous, and People of Colour (BIPOC), people from the Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Transsexual, Queer, Questioning, Two-Spirit, Intersex, Asexual + (LGBTQ2SIA+) community, and other equity-seeking groups.

Array Marketing is committed to providing accessible employment practices that are in compliance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act ('AODA'). If you require accommodation, please notify our HR team at hrto@arraymarketing.com.

title: Volunteer Coordinator
description:
About the role

  • The Volunteer Coordinator is responsible for the day-to-day coordination of the Museum’s volunteer program—from recruiting and onboarding new volunteers to scheduling, training, communication, engagement, recognition, and recordkeeping.

This role is ideal for an organized, people-focused professional who enjoys building relationships, coordinating multiple moving pieces, and creating a welcoming experience for volunteers. The successful candidate will partner with Museum department leaders to understand their volunteer needs and ensure volunteers are prepared, supported, and connected to the Museum’s mission.

What you'll do

  • · Develop and implement volunteer recruitment strategies to attract qualified and engaged volunteers.

· Recruit, interview, onboard, orient, and train volunteers.

· Coordinate volunteer schedules, assignments, coverage, and communications.

· Partner with department leaders to identify and fulfill volunteer staffing needs.

· Maintain accurate volunteer records, applications, agreements, training documentation, schedules, and other required records.

· Coordinate volunteer appreciation and recognition initiatives.

· Ensure volunteers understand and follow Museum policies, safety procedures, and expectations.

· Respond to volunteer questions and concerns and provide timely follow-up.

· Prepare reports regarding volunteer participation, coverage, retention, and program effectiveness.

· Help strengthen volunteer engagement and retention through consistent communication, support, and recognition.

· Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • · Associate’s degree required; bachelor’s degree preferred in Human Resources, Nonprofit Management, Business Administration, Communications, or a related field.

· At least two (2) years of experience coordinating volunteers, employee engagement, customer service, nonprofit administration, or a related area.

· Previous museum or nonprofit experience preferred.

· Demonstrated success recruiting and retaining volunteers.

· Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple assignments, schedules, and deadlines.

· Strong written and verbal communication skills.

· Ability to build positive relationships with volunteers, employees, department leaders, and Museum visitors.

· Ability to work effectively with individuals from diverse backgrounds.

· Ability to maintain accurate records and handle confidential information appropriately.

· Proficiency with Microsoft Office and other technology used for communication, recordkeeping, reporting, and program administration.

· Sound judgment, professionalism, dependability, and appropriate escalation of concerns.

What Will Make You Successful

· You genuinely enjoy working with people and creating a welcoming environment.

· You are highly organized and can manage people, schedules, documentation, and deadlines.

· You communicate clearly and follow through on commitments.

· You know how to recruit people, build relationships, and keep volunteers engaged.

· You are comfortable partnering with leaders across different Museum departments.

· You understand that volunteers are an important part of delivering an exceptional visitor and program experience.

What Success Looks Like

· Recruit and onboard qualified volunteers who meet the Museum’s program needs.

· Maintain strong volunteer coverage for scheduled events and assignments.

· Provide timely orientation, training, communication, recognition, and support.

· Maintain accurate, complete, and current volunteer records and required documentation.

· Build strong working relationships with department leaders and provide dependable coordination of volunteer assignments.

· Create a volunteer experience in which people feel welcomed, prepared, valued, and connected to the Museum’s mission.

· Support strong volunteer participation and retention that contributes to the Museum’s visitor experience, programs, and special events.

Why This Role Matters

Volunteers play an important role in helping Motown Museum deliver meaningful experiences to visitors, students, community members, and guests. The Volunteer Coordinator helps make that experience possible by ensuring the right volunteers are recruited, prepared, scheduled, supported, and recognized.

Join the Motown Museum Team

If you are an organized, relationship-focused professional who enjoys connecting people with meaningful opportunities to contribute, we invite you to apply for the Volunteer Coordinator position.

Motown Museum is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and welcoming workplace.

title: Structural Engineering Intern | Summer 2027
description:
DLR Group is an integrated design firm with a promise to elevate the human experience through design. This fuels the work we do around the world and inspires our mission to improve the lives of our clients, our communities, and our planet. If this sparks your interest, you’re in the right place.

DLR Group’s Minneapolis studio has an opening for a Structural Engineering Summer Intern.

  • Minneapolis, MN

We have multiple positions and locations available; please refer to all openings posted and apply to the locations that are most suitable for your living situation during the course of your internship. This is not a remote position.

About EPX at DLR Group

As an intern at DLR Group, you’ll be part of our Emerging Professional Experience (EPX) Program, designed to give you a meaningful introduction to life within an integrated design firm and a strong foundation for your career in the AEC industry.

Each person at DLR Group has a design voice, and EPX gives you opportunities to develop and share yours. Through hands-on project work, mentorship, and learning experiences, you’ll gain exposure to the people, disciplines, and ideas that shape the built environment. You may participate in design discussions, project meetings, site visits, business development efforts, office activities, and other experiences that broaden your understanding of the design profession.

The program combines three core components: mentorship, project work, and weekly learning sessions. Topics may include design culture, sustainability, design technology, communication, marketing and business development, project and resource management, research, equity, career development, and more. Along the way, you’ll hear from leaders and integrated designers across DLR Group and build connections with fellow emerging professionals.

Position Summary

As a Structural Engineering Intern at DLR Group, you will be an important part of our integrated design team, contributing to the design of structural systems for buildings of various types, sizes, and complexities. Working alongside structural engineers and professionals across architecture, engineering, interiors, and other disciplines, you will gain hands-on experience with the design process from early concepts and system development through documentation and construction administration.

Our Summer Internship Program is a paid, full-time opportunity running May 18 through August 6, 2027, and interns are expected to participate for the duration of the program. This is an opportunity to apply what you’ve learned in the classroom, build your technical and professional skills, and contribute your perspective to design solutions that support our brand promise of Elevating the Human Experience through design.

What you will do

  • Work with a licensed engineer designing structural systems for new construction and/or building renovation projects
  • Attend design team meetings with a structural engineer and observe the coordination that occurs among the team members of a multi-disciplinary design team
  • Assist a structural engineer with the design and development of construction documents primarily using Revit
  • Visit an active construction site (contingent on the status of local construction projects)
  • Coordinate structural design requirements with architecture and other disciplines

Required Qualifications:

  • Completed at least one year at an ABET-accredited Structural Engineering, Civil Engineering, or Architectural Engineering program
  • Experience or interest in BIM (e.g. Autodesk Revit MEP) workflow

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam
  • Interest in architectural building design
  • A third-year student in an accredited engineering program

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future.

Our comprehensive Benefits at DLR Group include medical, dental, vision, disability, wellness programs, flex spending, paid holidays, and paid time off. We also offer a 401(k) plan, employee stock ownership, and bonus opportunities. Compensation considerations are based on location, experience, and skills. The suggested hourly rate for this position is:

Hourly Rate
$20—$26 USD

DLR Group is an integrated design firm delivering architecture, engineering, interiors, planning, and building optimization for new builds, renovations, and adaptive reuse projects.

We are 100% employee-owned: every employee is literally invested in our clients’ success. At the core of our firm are interdisciplinary teams engaged in every step of project lifecycles. Our teams champion true collaboration, open information sharing, shared risk and reward, value-based decision making, and proficient use of technology to deliver exceptional design. We are pursuing the goals of the 2030 Challenge, the ME2040, and the SE2050, and are an initial signatory of the China Accord and the AIA 2030 Commitment.

Through our values – commitment, creativity, environmental stewardship, fun, integrity, ownership, sharing, teamwork – we elevate the human experience through design, together.

DLR Group follows a four-day in-office work model, with employees having the flexibility to work somewhere other than the office on Fridays.

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action/M/F/Veteran/Disabled employer.

title: Junior Information System Security Officer, National Vetting Center
description:
Tharros supports the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) with cybersecurity services across its Intelligence Enterprise. In support of this mission, we have an immediate opportunity for a Junior Information System Security Officer, National Vetting Center.

In this role you will work with the senior NVC ISSO to maintain authorization artifacts, track POA&Ms, review audit logs, and support assessment and cloud security engineering activities for NVC systems. This position is on-site in a Government SCIF in Washington, DC.

Duties include but not limited to:

  • Maintain security artifacts (SSP, POA&Ms, risk exceptions, contingency plans, PTAs) for NVC systems in the GRC tool.
  • Track POA&Ms on 30/60/90/120/180-day review intervals and provide weekly or bi-weekly activity reports.
  • Perform audit log reviews at least weekly and respond to NOSC alerts.
  • Ensure periodic vulnerability scans are performed and review scan results.
  • Support security control assessments and cloud security engineering for NVC systems.
  • Submit IATT requests and notify the ISSM, SCA, and AO of changes affecting authorization.
  • Serve as SCIF Information Security Compliance Representative for assigned spaces.
  • BS degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Information Systems, or Computer Science OR minimum of 4 years' experience in IT or cybersecurity.
  • Minimum of 1 year of experience in ISSO, RMF, or security compliance support.
  • Active TS/SCI clearance and U.S. citizenship; willingness to undergo a DHS counterintelligence-scope polygraph.
  • Knowledge of the Risk Management Framework (RMF), NIST SP 800-37, and NIST SP 800-53.
  • Knowledge of hybrid classified/unclassified, on-premise and cloud environments.
  • Knowledge of DevSecOps and agile methodologies.
  • Skill in securing Linux and Windows operating systems.
  • Skill in POA&M tracking and audit log review.

title: Director, Partner Success
description:
Who we are

The real world is the next frontier, and at Metropolis, we are creating the artificial intelligence to make it responsive. We are pioneering the Recognition Economy — a future where mundane repetition disappears and being known unlocks access, comfort, and belonging everywhere you go. From transforming parking into a seamless drive-in, drive-out experience for millions of Members to expanding our intelligence layer across retail and hospitality, we are building a world that feels instinctive and magical. The future isn’t coming; it’s here, and we need builders, innovators, and problem solvers to help us create it.

Who you are

Metropolis is seeking a Director, Partner Success to own a portfolio of strategic partners and serve as their trusted advocate and operational champion across product, data, operations, and finance. Reporting directly to the VP of Partner Success, you will focus on driving measurable value and retention for our most important portfolio partners rather than traditional sales-focused roles. By translating partner objectives into actionable cross-functional initiatives, delivering high-quality reporting, and building durable executive-level trust, you will ensure consistent performance and unlock organic growth opportunities across your portfolio.

What you'll do

  • Own end-to-end partner success and retention for a portfolio of strategic partners
  • Serve as the primary day-to-day relationship owner and the partner’s internal advocate at Metropolis, channeling partner reporting, product, and data needs to appropriate internal teams, driving follow-up to completion, and closing the loop
  • Develop a deep understanding of each partner’s business objectives, operational goals, and financial budget while ensuring Metropolis consistently delivers against them
  • Own the financial performance of your portfolio, delivering on partner budget commitments while ensuring internal financial targets are met
  • Partner closely with the Data team to produce high-quality weekly updates, Monthly Business Reviews (MBRs), and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) that clearly demonstrate driven value
  • Champion new Metropolis initiatives, products, and service offerings with partners to build the value case, secure buy-in, and drive adoption
  • Unlock growth across the portfolio by adding new accounts within existing partner portfolios and expanding service offerings within accounts already under contract
  • Build durable, executive-level trust through consistent delivery, financial discipline, fast responsiveness, and visible ownership of commitments
  • Lead the resolution of partner escalations by coordinating cross-functional responses and driving root-cause follow-through
  • Serve as the voice of the partner internally to represent their needs in product, operations, and data discussions and help shape priorities accordingly

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years of relevant experience in a client success, account management, or strategic customer-facing role with a track record of retaining and growing complex accounts
  • Demonstrate strong financial acumen, including comfort owning P&L performance, interpreting financial reports, managing budgets, and discussing performance with partner executives
  • Communicate clearly, concisely, and professionally in writing and in person with cross-functional internal teams and external audiences from site operators to the C-suite
  • Maintain high responsiveness to set the standard for timeliness and follow-through on all partner and colleague commitments
  • Take complete ownership of projects, action items, and commitments to drive them to completion independently
  • Build trusted relationships at multiple levels of a partner organization from local operations through to executive leadership
  • Navigate and influence internal product, data, operations, and finance teams to deliver results on behalf of the partner
  • Utilize strong data storytelling skills to translate operational and financial metrics into clear, persuasive value narratives for weekly updates, MBRs, and QBRs
  • Remain composed under pressure to defuse partner escalations and make sound decisions with imperfect information
  • Travel approximately 5–10% for a mix of partner meetings, team meetings, and corporate events

While not required, these are a plus:

  • Possess a background in the parking industry, or experience in real estate, mobility, hospitality, or other operationally complex B2B service environments

4 Days in Office: Metropolis values in-person collaboration to drive innovation, strengthen culture, and enhance the Member experience. Our corporate team members hold to our office-first model, which requires employees to be on-site at least four days a week, fostering organic interactions that spark creativity and connection

When you join Metropolis, you'll join a team of world-class product leaders and engineers, building an ecosystem of technologies at the intersection of parking, mobility, and real estate. Our goal is to build an inclusive culture where everyone has a voice and the best idea wins. You will play a key role in building and maintaining this culture as our organization grows. The anticipated base salary for this position is $150,000.00 USD to $175,000.00 USD annually. The actual base salary offered is determined by a number of variables, including, as appropriate, the applicant's qualifications for the position, years of relevant experience, distinctive skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location of residence and/or place of employment. Base salary is one component of Metropolis' total compensation package, which may also include access to or eligibility for healthcare benefits, a 401(k) plan, short-term and long-term disability coverage, basic life insurance, a lucrative stock option plan, bonus plans, and more. #LI-WT1 #LI-Onsite

Metropolis may utilize an automated employment decision tool (AEDT) to assess or evaluate your candidacy for employment or promotion. AEDTs are used to assist in assessing a candidate’s application relative to the required job qualifications and responsibilities listed in the job posting.

As part of this process, Metropolis retains data relevant to your candidacy, including personal information, for a period that is reasonably necessary for the use of the tool. If you are hired for the position, your data may become part of your employee records.

Metropolis Technologies is an equal opportunity employer. We make all hiring decisions based on merit, qualifications, and business needs — without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including gender identity, sexual orientation, and pregnancy), national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under federal, state, or local law.

title: RESIDENTIAL STRATEGIC ANALYST
description:

These skills will be used to:

  • Complete competitive market analyses for assigned divisions by high school district, including analyses for hypothetical communities as requested and active communities twice annually.

  • Determine trends across divisions and identify gaps and opportunities for success.

title: Special Events & Maintenance Specialist
description:
Position Overview

The Special Events & Maintenance Specialist is responsible for special events operations and building facility maintenance support for The Tech Interactive. The primary emphasis is on delivering facility services professionally, competently, on time, and courteously while ensuring the safety and security of guests, fellow staff, contractors, and volunteers. This non-exempt (hourly) role reports to the Special Events department.


Responsibilities

Special Events:

  • Prep and stage inventory items according to event profile specifications and floor plans.
  • Collaborate with the Special Events team to meet client needs and requests in real time.
  • Set up and strike equipment such as staging, pipe and drape before the museum opening the following day.
  • Return equipment to appropriate storage areas.
  • Attend weekly Special Events Meeting as applicable.
  • Report maintenance issues through proper documented channels
  • Complete additional related tasks or duties as assigned by Operational & Special Event Management.


Facilities:

  • Perform preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, repairs and maintain building systems including electrical, plumbing, HVAC, painting, carpentry, mechanical infrastructure, and usage of the related Building Management Systems (BMS).
  • Integrate mechanical, electrical, AV, and interactive components into fabricated assemblies and exhibit systems when required.
  • Support the installation, maintenance, repair, and improvement of interactive exhibits and equipment, and exhibit infrastructure.
  • Perform loading dock and warehouse functions and responsibilities, including forklift operation, loading and unloading of equipment, supplies, deliveries, and event items
  • Maintain safe, organized shop and work environments, and ensure proper use and maintenance of tools, materials, and equipment.
  • Collaborate with facilities staff, exhibit developers, designers, and operations teams to implement creative technical solutions for facility and exhibit infrastructure and visitor experiences.
  • Track facilities supply inventories.
  • Complete additional related tasks or duties as assigned by Operational & Special Event Management.
  • Maintain compliance with all applicable codes relevant to duties, including, but not limited to, Title 24, Cal/OSHA, NFPA 72, NFPA 70, EPA, ADA, and all local regulating agencies.


Requirements and Skills

  • High school diploma or equivalent education and experience required.
  • 1 year of experience in facilities maintenance, including plumbing, electrical, painting, HVAC, and minor construction.
  • Good oral and written communication skills.
  • General knowledge of tools, hardware, and building materials pertaining to maintenance and upkeep.
  • Training in the operation of scissor lift and forklift operation desired.
  • Valid California driver’s license with a favorable driving record.


Working Conditions and Schedule

  • This role works primarily on-site Tuesday-Saturday and will include evenings but you will be given at a minimum 2 weeks' advance notice.
  • Must be available for a flexible schedule, including evenings, as required by projects and maintenance schedules.
  • Role will be split between the Special Events and Facilities Department depending on operational needs and will fluctuate seasonally.
  • Ability to safely carry out daily duties, including lifting to 75 lbs, bending, climbing, reaching, pushing, and pulling of furniture and equipment.
  • High noise levels that require hearing protection.
  • Working around lubricants, solvents, batteries, cleaning fluids, and paints.
  • Basic facility maintenance troubleshooting.

Je werkt samen met collega's uit het EIFFEL Solutions Lab aan innovatieve oplossingen op het snijvlak van business, technologie en AI. Samen ontwikkelen, valideren en schalen we proposities die klanten helpen slimmer, sneller en toekomstbestendiger te werken.

title: Research Associate in Electromagnetic Non-Destructive Evaluation and Inspection
description:
We are seeking a motivated and collaborative individual to join our team as a Research Associate in Electromagnetic Non-Destructive Evaluation and Inspection. This role offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to the EPSRC-funded Frontiers in Electromagnetic Non-Destructive Evaluation Research (FENDER) programme, which seeks to bring game-changing ideas and exploit advances in complimentary areas of science to trigger a UK-led renaissance in electromagnetic NDE, boosting the UK’s reputation, energising a world-leading research community and achieving downstream commercial impact via a broad network of industrial partners. The Programme is led by the University of Manchester and involves four other Universities (Bristol, Warwick, Newcastle and Strathclyde). The initiative is supported by approximately 25 industrial partners which are some of the major NDE users, within a dynamic and inclusive environment.

**You will have responsibility to:**

- Model and optimise electromagnetic sensors and coil configurations. Design, prototype and validate EM sensors and arrays for defects and materials.
- Develop sensor-interface electronics and multi-channel data acquisition, improving the real time hardware and firmware, and implementing algorithms with other team members.
- Develop real-time acquisition, processing and control software.
- Assist in the development of the data acquisition system for sensor arrays
- Support commercialisation partners in the further development of systems into a commercial product

We welcome candidates who bring diverse perspectives, experiences, and approaches to their work.

**About You**

We encourage applications from individuals with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. You should demonstrate:

**Essential Criteria:**

- Possess, or be about to obtain, a PhD in a relevant STEM discipline or have equivalent industrial research experience.
- Proven track record of successfully applying electromagnetic theory to engineering applications.
- Demonstrate a record of publications with leading academic journals and be able to write scientific reports and research papers
- Be able to efficiently present research findings at national and international meetings and conferences
- Possess excellent oral and written scientific communication skills

We value transferable skills and real-world experience as much as formal qualifications.

Our benefits include:

• Generous employer contribution pension

• 29 days annual leave plus bank holidays, along with Christmas closure

• Ride to work and EV car scheme available

For more information, please see [University of Manchester Benefits](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/connect/jobs/benefits-working-here/). You can also find information on our Flexible and Hybrid working [here](https://www.staffnet.manchester.ac.uk/people/current-staff/flexible-and-hybrid-working/).

We are an open place of enquiry and challenge. We embrace and celebrate difference, diversity and debate, and we pride ourselves on being a place of education, learning and community where we are able, within the law, to question and test received wisdom, express new ideas and explore controversial or unpopular topics and opinions. Find out more from our [Freedom of Speech Policy](https://www.staffnet.manchester.ac.uk/news/display/?id=32905).

title: 340B Program Manager
description:
340B Program Manager
Remote | Full-Time

Who We Are

NuvemRx helps community health providers deliver on their mission by simplifying the complexity of pharmacy operations, with a suite of scalable solutions that integrate software, intelligence, and expert support to illuminate savings, expand access, and elevate patient care.

What We Are Looking For

At NuvemRx, we hold a high bar because our work directly impacts patient care. We look for people who embody our core values:

  • Mission Always: Every choice is a chance to serve our customers and improve healthcare
  • Be a Pioneer: Take initiative, solve problems, and build what does not yet exist
  • Do the Right Thing the Right Way: Lead with integrity, compliance, and thoughtful execution
  • Stronger Together: Own your role, collaborate deeply, and elevate the team

We are also a fast-growing company, which means you bring strong ownership, comfort with ambiguity, resilience, and a bias toward action.

About the Role

The 340B Program Manager is responsible for the oversight, administration, and ongoing compliance monitoring of the 340B Drug Pricing Program for assigned Covered Entity (CE) clients supported by NuvemRx. This position supports a variety of 340B-eligible organizations, including Federally Qualified Health Centers, Disproportionate Share Hospitals, FQHC Look-Alikes, and other eligible provider organizations.

The 340B Program Manager ensures program compliance with HRSA guidance, federal regulations, manufacturer requirements, and internal operational standards. This role oversees compliance monitoring activities, audit readiness, operational workflows, and program documentation while serving as a key liaison between clients and internal operational teams. The ideal candidate is highly organized, analytical, and capable of independently managing multiple client accounts and priorities in a fast-paced healthcare environment.

What You'll Do

Program Administration & Compliance

  • Manage and oversee day-to-day administration of assigned 340B programs to ensure compliance with HRSA guidance and applicable federal and state regulations.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact and compliance resource for assigned Covered Entities regarding 340B program operations, audit readiness, and regulatory requirements.
  • Conduct routine compliance reviews, internal audits, account monitoring, reconciliations, and operational assessments to identify potential risks or compliance concerns.
  • Monitor program activity, data integrity, accumulations, replenishment activity, and operational workflows to ensure compliant program administration.
  • Support and manage 340B ESP submission activities and manufacturer inquiry resolution processes as needed.
  • Develop, maintain, and update policies, procedures, workflows, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) to support compliant 340B program operations.

Audit Readiness & Risk Management

  • Support preparation for HRSA audits, manufacturer audits, payer reviews, and internal compliance assessments, including documentation collection, audit support, and corrective action tracking.
  • Maintain accurate, organized, and audit-ready documentation related to compliance monitoring, operational activities, and client program management.
  • Analyze program data and operational performance to identify opportunities for process improvement, operational efficiency, compliant savings optimization, and risk mitigation.

Client Engagement & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with Covered Entity leadership, pharmacy operations, finance, wholesalers, manufacturers, contract pharmacies, and third-party administrators (TPAs) to support compliant and effective program operations.
  • Participate in client meetings, compliance discussions, operational reviews, onboarding activities, and strategic program initiatives.
  • Provide education and operational guidance to clients and internal stakeholders regarding 340B program requirements and best practices.

What You Bring

Core Capabilities

  • Deep working knowledge of the 340B Drug Pricing Program, including HRSA guidance, compliance requirements, and program operations.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple client accounts and complex compliance workstreams simultaneously, with high accuracy and accountability.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret program data, identify trends, and surface actionable insights.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with both frontline pharmacy staff and executive-level stakeholders.
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to maintain audit-ready documentation standards.
  • Comfortable working independently in a remote, fast-paced environment with shifting priorities.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience managing 340B programs for FQHCs, DSH hospitals, FQHC Look-Alikes, or other covered entities.
  • Familiarity with 340B third-party administrators (TPAs), ESP submissions, and manufacturer compliance processes.
  • Experience supporting HRSA audits or internal compliance assessments.
  • Background in pharmacy operations, healthcare compliance, or healthcare administration.
  • Proficiency in data analysis tools and 340B software platforms.

Who Thrives in This Role

  • You are a compliance-minded professional who takes ownership of program integrity without being prompted.
  • You are energized by complex regulatory environments and find purpose in keeping programs airtight for clients that serve vulnerable patient populations.
  • You proactively identify risks before they become problems and bring a clear, recommended path forward.
  • You build trust with clients through consistent expertise, responsiveness, and follow-through.
  • You thrive in a role that requires both deep subject matter expertise and strong cross-functional collaboration.

Benefits

  • Remote-first work environment
  • Competitive compensation
  • Flexible PTO
  • Medical, dental, vision
  • 401(k) with match
  • Life and disability coverage
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Mission-driven team
  • WFH stipend

Compensation

The expected base compensation for this role is $80,000-85,000 per year.

Actual compensation may vary based on factors such as skills, location, and internal equity.

NuvemRx complies with applicable pay transparency laws. The compensation range listed reflects the expected base salary at the time of posting, and actual compensation may vary.

NuvemRx is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other protected status in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

NuvemRx is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need assistance or an accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact us at recruiting@nuvemrx.com.

title: QA Automation Engineer
description:
Who We Are

SWTCH is pioneering EV charging solutions for multifamily and commercial properties across North America. Since 2016, our team of entrepreneurs, energy professionals, and technologists has been focused on unlocking the social, economic, and environmental benefits of widespread EV adoption. Today, our solutions are deployed in tens of thousands of locations —many of which are low-to-moderate income housing—helping to make clean mobility accessible for all.

With an expanding footprint across Canada and the U.S., we’re scaling quickly and looking for mission-driven talent to help accelerate our growth.

The Role

At SWTCH, we're accelerating the adoption of electric vehicles by delivering intelligent charging solutions that make EV charging more accessible, reliable, and efficient. Our platform powers thousands of charging stations across North America, helping property owners, businesses, utilities, and drivers transition to a more sustainable future.

We're looking for a QA Automation Engineer who is passionate about software quality and automation to help ensure our products are reliable, scalable, and deliver an exceptional customer experience.

The Opportunity

Today, our automated test coverage is unit tests and some integration testing — we have no systematic automated coverage of end-to-end user flows. That's the gap this role exists to close. You'll design and build our automated E2E testing practice from the ground up, working closely with Product and Engineering to make sure we stop shipping regressions as we scale. You'll have real latitude here: this isn't a role where testing requirements arrive fully formed. Product can tell you what the product needs to do; figuring out how we verify it actually does that reliably is yours to define.

How We Work

  • Decisions live as close to the work as possible — you'll own how testing gets built, not just execute a checklist someone else wrote.
  • We're kind, not nice — we say the hard thing early, in a way that respects the person hearing it. Feedback is specific and timely, not saved for a review cycle.
  • We ship in small increments and treat real usage as the fastest way to learn what's working.
  • We hold strong opinions loosely — bring conviction, stay open to being wrong.

What you'll be doing

  • Guide Product Managers in translating use cases into testable requirements and edge cases — PMs bring the "what," you bring the "how do we know it actually works."
  • Own the definition of test strategy and testing standards, and design our automated E2E / user-flow testing approach from scratch.
  • Develop and execute automated functional, regression, integration, and end-to-end test suites.
  • Implement the automated portions of the testing plans you define.
  • Mentor and train engineers on writing, maintaining, and extending automated tests — part of this role's mandate is building testing capability across the team, not just within QA.
  • Perform manual/exploratory testing where automation isn't yet in place.
  • Identify, document, and track defects, working with engineering to drive timely resolution.
  • Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Monitor test execution, analyze failures, and continuously improve coverage and reliability.

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years of experience in Software Quality Assurance, including 3+ years focused on test automation.
  • Experience in testing web applications, APIs, mobile apps and backend services.
  • Experience designing an automated testing practice from scratch — not just extending one that already exists.
  • Comfort partnering with Product Managers who rely on you to help surface testing needs and edge cases
  • Hands-on experience with test automation frameworks (Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, or similar).
  • Experience testing REST APIs (Postman or similar).
  • Proficiency in Python and/or TypeScript; Ruby experience is a plus given our Rails services.
  • Experience with Git, CI/CD pipelines, and Agile practices.
  • Experience mentoring or upskilling other engineers in testing practices.
  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills; excellent communication.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with IoT, connected devices, or hardware-interfacing software — this is the environment you'd be working in day to day, though not a requirement.
  • Experience with EV charging, OCPP, or similar device-communication protocols.
  • Familiarity with AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Performance or load testing experience.

A Note on Our Stack

We're primarily Python and TypeScript, with React on the frontend and some Ruby on Rails services. We're directionally leaning toward Playwright as our automation framework, but that's not locked in — it's unproven at our scale, and if you've got a strong point of view otherwise, we want to hear it.

Why Join SWTCH?

You'll be building something that doesn't exist yet at a company where your judgment on how to build it is genuinely trusted, not just tolerated. If you want ownership over a testing practice from day one — and the chance to shape how an engineering team thinks about quality — we'd love to talk.

Benefits

  • Business Impact - As a core member of the team, you have the opportunity to take a supporting role and make a significant impact on the culture and values of the company.
  • Environmental Impact - We are a clean energy company with a mission to reduce carbon emissions globally to ensure a clean and sustainable future.
  • Diversity - People develop their talents and skills in different ways. We value different paths and experiences. If you think you meet the qualifications we are seeking, take a chance and express your interest here.

SWTCH does not offer employment to prospects without first ensuring that qualified candidates speak directly with the hiring manager and a member of our P&C team. All qualifications will be done face-to-face, whether that is in person or over Google Meet. SWTCH does not send out offers of employment without meeting candidates and does not offer employment via text. If you are contacted for any personal information via test and/or without having met a member of our hiring team in person, please disregard.

SWTCH Energy is an equal opportunity employer, all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.
