title: Chief Legal Officer
description:
About the Role

Incline Insurance Group is seeking an accomplished Chief Legal Officer (CLO) to serve as the Company’s senior legal executive and a member of the executive leadership team. The CLO will advise the CEO, Board, and executive team on enterprise legal strategy, corporate governance, financing, strategic transactions, and the legal matters supporting a growing property and casualty insurance platform.

This role combines strong insurance industry expertise with substantial experience advising private equity-backed businesses and leading complex corporate and financing transactions. The successful candidate will bring sound commercial judgment, credibility with directors and investors, and the ability to translate legal advice into practical business decisions. The CLO must be comfortable setting strategy while remaining directly involved in significant matters.

What You Will Do

Executive Legal Leadership Serve as the principal legal advisor to the CEO, Board, and executive leadership team. Shape legal strategy in support of the Company’s business objectives, evaluate significant opportunities and risks, and provide clear recommendations on complex or sensitive matters.

Private Equity and Ownership Matters Advise on the legal matters associated with private equity ownership, including shareholder arrangements, investor rights, governance requirements, management equity arrangements, and ownership transitions. Work with leadership and sponsor representatives to support growth and value-creation initiatives while protecting the Company’s interests.

Capital Markets and Financing Partner with the CFO to lead the legal aspects of debt and equity financings, credit facilities, refinancings, recapitalizations, and potential liquidity transactions. Oversee transaction structuring, diligence, documentation, negotiation, and execution, including coordination with lenders, investors, regulators, and external advisors.

Board and Corporate Governance Advise the Board and relevant committees on governance, fiduciary considerations, conflicts of interest, and significant corporate decisions. Oversee legal support for Board and committee activities, corporate records, delegated authorities, legal entity governance, and shareholder matters.

About the Legal Team

Incline’s Legal team partners with the business on insurance and reinsurance agreements, program relationships, regulatory matters, corporate transactions, and dispute resolution. The CLO will lead and develop the General Counsel and broader Legal team, establish clear responsibilities and escalation practices, and build the capabilities needed to support Incline’s growth. The role will work closely with Finance, Risk, Compliance, Underwriting, Reinsurance, Claims, Technology, and other business leaders.

What You Will Do Continued

Mergers and Acquisitions and Strategic Transactions Lead legal work for acquisitions, investments, divestitures, partnerships, and other strategic transactions. Oversee due diligence, transaction negotiation and documentation, required approvals, closing, and integration. Help leadership assess transaction risks, obligations, and strategic implications.

Insurance and Reinsurance Provide senior legal oversight of Incline’s property and casualty insurance and reinsurance operations, including fronting and program structures, delegated authority arrangements, ceded and assumed reinsurance, and collateral arrangements. Guide the Legal team on complex agreements and material issues, and directly lead negotiations or escalations requiring executive involvement.

Commercial Agreements and Program Relationships Oversee legal support for relationships with MGAs, program administrators, reinsurers, brokers, TPAs, vendors, and strategic partners. Establish contracting standards, negotiation guidelines, and approval processes that protect the Company’s interests and enable timely business decisions.

Insurance Regulation and Compliance Counsel Provide legal advice on the regulatory requirements affecting Incline’s carriers and multi-entity operations. Partner with Compliance on examinations, inquiries, filings, licensing, regulatory approvals, and interactions with insurance regulators. Advise on the regulatory implications of growth, financing, and corporate transactions.

Enterprise Legal Risk and Disputes Identify and oversee material legal exposures, establish escalation protocols, and advise on mitigation strategies. Partner with the CRO and Compliance to integrate legal considerations into enterprise risk management. Provide executive oversight of significant litigation, coverage and reinsurance disputes, investigations, and other contested matters, working with Claims and outside counsel as appropriate.

Technology and Data Oversee legal advice on technology agreements, intellectual property, privacy, cybersecurity, data rights, and artificial intelligence. Partner with Technology and business leaders to support responsible adoption of new capabilities and address material legal risks.

Legal Team and Operations Lead, mentor, and develop the General Counsel and Legal team. Set priorities and clear accountability, allocate work effectively, and strengthen succession and team capabilities. Manage the legal budget and outside counsel relationships, ensuring appropriate expertise, quality, and cost discipline. Improve contract management, workflows, legal technology, and knowledge sharing as the organization grows.


What We Are Looking For


We are seeking a commercially minded legal executive who combines insurance expertise with the corporate, financial, and governance experience needed to advise a growing, private equity-backed business.


Experience 15+ years of progressively responsible legal experience, including substantial property and casualty insurance experience and senior legal leadership responsibility. Experience advising CEOs and boards and leading complex, high-impact matters is required. Prior experience as a CLO, General Counsel, or senior legal leader with comparable scope is strongly preferred.

Private Equity Experience Demonstrated experience advising private equity-backed companies or representing private equity sponsors and their portfolio companies is required. Candidates should understand sponsor governance, shareholder arrangements, management equity, and the legal considerations associated with growth and ownership transitions.

Financing and Transaction Experience A demonstrated record of leading the legal aspects of material debt or equity financings and complex corporate transactions is required. Relevant experience includes credit facilities, recapitalizations, acquisitions, divestitures, or liquidity events. Candidates must be able to direct outside specialists while independently advising leadership on significant transaction issues and trade-offs.

Insurance and Regulatory Expertise Strong knowledge of property and casualty insurance, reinsurance, state insurance regulation, and multi-entity insurance organizations is required. Experience with fronting carriers, MGA and program relationships, delegated authority, and reinsurance structures is strongly preferred. The ability to oversee complex insurance agreements and engage effectively with regulators is essential.

Governance and Commercial Judgment Experience advising boards and senior executives on corporate governance, significant business decisions, and material legal risks. Ability to assess issues across the enterprise, communicate clear recommendations, and balance commercial objectives with legal and regulatory obligations.

Leadership Proven ability to lead and develop experienced attorneys, establish effective working relationships across functions, and manage outside counsel and legal spend. Strong executive presence, negotiation skills, discretion, and communication. Willingness to work directly on important matters in a lean, fast-moving organization.

Education and Licensure Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree from an accredited law school and an active license to practice law in at least one U.S. jurisdiction. Must be eligible to satisfy applicable requirements to provide legal services on behalf of the Company.

Location

Our preference is for this role to be based in Austin, Texas, operating within a hybrid work model.

Why Incline Insurance Group

This is an opportunity to shape the legal strategy of a growing, private equity-backed insurance platform. The CLO will work directly with executive leadership and the Board, influence significant financing and transactional decisions, and develop a legal function that supports Incline’s next stage of growth.

title: Product Designer
description:
We are looking for a talented Product Designer to help create intuitive and impactful product experiences across our customers' journey with Bally Sports Live. Product designers at Bally's Media play a central role in the product development process, partnering with Product Management and Engineering to solve customer problems in an agile environment.

You will be involved in every aspect of the product development process, from early discovery and user testing through to tweaking pixels right before launch. You bring a craft-focused eye, balancing strategic user goals with strong visual taste. Bally Sports Live competes for attention in living rooms and on phones against the most polished consumer products in the world, and our customers hold us to that standard.

You are passionate about working with customers and building empathy with users, and about collaborating with cross-functional teammates to craft engaging and intuitive experiences across TV, mobile, and web. You'll work alongside an experienced design lead who sets direction and holds the craft bar, with real ownership of your own surfaces from day one. This role is built to grow, and we're looking for someone ready to take on more scope over time. Your success will be measured by the experiences that your team ships and the outcomes they deliver for customers and the business.

Responsibilities:

  • Partner across the product team. Collaborate with Product Management and Engineering to design and ship solutions that are elegant, practical, and a pleasure to use.
  • Design for everyone, on every screen. Living-room TV, mobile, and web each reach a wide range of ages, devices, and technical comfort, and each context has its own rules.
  • Learn directly from users. Run research, tests, and experiments to understand real motivations, goals, and pain points, and lead the design sprints and discovery sessions that turn what you learn into direction.
  • Follow the data. Dig into product analytics, customer support contacts, and social feedback to see how the product is really used, and where the next opportunities are.
  • Own problems end to end. Take a loosely defined problem and drive it to a shipped solution: explore multiple directions, push past the obvious one, weigh the tradeoffs, and make the call.
  • Use AI to move faster. Augment your workflow so you can explore more directions, prototype quicker, and spend more of your time on judgment and craft.
  • Hold the craft bar. Intuitive experiences, premium visual quality, and meticulous attention to detail, on every surface.
  • See it through to ship. Hand off UX specs, assets, and prototypes to engineering, and QA the builds from a design perspective.
  • Make your thinking visible. Present your work to stakeholders, showing the reasoning behind the decisions and how the design serves product goals.
  • Bring a point of view. Go beyond designing features, have an opinion on where the product should go next, and advocate for the user in those conversations.

title: Compounder II
description:
Position Summary

The Compounder II manufactures bulk product batches of all standard types — including emulsions, reverse emulsions, scrubs and washes — in accordance with approved master formulas and process instructions, working independently within the scope of current qualification. The role operates processing equipment for which the incumbent is trained and qualified, assists with the training of new and temporary employees, works in compliance with current Good Manufacturing Practices for OTC drug products (21 CFR Parts 210 and 211) and for cosmetic products (ISO 22716), and maintains a clean, safe and orderly work environment.

Responsibilities and Essential Duties

  • Manufacture product batches of all standard types (reverse emulsions, emulsions, scrubs, washes) in accordance with the approved master formula and process instruction, working independently within the scope of current qualification.
  • Assist with the training of new and temporary employees, and act as second-person verifier for weights, measures and critical process steps performed by others (21 CFR 211.101(c), 211.188).
  • Operate only the processing equipment for which training and qualification are current and documented.
  • Complete and maintain current all assigned cGMP, SOP, safety and equipment-specific training (21 CFR 211.25).
  • Verify raw material identity, lot number, expiry or retest date and quantity at charge-in and perform second-person verification of weights and measures (21 CFR 211.101(c)).
  • Record all batch, cleaning and equipment data contemporaneously, legibly, accurately and attributably. Correct an entry with a single line through it, initials, date and reason. Do not pre-record, back-date or overwrite any entry.
  • Perform and record in-process checks, interpret the result against specification, and escalate an out-of-specification result before proceeding to the next step.
  • Reconcile actual yield to theoretical yield at the required phases and investigate any discrepancy with the Supervisor (21 CFR 211.103).
  • Perform line clearance and verify equipment and area status labelling before starting a batch.
  • Wash, sanitize and set up manufacturing equipment in accordance with the validated cleaning and sanitization procedures, observing clean-hold time limits.
  • Initiate a Notification of Event (NOE) in ETQ for any deviation from the process instruction, out-of-specification result, equipment failure or suspected product quality defect, and contribute to the resulting investigation and corrective action.
  • Maintain efficient compounding operations by troubleshooting routine process problems, adjusting equipment within the limits of the process instruction, and raising maintenance work orders with an accurate fault description.
  • Follow all safety rules, wear the prescribed personal protective equipment, hold current lockout/tagout authorized-employee status, recognize and report safety hazards and near misses, and keep the work area clean and orderly.
  • Observe personal hygiene and gowning requirements, and report to a supervisor any apparent illness, open lesion, or other health condition that may adversely affect product safety or quality, as required by 21 CFR 211.28.
  • Maintain regular and reliable attendance and punctuality in accordance with the Employee Attendance Punctuality Policy.
  • Report decisions, problems and questions to the Compounding Supervisor or Compounding Manager.
  • Follow and abide by the Company Employee Handbook at all times.
  • Perform other related duties or projects as required.

Competency and Performance Expectations

Proficiency requirements for this position are defined in the Compounding Competency Matrix. Qualification against the “Req. competency by level” column of that matrix is a condition of independent operation and consideration for progression to Compounder III. Performance is reviewed periodically against the measures below; the full Above / At / Below Expectation criteria are maintained in the Compounding KPI Scorecard.



Category

Level II Expectation — Compounder II

Safety

Follows all written safety requirements, GMP, SOPs, and safe work practices, including but not limited to LOTO, E-Stop, and machine guarding requirements, and does not bypass or shortcut safety procedures. Wears required PPE, maintains a safe and clean work area, and promptly reports injuries, near misses, unsafe conditions, and safety concerns.

Quality & Compliance

Performs assigned production activities in accordance with company policies, SOPs, Work Instructions, GMP requirements, and approved specifications. Maintains required documentation and traceability, and completes all required ETQ, company, and job-specific training.

Job Performance

Performs assigned production tasks accurately and demonstrates proficiency on assigned workstations and equipment. Develops the ability to perform assigned tasks independently while meeting established production standards.

Cost

Uses materials, components, equipment, and production time responsibly, and minimizes preventable waste, rework, errors, and material discrepancies.

Reliability & Conduct

Follows the Employee Handbook and company policies, including the Employee Attendance Punctuality Policy. Demonstrates punctuality, teamwork, communication, and professional conduct.

Level Progression – Compounder II builds on the Compounder I foundation and develops the production, quality, and safety skills required at the Compounder III level. Employees in this role will be evaluated for advancement to Compounder III based on demonstrated competencies, including qualification under the Compounding Competency Matrix and the criteria as well as performance, attendance, adherence to safety standards, and business needs. Advancement decisions are made at the Company's discretion. Advancement is not automatic or guaranteed, and time spent in this position does not alter the at-will nature of employment.

Technical Skills Required

  • Ability to read, interpret and execute a written process instruction and batch record in English, and to recognize when execution has departed from it.
  • Applied mathematics for batch work: percentages, unit conversion, dilution, and yield calculation.
  • Competence in emulsification (oil-in-water and water-in-oil), polymer and gum hydration, carbomer neutralization, surfactant systems, and heat-sensitive addition.
  • Competence in kettle operation: jacket heating and cooling profiles, ramp and hold control, agitation and rotor-stator homogenization, vacuum and deaeration, bulk transfer and filtration.
  • Ability to retrieve and interpret kettle / historian batch data and compare it against the process instruction.
  • Ability to perform in-process testing (pH, Brookfield viscosity, specific gravity) and interpret the result against specification.
  • Ability to author a factual, complete Notification of Event in ETQ.
  • Competence in ERP transactions: material consumption and yield reconciliation.
  • Ability to contribute to a productive and cooperative atmosphere, show commitment to team objectives, handle day-to-day work challenges, and manage multiple tasks at one time.
  • Meets every proficiency rating in the “Req. Compounder II” column of the Compounding Competency Matrix.

Experience Required

  • High school education or GED equivalent.
  • Previous work in a manufacturing environment.
  • 2 years batch blending experience.
  • Qualified against the Compounder II column of the Compounding Competency Matrix.

Physical Requirements

  • Regularly sit, stand, and walk for extended periods of time.
  • Ability to sit, balance, climb, stand, bend, squat, squeeze, kneel, turn, crouch, and stoop repeatedly.
  • Frequently lift, carry and position materials weighing up to 50 pounds, and occasionally up to 75 pounds. Move drums weighing up to 500 pounds using the drum handling equipment and lift assists provided; drums are not manually lifted.
  • Frequent exposure to varying temperatures, loud noises, heavy machinery, fumes or airborne particles, wet floors, moving mechanical parts, electrical hazards, chemicals, vibration, and work on elevated platforms.
  • Prolonged use of a computer screen.
  • Must be able to discern differences in colors and shades.
  • Good eye/hand coordination.
  • Ability to seize, hold, grasp, turn, or otherwise work with hand or hands.
  • Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

title: Family Partner
description:
Family Partner

Program & Location: Brockton Mobile Crisis Intervention Services
Education: High School or equivalent (GED)
Pay Range: $45,760 -$54,080 (Education & experience dependent)
Status: Full Time

About Us

High Point & Affiliated Organizations is a health and human service agency whose mission is to prevent and treat substance use and mental health disorders. High Point has programs located throughout Southeastern Massachusetts offering a full continuum of care for substance use and mental health treatment, including inpatient, outpatient, residential, and community-based services. Programs and services also assist survivors of abuse, violence, and families experiencing homelessness. High Point believes that everyone has inherent goodness, worth, and dignity. Our goal is to help individuals and families achieve personal change and improve their quality of life.

Family Partner Duties & Responsibilities

  • Provide emotional and social support to families (parent/caregiver) of a youth with behavioral health needs and lives in the community being served
  • Share lived experience and use coaching and mentoring
  • Support Parent/caregivers/family in making positive life changes and developing skills to facilitate their recovery
  • Provide on-going in-home crisis stabilization services and support to families/caregivers in navigating the behavioral health crisis response system and can support brief interventions that address behavior and safety
  • Assist parent/caregivers/family to discuss and try new strategies for developing recovery-supportive friendships, reconnecting or improving family relationships, and identifying and using community networks.
  • Assist Parent/caregivers in creating personally meaningful links to treatment, peer support services, and mutual aid and support them in their efforts to build their capacity to move between and among these services and supports as needed.
  • Act in an open and transparent way as a role model and living example of a peer support
  • When appropriate, use the peer relationship to assist with motivation and facilitate connections to primary and specialty medical, dental, and mental health services as well as social services, including applying for benefits and navigating other relevant systems, such as criminal justice and child protection/child welfare.
  • Demonstrate cultural humility through linguistically appropriate and culturally sensitive peer supports that embrace the diversity of Parent/caregivers’ identities, including racial, ethnic, gender/gender identity, sex, sexual orientation, physical and intellectual challenges
  • Serve as an advocate for parent/caregivers and assist parent/caregivers in learning self-advocacy skills.
  • Act as a mentor, assisting the parent/caregiver’s treatment process and supporting the parent/caregiver’s goals and decisions
  • Provide peer support services in a person-centered and strength-based manner.
  • Provide temporary assistance with transportation to essential self-help, peer support, and medical and behavioral health appointments while transitioning to community-based transportation resources.
  • Deliver services on a mobile basis to parent/caregivers in any setting that is safe for the parent/caregiver and staff.
  • Using a peer mentoring framework, work collaboratively with the pregnant and/or parenting Parent/caregiver to create and coordinate Plan of Safe Care (also called Family Support Plan) specifically designed to help the parent/caregiver identify needed services for recovery and parenting
  • Support the parent/caregiver around perinatal health and support needs, housing needs, health care needs, income needs, and mental health
  • Maintain appropriate level of productivity/billable hours
  • Accurately complete all required billing sheets and expense reports in required time frame
  • Accurately document all parent/caregiver progress on required forms in required time frame
  • Accurately document and submit weekly schedule in required time frame
  • Other duties as assigned by the Clinical Program Director.

Family Partner Requirements

  • Experience as a caregiver of a youth with special needs and preferably a youth with mental health needs.

  • Experience navigating any of the child and family-serving systems and teaching family members who are involved with the child and family serving systems.

  • Must present as courteous and professional at all times.

  • Demonstrated flexibility and ability to perform multiple tasks.

  • Must have excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to organize ideas in logical and clear fashion.

  • Proficient and knowledge of basic computer skills and software programs including the ability to learn, use and train HPAO`s electronic medical records.

  • Must have the ability to work with others in cooperative and collaborative manner.

  • An understanding of the relationship between substance use and mental health issues and/or self-help programs.

  • An understanding of boundaries and ethics.

  • Comply with Federal Regulations, 42 CFR Part 2, Substance Abuse Confidentiality Regulations and HIPAA Regulations.

  • Certification in the HPAO approved de-escalation program.

  • Ability to work collaboratively with behavioral health and substance use clients from diverse legal, social, economic, ethnic, cultural and racial backgrounds as well as family parent/caregivers, insurance providers and outside providers.

  • Possess the ability to maintain healthy boundaries.

  • Knowledge of appropriate confidentiality policies and procedures.

  • Ability to work independently without direct supervision while adhering to the program’s philosophical team approach.

  • Established contacts and recovery partnerships in the community.

  • Demonstrated ability to work with a diverse population.

  • Knowledge of the behavioral health and addiction treatment services system, and recovery support services.

  • Capacity to respond to tasks in a timely manner.

    Family Partner Qualifications

    • Bachelor’s degree in human services field from an accredited university and one (1) year of experience working with the target population; or Associate’s degree in a human service field from an accredited university and one (1) year of experience working with children/adolescents/transition aged youth; or High school diploma or GED and a minimum of two (2) years working with children/adolescents/transitional aged youth

    • Living or working in Brockton catchment area and surrounding towns

    • Minimum of 1 year of experience in navigating any of the child-and-family serving systems and supporting family members who are involved with the child-and0family serving systems

    • Lived experience of mental health, emotional health and/or trauma resulting in significant life disruption as a parent/caregiver of a youth with behavioral health needs

    • Willingness to share your recovery story in the context of peer/family support

    • Participation and completion of The Transformation Center (Kiva Center) CPS training and certification preferred or willing to complete if appropriate.

    Any compensation range provided is an estimate based on current market data. The actual offer may fall above or below this range, depending on the candidate’s experience, skills, and geographic location.

    High Points’ main objective is to ensure all employees and their families lead fulfilling and healthy lives. We offer essential resources and support to build and sustain physical, financial, and emotional strength to achieve this. Our focus is on overall well-being so you can concentrate on the things that matter most. Our benefits plan comprises medical, dental, vision, flexible spending and health savings accounts, life insurance, disability, 403b, paid vacation/time off, and other benefits.

    High Point and its affiliates are equal opportunity employers. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristics.

title: Licensing 1-2(CPG)
description:
About this Job




Mission:
Our mission is to serve and protect the public interest in real estate transactions and other real estate-related activities. We accomplish this by maintaining a tradition of open government; providing fair and equitable administration and enforcement of the Louisiana Real Estate License Law and Commission Rules and Regulations; and through the development of progressive education programs that promote knowledge, ethics, and advancement of the real estate industry.


About this Position:
This role involves processing professional license applications, renewals, and license status changes. New hires work under close supervision until fully trained. Expect to work with applicants/licensees, Licensing Division staff, a Licensing Analyst Supervisor, and the general public. A typical day would include processing a queue of applications and requests -verifying documents, following up on pending applications, and answering applicant questions by phone or email. Any unusual issues (flagged history, inconsistent records) get documented and routed to a supervisor.

An ideal candidate should possess the following competencies:
  • Communicating Effectively: The ability to relay information correctly and appropriately to connect people and ideas.
  • Following Policies and Procedures: The ability to comply with policies and procedures of the organization, as well as State Civil Service rules, and all applicable federal and state laws.
  • Thinking Critically: The ability to objectively question, analyze, interpret, and evaluate information to form a conclusion.
  • Using Data: The ability to use relevant and valid data to inform a recommendation for action.
  • Adapting to Change: The ability to adjust plans, expectations, and behaviors in response to change.
  • Demonstrating Innovation: The ability to generate original ideas that create value, improve processes, or provide new products or services.
  • Displaying Professionalism: The ability to recognize how your actions impact the perceptions of both you and your organization.
  • Learning Actively: The ability to acquire necessary knowledge and skills to improve performance and achieve organizational goals.
  • Solving Problems: The ability to discover solutions to problems.

Minimum Qualifications

Three years of experience in the issuance, maintenance, or reinstatement of licenses; OR

Six years of full-time work experience in any field; OR

A bachelor's degree.

EXPERIENCE SUBSTITUTION:
Every 30 semester hours earned from an accredited college or university will be credited as one year of experience towards the six years of full-time work experience in any field. The maximum substitution allowed is 120 semester hours which substitutes for a maximum of four years of experience in any field.

Job Specification

The official job specifications for this role, as defined by the State Civil Service, can be found here.

Job Duties and Other Information

Job Duties:

  • Examines and analyzes data submitted by and/or on behalf of each applicant for licensure for accuracy, authenticity, and completeness of factual information to document the determination of
    eligibility and qualification for licensure.

  • Advises applicants and/or licensees of the status of their application and/or requests relative to the requisite information for further disposition of the same.

  • Receives, analyzes, and verifies the authenticity of diplomas and licenses submitted by applicants, licensees, institutions, and/or other licensing authorities as well as federal and state documents authorizing work in the United States and/or in the State (i.e., J-1 Visas, naturalization papers, licenses).

  • Reviews the application to determine if requisite licensure fees have been received by the agency.

  • Determines when licensure files can be forwarded to the master file room and takes action accordingly.

  • Explains federal and state laws, rules, and regulations, standards, and agency policies to officials, staff, licensees, the public, and/or providers of services and interprets and applies the same.

  • Assists in the preparation and dissemination of reports of statistical data, official reports, and/or information regarding continuing education, compliance.

  • Interprets and explains statutes, agency rules, regulations, policies, and procedures of continuing
    education to the public.
    Provides input and recommendations to the Supervisor on policies and/or procedure development

Appointment Type: Probational

Career Progression: This position participates in a Career Progression Group.

Compensation: The salary offered will be determined based on qualifications and experience.

Annual salary and potential for an annual bonus

title: Software Development Engineer, Mobile App Foundations - Quality and Release
description:
What if every release of one of the world's most downloaded apps could ship faster and safer, with quality gates catching regressions before a single customer is affected?

Do you want to solve complex problems that require creative thinking and a deep understanding of the problem space at the scale of the Amazon Mobile Shopping app, with simple and elegant solutions? Do you want to work with talented engineers and be part of a team of enthusiastic individuals? Do you want to be part of a team that cares about finding the right initiatives for each of us so we can improve every day, grow our skills, and create long-term opportunities? Do you want to challenge yourself and others to constantly come up with innovative solutions impacting hundreds of teams and millions of Shoppers? Then we would like to hear from you!

Key job responsibilities
As a Software Development Engineer on the Release & Quality team, you will design, implement, and own the systems that get high-quality mobile releases into customers' hands safely, predictably, and fast, while accelerating development and integration by transforming the way we build mobile apps with AI. You will build and improve the release pipeline, automated quality gates, and testing enforcement that hundreds of teams and AI agents across Amazon depend on to ship to the iOS and Android Shopping apps. You will develop automation, tooling, and frameworks that raise the quality bar, including shift-left checks, AI-based test execution, and automated release-health signals such as dial-up monitoring, so issues are caught early and release decisions are automated and data-driven.

You will take ownership of features and components end to end, from design through implementation, testing, and operation, and drive them to production. You will dive deep into release incidents to find and fix root causes, hold a high bar for the accuracy of the signals your systems produce, and partner with TPMs and partner mobile teams to keep our tooling reliable. You will also help raise the team's engineering standards and mentor more junior engineers as we create mechanisms to release mobile apps at scale.

About the team
Our team owns the release, quality, and testing-enforcement systems used by hundreds of teams across Amazon to launch the latest features on the Amazon iOS and Android Shopping apps.

We keep releases predictable and safe by building automated quality gates, robust release tooling, and release health monitoring, setting the new standards of how we release mobile apps while raising the bar on quality as we adopt AI to develop apps at Amazon.

We are on a mission to change how customers shop on mobile. We take on problems no one has solved, make the hard calls, and ship something better than what we started with. Interested to change how we ship mobile apps? Join us!

title: Regional Director, SUD Outreach
description:
Why Charlie Health?

Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care. From limited local options and long wait times to treatment that lacks personalization, behavioral healthcare can leave people feeling unseen and unsupported.

Charlie Health exists to change that. Our mission is to connect the world to life-saving behavioral health treatment. We deliver personalized, virtual care rooted in connection—between clients and clinicians, care teams, loved ones, and the communities that support them. By focusing on people with complex needs, we’re expanding access to meaningful care and driving better outcomes from the comfort of home.

As a rapidly growing organization, we're reaching more communities every day and building a team that’s redefining what behavioral health treatment can look like. If you're ready to use your skills to drive lasting change and help more people access the care they deserve, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

Charlie Health is one of the fastest-growing startups in the healthcare industry, working tirelessly to connect people everywhere to life-saving behavioral health treatment.

As a Regional Director, SUD Outreach, you will lead a founding go-to-market team responsible for scaling Charlie Health's Substance Use Disorder (SUD) program across a state-wide or multi-state region. SUD represents our current major growth vertical, and you will be charged with building and running the regional playbook. You will manage and support the SUD Territory Managers who represent Charlie Health in the region, and you'll work hand-in-hand with our leadership team to define how we open and win in these markets.

You and your team will shape how Charlie Health engages referral partners in key SUD settings such as detox centers, residential treatment centers, rehabilitation facilities, and other SUD-focused organizations. You'll make sure these partners understand how our comprehensive SUD treatment and mental health programs support individuals on the path to recovery, and you'll obsess (in a healthy way) over ensuring that every SUD provider, patient, and family in your region is aware of Charlie Health's programs.

This role is best suited for a leader who thrives in high-accountability environments and wants to help build something meaningful from the ground up. You'll be granted an unparalleled level of responsibility while collaborating with sharp, spirited, ambitious, and mission-driven coworkers. In turn, you will drive field execution, develop your team, create accountability, use data and strategy to make decisions, and ultimately build a culture that consistently produces results.

At Charlie Health, we believe in leading with our “why” and connecting with our purpose every day. Join us to find not only a career but a calling.

Responsibilities

  • Own your region’s admissions goals; this role will be responsible for the team's overall performance, which may include carrying a book subject to current team size and growth
  • Manage and lead a team of SUD Territory Managers, ensuring that regional performance goals are met or exceeded
  • Cultivate a positive, high-energy, team-first culture that balances recognition, healthy competition, collaboration, urgency, and accountability
  • Hold your team accountable to activating new relationships and maintaining and growing existing relationships. Build accountability around declining relationships, and study and celebrate growing ones to replicate what's working
  • Enforce core expectations around calls, meetings, travel and field presence
  • Measure and own KPIs across your region, reporting upwards on a regular basis
  • Coach your team on in-field outreach and join them in the field regularly (2-3 days per week), observing execution, identifying skill gaps, reinforcing strengths, and following through on development
  • Build data literacy to quickly interpret performance data, identify trends and gaps, and make rapid decisions to drive outcomes
  • Partner with Growth Strategy and other internal stakeholders to proactively identify high-potential opportunities, and translate strategy into field execution
  • Represent Charlie Health in community settings as well as industry events, conferences, and educational sessions to promote awareness of our SUD program
  • Collect and synthesize feedback from partners, patients, and stakeholders to refine messaging, positioning, and go-forward marketing, operational, and product strategies

Requirements

  • 6-10+ years of business development experience, including 2-3+ years of experience in sales leadership
  • Experience in healthcare or behavioral health outreach preferred
  • Familiarity with the SUD treatment ecosystem and community ties across the region preferred
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Google Suite, CRM (Salesforce preferred), scheduling, and video conferencing technologies
  • Work authorized in the United States and native or bilingual English proficiency
  • Demonstrated track record of top-tier performance in the development, maintenance, and growth of customer accounts in a B2B / outreach setting
  • Experience managing, coaching, and motivating a business development team
  • Experience measuring, analyzing, and being accountable to well-defined sales metrics/KPIs
  • Exceptional interpersonal, relationship-building, and listening skills, with a natural, consultative style
  • Ability to energize, communicate, and build rapport at all levels within an organization
  • Ability to travel locally (within ~1 hour driving distance) for meetings with potential referral partners
  • Must have reliable transportation, a valid driver's license, and the ability to drive up to 1-hour each way on a regular basis
  • Strong project management skills, with a demonstrable ability to corral and manage details in a fast-paced, fluid environment
  • Expert in advising, presenting to, and persuading senior corporate personnel

Benefits

Charlie Health is pleased to offer comprehensive benefits to all full-time, exempt employees. Read more about our benefits here.

Additional Information

The total target base compensation for this role will be between $125,000 and $165,000 per year at the commencement of employment. In addition to base compensation, this role offers a target performance-based bonus. Please note, pay will be determined on an individualized basis and will be impacted by location, experience, expertise, internal pay equity, and other relevant business considerations. Further, cash compensation is only part of the total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may include stock options and other Charlie Health-sponsored benefits.

Our Values

  • Connection: Care deeply & inspire hope.
  • Congruence: Stay curious & heed the evidence.
  • Commitment: Act with urgency & don’t give up.

Please do not call our public clinical admissions line in regard to this or any other job posting.

title: Dining Services Aide
description:
Join our Dining Services team in a senior living community! Assist with meal preparation, food service, dishwashing, kitchen sanitation, and stocking while helping create a positive dining experience for residents.

Summary of Responsibilities:

Dining Service Aides are responsible for the courteous delivery of meals to residents and maintaining a pleasant atmosphere in the various dining areas and event areas as needed. This includes assisting residents with menu selection, delivering meals and between-meal snacks in Skilled Nursing Care and Personal Care dining, and delivering meals to residents in a timely and efficient manner. In addition, Dining Service Aides clear and reset tables, and maintain proper sanitation in dining areas.

Essential Functions:

• Assures resident, family or guests receive meals, snacks, and supplements as ordered.
• Promptly and efficiently obtain meal selection from residents, family, and guests.
• Serves resident, family or guests promptly, accurately, and efficiently with pleasant interaction and assistance.
• Responds to all food service requests and serve meals according to diet.
• Assembles trays for residents, family, and guests per tray line list with accuracy and timely delivery to nursing unit. Maintains attractive meal service by placing items on the tray and plate in correct locations with proper garnish and condiment.
• Anticipates needs for meal service and prepares items for service i.e.: condiments, and special equipment.
• Serve food using FIFO inventory system.
• Maintain food at safe temperature levels. Transports all food items from main kitchen to Skilled Nursing/Personal Care kitchen on covered cart and store items in timely manner not allowing food to sit out.
• Stocks Nursing care and Highlands Rehab per Dining Service protocol.
• Follow established cleaning procedures leaving dining area clean and reset for next meal.
• Preforms routine cleaning assignments within the department to ensure that a sanitary and safe environment exists for preparation and service of food.
• Provides ware washing support to department so that dishes, silverware, etc. are sanitized and safe for meal service to resident, family and guests.
• Uses proper PPE.
• Assists with cooking for all day dining items.
• Check meal trays and dining room tables for personal items left behind and return items to supervisor.
• Lists and comprehends all information given out during pre-meal, knows all special menu options for the meal period.
• Ensure all opening and closing side work is accomplished following all sanitation procedures and guidelines.
• Uphold food safety standards and consistently follows handwashing, glove usage, and hair net standards.
• Keeps fellow staff members advised of changes in work orders or rules.
• Communicates openly and honestly with fellow staff members and supervisors.
• Keeps confidential information safe and not divulged to outside parties.
• Listens effectively to supervisors, residents, and staff.
• Stays current with assigned training.

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work:

• This position may be full-time or part-time in a healthcare facility that is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Rotating shifts, as well as weekends, holidays, and work during inclement weather, will be required.

Education and Experience Requirements:

• High School Diploma or GED (required or being pursued by high school student)
• 1-3 years experience working in the food industry
• Prior experience working with senior population (preferred)
• Prior Waitstaff or kitchen experience preferred (preferred)

Certification and Licensure Requirements:

• SERV Safe Certification (Preferred)

Physical Requirements and Physical Demands:

• While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk and hear. Visual acuity must be adequate to perform job duties, including reading information from printed sources and computer screens.
• This position is continuously required to walk, climb crouch, reach above shoulder, lift from waist level up, lift above shoulders/head, and lifting 25 lbs.
• This position is occasionally required to sit, bend, squat, crawl, kneel, balance, pull with force, push/push up to 350 lbs., lift from floor level up, lift 50 lbs. and lift and/or carry objects weighing up to 25 lbs.

Safety Hazards and Physical Environment:

• May be exposed to blood-borne pathogens - Low Risk.
• May be exposed to communicable diseases.
• May be exposed to potential electrical shock
• May be exposed to toxic, caustic, chemicals, and/or detergents
• May be exposed to rare occasions during which it is necessary to interact with a resident exhibiting aggressive behavior.

title: Junior Security Engineer
description:
Tharros supports the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) with cybersecurity services across its Intelligence Enterprise. In support of this mission, we have an immediate opportunity for a Junior Security Engineer.

In this role you will support cybersecurity engineering across enterprise audit, cloud and Zero Trust architecture, security tooling, and DevSecOps. You will maintain security tools, automate STIG compliance, and help build the dashboards and Zero Trust roadmap the enterprise relies on. This position is on-site in a Government SCIF in Washington, DC.

Duties include but not limited to:

  • Maintain and update cybersecurity tools including ACAS/Nessus, SCAP, SonarQube, and GitLab.
  • Update Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) quarterly and Nessus plug-in IDs monthly.
  • Develop and troubleshoot scripts that automate STIG application and validation within the DevSecOps pipeline.
  • Organize security tool data into near-real-time dashboards in the GRC or approved tool.
  • Support implementation of ICS 500-27 enterprise audit requirements and build audit review dashboards with ISSOs.
  • Support Zero Trust capability gap analysis, the Zero Trust roadmap, and Zero Trust dashboards.
  • Maintain a tracking tool for network device end-of-life and end-of-service dates.
  • BS degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Information Systems, or Computer Science OR minimum of 4 years' experience in IT or cybersecurity.
  • Minimum of 1 year of experience in security engineering, systems administration, or DevSecOps.
  • Active TS/SCI clearance and U.S. citizenship; willingness to undergo a DHS counterintelligence-scope polygraph.
  • Proficiency with automation tools to include but not limited to Python, PowerShell, or shell scripting languages.
  • Knowledge of DISA STIGs and configuration compliance scanning.
  • Knowledge of audit logging concepts for Windows and Linux systems.
  • Knowledge of Zero Trust architecture principles.
  • Skill in using Nessus/ACAS or SCAP tools.
  • Ability to troubleshoot tool and script issues.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite to include Teams or similar workplace chat and videoconferencing tools.
  • Excellent written and oral communications skills.

Desired

  • CompTIA Security+ or an AWS/Azure fundamentals certification.
  • Experience with GitLab CI/CD or Splunk.

A SumUp Brasil está expandindo as formas de aquisição de lojistas para além dos nossos canais tradicionais. Parcerias com provedores de TEF, ERPs e plataformas de software comercial representam uma oportunidade de alto potencial para levar os pagamentos para dentro das ferramentas que os lojistas já utilizam. Nessa posição, você será responsável por construir esse canal do zero no mercado brasileiro, aproveitando a experiência da SumUp na Europa e adaptando a às necessidades locais.

O que você vai fazer

  • Construir o ecossistema: identificar e priorizar parceiros com alto potencial, desenvolvendo um pipeline de ERPs, provedores de TEF e outros softwares relevantes
  • Liderar da estratégia ao lançamento: estruturar propostas de parceria, conduzir discussões e negociações comerciais e criar planos conjuntos de GTM (go to market)

  • Construir para escalar: documentar decisões e criar playbooks que tornem as parcerias bem sucedidas replicáveis

Você será uma ótima pessoa para essa posição se…

  • Já construiu ou escalou parcerias comerciais, business development ou canais de aquisição
  • Tem mais de 3 anos de experiência com plataformas de software e o ecossistema de pagamentos
  • Consegue conectar integrações a resultados comerciais e trabalhar de forma próxima a Product e Engineering
  • Tem perfil empreendedor e analítico e se sente confortável criando estrutura em ambientes ambíguos
  • Consegue alinhar times internos e parceiros externos, mesmo sem autoridade formal
  • Tem inglês intermediário a avançado e se comunica com confiança com stakeholders globais

Por que você deve se juntar à SumUp

🌈 Compromisso com Diversidade e Inclusão: faça parte de um ambiente de trabalho que valoriza e promove a diversidade, cultivando um ambiente inclusivo onde as perspectivas de todos são respeitadas e acolhidas
🚀 Participação no nosso programa de Virtual Stock Options: você terá uma participação no sucesso futuro da SumUp

🏖 Tempo livre generoso: aproveite 22 dias úteis de licença remunerada, além de feriados e dias especiais de licença
💪 Mantenha se em forma: inclui plano Wellhub e academia no escritório

🧠 Bem estar mental: acesso ao Zenklub para terapia, coaching e recursos de bem estar emocional

Sobre a SumUp

Seja empoderado a fazer mais do que importa.

Na SumUp, nossa missão é empoderar pequenos negócios em todo o mundo, oferecendo ferramentas simples e acessíveis que permitem que eles prosperem. Hoje, mais de 4 milhões de negócios em 39 mercados confiam na SumUp como parceira financeira para gerenciar pagamentos, finanças e relacionamento com clientes.

Nosso compromisso com os pequenos negócios se reflete no nosso time diverso de mais de 4.000 SumUppers de mais de 90 nacionalidades, unidos pela colaboração global e por uma mentalidade inovadora. Nossos valores centrais são a base de quem somos e do que defendemos, moldando nossa cultura de trabalho e impulsionando nosso sucesso. Cultivamos a inclusão e uma cultura de aprendizado contínuo, oferecendo um espaço seguro para o crescimento pessoal e profissional. Nossas diferenças nos tornam únicos e fortes, à medida que buscamos criar um ambiente onde todos pertencem e se sentem apoiados, independentemente de como se identificam.

A SumUp tem orgulho de ser uma empregadora que promove a Igualdade de Oportunidades no Emprego, buscando e abraçando ativamente a diversidade em nossa força de trabalho. Não tomamos decisões de contratação ou emprego com base em raça, cor, religião ou crença religiosa, origem étnica ou nacional, nacionalidade, sexo, gênero, identidade de gênero, orientação sexual, deficiência, idade ou qualquer outra base protegida pelas leis aplicáveis ou proibida pela política da empresa. Nosso compromisso vai além do recrutamento, buscando criar um ambiente de trabalho seguro e respeitoso, onde qualquer forma de assédio é estritamente proibida. title: Construction Project Manager

title: Receiving Supervisor
description:
Lasko Products, an industry leader of home environment products for over 100 years, is seeking a Receiving Supervisor in our Ft. Worth, TX location.

The Receiving Supervisor will oversee and participate with the unloading, receiving and storing processes of all inbound and the staging of material for the following day’s production. Supervisor will be responsible to make sure team is staying on task and completing daily work activities. The Lead inspires, motivates and provides guidance to employees to meet daily tasks and reach certain goals.

Essential Functions

  • Manage through subordinates organized and efficient processes for the receiving of all Materials.
  • Responsible for overseeing the process of receiving inbound material.
  • Responsible for overseeing the process of returned goods.
  • Assist in training new hires.
  • Appropriately address warehouse issues with Manager such as inventory discrepancies, warehouse personnel coordination, employee job responsibilities, scheduling issues, forklift & warehouse maintenance.
  • Ensure loading/unloading, labeling, stacking/staging, take back to warehouse items, clearing out MSA is done in a timely and safely manner.
  • Ensure employees are properly trained and following the staging process in warehouse
  • Ensure staging lanes are fully stocked, and parts are all matching with the BOM based on the Model (Auditing the items) in order to maintain continuous productivity.
  • Coordinate and monitor operations to ensure safety and compliance with regulations.
  • Ensure accuracy and quality standards for products and maintain inventory records for audits.
  • Allocate necessary space for stock rotation and assist with proper FIFO process.
  • Supply production areas with materials using FIFO to ensure flow of production.
  • Timely, report accidents or near miss incidents as required by the Safety Program.
  • Ensure all products are stored in the conditions necessary to maintain quality.
  • Assist in daily scheduled production in all areas, ensuring the processing work is performed in an efficient & productive manner.

Required Education and Experience

  • High school diploma
  • Proficient Data Entry skills
  • Working knowledge of web-based inventory
  • Basic computer knowledge with Windows based programs (Outlook, Word, Excel)
  • Self-motivated and able to work with little supervision
  • Must have strong working knowledge of warehouse operations and product flow, as well as the systems modules pertaining to receiving, transferring, picking and billing
  • Must have at least four (4) years experience in warehouse environment
  • Must have experience on material handling equipment (i.e. forklift)
  • Experience in the supervision of personnel a plus.
  • Must have a detail orientation and the proven ability to prioritize work
  • Must have effective verbal and written communication skills
  • Must have the ability to work with limited supervision and as part of a team
  • Sound decision-making abilities
  • The position requires decisions relative to planning, maintenance, product throughput efficiency, employee relations and database management.
  • Strong interpersonal skills are required, as this position works closely with personnel from a variety of different areas within and outside the company.

Physical Demands

  • The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand; walk; use hands to finger, handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms. Must be able to lift to 50lbs. Bending, reaching frequently required.

About Lasko Products

Love Your Air™

Lasko Products is the leading air solutions brand with a reputation for reliable products, peak performance, and perpetual innovation – our commitment to our customers for over a century. Founded in 1906 by Henry Lasko in Philadelphia, Lasko has evolved for over a century to become the global leader in air solution products. From our roots in small appliances, fans, and portable heaters, we’ve grown to become the leading home comfort company while maintaining our unwavering commitment to quality and value. Today, Lasko stands as a symbol of innovation, offering consumers around the world high-performance products; portable fans, heaters, air purifiers, humidifiers, and home ventilation solutions. Our well-known brands, Lasko, B-Air, BlueDri, Air King, and Guardian Technologies, serve both consumer and commercial markets across North America and internationally. As an American company for 120 years, we take pride in upholding the spirit of hard work, trust and accessibility, ensuring that Lasko remains available to all, for generations to come. Headquartered in West Chester, Pennsylvania, with manufacturing and distribution facilities in Tennessee and Texas, Lasko intends to set the standard in the air solutions category for another 100 years.

Lasko’s mission is to provide comfort you can trust.

Our company’s success is based on our culture of GRACE, with five core “Be” values outlining how we live it.

Growth Mindset — Be Bold

  • We are never the finished product ─ every failure is a data point, every setback is a setup.

Recognition — Be Together

  • We win together. We celebrate together! High performance deserves to be seen ─ named, specific, remembered.

Authenticity — Be Real

  • No masks. No politics. Show up as you are, say what you mean, and mean what you say.

Clear Communication — Be Clear

  • Say it plainly. Say it once. Say it to the right person. Clarity is kindness.

Extreme Ownership — Be Accountable

  • No blame. No excuses. Own the win and the loss. No exceptions.

Why Join Lasko?

At Lasko, we believe people do their best work when they’re supported ─ personally and professionally. That’s why we offer flexible hours and a hybrid work schedule for our corporate team, promoting employees to balance life and work in a way that fits their lifestyle. Our dog-friendly corporate headquarters adds a fun, welcoming atmosphere, while our competitive salaries with bonus potential recognize and reward your contributions. We also offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes a strong 401(k) match, wellness incentives, and robust health coverage. Join Lasko and be part of a legacy of innovation – at a company that values flexibility, growth, and a culture where you can thrive.

description:

Help People Make Informed Choices and Access Exceptional Care

You will be trained to deliver:

Safe, evidence-based abortion care
Early medical and surgical procedures
Contraceptive services and counselling
Holistic, person-centred care throughout the client journey

A Career with Purpose

As part of our clinical team, you'll work alongside passionate and experienced colleagues who share a commitment to delivering safe, accessible and exceptional care. You'll be encouraged to develop your skills, contribute your ideas and grow your career in an environment where your wellbeing and professional development genuinely matter.

title: Structural Engineering Intern | Summer 2027
description:
DLR Group is an integrated design firm with a promise to elevate the human experience through design. This fuels the work we do around the world and inspires our mission to improve the lives of our clients, our communities, and our planet. If this sparks your interest, you’re in the right place.

DLR Group’s Los Angeles studio has an opening for a Structural Engineering Summer Intern.

  • Los Angeles, CA

We have multiple positions and locations available; please refer to all openings posted and apply to the locations that are most suitable for your living situation during the course of your internship. This is not a remote position.

About EPX at DLR Group

As an intern at DLR Group, you’ll be part of our Emerging Professional Experience (EPX) Program, designed to give you a meaningful introduction to life within an integrated design firm and a strong foundation for your career in the AEC industry.

Each person at DLR Group has a design voice, and EPX gives you opportunities to develop and share yours. Through hands-on project work, mentorship, and learning experiences, you’ll gain exposure to the people, disciplines, and ideas that shape the built environment. You may participate in design discussions, project meetings, site visits, business development efforts, office activities, and other experiences that broaden your understanding of the design profession.

The program combines three core components: mentorship, project work, and weekly learning sessions. Topics may include design culture, sustainability, design technology, communication, marketing and business development, project and resource management, research, equity, career development, and more. Along the way, you’ll hear from leaders and integrated designers across DLR Group and build connections with fellow emerging professionals.

Position Summary

As a Structural Engineering Intern at DLR Group, you will be an important part of our integrated design team, contributing to the design of structural systems for buildings of various types, sizes, and complexities. Working alongside structural engineers and professionals across architecture, engineering, interiors, and other disciplines, you will gain hands-on experience with the design process from early concepts and system development through documentation and construction administration.

Our Summer Internship Program is a paid, full-time opportunity running May 18 through August 6, 2027, and interns are expected to participate for the duration of the program. This is an opportunity to apply what you’ve learned in the classroom, build your technical and professional skills, and contribute your perspective to design solutions that support our brand promise of Elevating the Human Experience through design.

What you will do

  • Work with a licensed engineer designing structural systems for new construction and/or building renovation projects
  • Attend design team meetings with a structural engineer and observe the coordination that occurs among the team members of a multi-disciplinary design team
  • Assist a structural engineer with the design and development of construction documents primarily using Revit
  • Visit an active construction site (contingent on the status of local construction projects)
  • Coordinate structural design requirements with architecture and other disciplines

Required Qualifications:

  • Completed at least one year at an ABET-accredited Structural Engineering, Civil Engineering, or Architectural Engineering program
  • Experience or interest in BIM (e.g. Autodesk Revit MEP) workflow

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam
  • Interest in architectural building design
  • A third-year student in an accredited engineering program

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future.

Our comprehensive Benefits at DLR Group include medical, dental, vision, disability, wellness programs, flex spending, paid holidays, and paid time off. We also offer a 401(k) plan, employee stock ownership, and bonus opportunities. Compensation considerations are based on location, experience, and skills. The suggested hourly rate for this position is:

Hourly Rate
$20—$26 USD

DLR Group is an integrated design firm delivering architecture, engineering, interiors, planning, and building optimization for new builds, renovations, and adaptive reuse projects.

We are 100% employee-owned: every employee is literally invested in our clients’ success. At the core of our firm are interdisciplinary teams engaged in every step of project lifecycles. Our teams champion true collaboration, open information sharing, shared risk and reward, value-based decision making, and proficient use of technology to deliver exceptional design. We are pursuing the goals of the 2030 Challenge, the ME2040, and the SE2050, and are an initial signatory of the China Accord and the AIA 2030 Commitment.

Through our values – commitment, creativity, environmental stewardship, fun, integrity, ownership, sharing, teamwork – we elevate the human experience through design, together.

DLR Group follows a four-day in-office work model, with employees having the flexibility to work somewhere other than the office on Fridays.

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action/M/F/Veteran/Disabled employer.

title: Systems Administrator
description:
About us:

Thrive delivers upon the promise of technology by enabling our clients’ digital transformation journeys with best practices on an AI, cybersecurity and cloud focused NextGen managed services platform.

Thrive’s culture is powered by diverse talent, big ideas, and a customer-first mindset—and it’s what truly sets us apart. Thrive is built for people who want more than a weekday routine. If you’re hungry to grow, eager to tackle new challenges and ready to drive real impact in a rapidly expanding environment, then welcome to THRIVE!

Position Overview

System Administrators provide remote support across diverse, multi-tenant environments, handling escalated incidents and complex service requests. The role involves advanced troubleshooting, implementing changes, coordinating with other teams, and serving as an escalation point for engineers within the team, while maintaining clear client communication. Thrive seeks technically proficient professionals with strong verbal and written skills, a desire to learn across all aspects of IT, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative environment with broad technical exposure and opportunities for growth.

Responsibilities

  • Communicate with customers via phone, email, and chat in a timely, courteous, empathetic, and professional manner, providing clear updates and case status throughout the resolution process.
  • Perform secondary response and advanced troubleshooting of escalated customer issues, addressing single-user and system-impacting incidents while accurately documenting all actions in Thrive’s tools.
  • Analyze and document unfamiliar client server, workstation, and network environments to determine the fastest and most effective path to incident resolution.
  • Support and troubleshoot diverse computing environments across a wide range of business clients.
  • Perform rapid root-cause analysis of workstation-, server-, and network-level incidents, including complex and escalated issues.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve high-level workstation, server, and network incidents independently, following Thrive’s standard operating procedures and best practices.
  • Utilize appropriate software utilities and vendor- or application-specific tools to achieve timely resolution of customer incidents.
  • Set and manage client expectations throughout the troubleshooting process, providing appropriate updates, next steps, and demonstrating the correct level of urgency.
  • Communicate troubleshooting actions and resolutions clearly, using technical or non-technical language appropriate to the audience.
  • Provide guidance to clients on applications, Thrive best practices, and general infrastructure standards.
  • Develop, document, and help implement client standards based on Thrive best practices; evaluate client environments and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Identify recurring issues and contribute to permanent resolutions through problem management and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Review client environments for security best practices, proactively identifying risks and participating in change management activities.
  • Monitor and manage escalated service tasks, ensuring proper prioritization, documentation, and escalation.
  • Provide escalated support, mentoring, and technical leadership to other engineers, collaborating with team leadership to improve service delivery.

Requirements

  • Provide escalated support, mentoring, and technical leadership to other engineers, collaborating with team leadership to improve service delivery.
  • Experience supporting virtual desktops
  • 3–5 years in IT support/operations, including MSP or multi-tenant experience.
  • Deep experience with Windows Server, Active Directory, Azure AD/Entra, Exchange/M365 admin, Intune, and SharePoint.
  • Competent in networking (Layer 2/3, VLANs, DHCP/DNS, NAT, site-to-site VPNs).
  • Experience with endpoint security (EDR/AV), backup/DR, patch management.
  • Proficient with PowerShell scripting and automation.
  • Strong incident management, change control, and documentation.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, documentation, and time-management skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
  • Availability to work after hours or participate in on-call rotations as required.
  • Excellent customer service skills

Preferred Certifications

  • CompTIA Network+ / A+
  • Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator (AZ-104) or Microsoft 365 Administrator (MS-102)
  • ITIL v4 Foundation (modules)
