title: Director of Implementation
description:
About the role

You will own how every new Curve customer goes from signed contract to live, confident practice. That covers onboarding, go-live, and moving patient, clinical, and other data off legacy systems.

You will lead a team of ~30, report to the Chief Customer Officer, and be accountable for successful launches, time-to-value, data accuracy, customer satisfaction at go-live, and onboarding churn.

This is a builder role. We need someone who can run a high-volume delivery engine today while redesigning the process, tooling, and team structure to scale.

What you'll do

Lead onboarding and go-live

  • Own the end-to-end implementation journey, from sales handoff through kickoff, configuration, go-live, and handoff to Customer Success Management.
  • Set and hit targets for time-to-live, on-time go-lives, and customer satisfaction at go-live.
  • Build repeatable playbooks for single-location practices and phased rollouts for multi-location groups.
  • Be the escalation point for at-risk implementations, and step in personally on the highest-stakes accounts.

Own data conversion and migration

  • Lead the conversion team that moves patient demographics, charts, imaging links, ledgers, insurance, and scheduling data from legacy practice management systems.
  • Set data-accuracy standards, validation steps, and sign-off criteria before any go-live.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering to automate conversion tooling and reduce manual effort per conversion.

Build and lead the team

  • Lead 20–30 people through managers and team leads; hire, coach, and develop the next layer of leaders.
  • Design team structure, roles, and capacity models that scale with bookings.
  • Create a culture of ownership, accuracy, and calm under pressure.

Run the business of implementation

  • Forecast capacity against the sales pipeline and flag constraints early.
  • Report weekly on backlog, cycle time, conversion quality, and implementation cost per customer.
  • Tighten the handoffs with Sales (scoping and expectations), Support, and Customer Success.
  • Feed customer and conversion insight back to Product to improve setup and onboarding in the software itself.

What you bring

Required

  • 8+ years in implementation, professional services, or onboarding for B2B SaaS, with 4+ years leading managers.
  • Experience leading a team of 25+ in a high-volume, deadline-driven delivery model.
  • Hands-on understanding of data migration: mapping, validation, reconciliation, and cutover planning.
  • A track record of cutting time-to-live or improving go-live quality, with numbers to show it.
  • Strong operating rigor: capacity planning, metrics, forecasting, and clear executive reporting.
  • Calm, direct communication with customers, executives, and cross-functional partners.
  • Demonstrated AI chops. We value someone that is using AI in practical ways to improve the customer experience.

Preferred

  • Experience with dental, healthcare, or other practice management software.
  • Experience rolling out software across multi-location groups or DSOs.
  • Experience partnering with Product and Engineering to automate onboarding or conversion tooling.
  • Experience with implementation tools such as Rocketlane, GuideCX, Salesforce, or Jira.

What we offer

  • Competitive base salary, bonus, and benefits
  • Hybrid schedule from our Provo, Utah office.
  • A seat on the customer leadership team and a direct line to the Chief Customer Officer
  • The chance to shape how thousands of dental professionals first experience Curve

title: IT Business Analyst Journey
description:
Description

IT Business Analyst Journey

Full Time | Permanent

Salary Range: $85,800 - $115,416 Annually


This is a telework/hybrid position. The candidate of choice may work from anywhere within the state of Washington with a reliable internet connection. Travel may be required.


Are you passionate about using technology and business analysis to drive meaningful change? The Washington State Department of Corrections (DOC) is seeking highly skilled professionals to serve in the role of IT Business Analyst Journey! As trusted business and technical experts, the candidates of choice will work with the goal of supporting mission-critical enterprise applications, such as D365, that strengthen operations and contribute to public safety.


In this role, you will perform focused analysis of business needs, define requirements, and provide expert consultation to support agency-wide systems and processes. You will facilitate requirements gathering, maintain technical documentation, and participate in the validation and resolution of issues affecting enterprise applications. By evaluating system complexities, dependencies, and interactions, you will help ensure reliable technology solutions that improve business practices and organizational performance.


This position serves as a key liaison between business and technology, requiring deep knowledge of DOC operations and enterprise applications across all divisions and back-office functions. As a technical subject matter expert, you will assess the impact of proposed changes, provide informed recommendations, and support solutions that align with the department’s mission to improve public safety by positively changing lives.


A completed application packet will include:

  • A cover letter regarding your interest in this position with our agency
  • A detailed resume
  • Three professional references

Duties

We are looking for teammates who share our vision of public service and are committed to an equitable and inclusive culture that fosters and inspires excellence, while promoting innovation, engagement, and safety, leading to better outcomes for our incarcerated population, our agency, and our community.

As an IT Business Analyst Journey, some of your duties will include:

  • Performing business and technical requirements definition for mission-critical and highly complex enterprise-wide applications and systems which could look like:
    • Independently facilitating definition and elicitation of business requirements
    • Validating and prioritizing requirements to ensure the business needs are met with the delivered functionality
    • Identifying gaps between functional specifications and the capabilities of the technology.
    • Translating business and functional requirements into user stories.
    • Creating and refining features, user stories and tasks for tracking requirements using Azure DevOps (ADO)
    • Independently meeting with business subject matter experts to clarify and refine requirements
    • Converting requirements into various types of models or diagrams using the Business Analyzing Book of Knowledge (BABOK) techniques and best practices
    • Complying with the standards of the SLDC and follow strategies, plans, and procedures according to industry standards and best practices
    • Collaborating between business stakeholders and agile team to ensure both areas understand complex business processes and rules
    • Explaining IT tools, processes and technologies in terms easily understood by non-technical staff
    • Performing ongoing strategic analysis
  • Providing support for user submitted ticket analysis and resolution while managing system defects and enhancements for DOC/CI and vendor-supported applications to include:
    • Serving as the IT Subject Matter Expert (SME) for technical support to the business users
    • Analyzing and determining the impact of system malfunctions and elicit further information from the user
    • Identifying data corrections required because of a system or user malfunction
    • Independently performing testing on applications
    • Participating with other IT staff in root cause analysis
  • Independently conducting focused analysis and support for mission-critical applications and systems components in D365 and other DOC/CI applications as needed
  • Participating in user acceptance testing (UAT) for mission-critical applications and systems
  • Providing support and training for the implementation and maintenance and operations of the DOC systems.
  • Communicating effectively with DOC system users, technical staff, contractors, and vendors
  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

What we need (required qualifications):

  • Bachelors degree in Computer Science, Business Administration, Public Administration, or closely related field*

And

  • 2 years of professional experience in any of the following areas:
    • Business analysis
    • Eliciting and managing technical and functional requirements
    • Analyzing systems and data
    • Providing customer or technical support for enterprise applications
    • Design documentation
    • User acceptance testing
    • Project management
    • Technical documentation

OR

  • 6 years of experience may be substituted for education in any of the following areas:
    • Business analysis
    • Eliciting and managing technical and functional requirements
    • Analyzing systems and data
    • Providing customer or technical support for enterprise applications
    • Design documentation
    • User acceptance testing
    • Project management
    • Technical documentation
  • Ability to plan and manage time effectively by identifying and handling competing priorities professionally
  • Make effective decisions within short timeframes, taking appropriate action to ensure continued delivery of services
  • Possess strong verbal and written communication skills and be able to bridge the gap between technical and business requirements

*Correctional and/or relevant experience may substitute year for year for post-secondary education


What will make your application stand out (preferred qualifications):

  • Business Analysis Certification and/or experience applying Business Analysis Body of Knowledge (BABOK) techniques
  • Project Management Certification and/or experience applying Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK) techniques
  • Knowledge and experience with software development life cycle (SDLC) and system implementation process, including requirements gathering
  • Knowledge and experience using Azure DevOps (ADO), Easy Vista, Visio, SnagIt, SharePoint, and Microsoft Office Suite Software

Supplemental Information

Vision: Working together for safer communities.

Mission: Improving public safety by positively changing lives.

Our Commitment: To operate a safe and humane corrections system and partner with others to transform lives for a better Washington.


Our Core Values:

  • Cultivate an environment of integrity and trust: Corrections values partnership and trust. We foster openness and support courageous conversations. We are committed to doing what we say we are going to do by being accountable and taking personal ownership in our actions.
  • Respectful and inclusive interactions: Corrections appreciates and values individuals by promoting an inclusive and diverse environment, which encourages safety. We respect, value, and listen to the thoughts, feelings, and perspectives of our stakeholders and consider the impact on those we serve as well as each other.
  • People's safety: Corrections believes in creating an environment that values physical, mental, and emotional security and well-being. We honor those who advance safety for all.
  • Positivity in words and actions: At Corrections, we assume positive intentions and believe there is a shared desire for the best outcome. We consistently demonstrate positive behavior and always put forth our best effort.
  • Supporting people's success: Corrections is committed to our community – understanding individuals, instilling hope, embracing change, and providing opportunities.


DOC is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, creed, color, national origin, sex, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, honorably discharged veteran, veteran status, genetic information, or the presence of any sensory, mental or physical disability or the use of a trained guide dog or service animal by a person with a disability.


IMPORTANT NOTES:

  • DOC complies with the employment eligibility verification requirements for the federal employment eligibility verification form I-9. The selected candidate must be able to provide proof of identity and eligibility to work in the United States consistent with the requirements of that form. https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/form-i-9-acceptable-documents
  • DOC does not use E-Verify; therefore, we are not eligible to extend STEM-Optional Practice Training (OPT). For information, please visit .
  • This recruitment may be utilized to fill more than one position.
  • Please include a minimum of three (3) professional references with your application. A professional reference is defined as an individual who has been paid to supervise your work and can attest to your work performance, technical skills, and job competencies. If you do not have any or sufficient professional references, please include non-related professionals, such as educators or other professional associates.
    **Please note: Phone number AND email address are required for all professional references.
  • A background check including criminal record history will be conducted prior to a new hire. Information from the background check will not necessarily preclude employment but will be considered in determining the applicant’s suitability and competence to perform in the position.
  • Employees may work directly with or near incarcerated individuals in a potentially hazardous setting. Please consider this when deciding whether to apply.
  • We are committed to maintaining a drug and alcohol-free work environment, and our employees are expected to comply with all state and federal laws. A pre-employment drug test may be administered as part of the selection process, and applicants who test positive for any controlled substances, will be disqualified from consideration.
  • Oleoresin Capsicum (OC) is an aerosol pepper spray made available as a means of self-defense and/or de-escalation. Applicants with sensitivities or allergies are encouraged to ask about the level of exposure they could expect in this position.
  • Animal care projects are a common component of most Washington State prisons, including dog and cat programs. Applicants with animal sensitivities or allergies are encouraged to ask about the level of exposure they could expect in this position.
  • Tuberculosis (TB) is a priority health issue for DOC employees. The successful candidate may be required to provide valid proof of a baseline TB skin test within 60 days from the date of hire. When positive tests result, further information, testing and treatment will also be required. Employment is not contingent upon test results.
  • Foreign equivalent degrees awarded outside the United States must have a credential evaluation report attached to your application. You may request the required evaluation/documentation from www.wes.org and www.aice-eval.org. Until this documentation is provided, you will not be selected to move forward in the hiring process.


Telework Details

This position may be allocated for telework. If authorized for the role, work may be performed from your home or another offsite location within the state of Washington using a reliable internet or cellular hotspot service at that time. Employees are expected to perform assigned duties in a safe manner, to take proper care all state-issued equipment, and maintain confidentiality of all information in possession while working offsite. Employees will be required to commute to a Department of Corrections facility or field office as business requires, to potentially include components of the onboarding process. Some offices will have a “drop in” area available, however, a dedicated workspace within a DOC facility will not be provided.


What We Offer:

As an employee of the Department of Corrections, your work-life integration is a priority. Washington State employees are offered one of the most inclusive and competitive benefits packages in the nation. Besides comprehensive family insurance for medical, dental, and vision, these perks also may include:

  • Remote/telework/flexible schedules (depending on position)
  • Up to 25 paid vacation days a year
  • 8 hours of paid sick leave per month
  • 12 paid holidays a year
  • Generous retirement plan
  • Flex Spending Accounts
  • Dependent Care Assistance
  • Deferred Compensation and so much more!

*Teamsters 117 represented positions receive 3 days of bereavement leave.

PERS: State Employees are members of the Washington Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS). New employees have the option of two employer contributed retirement programs. For additional information, check out the Department of Retirement Systems' web site.

For questions about this recruitment, or to request reasonable accommodation in the application process, please email mackenzie.conley@doc1.wa.gov or call us at 509-630-9160. For TTY service, please call the Washington Relay Service at 7-1-1 or 1-800-833-6388.

title: Shopper Insights Senior Client Lead
description:
À propos de dunnhumby

dunnhumby est le leader mondial de la Data Science appliquée aux clients, aidant les enseignes et les marques les plus ambitieuses au monde à placer le client au cœur de chaque décision. Avec près de 3 000 experts répartis en Europe, en Asie, en Afrique et dans les Amériques, nous collaborons avec des entreprises emblématiques telles que Tesco, Coca-Cola, Meijer, Procter & Gamble et Metro afin de transformer les données en croissance, en innovation et en valeur mesurable pour leurs clients.

Leadership Client

Nos équipes Leadership Client constituent le moteur commercial de dunnhumby. Elles développent des partenariats de confiance à long terme qui transforment les données clients en croissance mesurable pour les plus grandes enseignes et marques mondiales. Nous travaillons dans les secteurs de l’alimentation, de la grande distribution et du commerce spécialisé, en transformant les insights en actions concrètes sur des sujets tels que l’assortiment, la tarification, les médias et les promotions.

À propos du poste

Nous nous préparons à un éventuel nouvel engagement client et renforçons nos capacités d’analyse des acheteurs au Canada. Ce poste sera responsable de la livraison des projets et de la gestion des relations auprès des fournisseurs clients ou des catégories qui lui seront confiés, tout en contribuant à définir et à développer des partenariats fondés sur la donnée et les insights. [Ajouter : portefeuille ou périmètre de catégories. Pour Montréal, ajouter l’exigence approuvée concernant la maîtrise du français, le cas échéant.]

Ce que vous ferez

Vous combinerez la gestion des relations clients, la compréhension des enjeux commerciaux et la livraison d’insights afin de créer de la valeur orientée client pour les clients et catégories dont vous serez responsable.

  • Développer et gérer les relations avec les fournisseurs clients attribués ainsi qu’avec les parties prenantes pertinentes du distributeur.
  • Définir et superviser les plans de compte, les priorités de livraison et la gouvernance des activités relevant de votre périmètre.
  • Transformer les analyses en présentations clients claires et en recommandations favorisant des résultats mesurables.
  • Identifier les opportunités de développement commercial, de ventes additionnelles et croisées, et soutenir la croissance du chiffre d’affaires ainsi que les renouvellements de contrats.
  • Accompagner et coacher les collaborateurs plus juniors et contribuer à une stratégie client cohérente et intégrée entre les différentes équipes.

Ce que nous recherchons

Vous apporterez une expérience de gestion de la relation client, un esprit analytique solide et la capacité de transformer les insights en recommandations commerciales concrètes.

  • Expérience dans la gestion de relations avec des fournisseurs ou des entreprises de produits de grande consommation (CPG) dans un environnement orienté retail.
  • Excellentes capacités d’analyse, soutenues par de solides compétences en storytelling et en présentation.
  • Sens commercial développé et expérience dans la création de valeur et la contribution à la croissance.
  • Aisance à influencer les décisions auprès de multiples groupes de parties prenantes.
  • Capacité de coaching ou expérience dans l’accompagnement et le développement d’autres collaborateurs.

Ce que vous pouvez attendre de nous

Nous ne nous contenterons pas de répondre à vos attentes. Nous les dépasserons. Vous bénéficierez ainsi d’un ensemble complet d’avantages digne d’une entreprise technologique de premier plan, mais aussi d’un niveau de flexibilité personnelle auquel vous ne vous attendiez peut-être pas. Vous profiterez également d’avantages pensés avec attention, tels que des horaires de travail flexibles et un jour de congé pour votre anniversaire.

Et nous ne faisons pas que parler de diversité et d’inclusion. Nous les vivons au quotidien grâce à nos réseaux dynamiques tels que dh Gender Equality Network, dh Proud, dh Family, dh One, dh Enabled et dh Thrive. Nous souhaitons que chacun ait la possibilité de révéler tout son potentiel et de donner le meilleur de lui-même tout au long du processus de recrutement. N’hésitez pas à informer votre recruteur des aménagements qui pourraient vous être utiles.

Avantages chez dunnhumby Canada

  • Couverture médicale et dentaire privée par l’intermédiaire de Desjardins.
  • dunnhumby prend en charge 90 % du coût total de la prime et l’employé contribue à hauteur de 10 %.
  • Assurance vie.
  • Assurance décès et mutilation accidentels.
  • Assurance invalidité de courte durée et de longue durée via Desjardins.
  • Allocation en espèces équivalente à 5 % du salaire de base destinée à un régime personnel de retraite ou d’épargne-retraite.
  • 25 jours de congés payés par année, en plus des jours fériés tombant pendant la semaine de travail.
  • Fin de journée anticipée le vendredi.
  • Journées de fidélité (loyalty days).
  • Une journée de congé pour votre anniversaire.
  • Allocation annuelle Santé et Bien-être de 500 $.
  • Accès au dh Wellness Hub.
  • Programme d’aide aux employés comprenant des ressources de soutien et jusqu’à six séances gratuites de consultation professionnelle pour les employés et leur famille.

Notre approche du travail flexible

Chez dunnhumby, nous valorisons et respectons les différences et nous nous engageons à bâtir une culture inclusive en créant un environnement où vous pouvez concilier une carrière réussie avec vos engagements et centres d’intérêt en dehors du travail.

Nous sommes convaincus que vous donnez le meilleur de vous-même lorsque vous bénéficiez d’un bon équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie personnelle. Certains postes se prêtent davantage à des modalités de travail flexibles que d’autres. Si cela est important pour vous, veuillez en discuter avec votre recruteur. Nous sommes ouverts à l’exploration de solutions de travail flexibles tout au long du processus de recrutement.

Pour plus d’informations sur la manière dont nous collectons et utilisons vos renseignements personnels, veuillez consulter notre avis de confidentialité : Avis de confidentialité relatif au recrutement.

About dunnhumby

dunnhumby is the global leader in Customer Data Science, helping the world's most ambitious retailers and brands put the customer at the heart of every decision. With nearly 3,000 experts across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas, we partner with iconic businesses like Tesco, Coca-Cola, Meijer, Procter & Gamble and Metro to turn data into growth, innovation and measurable value for their customers.

Client Leadership

Our Client Leadership teams are dunnhumby's commercial engine - building the long-term, trusted partnerships that turn customer data into measurable growth for the world's biggest retailers and brands. We work across grocery, mass and specialty retail, translating insight into action on everything from ranges and pricing to media and promotions.

About the Role

We are preparing for a potential new client engagement and building shopper-insight capability in Canada. This role will own delivery and relationships across assigned supplier clients or categories, helping shape how insight-led partnerships are established and grown. [Add: portfolio or category scope. For Montreal, add approved French-language requirement if applicable.]

What You'll Be Doing

You will combine relationship ownership, commercial awareness and insight delivery to create customer-first value for assigned clients and categories.

  • Build and own relationships with assigned supplier clients and relevant retailer stakeholders.
  • Set and oversee account plans, delivery priorities and governance for assigned areas.
  • Translate analysis into clear client presentations and recommendations that support measurable change.
  • Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities and support revenue growth and renewals.
  • Coach junior colleagues and contribute to a joined-up client plan across teams.

What We're Looking For

You'll bring client ownership, analytical thinking and the confidence to turn insight into practical commercial recommendations.

  • Experience owning supplier or CPG relationships in a retail-facing environment.
  • Strong analytical thinking supported by clear storytelling and presentation skills.
  • Commercial awareness and experience contributing to value creation and growth.
  • Confidence influencing decisions across multiple stakeholder groups.
  • Coaching capability or experience supporting the development of others.

What You Can Expect From Us

We won't just meet your expectations. We'll defy them. So you'll enjoy the comprehensive rewards package you'd expect from a leading technology company. But also, a degree of personal flexibility you might not expect. Plus, thoughtful perks, like flexible working hours and your birthday off.

And we don't just talk about diversity and inclusion. We live it every day - with thriving networks including dh Gender Equality Network, dh Proud, dh Family, dh One, dh Enabled and dh Thrive as the living proof. We want everyone to have the opportunity to shine and perform at your best throughout our recruitment process - please let your recruiter know what adjustments would help.

Benefits at dunnhumby Canada

  • Healthcare: Private medical and dental coverage through Desjardins. dunnhumby funds 90% of the full premium cost and the employee funds 10%.
  • Protection and retirement: Life insurance, Accidental Death & Dismemberment, Short Term Disability and Long Term Disability through Desjardins, plus a 5% cash allowance of base salary for personal pension or retirement provision.
  • Time off: 25 days holiday per holiday year in addition to public holidays that fall during the working week, Early Friday finishes, loyalty days and a birthday day off.
  • Wellbeing: A $500 annual Health & Wellness allowance, the dh Wellness Hub and an Employee Assistance Program with support resources and up to six free professional counselling sessions for employees and their families.
  • Lifestyle and extras: Long Service Awards and the Talent Scout referral programme. A car allowance is provided to G4+ roles.

Our approach to Flexible Working

At dunnhumby, we value and respect difference and are committed to building an inclusive culture by creating an environment where you can balance a successful career with your commitments and interests outside of work.

We believe that you will do your best at work if you have a work / life balance. Some roles lend themselves to flexible options more than others, so if this is important to you please raise this with your recruiter, as we are open to discussing agile working opportunities during the hiring process.

title: Electrical Engineering Intern | Summer 2027
description:
DLR Group is an integrated design firm with a promise to elevate the human experience through design. This fuels the work we do around the world and inspires our mission to improve the lives of our clients, our communities, and our planet. If this sparks your interest, you’re in the right place.

DLR Group’s Orlando studio has an opening for an Electrical Engineering Summer Intern.

We have multiple positions and locations available; please refer to all openings posted and apply to the locations that are most suitable for your living situation during the course of your internship. This is not a remote position.

About EPX at DLR Group

As an intern at DLR Group, you’ll be part of our Emerging Professional Experience (EPX) Program, designed to give you a meaningful introduction to life within an integrated design firm and a strong foundation for your career in the AEC industry.

Each person at DLR Group has a design voice, and EPX gives you opportunities to develop and share yours. Through hands-on project work, mentorship, and learning experiences, you’ll gain exposure to the people, disciplines, and ideas that shape the built environment. You may participate in design discussions, project meetings, site visits, business development efforts, office activities, and other experiences that broaden your understanding of the design profession.

The program combines three core components: mentorship, project work, and weekly learning sessions. Topics may include design culture, sustainability, design technology, communication, marketing and business development, project and resource management, research, equity, career development, and more. Along the way, you’ll hear from leaders and integrated designers across DLR Group and build connections with fellow emerging professionals.

Position Summary

As an Electrical Engineering Intern at DLR Group, you will be an important part of our integrated design team, contributing to the design of electrical systems for buildings of various types, sizes, and complexities. Working alongside electrical engineers and professionals across architecture, engineering, interiors, and other disciplines, you will gain hands-on experience with the design process from early concepts and system development through documentation and construction administration.

Our Summer Internship Program is a paid, full-time opportunity running May 18 through August 6, 2027, and interns are expected to participate for the duration of the program. This is an opportunity to apply what you’ve learned in the classroom, build your technical and professional skills, and contribute your perspective to design solutions that support our brand promise of Elevating the Human Experience through design.

What you will do

  • Work with a licensed engineer designing electrical systems for new construction and/or building renovation projects
  • Attend design team meetings with an electrical engineer and observe the coordination that occurs among the team members of a multi-disciplinary design team
  • Assist an electrical engineer with the design and development of construction documents primarily using Revit
  • Visit an active construction site (contingent on the status of local construction projects)

Required Qualifications:

  • Completed at least one year at an ABET-accredited Electrical Engineering or Architectural Engineering program
  • Experience or interest in BIM (e.g. Autodesk Revit MEP) workflow

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam
  • Interest in architectural building design

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future.

#LI-

DLR Group is an integrated design firm delivering architecture, engineering, interiors, planning, and building optimization for new builds, renovations, and adaptive reuse projects.

We are 100% employee-owned: every employee is literally invested in our clients’ success. At the core of our firm are interdisciplinary teams engaged in every step of project lifecycles. Our teams champion true collaboration, open information sharing, shared risk and reward, value-based decision making, and proficient use of technology to deliver exceptional design. We are pursuing the goals of the 2030 Challenge, the ME2040, and the SE2050, and are an initial signatory of the China Accord and the AIA 2030 Commitment.

Through our values – commitment, creativity, environmental stewardship, fun, integrity, ownership, sharing, teamwork – we elevate the human experience through design, together.

DLR Group follows a four-day in-office work model, with employees having the flexibility to work somewhere other than the office on Fridays.

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action/M/F/Veteran/Disabled employer.

title: Laboratory Tech (Tuesday through Saturday 2:00 PM to 10:30 PM)
description:
Build What Matters Most—Families, Futures, and Your Career

Luminary Genetics (NextGen Genetics) is a leading provider of advanced genetic testing services for the IVF field. With a state-of-the-art Next Generation Sequencing platform and a committed team of scientists and geneticists, we deliver unparalleled precision to give patients peace of mind about their future family's health.

Opportunity Overview

We have an immediate opening for a Laboratory Tech to join our team at Luminary Genetics in San Jose, California.

  • Schedule: Tuesday through Saturday, from 2:00 PM to 10:30 PM Pacific Time
  • Compensation: $27 per hour (commensurate with experience)

This role provides the opportunity to grow within a nationally respected organization while remaining closely connected to the patients and teams you support every day.

How You’ll Contribute

In this role, the Laboratory Tech will:

  • Assist with sample receiving and specimen verification
  • Perform DNA amplification and NGS testing
  • Analyze NGS data for chromosomal abnormalities and accurately compile patient results into report summaries
  • Maintain laboratory equipment under the supervision of the laboratory manager
  • Complete regular cleaning and stocking of laboratory
  • Adhere to all Standard Operating Procedures in compliance with regulatory requirements and standards for the laboratory
  • Follow quality assurance and quality control programs
  • Observe all laboratory safety policies
  • Troubleshoot protocol and equipment malfunctions under the direction of laboratory manager
  • Handling blood-borne pathogens and general laboratory reagents
  • Additional responsibilities as deemed necessary
  • Be responsible for learning all aspects of PGT-A/PGT-SR testing
  • Sample receiving, amplification, library preparation, sequencing, and reporting
  • This position requires high attention to detail and the ability to accurately follow protocols

What You'll Bring

We’re looking for professionals who bring both technical skill and a deep sense of responsibility to the care experience—individuals who thrive in environments where excellence, empathy, and accountability matter.

Qualifications and Skills Include:

  • Bachelors of Science degree in Biology or relevant field required. Lab degree and/or work experience preferred
  • Minimum 1 year experience in laboratory setting
  • Computer proficiency required
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work as part of a multi-disciplinary team
  • Ability to maintain the highest level of confidentiality
  • Flexibility and willingness to learn at all times
  • Excellent multi-tasking abilities
  • Ability to make timely, accurate, and legible records
  • Ability to follow detailed protocols with a high level of accuracy
  • Ability to perform benchwork 75-100% of the time
  • Ability to adhere to requirements of HIPAA and other ethical standards with respect to patient-specific information
  • Ability to observe the safety practices and protocols common to all laboratory activities and those specific to a genetics laboratory
  • Working knowledge of Office programs (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)
  • Ability to multi-task, be self-motivated, and to work independently to meet deadlines
  • Possession of a high attention to detail, with low technical and clerical error rates

    What We Offer

    We are proud to provide a competitive, comprehensive benefits package designed to support our team members—professionally and personally—across all employment types.

    Full-Time Employees (30+ hours/week)

    • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
    • 401(k) with company match
    • Tuition assistance and professional development support
    • Performance-based bonus opportunities
    • Generous paid time off, paid holidays, and paid parental leave
    • Life and disability benefits
    • Fertility Discount Program
    • Employee wellness and recognition programs

    Part-Time Employees

    • 401(k) with company match
    • Performance-based bonus opportunities
    • Employee wellness and recognition programs

    Per Diem Employees

    • 401(k) with company match
    • Employee wellness and recognition programs

    Our Commitment to Inclusion and Opportunity

    We believe that a diverse workforce is essential to fulfilling our mission of expanding patient access to the highest standards of fertility care. We are committed to equitable and inclusive hiring practices that ensure our clinical and operational teams reflect and support the diverse communities and patients we serve.

title: People & IT Coordinator
description:
Role: People & IT Coordinator

Location: Remote - U.S.

Employment Type: Full-time

About Rhymetec:

Rhymetec is a leading security and compliance MSP helping companies build mature, scalable security programs. We partner with high-growth organizations to deliver services across vCISO, penetration testing, and compliance frameworks including SOC 2, ISO 27001, CMMC, and FedRAMP. We pride ourselves on being customer-centric and execution-focused delivering real outcomes, not just checking compliance boxes.

Role Overview:

We're hiring a People & IT Coordinator to support our HR Manager and Executive Assistant with the day-to-day operational, administrative, and logistical work that keeps a fast-growing remote company running smoothly. This is a hands-on, detail-oriented role covering IT onboarding/offboarding logistics, equipment management, HRIS/ATS data hygiene, and cross-department projects, freeing up senior team members to focus on strategic, high-touch work.

This is a great fit for someone who is highly organized, comfortable juggling multiple systems and stakeholders, and eager to grow their career in Admin and People Operations at a company that's scaling quickly.


Responsibilities:

IT & Equipment Logistics:

  • Manage IT equipment lifecycle logistics for new hires and departing employees: preparing, shipping (FedEx), tracking, and retrieving laptops and equipment
  • Coordinate equipment inventory and storage tracking
  • Support the operational/logistics side of onboarding and offboarding (equipment, system access requests, account setup checklists); onboarding and offboarding conversations remain owned by the HR Manager

HR Systems & Data Administration:

  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date employee data in Greenhouse (ATS)
  • Support the HR Manager and Executive Assistant in data entry and projects across HR systems to ensure accuracy and compliance
  • Assist with intern timecard collection and I-9 documentation collection support when needed
  • Help maintain HR documentation, trackers, and process checklists

General People Ops & Admin Support:

  • Provide administrative support to the HR Manager, Executive Assistant, and CISO as needed



Qualifications:

  • 1-3+ years of experience in HR operations, people operations, administrative support, or a related coordination role
  • Bachelor's degree in human resources, business administration, or a related field
  • Highly organized with strong follow-up habits, comfortable asking questions
  • Experience with an ATS (Greenhouse a plus) and/or PEO platform (Justworks a plus), and strong general comfort learning new systems
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable in a fully remote environment
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent priorities (shipping logistics, resume review, data entry) without dropping details
  • Discretion with confidential employee information
  • Prior experience in a fast-growing startup or tech/cybersecurity environment

Rhymetec offers a robust employee package, including:
Employee covered medical premiums (100%)

  • Dental and Vision Benefits
  • PTO and Sick Time, including 11 paid Holidays
  • 401K retirement option plus company match
  • Company paid Life Insurance
  • Annual Subscription to TalkSpace (online counseling & therapy service) & additional benefits
  • Summer Friday’s!

Rhymetec is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetic, disability, age, or veteran status.

title: Employee Experience Specialist
description:

title: Production Load Builder operator
description:

Other duties as assigned.

Working knowledge of basic math skills.
Good verbal and written communication skills.

title: Manufacturing Scheduler
description:
Come Join the Winning Team!

Carpenter & Paterson, Inc. is currently hiring for a full-time Manufacturing Scheduler/Expediter to work out of our Waggaman, LA location. The Manufacturing Scheduler/Expediter is responsible for planning, scheduling, monitoring, and expediting production activities to ensure customer orders are completed on time and in accordance with company quality standards. This role serves as a key liaison between Production, Engineering, Purchasing, Sales, and Operations to coordinate resources, resolve scheduling conflicts, and remove obstacles that may impact delivery commitments. The ideal candidate will possess strong organizational skills, project management experience, and/or previous leadership experience in a manufacturing environment.

Essential Duties:

Develop and maintain production schedules based on customer requirements, material availability, labor capacity, and equipment utilization.
Monitor workflow and production progress to ensure schedules are achieved and delivery commitments are met.
Expedite materials, components, and work orders throughout the manufacturing process to eliminate delays and bottlenecks.
Coordinate with Purchasing to ensure timely receipt of materials and address supply chain issues impacting production.
Work closely with Production Supervisors and department leaders to balance workloads and optimize manufacturing efficiency.
Provide schedule updates and communicate production priorities to relevant stakeholders.
Analyze production capacity, labor availability, and material requirements when planning schedules.
Identify potential risks to delivery timelines and develop corrective action plans.
Track and report key production metrics, including schedule adherence, lead times, and on-time delivery performance.
Collaborate with Engineering, Quality, and Operations teams to resolve issues affecting production flow.

Ideal Candidate:

Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Engineering, or a related field.
Project management experience coordinating multiple projects, schedules, and deadlines.
Previous leadership, supervisory, or team lead experience in a manufacturing environment.
Experience with lean manufacturing principles and continuous improvement initiatives.

Required

High school diploma or equivalent.

Minimum of 3 years of experience in manufacturing, scheduling, planning, production control, or expediting.

Strong organizational, time management, and problem-solving skills.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.

Experience using ERP/MRP systems.

Days/Shift:

Monday thru Friday 6:00am-2:30pm

What We Offer:

Competitive pay based on experience
Opportunity to grow within a rapidly expanding manufacturing operation
Hands‑on training and certification opportunities
A strong culture of safety, teamwork, and continuous improvement

Benefit Highlights:

Weekly pay
Competitive hourly pay based on previous experience
8 paid holidays plus 2 floating holidays
Paid Time Off
Low affordable rates for Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance as well other benefits such as 401k with company matching (4%), Short-Term Disability, Long-Term Disability and Life Insurance after 60 days
Growth Opportunities

We specialize in the manufacture and distribution of a complete line of pipe hangers and supports for commercial and industrial applications since 1913. With five locations in the U.S and growing., our supports have been specified and installed on major water treatment, pharmaceutical, process piping, petro-chemical, hospitals, and school buildings as well as many other industrial projects throughout the world.

DLR Group is an integrated design firm delivering architecture, engineering, interiors, planning, and building optimization for new builds, renovations, and adaptive reuse projects.

title: Postdoctoral Fellow--Karim Lab
description: Special Instructions to Applicants Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. Applicants should submit a cover letter detailing qualifications and relevant experience, a CV, and contact information for 3 professional references. For inquiries about the position, please contact Dr. Shahid Karim at Shahid.Karim@usm.edu. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without the need for visa sponsorship. The University will not sponsor applicants for work visas (e.g., H-1B). Job Summary The Postdoctoral Fellow conducts scientific research in the Karim Laboratory focused on Alpha-Gal Syndrome (AGS), a tick bite-induced meat allergy of public health significance. This position collaborates with the Principal Investigator and research team to design and conduct research using molecular biology, immunology, and functional genomics approaches to investigate how components of tick saliva contribute to the development of AGS. The Postdoctoral Fellow conducts laboratory experiments, maintains tick colonies, analyzes and documents research data, and contributes to manuscripts, grant applications, and scientific presentations. This is a restricted position with no defined end date. Continued employment is dependent upon project needs, availability of funding, and satisfactory performance. Primary Duties and Responsibilities Collaborates with the Principal Investigator and research team to plan, design, and execute scientific research projects related to Alpha-Gal Syndrome and tick-host interactions. Conducts laboratory experiments using molecular biology, immunology, functional genomics, and other appropriate research methods to investigate tick bite-induced meat allergy. Maintains and manages laboratory tick colonies in accordance with established research protocols and laboratory procedures. Maintains accurate and detailed laboratory notebooks, research data, experimental records, and other required research documentation. Analyzes and interprets research findings and contributes to the preparation of data, figures, and other materials used to communicate research results. Drafts and revises scientific manuscripts, abstracts, reports, and other research materials for publication and dissemination. Prepares and contributes research data and scientific content for extramural grant applications and presents research findings at scientific conferences and other professional meetings. Performs other duties as assigned.

title: Project Manager, Sr. Project Manager or Principal Project Manager
description:
Build What’s Next for Ada County — Join ACHD’s Projects Division

Ready to manage projects that people see, use, and rely on every day? Ada County Highway District (ACHD) is looking for an experienced Project Manager, Senior Project Manager, or Principal Project Manager to join our Projects Division in the Boise area. This is a full-time, exempt position with a starting salary range of $79,872 – $118,560 per year, DOQ. The level at which you are hired will be based on your qualifications and experience.

As a Project Manager at ACHD, you’ll help turn transportation needs into real projects—from early planning and concept development through design, right-of-way acquisition, environmental clearance, and construction. You’ll work with internal teams, consultants, government and community partners, and the public to keep complex projects moving forward.

What You’ll Do:

You’ll manage multiple capital projects at various stages of development, balancing technical requirements, budgets, schedules, stakeholder needs, and public expectations.

Your work may include:

  • Lead projects from concept through construction, keeping scope, schedule, budget, and deliverables on track.
  • Plan and coordinate all phases of capital project development, including scoping, concept development, design, environmental clearances, right-of-way acquisition, and construction.
  • Manage multiple projects at the same time, ranging from routine projects to large, complex, highly visible projects with significant community impact.
  • Manage federally funded transportation infrastructure projects that require extensive coordination with FHWA, ITD and cities.
  • Coordinate environmental assessments and reviews to ensure project compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA).
  • Lead interdisciplinary project teams, bringing people together, communicating expectations, solving problems, and keeping projects moving.
  • Use project management best practices to identify risks, address challenges, and deliver projects within established scope, schedule, and budget.

What We’re Looking For:

We're looking for project professionals who can see the big picture while staying on top of the details. You should be comfortable managing competing priorities, working with a variety of stakeholders, making decisions, and moving projects forward in a fast-paced environment.

Project Manager

You’ll bring knowledge and experience into areas such as:

  • Ability to successfully manage multiple complex projects simultaneously.
  • Civil engineering design and construction practices that meet ACHD, ITD, and FHWA standards and specifications
  • Consultant selection, contract negotiation and administration
  • Right-of-way acquisition and environmental clearances, including coordination of NEPA and water quality permitting
  • Budget development and management
  • Public involvement and stakeholder communication
  • Develop and manage project schedules to ensure timely completion of deliverables
  • Interpret and apply FHWA and ITD policies for project scheduling and cost controls, contract administration, and quality assurance
  • Leading interdisciplinary project teams

Senior Project Manager

In addition to the Project Manager qualifications, the Senior Project Manager role requires:

  • Proven experience managing complex projects, particularly in transportation infrastructure design, right-of-way acquisition, environmental clearances, and public involvement.
  • Experience leading project teams and coordinating multiple disciplines, priorities, and stakeholders.
  • Provide technical guidance and support to Project Managers and Project Assistants, depending on the level of the position.
  • A bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Planning, or a related field is preferred.
  • An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience that provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities may be acceptable.

Principal Project Manager

In addition to the Senior Project Manager qualifications, the Principal Project Manager role requires:

  • 10+ years of related transportation experience and a proven track record of successfully managing complex and challenging projects.
  • A Professional Engineer (PE), American Institute of Certified Planners (AICP), or Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
  • Knowledge and experience in supervisory principles and practices.
  • The ability to develop and deliver clear, concise presentations at formal meetings.
  • The ability to make complex administrative, procedural, and technical decisions while considering a broad range of internal and external factors.
  • A bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Planning, or a related field is preferred.

Why Work for ACHD?

At ACHD your work has a visible impact. The projects you manage can shape how people travel through Ada County for years to come. You’ll help solve transportation challenges, improve infrastructure, and deliver projects that the community uses every day. At ACHD, you’ll work alongside professionals who care about doing meaningful work and keeping Ada County moving.

We offer an amazing benefits package designed to support you:

  • Affordable medical, vision, and dental insurance -- including $0 premiums for employee-only coverage
  • Paid vacation time - accrue up to 4 weeks per year
  • 12 paid holidays
  • Paid parental leave designed to help support you and your family
  • Membership in one of the nation's best pension plans; the Public Employee Retirement System of Idaho (PERSI)
  • 401(k) matching opportunities
  • Tuition reimbursement and professional development to help you continue learning and growing
  • And the opportunity to do work that has a visible impact on the community every day

Ready to Manage Projects That Matter?

If you’re an experienced project manager who enjoys solving complex problems, bringing people together, and seeing projects move from an idea to something the community can use, we’d like to hear from you.

Apply online at by 4:30 p.m., October 16, 2026. Applications will be reviewed periodically, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Applications may be submitted online or are available at 5800 N. Meeker Ave., Boise, ID.

title: Senior Continuous Monitoring Analyst
description:
Tharros supports the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) with cybersecurity services across its Intelligence Enterprise.

In support of this mission, we have an immediate opportunity for a Senior Continuous Monitoring Analyst. In this role you will mature DHS continuous monitoring (ConMon) program toward an advanced Intelligence Community Zero Trust maturity level. You will integrate security tool data into automated dashboards and cyber heat maps, produce IC vulnerability and performance reporting, and brief leadership on enterprise risk posture. This position is on-site in a Government SCIF in Washington, DC.

Duties include but not limited to:

  • Provide continuous monitoring of DHS IE networks, systems, and users using Government-approved tools.
  • Integrate automated data feeds (GRC, Nessus, Axonius, GitLab, Splunk, SCCM) into cyber heat maps and dashboards.
  • Develop and maintain RIVET dashboards and analytics integrated with the GRC tool.
  • Produce and maintain the automated feed for monthly IC Vulnerability Alerts (ICVA) and IC Vulnerability Management (ICVM) reports.
  • Produce the CISO Scorecard and quarterly Cybersecurity Performance Evaluation Model (CPEM) submissions.
  • Conduct weekly POA&M monitoring and track system owner remediation.
  • Identify anomalies in the operational environment and report them to designated personnel.
  • Recommend ConMon improvements and update ConMon SOPs.
  • BS degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Data Science, or Computer Science OR minimum of 10 years' experience in IT or cybersecurity.
  • Minimum of 7 years' experience in vulnerability management or continuous monitoring.
  • Active TS/SCI clearance and U.S. citizenship; willingness to undergo a DHS counterintelligence-scope polygraph.
  • Knowledge of continuous monitoring program requirements under NIST SP 800-137 and RMF.
  • Knowledge of vulnerability management metrics and reporting.
  • Knowledge of Federal or IC security performance reporting (e.g., ICVM/ICVA, CPEM, FISMA ConMon).
  • Skill in using Tenable.sc/ACAS or Nessus.
  • Skill in building dashboards in Splunk or Tableau.
  • Ability to integrate data from multiple security tools into a single view of risk.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite to include Teams or similar workplace chat and videoconferencing tools.
  • Excellent written and oral communications skills.

Desired

  • Knowledge of IC Zero Trust maturity levels.
  • Experience with RSA Archer, Axonius, Tanium, or CyberArk.
  • Proficiency with Python, PowerShell, or Splunk SPL.
  • CISSP, CySA+, GCIA, or Tenable certification.

As a Civil Engineering Intern at DLR Group, you will be an important part of our integrated design team, contributing to the design process of civil building systems from schematics through construction administration, for buildings of various types, sizes, and complexities. Working alongside electrical engineers and professionals across architecture, engineering, interiors, and other disciplines, you will gain hands-on experience with the design process from early concepts and system development through documentation and construction administration.

Our Summer Internship Program is a paid, full-time opportunity running May 18 through August 6, 2027, and interns are expected to participate for the duration of the program. This is an opportunity to apply what you’ve learned in the classroom, build your technical and professional skills, and contribute your perspective to design solutions that support our brand promise of Elevating the Human Experience through design.

What you will do

  • Collaborate with architects and engineers as part of our integrated design process
  • Learn the tools, technology and workflow involved with BIM and how today’s designers deliver successful projects, including creating and coordinating documents using Autodesk’s Civil 3D software
  • Accompany team members on site visits to project sites to see the real-world results of what you do
  • Assist in developing concepts, calculations, modeling, drawing review, and project execution
  • 2D Drafting and 3D Modeling using Autodesk Revit Software
  • Help write and review civil-related specifications
  • Assist team with civil engineering calculations and code research

Required Qualifications:

  • Completed at least one year at an ABET-accredited Civil Engineering program
  • Experience with drafting programs such as Revit
  • Excellent communication, technology, and organizational skills
  • Good multitasking skills to easily switch between projects while keeping track of tasks
  • Ability to work individually as well as in a team environment
  • A desire to learn about the architecture/engineering design process

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Goal oriented with strong skills in problem solving, creativity, and attention to detail
  • Experience and interest in sustainable building design
  • Goal oriented with strong skills in problem solving creativity and attention to detail
  • Experience and interest in sustainable and low-impact site and landscape design
  • An appreciation and understanding of landscape engineering and architectural systems and design and how architects work and think
  • A third-year student in an accredited engineering program

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future.

DLR Group is an integrated design firm delivering architecture, engineering, interiors, planning, and building optimization for new builds, renovations, and adaptive reuse projects.

We are 100% employee-owned: every employee is literally invested in our clients’ success. At the core of our firm are interdisciplinary teams engaged in every step of project lifecycles. Our teams champion true collaboration, open information sharing, shared risk and reward, value-based decision making, and proficient use of technology to deliver exceptional design. We are pursuing the goals of the 2030 Challenge, the ME2040, and the SE2050, and are an initial signatory of the China Accord and the AIA 2030 Commitment.

Through our values – commitment, creativity, environmental stewardship, fun, integrity, ownership, sharing, teamwork – we elevate the human experience through design, together.

title: Mental Health Worker - Cape CBHC CCS (Mon-Fri 3pm-11pm)
description:
Bay Cove Human Services’ mission is to partner with people to overcome challenges and realize personal potential. Bay Cove pursues this mission by providing individualized and compassionate services to people facing the challenges associated with developmental disabilities, mental illness, substance use disorders, and homelessness at more than 175 program sites throughout Greater Boston and Southeastern Massachusetts.
Job Summary: The CCS Mental Health Worker (MHW) provides direct services to adults in crisis at the CCS. The Mental Health Worker will carry a case load based on daily census and will provide direct care supports including admission, treatment planning, running groups, case management, and discharge. The Mental Health Worker ensures safety of all clients through provision of as needed 1:1 supervision, conducting and documenting checks, proactively addressing escalating behaviors. The MHW also provides for operation of the CCS in terms of meal set-up and clean-up; room maintenance; keeping the unit clean; and doing laundry. This is a non-exempt position. The Mental Health Worker supports coordination with the Cape Cod Community Behavioral Health Center (CBHC), helping clients understand available services and supporting warm handoffs and follow-up after crisis stabilization.
Essential Functions of Position:

Completes and documents admissions, treatment plans, client daily documentation, and discharge summaries in accordance with BCHS, DMH and applicable payer and regulatory standards.

Ensure that the unit follows the daily schedule of program activities, client meetings, and groups. Oversight of therapeutic groups as leader, co-leader, and observer.

Ensures for the cleanliness and upkeep of the unit, assists in meal preparation and cleanup, completes bed set up and gathers linens.

Maintains effective working relationships with insurers, DMH, local community resources, and treatment/rehabilitation programs throughout the Cape Cod community.

Participation in daily rounds with multidisciplinary team and follows up on identified issues for the unit and for the individual clients.

Ensures that safety protocols are routinely reviewed and followed consistently by all staff (such as emergency systems; identification and remedy of facility safety hazards; security systems; lock up of sharps and any potential toxins; hazardous waste management; checks protocols, checking vitals protocols, etc).

Support referrals and warm handoffs to Cape Cod CBHC outpatient, urgent, crisis, care coordination, peer, and recovery-support services under the direction of the clinical team.

Complete timely documentation in eHana and communicate information needed for CCS/CBHC admission, discharge, follow-up, and continuity-of-care workflows.

Participate in CCS/CBHC training, team consultation, and quality-improvement activities as assigned.

Performs all other duties and projects as assigned by supervisor.

Requirements for the position:
Schedule/shift: Monday-Friday 3pm-11pm

Full-time, part-time/per-diem schedule for each opening.

Minimally 3 years’ experience working in a mental health setting.

Excellent writing and oral communication skills.

Demonstrated skills in working as an effective team player in a fast-paced unit

Ability to work collaboratively as a member of multi-disciplinary and cross-functional teams.

Demonstrated ability to work in a pressured situation and maintain clarity, focus, judgment, and compassion

Ability to provide leadership

Ability to identify problems and initiate solutions to problems

Ability to work with people in crisis in a hopeful and compassionate manner and model this for others

Ability to work independently

Physical Requirements

Must be able to lift 20 pounds and complete cleaning and laundry

Bay Cove Human Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, national origin, sexual orientation, disability, age, veteran status, or any other groups as protected by Massachusetts or federal law. All qualified candidates, regardless of background, are encouraged to apply.

title: Youth Development Site Lead - Weber - Perry
description:
Earn an Additional $3.00 Per Hour!

The YMCA is currently offering a temporary $3.00 per hour stipend for Youth Development Site Leads working in our Before/After School Programs serving Katy ISD, Conroe ISD, and Humble ISD.

This temporary stipend is separate from base pay and is available only to employees assigned to eligible locations. The stipend may be modified or discontinued based on organizational needs and funding availability.

Join a team that’s shaping the next generation.

At the YMCA, we’re more than an afterschool program provider—we’re a community dedicated to helping young people grow, learn, and thrive. If you’re a motivated leader who is passionate about youth development, safety, and program excellence, this role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while leading a high-quality program that supports children and families every day.

What You’ll Do

As an Afterschool Site Lead, you'll serve as the primary leader for a licensed school-age enrichment program, ensuring children are safe, supported, and engaged every day. You'll coordinate daily program operations, implement the YMCA curriculum, ensure licensing compliance, and build strong relationships with families, school partners, and YMCA staff.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  1. Keep Children Safe: Create and maintain a physically and emotionally safe environment where every child can learn, grow, and thrive. Ensure proper supervision, conduct regular headcounts, monitor activities, maintain attendance records, and respond appropriately to emergencies while following YMCA and state licensing requirements.
  2. Site Management: Serve as the designated Texas Childcare Licensing Site Director, ensuring compliance with all YMCA Houston and state regulations and standards. Oversee the daily operations of the afterschool program, ensuring a safe, nurturing, and stimulating environment for all children. Maintains the program site and equipment, assists with the set-up and breakdown of activity centers and cleaning of the program area.
  3. Supervision and Safety: Ensure the safety and security of all children and staff at the site. Maintain accurate records, including attendance, incident reports, and compliance documentation. Monitor the children’s activities to ensure they engage in safe and age-appropriate behaviors. Monitor site staff adherence to policies and redirect as needed. Conduct regular headcounts and maintain accurate attendance records. Respond appropriately and promptly to emergencies and incidents, following established YMCA policies.
  4. Behavior Management: Implement positive behavior management techniques to promote a respectful and inclusive environment. Address behavioral issues in a calm and constructive manner, following established guidelines.
  5. Program & Policy Compliance: Conduct regular safety drills and inspections to ensure compliance with licensing requirements and organizational policies. Ensure required postings are on display. Follow all organizational policies and procedures, including those related to health and safety, child protection, and confidentiality. Maintain a clean and organized environment, adhering to sanitation and safety standards. Report any concerns or issues to Program Director in a timely manner.
  6. Program Planning and Implementation: Oversee the implementation of age-appropriate activities, including structured and unstructured activities as outlined in YMCA approved curriculum. Encourage and facilitate positive social interactions among children. Adapt activities to meet the diverse needs and interests of all children. Evaluate program effectiveness and make adjustments as necessary.
  7. Parent and Community Engagement: Communicate regularly with parents regarding their child’s progress, behavior, and any concerns. Address parent inquiries and concerns promptly and professionally. Follow all organizational policies and procedures, including those related to health and safety, child protection, and confidentiality. Maintain a clean and organized environment, adhering to sanitation and safety standards. Report any concerns or issues to Program Director in a timely manner
  8. Administrative Duties: Maintain accurate enrollment and attendance records, including sign-in sheets and daily rosters.
  9. Program Growth and Retention: Develop and implement strategies to promote program growth and increase enrollment. Create and execute retention plans to ensure high levels of participant satisfaction and continuity. Monitor and analyze enrollment trends and feedback to identify areas for improvement and opportunities for expansion.
  10. Program Quality: Plan and implements lesson/activity plans curriculum that includes both formal and informal play within the center and outdoors in adherence to Y program model, curriculum and quality standards.
  11. Program Evaluation: Lead Youth Program Quality (YPQ) intervention process. Use continuous program monitors to evaluate youth participation and the effectiveness of program and makes adjustments to program as needed.
  12. Child Abuse Prevention: Reports suspicious and inappropriate behaviors and policy violations. Follows mandated abuse and incident reporting requirements. Ensures youth are properly signed in and signed out, ensures only authorized adults are allowed in the facility, etc. Adheres to policies related to boundaries with each child. Ensures unused rooms and closets remain locked; routinely monitors high-risk locations (bathrooms), etc.

QUALIFICATIONS

  1. At least 21 years of age.
  2. High school diploma or general education degree (GED). Minimum of 70 clock hours of training in child or youth development, recreational leadership or management. Two (2) college courses are equivalent to 100 clock hours. Minimum Standard #744.1017.
  3. At least one year of experience working with youth in a licensed childcare facility, school, church, or similar setting
  4. CPR, First Aid, AED, and Child Abuse Prevention certifications (or ability to obtain)
  5. Ability to plan, organize, and implement age-appropriate activities and programming
  6. Experience working with diverse populations
  7. Ability to pass state and local background checks and FBI fingerprinting requirements
  8. Current TB test and any required health screenings or immunizations per state and local regulations

Physical & Work Environment Expectations

This is an active leadership role that requires regular movement throughout the program site. You may be required to stand, walk, bend, kneel, reach, and participate in indoor and outdoor activities. The ability to lift up to 50 lbs occasionally is required. Work environments include classrooms, cafeterias, playgrounds, gymnasiums, and outdoor recreation spaces, with exposure to varying weather conditions, moderate noise levels, and active youth programming.

During camp seasons, Afterschool Site Leads may transition into Youth Development Counselor responsibilities and participate in outdoor activities such as hiking, swimming, field trips, and extended periods of standing and walking.

Typical Schedule

Before/After School Program: Part-time, Monday–Friday, typically 6:30 am–8:30 am and/or 2:30 pm–6:30 pm (aligned with the ISD calendar). Occasional Saturdays may be required.

Camp Program: Monday–Friday, operating between 6:30 am–6:30 pm with multiple shift options (aligned with school district breaks). Occasional Saturdays may be required.

Participation in family nights, staff meetings, trainings, and program events is required with advance notice.

Why the YMCA

When you join the YMCA, you join a mission-driven organization that values leadership, service, and community impact. As an Afterschool Site Lead, you'll play a critical role in creating safe, high-quality youth experiences, fostering meaningful relationships with families, and ensuring your program site operates successfully each day. If you're ready to lead with purpose and help children thrive, we encourage you to apply.

Benefits of Working at the YMCA

  • Free YMCA Membership
  • Discounts on YMCA programs
  • Paid training and professional development opportunities
  • Leadership growth pathways within youth development and YMCA operations
  • A supportive, mission-driven team environment
  • Flexible scheduling opportunities
  • Opportunities to make a lasting impact on the community and families

The YMCA of Greater Houston provides Equal Employment Opportunities for employment to all employees and applicants, including disability and protected veteran status.

title: Major League or AAA Strategy Associate
description:

title: Distribution Engineer
description:
We have an opening for a Distribution Engineer in our Burnaby office.

Responsibilities:

Technical review of electric utility distribution design packages, including drawings, material take-offs, and calculations.
Sealing of electric utility distribution design drawings.
Technical mentorship of engineers and technologists.
Electrical and civil design of underground and overhead electric utility infrastructure.
Material take-offs and project estimating.
Voltage drop and transformer loading calculations.
Cable pull calculations using Pull Planner.

P.Eng. or P.L.Eng. designation through EGBC.
Minimum of 2 years of experience in the design of electrical utility distribution projects.
Class 5 driver’s license.
