Demonstrated self-motivation and drive for improvement.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to develop business relationships conducted in a professional manner.
Proven ability to prioritize and manage multiple competing responsibilities concurrently.
Strong attention to detail, problem-solving, and analytical skills.

title: L&I Administrative Regulations Analyst 4
description:
Description


Our Mission: Keep Washington Safe and Working!
Our Values: Customer Focus, One L&I, Respect, Diversity, Equity and Inclusion, Learning and Growth, Reliability


Please Note: This opportunity and is open to current Labor & Industries
employees only. If you apply and are not a current employee, you will not be considered.

This recruitment is for a project position that is expected to last until June 2028.


Job Highlights

Are you looking for an opportunity to take your experience in analysis, research, evaluating for compliance, and rule writing to the next level? Do you want to work on a positive, goal-oriented team and focus on implementing new legislation to help injured workers access medical services? If so, check out this opportunity and consider joining our team as an Administrative Regulations Analyst 4 (ARA 4).


This position is in the Insurance Services Division, Health Services Analysis (HSA), Payment Policy and Provider Support (PPPS) section and is intended to support implementation of legislation in E2SSB5847 concerning access to medical care. In this role you will coordinate with staff across Insurance Services to lead the rulemaking activities and implement Washington Administrative Code (WAC) changes required by the passing of E2SSB5847.


Why Work for us:

The Department of Labor & Industries (L&I) is a diverse state agency dedicated to the safety, health, and security of Washington's workers. We help employers meet safety and health standards and inspect workplaces when alerted to hazards. As administrators of the state's workers' compensation system, we are similar to a large insurance company providing medical and limited wage-replacement coverage to workers who suffer job-related injuries and illness. Our rules and enforcement programs help ensure workers are paid what they are owed, that children and teens' work hours are limited, and that consumers are protected from unsound business practices.


Insurance Services is the largest division within the agency and administers one of the premier workers’ compensation organizations in the nation serving over 3.8 million employees working for 260,000 employers.


The Insurance Services Health Services Analysis program is comprised of various work units with a shared vision to achieve provider excellence to reduce work disability by ensuring worker access to high-quality care.


Here is what we are looking for:


  • Demonstrated ability to research, review, analyze and interpret proposed and existing rules and laws to advise and provide consultation to leadership.
  • Demonstrated ability in rule writing and understanding of the rule-making process.
  • Project management skills to ensure work progresses toward the achievement of goals and objectives.
  • Ability to effectively communicate complex information clearly and succinctly in a way that is easy to understand for a variety of audiences both orally and in written format.
  • Experience creating and presenting information using a variety of Microsoft applications.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate and build rapport with others to contribute to team cohesion and respectful working relationships.

Duties

Some of what you will do:


  • Lead rulemaking and rule writing related to implementation of E2SSB5847.
  • Promulgate rules adhering to the standard rulemaking process within the requirements and timelines of the Administrative Procedures Act.
  • Research and analyze proposed and existing rules and laws to determine how they may affect the implementation of E2SSB5847.
  • Interpret existing rules related to statutory and program administrative provisions and advise leadership on compliance.
  • Ensure rulemaking related to E2SSB5847 conforms to the necessary timelines and program goals.
  • Lead the work of cross functional teams as they review and assess potential impacts of implementing rulemaking related to E2SSB5847.
  • Act as subject matter expert and primary point of contact during the legislative session for questions related to bills that may affect the implementation of E2SSB5847.
  • And much more!

Qualifications

Required:

  • A Master’s degree involving major study in public or business administration, journalism, communications, writing, English, or closely allied field
    AND
    One (1) year of professional, or supervisory, or consultative experience writing or evaluating for compliance with departmental standards and legal requirements.

OR

  • A Bachelor’s degree involving major study in public or business administration, journalism, communications, writing, English, or closely allied field
    AND
    Three (3) years of professional, or supervisory, or consultative experience writing or evaluating for compliance with departmental standards and legal requirements.

OR

  • A total of seven years of professional, supervisory, or consultative experience in writing or evaluating for compliance with departmental standards and legal requirements may substitute for education.

AND

  • The ability to take action to learn and grow.
  • The ability to take action to meet the needs of others.

Desired:


  • In-depth knowledge of Title 51 and Chapter 296-20 WAC through Chapter 296-23B.
  • WAC writing and modification, especially as it applies to the L&I’s Medical Provider Network or other provider rules.
  • Legislative bill analysis related to medical providers.
  • Effective collaboration and ability to build strong working relationships with partners across Insurance Services.

Supplemental Information

Things You Need To Know


At L&I, your voice matters. L&I is a diverse state agency dedicated to the safety, health and security of Washington's 3.3 million workers. Watch this brief video and learn more about why L&I is an employer of choice.


L&I provides a modern work environment and excellent benefits including paid leave, tuition reimbursement, Infants at Work Program and a generous retirement package for qualified employees at the end of their career. Click on the “Benefits” tab to learn more.


We value our employees and their work-life balance. We support a hybrid work model and offer flexible custom work schedules. This position is eligible for a flexible schedule (4/10’s, 9/80’s, 5/8’s, etc.) upon approval by management.


For this position, you can expect to telework up to full time with the expectation of working from the office at least once a month to attend in-person meetings and training, or upon business need. The assigned duty station for this position is Tumwater, Washington.


Application process

To be considered for this opportunity, you must submit a complete online application including detailed work history and professional references with current phone numbers.

Please include the following documents with your application:


  1. A cover letter describing your specific qualifications.
  2. A current resume detailing your applicable experience and education

We will contact the top candidates directly to advance in the selection process. Because we base the selection on the information you provide, please ensure your application clearly demonstrates how your experience relates to the qualifications and responsibilities described in this announcement.


Applications with incomplete work history, references to a resume in place of detailed work experience, or missing attachments may be considered incomplete and not considered for further review.


Please do not attach or place any medical information within the application, resume, or cover letter. If you do, we will have to reject your application to safeguard others from receiving your confidential information. You will have to remove the confidential information before you can apply again.


To learn more about our hiring process timeline at L&I please visit our L&I recruiting page at Hiring Process at L&I. If you would like to read our website in a language other than English, scroll up to the top of the page to select your language of choice from the banner.


Background Check Notice


Prior to placement in this position, a background check, including criminal history records will be conducted. Information from your background check will not necessarily preclude employment but will be considered in determining your eligibility to perform the requirements of the position.


Other information


  • For positions requiring travel, you must have a valid unrestricted driver's license and have insurance if driving a privately owned vehicle on state business.
  • This position is represented by the Washington Federation of State Employees (WFSE).
  • Candidates who are offered a job with L&I must possess work authorization that does not require sponsorship by the employer for a visa now or in the future.
  • The Department of Labor & Industries complies with the employment eligibility verification requirements of the federal employment eligibility verification form, I-9. The selected candidate must be able to provide proof of identity and eligibility to work in the United States consistent with the requirements of that form on the first day of employment.
  • Please note: L&I may use this announcement to fill multiple permanent and/or non-permanent positions.

Did You Know?


Washington is America's Top State to live, play, and work, according to U.S. News (2021). Join the L&I team and enjoy all the Evergreen State has to offer.


Veterans Preference

Applicants wishing to claim Veterans Preference should attach to their application a copy of their DD-214 (Member 4 copy), NGB 22, or signed verification of service letter from the United States Department of Veterans Affairs. Please blackout any personally identifiable data such as Social Security numbers. For further information, contact L&I’s Jobs@lni.wa.gov.

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Employer

L&I employees come from all walks of life. We strive to hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

We believe in the importance of recognizing the value each of us contributes to the success of the agency mission. Having a diverse workforce is this agency’s greatest source of strength and knowledge. It is through the combination of talents and abilities that we can pursue finding effective measures to provide the best customer service. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace for everyone and we strongly mean everyone.

The State of Washington is an equal opportunity employer. Persons with a disability who need an accommodation in the application process or testing process, or those needing this announcement in an alternative format, may call 360-902-5700. TTY users should first call 711 to access the Washington Relay Service.

You are welcome to include the name and pronoun you would like to be referred to in your materials, and we will honor this as you interact with our award-winning diverse and inclusive organization.

For more Information

If you have any questions regarding this job posting, program, or the agency, please contact Angela Laramie at hrbtu@lni.wa.gov.

title: Quality Technician I - 1st Shift
description:
Job Summary:
The Quality Tech is responsible for ensuring that all elements of food safety within the Quality Monitoring Scheme are being met. Ensures that all regulatory, customer, and company quality initiatives are being met and maintained.

Job Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Perform Quality checks on production lines in a timely and accurate fashion every hour per line. (Will frequently be responsible for 3 lines at any given time).
  • Brings discrepancies with the QMS to the attention of Supervisor or Quality Manager. These discrepancies are but not limited to HACCP programs, Allergen programs, Sanitation procedures, GMP findings, Foreign Material findings, and HOLD procedures.
  • Ensure that product being produced meets all legal and customer requirements as outlined in the Bluebook for each product.
  • Complete paperwork in a timely and accurate fashion each day.
  • Perform required tasks to maintain 5-S and keep work areas clean.
  • Keep all information pertaining to our operations (products, customers, production details, etc.) confidential.
  • Maintain instrumentation and equipment in good condition and store appropriately.
  • Label, store, and organize samples and product retentions.
  • Follow Hold Procedures for all non-conforming materials or product.

  • Perform other audits or inspections as required.

title: Associate Scientist Research Laboratory Operations
description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

Revolution Medicines is seeking an individual with a strong background in rodent laboratory animal research. The position will receive study designs from scientists and independently execute in vivo pharmacology studies in mice, while demonstrating excellent communication and coordination across teams. In addition, this role will support vivarium management, including management of weekend staff to ensure uninterrupted in vivo operations during weekends and holidays.

  • Plan, conduct, analyze, and report in vivo studies (efficacy, PK/PD).

  • Carry out pre-clinical model development and characterization.

  • Manage and supervise multiple research associates.

  • Conduct standard vivarium operations-managing inventory/supplies, maintain laboratory equipment, and record keeping.

  • Contribute to continuous improvement of current SOPS and ensure that the appropriate SOPs are followed by all Vivarium users.

  • Support adherence to animal welfare guidelines and regulations.

  • Learn and conduct other in vivo related techniques.

  • Train junior team members on in vivo techniques.

  • Interface with cross-functional project team members, and participation in and presentation at project team meetings and cross-departmental team meetings.

  • Formulate and administer drugs and experimental compounds by various routes.

  • Troubleshooting issues with the facility, animal welfare, or executing in vivo.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

  • BS or MS in Biology or Pharmacology related discipline (or 5 - 8 years of relevant experience).

  • Proficiency with various mouse handling techniques including dosing (IV, PO, SC, IP), tumor inoculation/measurements, in life and terminal blood collection, survival surgeries, and handling of tissues during necropsy and processing for ex vivo analysis.

  • Computer literacy, especially proficiency with GraphPad Prism, Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.

  • Research experience with mouse models of cancer and/or cancer immunotherapy.

  • Excellent organizational and communication skills, along with the ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team environment.

  • The ability to work independently on day-to-day responsibilities and research goals.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience with Studylog, Prism, and Benchling.

  • Rodent Surgical Experience.

  • Sterile tissue culture.

  • Familiarity with sample collection for IHC and cellular biology assays such as: FACS, western blot, and qPCR.

title: Information System Security Officer
description:
Tharros supports the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) with cybersecurity services across its Intelligence Enterprise.

In support of this mission, we have an immediate opportunity for an Information System Security Officer (ISSO). In this role you will independently own the security posture of a portfolio of DHS Intelligence Enterprise systems, including Cross Domain Solutions and cloud-hosted systems, in accordance with ICD 503 and DHS 4300C. You will maintain ATO packages, manage POA&Ms and change control, and serve as a SCIF Information Security Compliance Representative (ISCR). This position is on-site in a Government SCIF in Washington, DC.

Duties include but not limited to:

  • Create and maintain ATO packages for assigned systems in the GRC tool and monitor their compliance.
  • Perform self-assessments of assigned on-premise and cloud systems against the A&A SOP.
  • Manage POA&Ms, waivers, and risk exceptions; provide weekly or bi-weekly activity reports.
  • Perform audit log reviews at least weekly, respond to NOSC alerts, and ensure periodic scanning.
  • Coordinate system changes through IATT requests and serve on the Configuration Management Board when designated.
  • Facilitate annual contingency plan tests and submit quarterly CPEM reporting.
  • Deliver ISSO reports (incident response, POA&M, ConMon metrics) to ISSMs and system owners.
  • Serve as SCIF ISCR and mentor junior ISSOs.
  • BS degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Information Systems, or Computer Science OR minimum of 6 years' experience in IT or cybersecurity.
  • Minimum of 3 years' experience as an ISSO or in RMF package ownership.
  • Active TS/SCI clearance and U.S. citizenship; willingness to undergo a DHS counterintelligence-scope polygraph.
  • Knowledge of the Risk Management Framework (RMF), NIST SP 800-37, NIST SP 800-53, and ICD 503.
  • Knowledge of Cross Domain Solution engineering and governance, including NCDSMO mandates and Raise the Bar requirements.
  • Knowledge of hybrid classified/unclassified, on-premise and cloud environments, DevSecOps, and agile methodologies.
  • Skill in securing Linux and Windows operating systems and cloud technologies.
  • Skill in managing change control and authorization impacts.
  • Ability to independently manage a portfolio of systems.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite to include Teams or similar workplace chat and videoconferencing tools.
  • Excellent written and oral communications skills.

Desired

  • CGRC (formerly CAP), CompTIA Security+, or CySA+ certification.
  • Experience with RSA Archer, eMASS, or a similar GRC tool.

title: Sr. Project Manager (Federal Construction/MEP Focus)
description:
Seneca Federal Solutions is part of the Seneca Nation Group (SNG) portfolio of companies. SNG is Seneca Holdings’ federal government contracting business that meets mission-critical needs of federal civilian, defense, and intelligence community customers. Our portfolio comprises multiple subsidiaries that participate in the Small Business Administration 8(a) program. To learn more about SNG, visit the website and follow us on LinkedIn.

Our team of talented individuals is what makes us successful. To support our team, we provide a balanced mix of benefits and programs. Your total rewards package includes competitive pay, benefits, and perks, flexible work-life balance, professional development opportunities, and performance and recognition programs. We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life, and disability, voluntary benefit programs (critical illness, hospital, and accident), health savings and flexible spending accounts, and retirement 401K plan. One of our fundamental principles is to offer competitive health and welfare benefits to our team members, providing coverage and care for you and your family. Full-time employees working at least 30 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in our benefits and paid leave programs. We pride ourselves on our collaborative work environment and culture, which embraces our mission of providing financial and non-financial benefits back to the members of the Seneca Nation.

Seneca Federal Solutions, a Seneca Nation Group (SNG) company, is seeking a Senior Project Manager to deliver high‑value technical and building-envelope work at federal facilities and government agencies, such as the Department of Defense, Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), and Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC).

This role is 100% remote with approximately 30% travel to job sites to conduct site visits for inspections, installation and start-up activities, lead client meetings, and to assess project progress and compliance. The ideal candidate will reside in an area with convenient access to a major airport. Additionally, access to federal worksites is required for this role. As such, candidates must meet eligibility requirements and successfully pass associated background checks.

Responsibilities include but not limited to:

  • Manage medium to large, full-lifecycle turnkey projects, reporting financials, controlling budgets, streamlining operational functions, and resolving project issues, while meeting stringent deadlines
  • Project Management tasks to include proposal development, management of resources, project budgets and forecasting, and schedule management throughout to project closure
  • Develop and manage a detailed traditional project schedule and work plan

  • Provide project presentations to various stakeholders about strategy, adjustments, and estimates to complete
  • Create and maintain strong federal customer relationships

    • Project Engineers, Assistant Project Managers

Basic Qualifications:

  • Seven to Ten years of project management experience overseeing full lifecycle of medium to large complex multi-year projects within the Federal building-envelope space.
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Construction Management from an ABET-accredited program
  • Safety, Health and Environmental (SHE) Management experience.
  • Advanced proficiency in MS Project and/or Primavera P6.
  • Experience and understanding of commercial/industrial infrastructure design, engineering, manufacturing, and construction processes.
  • Knowledge and experience managing Electrical, Mechanical, and building-envelope construction projects.
  • Strong understanding of construction safety.
  • Valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record.
  • Ability to pass background investigations, drug screening, and site-access requirements.
  • Ability to travel and work at federal, military, correctional, industrial, and other controlled-access facilities.
  • Ability to communicate professionally with government officials, commercial customers, subcontractors, field personnel, and executive management.
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects in geographically dispersed locations.

Desired Skills:

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification / Certified Construction Manager (CCM) / Certified Professional Constructor (CPC)
  • Demonstrated experience managing interior building construction projects including Electrical, Fire Suppression, and HVAC.
  • Civil infrastructure experience for underground utilities and structural foundations.
  • Mechanical infrastructure experience with building construction for water/wastewater utilities.
  • Power infrastructure experience with backup generators and/or micorgrids.
  • Experience managing building-envelope projects including repairs, restorations, and roof replacements.
  • OSHA 30-Hour Construction certification.
  • Experience managing projects requiring bonding, security clearances, Buy American compliance, or domestic material sourcing.
  • Convenient access to a major airport to accommodate travel

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to visit active construction sites and access rooftop work areas.
  • Ability to climb ladders and stairs and navigate uneven or elevated surfaces.
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, and inspect work for extended periods.
  • Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
  • Ability to wear required personal protective equipment and fall-protection equipment.
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds when necessary.
  • Ability to travel by automobile and commercial aircraft.

title: Senior Manager, Data Analytics and Revenue Forecasting
description:
WHO WE ARE

Zeta Global (NYSE: ZETA) is the AI-Powered Marketing Cloud that leverages advanced artificial intelligence (AI) and trillions of consumer signals to make it easier for marketers to acquire, grow, and retain customers more efficiently. Through the Zeta Marketing Platform (ZMP), our vision is to make sophisticated marketing simple by unifying identity, intelligence, and omnichannel activation into a single platform – powered by one of the industry’s largest proprietary databases and AI. Our enterprise customers across multiple verticals are empowered to personalize experiences with consumers at an individual level across every channel, delivering better results for marketing programs. Zeta was founded in 2007 by David A. Steinberg and John Sculley and is headquartered in New York City with offices around the world. To learn more, go to .

The Role

Zeta is seeking a Senior Manager, Data Analytics and Revenue Forecasting to lead the Finance-owned view of Programmatic revenue, gross profit, and performance. This role will turn complex commercial and financial data into a clear forward-looking forecast, actionable pacing insights, and executive-ready recommendations. The role is a core business partner to Programmatic leadership and will help strengthen planning discipline as the business scales.

This is a hybrid role based out of our NYC office.

What you will do

· Own the Finance revenue and gross-profit forecast for Programmatic, including the weekly and monthly outlook, forecast assumptions, risks, and opportunities.

· Build and maintain a forecast architecture that connects historical performance, daily pacing, advertiser and agency trends, pipeline, churn, seasonality, and other commercial drivers to a dependable Finance point of view.

· Lead P&L forecasting, variance analysis, gross-margin and COGS analysis.

· Create timely daily and weekly performance views that identify variance drivers early and translate them into clear actions for Finance and business leaders.

· Develop executive materials and narratives for Programmatic leaders, including performance readouts, forecast updates, and decision support.

· Partner with Commercial Finance on quarterly revenue-target modeling.

· Advance automation and data reliability across Snowflake, Adaptive Planning, Workday, and reporting tools, reducing manual effort and increasing confidence in performance and forecast reporting.

· Establish strong controls and documentation around forecast inputs, reporting logic, and recurring data-quality checks.

What you will bring

· 7+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, data analytics, revenue forecasting, business analytics, or strategic finance; experience supporting a high-growth, data-rich commercial business is strongly preferred.

· Demonstrated ownership of a revenue, gross-profit, or P&L forecast and the ability to explain performance drivers, risks, and tradeoffs to senior leaders.

· Strong analytical and financial-modeling skills, including comfort working with large and imperfect data sets and turning analysis into a point of view.

· Experience with planning, financial-reporting, and data tools such as Adaptive Planning, Workday, Snowflake, SQL, Tableau, Power BI, or similar platforms.

· Excellent executive communication skills. You can make a clear recommendation, explain the underlying evidence, and tailor the message for a senior business audience.

· A collaborative operating style with the judgment to challenge assumptions constructively and work across Finance, Sales, Operations, and data teams.

BENEFITS & PERKS

  • Unlimited PTO
  • Excellent medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Employee Equity
  • Employee Discounts, Virtual Wellness Classes, and Pet Insurance And more!!

SALARY RANGE

The salary range for this role is $170,000 - $180,000, depending on location and experience.

Zeta considers applicants for employment without regard to, and does not discriminate on the basis of an individual’s sex, race, color, religion, age, disability, status as a veteran, or national or ethnic origin; nor does Zeta discriminate on the basis of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression.

description:
Department Information

Description of Job

About the Division of Behavioral Health Administration (BHA)
This position is located within the fiscal division of the Behavioral Health Administration (BHA). Located within the Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS), BHA is responsible for policy development, service provision and coordination, program monitoring and evaluation, and administrative oversight of the public behavioral health system. BHA funds, supports, and monitors numerous community behavioral health programs and providers, reviews and designates the State’s 27-65 providers, and licenses substance use disorder service providers. BHA executes the State’s federal responsibilities as the State Mental Health Authority and the State Substance Abuse Authority for the purposes of administering federal mental health and substance abuse block grant funds. This position, housed within the fiscal division of BHA, will be responsible for overseeing the fiscal data reporting requirements for block grants, as well as the development and maintenance of Tableau and ad-hoc reports based upon the BHA financial reporting needs.

Summary of the Position:
BHA needs advanced technical assistance to modernize and improve legacy fiscal and program management processes, as well as ongoing maintenance and support of these resources once established. This position possesses a unique level of expertise that is critical to maintaining compliance with federal regulations and reporting requirements and advising leadership on critical financial decisions. This position serves as the financial data manager and acts as the subject matter expert regarding reporting and data visualization for the fiscal division of BHA. Duties include developing, implementing, and/or modernizing standard visualization tools for all audiences across BHA, with an emphasis on fiscal data components. This position works independently as a dedicated fully operational financial data analytics, visualization, and data management expert. This position advises leadership regarding financial decisions and creates/maintains best practices in data management, data integrity, and data visualization. This position works independently to develop and implement guidelines to maintain the agency’s mission while using judgment and resourcefulness to direct the implementation of statewide processes for data collection, reporting, analysis, and tracking.

Job Description:
General Financial Data Collection, Analysis, and Process Development:
Oversee and implement financial data tracking, reporting, and visualization primarily using Tableau and the state’s CORE accounting system. Implement and oversee data collection processes and analysis. Determine the appropriate data analysis methods to employ. Determine appropriate methodology for data collection, tracking, and monitoring based on reporting requirements for multiple funding sources, legislative requirements, and division objectives. Advise financial and agency-wide leadership regarding financial considerations essential to agency operations.
  • Implements and documents processes for data collection, reporting, and analysis in alignment with division and regulatory needs.
  • Uses incoming data from financial systems (CORE) to create user-friendly, accessible performance measurement dashboards and other data visualization products.
  • Collaborates with department staff and leadership to gather information and reporting requirements.
Data Collection, Analysis and Reporting:
Design, coordinate, and implement processes to complete the fiscal aspects of the annual mental health and substance use block grant application and reporting processes. Support the execution of these efforts to determine the most effective and accurate practices, as well as develop sustainable and repeatable processes with thorough documentation followed by ongoing support and maintenance of these established processes. Directly influence and inform leadership decisions regarding block grant reporting and monitoring, coordinating a statewide approach to essential data collection and analysis.

As a fiscal team member, this position may be utilized to assist the accounting, procurement, grants, program, or leadership teams as well as other budget positions as workload dictates.

Other Duties as Assigned

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment & Appeal Rights

Minimum Qualifications:

Option 1 - Experience Only:

title: Senior Product Manager - Developer Productivity
description:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

Role Overview

AI is rapidly changing how software is designed, built, tested, reviewed, deployed, and operated — and the industry playbook is being rewritten monthly. Okta's Developer Productivity and AI Enablement Engineering teams own building and operating the capabilities that make our engineers fast across the inner and outer development loops. This role is the product counterpart, embedded full-time with that organization, that makes those investments compound by uncovering and prioritizing frictions, bringing the outside in, driving standardize-vs-federate decisions, spreading what works across teams, funding and clearing the path for the best tools, and proving the value.

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own developer productivity as a product across Okta's development lifecycle — AI-native and traditional tooling alike. You will start bottom-up: interviewing engineers, managers, tech leads, and architects; mapping current inner- and outer-loop tooling and the frictions; and baselining dev-cycle metrics. From there, you will own the roadmap with engineering leadership; benchmark how the best engineering organizations build with AI; define tooling requirements and/or run the tooling evaluations engineering needs in a landscape that changes monthly; find the teams inside Okta getting outsized results and turn their patterns into playbooks; lead build, buy, integrate, and standardize decisions, including the vision for reducing implementation diversity across Okta and Auth0; clear the security, legal, procurement, and budget paths that slow adoption; and own the measurement that connects investment to engineering outcomes — evidence engineering leaders can take into any room.

This is a highly technical internal platform role that creates value for Okta through a cross-team, cross-industry, cross-functional layer that turns individual wins into organizational capability.

What You'll Do

  • Product Strategy & Discovery: Own the vision, PRDs, and prioritized backlog for Okta's internal developer productivity and AI tooling. Treat engineers as your customers: start with deep, bottom-up discovery (dozens of engineer, EM, tech lead, and architect interviews), baseline dev-cycle metrics, and secure tooling budgets with rigorous, ROI-driven business cases.
  • Ecosystem Validation (Build vs. Buy): Drive definitive "adopt, build, or pass" decisions. Run hands-on, structured evaluations of inner- and outer-loop tooling — from coding agents and MCPs to build, CI/CD, and code review systems — against strict security and TCO criteria to ensure internal investments amplify vendor capabilities.
  • Hands-On Execution: Embed full-time with Developer Productivity Engineering and own the roadmap jointly with its engineering leads. Define MVP scopes, manage sprints, and incrementally ship workflows. You own the strategy and requirements (the what and why); Engineering owns the technical execution (the how).
  • Adoption & Outcomes: Own org-wide adoption, clearing security, legal, and privacy hurdles along the way. Measure success by connecting tool usage directly to hard engineering outcomes (cycle time, quality, toil reduction).
  • Standardization & Lighthouses: Coordinate the vision for reducing implementation diversity across Okta and Auth0 engineering. Study high-performing teams to see who is getting exceptional results, and convert those patterns into scalable playbooks that shift the broader org from passive AI use to agentic workflows.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of product management experience with developer platforms, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, or AI products.
  • Experience owning internal or platform products where users have alternatives — adoption driven through product quality rather than mandate.
  • Strong understanding of modern software development workflows — source control, IDEs, CI/CD, testing, code review, observability, production operations — across the inner and outer loops of development.
  • Hands-on, current fluency with AI-assisted software development — coding agents, context management, MCP, evaluation frameworks — and informed views on where these tools create leverage and where they introduce risk.
  • Demonstrated ability to design and run technology evaluations and controlled experiments, and to define measurement systems for developer productivity with judgment about their failure modes.
  • Ability to engage credibly in technical and architectural discussions with senior engineers while maintaining clear boundaries between product outcomes and engineering implementation.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership and the ability to influence senior stakeholders across engineering, security, architecture, and finance without direct authority.
  • Excellent written communication in a docs-first culture; you can produce solid action plans from incomplete, conflicting, or ambiguous inputs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience deploying or scaling developer tools across a large, multi-org engineering organization — including consolidating divergent stacks and the change management that comes with it.
  • Hands-on familiarity with developer AI tools, harnesses, APIs, MCPs, and agent orchestration frameworks.
  • Familiarity with developer productivity research (DORA, SPACE, DX Core 4) and its failure modes.
  • Experience establishing governance, evaluation frameworks, or spend management for rapidly evolving, consumption-priced technologies.

Why This Role Matters

AI-assisted development is becoming both one of the largest levers on engineering velocity and one of the largest new variable costs in R&D. The playbook changes monthly, and the organizations that win are the ones that learn fastest from the outside, spread what works internally, and measure honestly. That learning-and-leverage layer doesn't build itself — engineering teams optimizing locally, however well, still leave organizational value uncaptured and accumulate divergent implementations that slow everyone down.

This role exists to capture it: dedicated product leadership that brings engineering the external intelligence, funded tooling, cleared paths, shared patterns, and defensible evidence to build with AI faster than any single team could alone — while deepening Okta's firsthand credibility as the company that secures the AI-powered enterprise for its customers.

  • Beheren en optimaliseren van cloudomgevingen, zoals Azure en AWS.

  • Samenwerken met development en operations teams om een cultuur van Continuous Improvement te stimuleren.

Je bent fit for the job als je...

Je hebt ruime ervaring als DevOps Engineer en voelt je thuis in een dynamische consultancy omgeving. Je kent containertechnologieën en cloudplatformen door en door en schakelt moeiteloos tussen techniek en advies. Met jouw communicatieve vaardigheden weet je klanten helder mee te nemen in keuzes, oplossingen en best practices. Je wilt blijven groeien, nieuwe technieken ontdekken en werkt graag in omgevingen waar je impact maakt.

Harde eisen:

  • Hbo opleiding richting business IT & management of een vergelijkbare studie.
  • Minimaal 5 jaar ervaring als DevOps Engineer binnen consultancy of een vergelijkbare dynamische omgeving.

Zachte eisen:

For international candidates: our consultants must be able to communicate in Dutch at a minimum of C1 level, both spoken and written.

Dit krijg je van ons

Je ontvangt een salaris tussen 6.000 en 7.800 euro bruto per maand op basis van 40 uur, afhankelijk van jouw ervaring, kennis en relevante certificaten. Daarnaast krijg je toegang tot meer dan 950 trainingen en cursussen die je onbeperkt kunt volgen.

Je werkt aan uitdagende projecten in een inspirerende consultancy omgeving waar je niet sectorgebonden bent. Binnen de Business Unit Technology werk je samen met 75 consultants, waarvan 30 IT consultants in jouw directe team. De sfeer is business casual: hard werken, veel humor en volop ruimte voor persoonlijke ontwikkeling.

  • Creëer je ideale thuiswerkplek met onze vergoeding

  • Boost je salaris met onze verschillende bonussen
  • Met 25 vakantiedagen heb je alle tijd voor jouw avonturen
  • Met kennissessies en webinars blijf je bij in je vakgebied
  • Op tijd naar je afspraak in je (elektrische) leaseauto
  • Ontwikkel je onbeperkt met de Team EIFFEL Academy trainingen

Dit zijn wij

Groot in interim capaciteit en sterk in consultancy, dat is Team EIFFEL. We versterken organisaties precies waar dat nodig is. Of je nu werkt voor een bank, gemeente of ziekenhuis: jij helpt teams slimmer werken en brengt ideeën van papier naar praktijk. Soms voor grote transformaties, soms voor snelle oplossingen. Van startup tot multinational: als professional bij EIFFEL kom je overal binnen.

Binnen de Business Unit Technology werk je met 75 consultants verdeeld over drie specialisaties: Data & Analytics, IT en GEOS. Als DevOps Engineer maak je deel uit van het IT team, samen met zo'n 30 collega consultants. Omdat we niet sectorgebonden werken, krijg je de kans om in verschillende omgevingen ervaring op te doen. IT raakt alle sectoren, daardoor is er altijd een project dat past bij jouw kennis, ambitie en energie.

Elke vrijdag is onze samenwerkdag in het clubhuis in Arnhem. Die staat in het teken van kennisdeling, sparren met collega's en het versterken van de onderlinge verbinding. Moet je opdrachtgever je die dag op kantoor hebben? Dan gaat dat natuurlijk voor.

Team EIFFEL is onderdeel van een community van ruim 3.000 experts, verspreid over 24 kennisdomeinen en meer dan 600 opdrachtgevers. Groot in omvang, maar persoonlijk in cultuur. Ons clubhuis staat open voor iedereen die wil groeien, ontwikkelen en zichzelf scherp wil houden.

Deze skills komen van pas

  • Software testing en automatisering

Je communiceert sterk en weet klanten op een duidelijke, rustige manier mee te nemen in complexe DevOps vraagstukken. Je werkt graag samen en stimuleert teams om continu te verbeteren. Met jouw analytische blik zie je snel waar knelpunten zitten en vind je oplossingen die werken, altijd met aandacht voor security en compliance. Je blijft op de hoogte van de nieuwste ontwikkelingen in DevOps en cloudtechnologie en past die kennis toe in je werk. Je houdt van hard werken, maar zeker ook van humor op de werkvloer. En misschien wel het belangrijkste: je bent gericht op groei en persoonlijke ontwikkeling.

title: Senior Technical Project Manager I
description:
Job Title: Senior Technical Project Manager I

Work Location: Austin, TX Office - Hybrid working environment (Mon/Wed/Fri in office)

Reports to: Head of Product & Data

Level: 5

About Grocery TV

Grocery TV is a leading in-store retail media platform. Over 120 retailers partner with Grocery TV to modernize stores and drive incremental revenue while delivering a more engaging shopping experience. We manage the complexities of operating an in-store media network, allowing retailers to focus on serving customers. Reaching 1 in 4 Americans across 6,500+ stores, Grocery TV connects brands with shoppers at the moment of decision, where 90% of purchases take place. For more information, visit .

About the role

We're hiring a Technical Project Manager to own delivery of our most complex cross-functional work, reporting to the Head of Product and Data.

Our programs rarely live inside one team. A single launch can touch hardware in hundreds of stores, the content scheduling platform, data pipelines, measurement methodology, a partner's API, and a retailer's rollout calendar. You'll be the person who turns that into a plan, keeps it honest, and gets it shipped.

This is a hands-on role for someone with a real technical background. You won't write production code, but you'll be expected to understand the architecture well enough to challenge an estimate, spot a hidden dependency, and explain a technical tradeoff to a sales leader or a retail partner in plain language.

Responsibilities

  • Own delivery end to end. Take multi-team programs from scoping through launch across our device platform, content and scheduling systems, data infrastructure, measurement, and partner integrations.
  • Turn priorities into plans. Break roadmap goals into milestones with clear owners, dependencies, and dates, and keep them current as things change.
  • Run the operating rhythm. Lead planning, status, and risk reviews. Keep our project tracking (Linear) accurate enough that leadership can trust it without asking.
  • Surface risk early. Flag slips before they happen and come with options and tradeoffs, not just a red status.
  • Coordinate partner and customer technical work. Scope and track retailer rollouts, pilots, and integrations with ad servers, SSPs, and data partners. Support technical answers for RFIs and RFPs.
  • Translate between worlds. Bridge Engineering and Data with Sales, RevOps, and Account teams so commitments made to customers match what we can actually build.
  • Report upward. Write concise weekly summaries for executive leadership on progress, risks, and decisions needed.
  • Improve how we work. Build and refine the templates, health checks, and playbooks that make delivery repeatable as the team grows.

Requirements/Experience

  • 5+ years delivering technical work, with at least 3 in a project, program, or delivery lead role.
  • A hands-on technical foundation, ideally time spent as a software or data engineer. You can read an architecture diagram, reason about APIs and data pipelines, and tell a sound estimate from a hopeful one.
  • A track record shipping complex programs across engineering, data, design, and business stakeholders, including at least one where scope, people, or priorities shifted midstream.
  • Clear, concise writing. Your status updates get read, and your plans answer questions before they're asked.
  • Fluency with Agile practices (Scrum, Kanban) and the judgment to use only as much process as the work needs.
  • Comfort with budgets, capacity planning, and scoping work against real constraints.
  • Experience working directly with clients or external partners. A consulting or agency background is a strong plus.

Nice to have

  • Experience in retail media, adtech, or digital out-of-home (DOOH).
  • Background with IoT, connected devices, or managing hardware deployed in the field.
  • Familiarity with data platforms and BI tools (Omni, Looker, dbt, Snowflake, or similar).
  • Exposure to measurement, attribution, or experimentation work.
  • Experience building a program management practice or delivery playbook from scratch.
  • Experience with AI-assisted delivery workflows and a point of view on where they help.

Interview Process

  1. Apply: We review applications as soon as we can. You should hear back about your application within two weeks.
  2. Hiring Manager Interview: Meet with the hiring manager (virtually or in-person) to share your background, learn about the role, and confirm this is the right role/environment for you.
  3. Introduction to HR: Meet our HR team virtually to align on logistics, include compensation, in office expectations, benefit offerings. This is a great time to ask any questions you missed during your interview with the hiring manager.
  4. Technical Interview: Visit our office in-person or remotely for a technical interview that relates to the role. You’ll respond to a prompt, and our team will ask questions to better understand your skillset.
  5. Virtual Values Interview: Meet with two Grocery TV employees who you’ll work cross functionally with to discuss team collaboration. This is a perfect opportunity for you to ask us questions, too!
  6. Virtual Leadership Interview: Lastly, all candidates have a final interview with a member of the leadership team. This conversation gives you the opportunity to reflect on the interview process and affirm this is the right role for you.

Why Grocery TV?

  • 100% medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • $1,200 annual HSA match
  • $1,000 annual learning & development budget
  • Unlimited PTO
  • 12 weeks of parental leave for all new parents
  • Hybrid work model: three days in office per week
  • Monthly DoorDash lunch stipend
  • $500 home office setup stipend

title: UTILITIES SENIOR WATER ENGINEER - ONE STOP SHOP
description:
The Position



The City of Riverside, Public Utilities Department (RPU) is accepting applications for the position of SENIOR WATER ENGINEER - ONE STOP SHOP to fill one (1) vacancy in the Water Engineering - Development Services Division. The eligibility list established may be used to fill the current and/or upcoming vacancies within this classification for up to six (6) months.


Under general supervision, the Senior Water Engineer - One Stop Shop is to perform supervisory and/or professional water engineering work in the design, investigation and construction of water utility projects and to do related work as required.

*For positions indicating a salary range from 1N – 2X, the top 15% of the pay range cannot be offered upon hire or upon an employee promotion.

Work Performed

Duties may include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Performs studies of technical, environmental, and economic feasibility, engineering field studies, and related studies pertaining to proposed and existing municipal facilities.
  • Prepares contracts and specifications for engineering and construction services.
  • Plans and performs their own work and completes special projects requiring engineering and technical ability as assigned.
  • Provides background information and documentation for management consideration on various projects.
  • Makes sound decisions on minor problems related to the work being performed based on established guidelines and principles and supervisor guidance.
  • Completes special projects requiring advanced engineering and technical ability.
  • Develops and updates written directives for the department and for use by other employees to include engineering guidelines, standard material lists, standard specifications, and other technical and administrative policies and procedures as applicable.
  • Researches activities pertaining to water materials and engineering practices.
  • Prepares and review economic, hydraulic and hydrogeologic analyses and project justification reports.
  • Develops major engineering projects and other engineering projects with unique problems which have an important effect on major public works projects.
  • Provides background information and documentation for management consideration on major projects and technical matters involving advanced engineering theories, concepts and principles.
  • Performs complex studies of technical, environmental, and economic feasibility, engineering field studies, and related studies pertaining to proposed and existing system facility improvements.
  • Plans own work and the work of others.
  • Completes special projects that are frequently of long duration and complexity.
  • Works with other engineering personnel with limited experience in an advisory or supervisory capacity.
  • Makes decisions independently on technical problems and methods related to the work being performed.

Qualifications

Education:

  • A Bachelor's degree in civil or mechanical engineering from an accredited college or university and four years of experience in professional water engineering work comparable to that of an Utilities Assistant/Utilities Associate Engineer in the City of Riverside, or a Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in a closely related area.

Experience:
  • Five (5) years' of experience performing professional water utility or related engineering work comparable to that of an Utilities Assistant/Utilities Associate Engineer in the City of Riverside.

  2. Experience with water rules and rates, including interpretation and resolution of development issues associated with water rules and rates.

  3. Plan check and review of water utility plans, related civil engineering construction plans, and building plans.

  4. Preparing or reviewing of construction cost estimates.

  5. Processing fire flow tests and reviewing results.

  6. Customer service experience working directly with the public at a public facing customer counter.

title: Project Manager
description:
Cornell Human Ecology explores the complexity of human life. We bring together a wide range of perspectives to understand the full context of the human experience and improve lives at every scale, from cells to society. Our research and academic programs focus on the interaction of humans with their biological, economic, social and physical environments. Using Cornell's far-reaching extension network and the college's translational research methods, we deliver our findings directly to communities and families, ensuring that our work reaches those who need it most.

**The Opportunity**

Health Behaviors Lab: The Health Behaviors Lab conducts community-engaged research to understand and improve the behaviors and environments that shape health and well-being. Our work focuses on nutrition, physical activity, and other health behaviors, with particular attention to children, families, caregivers, and the early childhood workforce. We partner with communities, practitioners, and other stakeholders to design, implement, and evaluate interventions that are responsive to real-world needs and can be translated into programs, practice, and policy. Our research draws on behavioral, intervention, and implementation science and uses a range of quantitative, qualitative, and technology-enabled methods. Across projects, our goal is to conduct research that is driven by communities, rigorous in its methods, and intended to create knowledge that others can use to improve health and reduce inequities. To learn more about the HBL visit – blogs.cornell.edu/healthbehavlab/.

**What You Will Do**

The Project Manager will serve as an integral member of the Health Behaviors Lab and will work under the direction of the HBL Director, Dr. Laura Bellows, to coordinate and support multiple research projects focused on health behaviors and community-based interventions. The Project Manager will oversee day-to-day project activities, coordinate timelines and deliverables, communicate with community partners and research participants, and organize and delegate project tasks to undergraduate and graduate student researchers.

The Project Manager will contribute to all phases of the research process, including developing and testing study materials, resources, and intervention components; participant recruitment and data collection; data management and analysis; and preparation of manuscripts, abstracts, presentations, and reports. The position will coordinate human subjects research activities, including preparing and maintaining Institutional Review Board (IRB) submissions, modifications, and study documentation, and supporting adherence to approved protocols and research requirements.

The Project Manager will also contribute to the development of grant applications and other research proposals and help establish systems and procedures that support efficient implementation of the Lab’s research portfolio. Working across multiple projects, the Project Manager will collaborate closely with Dr. Bellows, students, research collaborators, community partners, and other stakeholders to ensure that research activities and deliverables are completed accurately, efficiently, and on schedule.

This is a full-time, benefits eligible, one-year term position with the possibility of renewal, contingent upon funding, available work, and successful performance. This is an in-person position, and your primary work location will be located on the Ithaca, NY campus.

**To be considered for the position, please upload a cover letter expresssing your interest and relevant experience, as well as a resume or CV.**

**No visa sponsorship or relocation assistance are provided for this position.**

**Required Qualifications:**

- Bachelor’s degree and at least one year of related experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

**Key qualifications that will lead to your success:**

- Experience supporting research projects, including experience with data collection, management, and/or analysis.
- Demonstrated ability to take initiative, prioritize tasks, and coordinate multiple projects or research activities simultaneously.
- Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to meet deadlines and maintain accurate records.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with multiple audiences (e.g., research participants, community partners, students, faculty, and staff.)
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite.
- Experience with or ability to learn survey and data collection platforms such as Qualtrics and REDCap.
- Ability to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a research team.
- Ability to cultivate and develop inclusive working relationships with students, faculty, staff, and community members.


**Preferred Qualifications**

- Master’s degree in public health, nutrition, psychology or a related field.

**Rewards & Benefits**

- Cornell receives national recognition as an award-winning workplace for our health, wellbeing, sustainability, and diversity initiatives.
- Our benefits programs include comprehensive health care options, generous retirement contributions, access to wellness programs, and employee discounts with local and national retail brands. We invite you to follow this link to get more information about our benefits: [https://hr.cornell.edu/benefits-pay](https://hr.cornell.edu/benefits-pay).
- Follow this link to learn more about the Total Rewards of Working at Cornell: [https://hr.cornell.edu/jobs/your-total-rewards](https://hr.cornell.edu/jobs/your-total-rewards).
- Our leave provisions include health and personal leave, three weeks of vacation and 13 holidays: Martin Luther King, Jr. Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, and an end of the year winter break from December 25-January 1.
- Cornell's impressive educational benefits include tuition-free Extramural Study and Employee Degree Program, tuition aid for external education, and Cornell Children's Tuition Assistance Program.

title: Kitchen Supervisor
description:
TITLE: Café Assistant DEPARTMENT: Café

STATUS: FT, Assistant, Union, Hourly REPORTS TO: Café Manager

JOB SUMMARY: To ensure the highest level of service possible to Outpost’s internal and external customers. Supervise and motivate café staff to uphold high standards in the department. Order product to maintain a fully stocked department. Ensure a well maintained, clean, and efficient café.

WORK ENVIRONMENT: Fast paced retail floor and café. Work near moving mechanical parts (i.e. coffee/juice machines, slicer) and in cold/hot climate conditions (i.e. cooler or near stove). Ability to work in moderate and loud noise environments including, but not limited to: computers, paging, telephones, human voices, and machinery. Position requires working during busy retail times, which include weekends, afternoons, and evenings.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITES:
1. Customer Service

Treat people fairly, consistently, and with respect.
Ensure efficient, informative, and friendly service according to established customer service vision and standards.

2. Café Department Responsibilities
Department Operations

Plan, organize, and supervise all department operations in absence of café manager.
Ensure customer service is the first priority of all staff in the department.
Expedite customer orders with kitchen.
Ensure customers receive their orders in a timely manner and have what they need to enjoy their dining experience.
Check out customer’s purchases quickly and accurately, using correct prices, codes and departments.
Assign production and other tasks to café staff to ensure that daily jobs and all opening and/or closing duties are accomplished efficiently and accurately.
Assist café manager with the production schedule.
Coordinate the stocking of café items and supplies.
Follow proper procedures in opening and/or closing café areas including: juice bar, hot case, prepack station, sandwich bar, bakery case, and seating area.
Check all par levels of sub-departments including juice bar, sandwich bar, prepack station, and miscellaneous items.
Maintain a clean and organized backstock area.
Stock grab and go case to maintain an abundant and fully stocked display.
Uphold department’s sanitation standards and health department requirements for food storage and handling. Ensure staff do the same.
Uphold department safety guidelines to ensure the safety of all department staff.
Ensure café equipment is maintained and properly serviced. Advise café manager of equipment/replacement needs.
Assist with department resets and quarterly inventory.
Backup café kitchen staff when needed.
Attend department meetings as scheduled.

Customer Service

Ensure professional and friendly service from café staff.
Handle customer questions and complaints including on the premises and follow up phone calls.
Ensure customers are all greeted and assisted in a timely manner.
Provide product information to staff and customers.

Ordering and Receiving

Order product and supplies to ensure department is fully stocked, while keeping inventory to a minimum.
Receive and stock orders in a timely manner. Check condition of product and invoices for accuracy upon delivery. Ensure correct product rotation.
Properly label café items with ingredient listing and pricing information.
Review and log invoices in store and departmental journals.
Assist in inventory control including: accurate recording of losses, department transfer of items, and quarterly inventory.

Merchandising

Maintain clean and organized department displays, cases and work areas.
Ensure department is kept neat and clean.
Ensure all display areas are properly fronted and faced.
Ensure proper shelf tags and sale signs are on products and displays.
Request signs from pricing as needed.

Personnel

Assign daily tasks to café staff and ensure they are always busy.
Positively encourage department staff to excel at their job.
Provide guidance and motivation and properly answer questions for department staff.
Replace vacant shifts when call ins, etc. occur. Notify manager of these occurrences.
Assist in training department staff.
Ensure café staff is following department standard operating procedures.
Assist café manager with employee job performance. Properly document employee performance during shift, when necessary.
Assist café manager in informing staff of any changes in policies and procedures affecting department staff.

Other

Perform all duties included in department journeyperson and clerk job descriptions.
Perform manager duties in their absence.

3. All Staff Duties

Abide by all Co-op policies and procedures as outlined in the Employee Handbook and other company documents.
Keep store orderly and clean.
Maintain a positive attitude.
Perform all other duties as assigned by department manager or supervisory staff.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES:

Outstanding customer service skills
Experience in food service and food prep
Previous supervisory experience

Ability to appropriately delegate work duties and manage and motivate staff

Attention to detail and good organizational skills
Ability to handle multiple demands, work under time pressures, and meet deadlines
Willingness to be open, to learn, and take on new responsibilities

Demonstrate objectivity, neutrality and calmness under pressure

Regular, predictable attendance

title: Production Tunnel Operator
description:

Other duties as assigned.

Ability to understand all required training, written, and verbal instructions.
Working knowledge of basic math skills.
Good verbal and/or written communication skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Ability to meet attendance schedule.

Working Environment / Safety Requirements

Work is performed in a warehouse setting and regularly exposed to outside weather conditions, extreme heat and cold conditions as well as dust and noise.
Work is based on a shift schedule, and may include weekends.

Position involves repetitive motions over the duration of an entire shift.
Requires bending, reaching, pulling, twisting, and lifting.

Education
High school degree or equivalent preferred.

title: Staff User Researcher
description:
About Us

AfterShip, a Great Place to Work Certified company, is transforming the global eCommerce landscape. Founded in 2012, AfterShip is a post-purchase SaaS company on a mission to build the world’s leading automation platform for ecommerce merchants.

AfterShip unifies shipping & labels, order tracking, AI predictive delivery, and returns management into one system—giving merchants a single place to manage and automate everything that happens after checkout. By centralizing these workflows, AfterShip enables merchants to reduce customer support inquiries, deliver a more reliable and engaging customer experience, and unlock incremental revenue at every post-purchase touchpoint.

AfterShip integrates seamlessly with eCommerce platforms including Shopify and TikTok Shop, and connects with more than 1,400 carriers worldwide. Today, over 20,000 businesses—including Samsung, Gymshark, Mejuri, Dr. Squatch, and Alo Yoga—rely on AfterShip to turn every post-purchase moment into an opportunity to build trust, reduce costs, and drive repeat purchases.

Built for a global market from day one, AfterShip operates with an engineering-driven, internationally distributed team. The company employs more than 450 people across 8 offices, spanning North America, Europe, and Asia, and representing over 20 cities worldwide.

Your Mission:

As a Staff User Researcher, you'll set and own the research agenda across multiple AfterShip product areas and systems, shaping post-purchase strategy at the organizational level. You'll proactively identify the questions and new opportunities that matter most and translate findings into a product and business perspective that leadership acts on. You'll also raise the bar for the research function as a whole: setting quality standards, mentoring researchers, and providing input into others' roadmaps.

You'll partner with cross-functional leadership across Product, Design, Product Marketing, Engineering, and Data, and report to the Manager of User Research. This is a remote position, with a preference for candidates in the United States. This role requires collaboration with teams located in Asia and Europe, which may require working outside of regular business hours 2-3 times/week.


What You’ll Do:

  • Identify, prioritize, lead, and execute on research that generates insights to inform product strategy across the company — leading your own roadmap independently and helping shape the broader team's.
  • Define, design, execute, and socialize a range of research studies that build a strong understanding of existing and future merchants and shoppers, and their experiences around the world.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams — Product, Design, Data Science, Engineering, and Product Marketing — to proactively develop research initiatives.
  • Translate research into a product and business perspective, and align cross-functional leadership — including Directors and VPs — on key strategic questions across domains.
  • Set the quality standard for the research team: mentor researchers, build repeatable practices, and serve as a subject-matter expert.
  • Identify best practices in existing and emerging research methodologies.
  • Proactively identify new areas of user and business opportunity.

Who We're Looking For:

  • 8+ years of applied UX/user research experience, including leading research across multiple product areas or a business domain (SaaS and/or e-commerce a plus).
  • Proven ability to lead research strategy and roadmap independently.
  • Deep, comprehensive expertise across qualitative and quantitative methods; recognized as a subject-matter expert who can set standards for others.
  • A track record of influencing at the executive level and aligning leadership on strategic questions.
  • Strong synthesis and storytelling — turning complex research into clear, actionable recommendations that drive decisions, evidenced by a portfolio or work samples.
  • Experience mentoring researchers and elevating a team's craft.
  • Bachelor's or Master's in Human-Computer Interaction, Psychology, Cognitive Science, Design, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience.
  • Thrives with full autonomy in a remote-first, distributed organization.
  • Mandarin proficiency is strongly preferred.

At AfterShip, we know great talent doesn’t always fit every requirement. If you’re passionate about our mission and believe you can make an impact, we encourage you to apply.


Why You Should Join Us:

  • Great Place to Work Certified: We’ve been recognized for our inclusive, values-driven culture that celebrates diversity and collaboration.
  • Innovative & Inclusive Culture: Started by our software engineer-turned-CEO, AfterShip is built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. We’re a passionate, global team of problem solvers who put egos aside to innovate together. We take immense pride in fostering a culture that’s inclusive, which has allowed us to surround ourselves with the industry's most talented professionals.
  • Ambitious Mission with Real Impact: Join us in transforming eCommerce by making buying and selling easier for everyone. It’s one of the most dynamic spaces in tech, with limitless opportunities to innovate and grow.
  • Thrive & Grow: There’s no ceiling to what you can achieve or learn here. We’re committed to empowering your career while advancing together as a company.
  • Flexible Work Setup: We’re a remote-first team, meaning by default that employees work from home or on a hybrid-flexible basis in our hub locations. You’re empowered to choose a work setup that works best for you and your team. With flexible hours depending on your time zone, you’ll be able to have a schedule that fits your working style and the requirements of your role.

Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Remote-first/hybrid-flexible work setups
  • Healthcare coverage offered from day 1
  • Retirement plans including company match
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Annual learning & wellness benefit
  • Monthly book perk
  • Career progression & professional development
  • In-office lunch and commuter benefits for those located in our hub locations

Base salary range for this role: USD$165,000 - $232,500/ CAD$151,000 - 200,000

We are an equal opportunity employer and provide accommodations upon request throughout the recruitment process, in accordance with local legislation. Please let us know if you require any support, and we’ll work with you to meet your needs.

We believe in hiring right over hiring fast. While timelines may vary, we’re looking to fill this role as soon as possible.

Our hiring process uses AI to help with initial resume screening and to support interview note-taking. These tools help our team stay organized and fair, but all hiring decisions are made by people.
