title: Cold Source Specialist
description:
Requisition Id 16871

**Overview:**

We are seeking a Cold Source Specialist who will focus on operation of the cryogenic cold source facility and support of shift personnel. This position resides in the Cold Source Operations Group in the High Flux Isotope Reactor (HFIR) Operations Section, Research Reactors Division, Neutron Sciences Directorate at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL).

**Major Duties/Responsibilities:**

Operations:

- Operate Cold Source cryogenic and support systems to support HFIR operations and neutron science missions.


- Supports shift operations in accordance with plant procedures, HFIR Technical Safety Requirements, and Cold Source Safety Authorization Basis.


- Serves as the single point of contact for authorizing, directing, and monitoring Cold Source activities.


- Performs actions necessary to mitigate the consequences of Cold Source transients.


- Works 12-hour rotating shift work during operating cycles.


- Safely perform hydrogen addition and venting operations and take proper actions in the event of an incident.


- Serves as Qualified Person for Lockout/Tagout(Lock/Tag/Verify) process per ADM-0200 to hang and clear equipment lockouts.


- Acts as the Cold Source Operations Lead (CSOL) as designated during absences.


- Provides backup for shift Cold Source Staff Member (CSSM) during plant operations.


- Provides shift relief on 12-hour rotating shifts for CSSMs.


Work Control:

- Authorize start of work affecting Cold Source equipment and systems.


- Authorizes the removal of equipment to service following maintenance, testing or operational actives.


- Authorizes the return of equipment to service following maintenance, testing or operational actives.


- Acts as Issuing Authority in the Lockout/Tagout (Lock/Tag/Verify) process per ADM-0200 when designated by the CSOL.


Administrative:

- Write Technical Safety Requirement Tacking documents for approval.


- Ensures plant operational deficiencies are identified and corrective action is initiated.


- Provides feedback to operating, emergency, and administrative procedures.


- Perform quarterly/annual audits for various operations procedures/programs.


- Order operational supplies and equipment.


- Develops and reviews Cold Source plant operating and emergency response procedures.


- Works with engineering, safety, and management to obtain approvals of new and revised procedures.


Engineering Support:

- Provides input to System Engineering for system upgrades to ensure the operational reliability and longevity of the Cold Source.


- Provides drawing and modification reviews, as needed to support modifications and deviations.


- Submits drawing discrepancy notifications and change requests when system drawing errors are noted.


- Perform software validation and verification testing and review for Cold Source Distributed Control System software.


Maintenance Support:

- Acquires and maintains Task Leader qualification, including writing, reviewing, and approving Maintenance Work Packages.


- Provide guidance to maintenance engineers during maintenance planning and oversight/guidance during execution, as necessary.


- Perform system and component testing to validate maintenance actions.


- Perform troubleshooting of systems or components to ensure proper issues are identified.


Safety:

- Serves as HFIR Emergency Response Team member during emergencies.


- Maintains control of hydrogen control areas and personnel access for Cold Source Areas per ADM-0604.


- Exercises "Stop Work" authority within the Cold Source facility for practices that could jeopardize safety.


- Ensures compliance with environmental, safety, health, and quality program directives.


- Ensures Cold Source activities are conducted in accordance withappropriate tagging, safety, configuration control practices and Conduct of Operations per ADM-0001.


- Ensures applicable environmental, safety, and health directives are followed for all Cold Source operation activities.


Professionalism:

- Maintains a strong commitment to the implementation and perpetuation of professional values and ethics.


- Deliver ORNL’s mission by aligning behaviors, priorities, and interactions with our core values of Impact, Integrity, Teamwork, Safety, and Service. Promote equal opportunity by fostering a respectful workplace – in how we treat one another, work together, and measure success.


**Basic Qualifications:**

- A BS degree in engineering or related science with at least 5 years of experience. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered (a high school diploma plus 9 years of relevant experience or an AS degree plus 7 years of relevant experience).


- Current or previous CSSM qualification.


- Familiarity with Conduct of Operations and Cold Source processes and procedures.


**Preferred Qualifications:**

- A minimum of 5 years of experience as a CSSM.


- Excellent written and oral communication skills.


- Motivated self-starter with the ability to work independently and to participate creatively in collaborative teams across the laboratory.


- Ability to function well in a fast-paced research environment, set priorities to accomplish multiple tasks within deadlines, and adapt to constantly evolving needs.


**Special Requirements**:

- This position is a Workplace Substance Abuse (WSAP) testing designated position. WSAP positions require passing a pre-placement drug test and participation in an ongoing random drug testing program.


- Work involves various physical requirements and working conditions. As such, a pre-hire physical will be required after offer.


- Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.


**Benefits at ORNL:**

We offer competitive pay and benefits programs to attract and retain hardworking people! The laboratory offers many employee benefits, including medical and retirement plans and flexible work hours, to help you and your family live happy and healthy. Employee amenities such as on-site fitness, banking, and cafeteria facilities are also provided for convenience.

Other benefits include the following: Prescription Drug Plan, Dental Plan, Vision Plan, 401(k) Retirement Plan, Contributory Pension Plan, Life Insurance, Disability Benefits, Generous Vacation and Holidays, Parental Leave, Legal Insurance with Identity Theft Protection, Employee Assistance Plan, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, Wellness Programs, Educational Assistance, and Employee Discounts. title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
Den of Data is op zoek naar Senior Data Engineer. Dit betreft zowel een communicatieve als een technische rol. Je werkt met de nieuwste technieken en zorgt dat er oplossingen komen op het gebied van Microsoft Fabric, Data Lakes, Cloud (Azure) implementaties, Databases, ETL/DWH, CI/CD, Pipelines, Power BI en AI.

Jouw rol

Wat ga je doen?

  • Je ondersteunt onze klanten om meer datagedreven te gaan werken;
  • Signaleert proces- en informatiebehoeftes en brengt deze samen;
  • Je schrijft ETL met data uit diverse databronnen;
  • Je ontwikkelt rapportages en dashboards met heldere visualisaties;
  • Je bent aanspreekpunt voor collega’s met vragen over de informatie architectuur die we aan onze klanten uitleveren;
  • Data ontsluiten uit diverse databronnen;
  • Het opzetten van Proof of Concepts en deze vervolgens door ontwikkelen tot schaalbaar eindproduct;
  • Het opzetten en onderhouden van complexe en uitdagende Data Warehouse omgevingen.

Wie we zoeken

  • Je hebt minimaal vijf jaar ervaring als Data Engineer;
  • Je hebt minimaal twee afgeronde end-to-end BI / Data projecten;
  • Je hebt kennis van Microsoft Azure (Fabric / Datalake / Data Factory / Synapse / CI-CD Pipelines);
  • Je hebt uitgebreide kennis van het Microsoft BI platform;
  • Je hebt uitgebreide kennis van SQL;
  • Je hebt kennis van data modelleren (Kimball) en ETL processen;
  • Je hebt kennis van Python;
  • Kennis van Microsoft Purview is een pré;
  • Je bent communicatief vaardig en begrijpt de vraag vanuit de klant;
  • Je hebt een open blik en kijkt altijd verder dan de initiële opdracht;
  • Je hebt data gerelateerde certificering zoals Databricks of van Microsoft Fabric of je bent hiermee bezig.

Wat we bieden

  • Ruimte om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen via ons Talent programma, met zowel technische diepgang als softskills trainingen;
  • 25 vakantiedagen;
  • Bij Den of Data is 10% van je tijd gereserveerd voor persoonlijke ontwikkeling, innovatie en het delen van kennis tijdens onze innovatiedagen (25 vrije dagen);
  • Een informele werksfeer en diverse (actieve) teamuitjes;
  • Om de vrijdag een ‘binnendag’;
  • Direct een contract voor onbepaalde tijd;
  • Een goed salaris (€6.500 - €7.500);
  • Een op maat gemaakt arbeidsvoorwaardenpakket, afgestemd op jouw persoonlijke wensen en behoeften;
  • Samenwerken met gepassioneerde specialisten die jouw enthousiasme voor AI en data delen;
  • Werken in een ondersteunende omgeving waar authenticiteit wordt gewaardeerd en waar naar jouw ideeën wordt geluisterd;
  • Een op maat gemaakt arbeidsvoorwaardenpakket, afgestemd op jouw persoonlijke wensen en behoeften;
  • Extra’s die je niet overal vindt: innovatiedagen, workation, Talent Program, Tosti-dag ♡ … en dat is nog lang niet alles!
  • Hybride werken is de standaard;
  • Werken met innovatieve klanten die de waarde van digitale transformatie begrijpen en openstaan voor moderne technologieën;
  • Een mentor die jou begeleidt tijdens je onboardingsperiode;
  • Kansen voor professionele groei worden actief gestimuleerd.

Over Den of Data

Wij zijn Den of Data, een toegewijd team van ervaren data professionals die de waarde van gegevens willen ontsluiten voor organisaties en professionals. Met onze expertise in dataverwerking, -analyse en -visualisatie streven we ernaar om maatwerkoplossingen te bieden die uw datamogelijkheden maximaliseren, rekening houdend met de unieke uitdagingen van uw bedrijf.

Met onze 19 top collega’s helpen we bedrijven vertrouwd, deskundig en doortastend om van data-ambities werkelijkheid te maken. Onze expertise ligt in het optimaliseren en automatiseren van bedrijfsprocessen met behulp van data. Dit resulteert direct in verbeterde bedrijfsresultaten en meer werkplezier voor uw personeel, terwijl uw bedrijf competitief blijft voor de toekomst.

Onze ambitie is om toonaangevend te zijn in ons vakgebied en deze kennis wereldkundig te maken door voortdurend te investeren in de ontwikkeling van ons team, het toepassen van de nieuwste effectieve technologieën, en het delen van kennis via verschillende activiteiten.

&Work helpt je verder

Den of Data werkt samen met &Work. &Work begrijpt dat het belangrijk is om te werken op een plek waar je gewaardeerd wordt, waar je je verder kunt ontwikkelen en waar je de ruimte krijgt om te groeien. Door via &Work te solliciteren, krijg je direct toegang tot hun brede netwerk van werkgevers. &Work kan je helpen bij de introductie bij Den of Data, achtergrondinformatie verstrekken, je voorbereiden op gesprekken zodat je jezelf overtuigend kan presenteren en je bijstaan tijdens de onderhandelingen om je een mooie stap vooruit te laten zetten in je carrière.

Vacature-informatie

  • Dienstverband: Fulltime
  • Ervaringsniveau: Senior
  • Salaris: €6500 - €7500

title: Family Wellness Coach
description:
Chimo: Where what you do matters for a lifetime. Chimo Youth Retreat Centre has been supporting children, youth and families involved with Children’s Services for over 50 years.
Job Description:

The Family Wellness Program provides trauma-informed, family-centred services that support the safety, wellbeing, connection, and permanency of children, youth, and families. Through collaboration with Children and Family Services, community partners, and natural supports, Family Wellness staff help families build on their strengths while navigating complex challenges and life transitions.

We are seeking an experienced and compassionate Family Wellness Coach to build and maintains safe, positive relationships with families, work cooperatively as part of the Family Wellness team, facilitate family time, and provide therapeutic youth work.

The Family Wellness Coach will be responsible for providing the following services:

  • In vivo family/parent support
  • Second-line family stabilization, intervention, preservation
  • Providing transportation for clients and supportive access through family time
  • Therapeutic youth work including cultural programming and connection to their heritage
  • Low ratio crisis intervention services
  • All other duties as required to support a family to thrive and achieve healthy lifestyle
  • Build positive relationships and work collaboratively with families, CFS staff and other stakeholders.
  • Maintain effective cross-functional relationships with staff, colleagues, and partners.
  • Work effectively with all Chimo Family Wellness staff and leadership.
  • Coordination of additional services to support great outcomes for families.
  • Advocacy for the child, youth and family services that ultimately support the reunification, unity or permanency of the family.
  • Possess knowledge of community resources that support families.

Physical Requirements:

  • Coaches work a variety of shifts including daytime, evenings, and weekends. Flexibility is important when planning shifts with the families and caregivers, as well as to support your team.
  • The work can be physically and mentally demanding, and requires the ability to carry car seats, lift children in/out of cars and car seats, etc.
  • You must be able and prepared to physically interact with children in both indoor and outdoor settings.
  • Outdoor engagements with children and families may occur in all seasons, with appropriate measures taken based on current weather conditions.

The successful candidate will possess and demonstrate:

  • Critical thinking and creative problem solving to provide high-quality services.
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong facilitation, organizational and time management skills.
  • Understanding of life span developmental theories, Foundations of Caregiver Support, Signs of Safety, Appreciative Inquiry, Peacemaking Circles, Trauma Informed/Resiliency Focused Practices and Lifelong Connections.

Education and Credentials:

  • Degree in the Human Services field (Child & Youth Care, Social Work, Early Childhood Development, etc.) is preferred but those with a post-secondary 2 year diploma and experience will be considered.
  • Minimum of two years of experience in a front-line role within Human Services.

Employment Requirements:

  • A valid Class 5 driver’s license
  • Proven experience as a Driver (minimum 3 years history)
  • 2 doses of COVID-19 vaccination
  • Have the ability to provide current auto insurance with $2 million liability and use for work coverage with no at-fault accidents in the past 3 years
  • Eligibility for fleet insurance approval (driver's abstract must not have more than 2 convictions).


What We Offer:

We believe in supporting the people who make a difference every day. As a member of our team, you'll enjoy:

  • Membership on a supportive team of skilled and passionate professionals dedicated to helping children, youth, and families reach their greatest potential.
  • Paid vacation starting at twelve (15) days per year.
  • Paid sick and wellness leave equivalent to eight (10) days per year.
  • Comprehensive health benefits following the successful completion of the 3-month probationary period.
  • Dental coverage after one (1) year of employment.
  • A Health Spending Account (HSA) to help cover eligible health-related expenses after the probationary period.
  • Access to our Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP), offering confidential counselling and wellness resources for employees and their immediate families.
  • Opportunities for ongoing professional development, training, and career growth.
  • Invitations to agency events, training and development, staff appreciation activities, celebrations.
  • A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven workplace where your leadership and contributions make a meaningful impact every day.


Applications will remain open until a suitable candidate is found.

title: Director, Physical Security & Facility Security Officer
description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

As Director of Physical Security & Facility Security Officer (FSO), you will build and lead Relativity's enterprise security organization, protecting personnel, critical assets and data, and classified information across all facilities. This role uniquely combines strategic executive leadership with deep regulatory expertise and execution. You'll serve as our designated FSO while simultaneously architecting and scaling a world-class physical security program. You will establish the security infrastructure for all future expansion, define enterprise standards and policies, and build the systems and teams that enable secure operations at hypergrowth scale. This is a transformational leadership role that demands both strategic vision and operational excellence.

About the Role: 25% travel to our other sites

  • Serve as Relativity's designated Facility Security Officer (FSO) with active TS/SCI clearance, owning all facility clearance requirements, DD254 management, and serving as primary interface with DCSA and government security agencies for classified program compliance.
  • Develop and execute the enterprise physical security strategy aligned with NISPOM (32 CFR Part 117), ICD 705, and export control regulations, including multi-year roadmaps for program maturity, risk management, and scalability across all current and future facilities.
  • Build and lead the physical security organization including site security operations, security engineering/systems, investigations, front desk operations, and contracted guard force management, establishing clear roles, career pathways, and training programs for all security personnel.
  • Establish and maintain 24/7/365 security operations, including command structure, escalation protocols, incident response, investigations, and insider threat programs, ensuring physical protection of personnel, property, and controlled/classified information.
  • Drive regulatory compliance and audit readiness for NISPOM and classified program requirements, including personnel access controls, visitor management, foreign national protocols, classified information handling, and continuous preparation for DCSA and government security agencies.
  • Partner strategically with executive leadership, EHS, Cybersecurity, Legal, People, and Facilities to integrate security requirements into business operations, personnel actions, construction projects, and emergency response plans, while serving as primary security advisor to the company.

About You:

  • Active TS/SCI security clearance and current FSO certification with demonstrated experience managing facility clearances and interfacing with DCSA and government security agencies.
  • 10+ years of progressive physical security experience, including at least 5 years in leadership roles building and scaling security programs, with 2+ years as a FSO.
  • Deep expertise in NISPOM (32 CFR Part 117), ICD 705, and classified program security requirements, with proven track record of successful government audits and regulatory compliance.
  • Demonstrated experience leading enterprise security operations including access control systems (e.g., Lenel), CCTV/VMS, intrusion detection, and visitor management platforms, with technical knowledge to drive security systems architecture and integration.
  • Proven ability to build and lead high-performing security organizations, including direct team management and oversight of contracted security services, with experience establishing training programs, performance standards, and operational excellence.
  • Executive presence with demonstrated ability to influence and advise , present complex security and risk topics to non-technical audiences, and drive cross-functional strategic initiatives.

Nice to haves but not required:

  • Professional security certifications such as CPP (Certified Protection Professional), PSP (Physical Security Professional), or equivalent industry credentials.
  • Aerospace, defense, or advanced manufacturing experience with exposure to SCIF, SAP, or other compartmented program security requirements.
  • Experience managing large security budgets (both CAPEX and OPEX) and leading major capital security projects for new construction or facility expansions.

title: Academic Department Administrator II
description:
The criminal justice system increasingly relies on professionals skilled in forensic psychology to help solve crimes and prevent future criminal behavior. The Academic Department Administrator will support the forensic psychology program by performing a wide range of duties under limited supervision.

This senior administrative support position provides enhanced administrative support to an academic department. This role is a key contributor to providing high quality customer service to meet the academic needs of the faculty and students. This position reports to a Faculty Department Chair or Program Director. This position may supervise an office assistant and/or temporary staff and student workers. The core responsibilities of this position are to manage the daily operation of an academic department within a school or college, primarily in the areas of human resources, compliance and financial management, to represent the department on business affairs and/or faculty affairs to the institution community, to develop and prepare budgets and to coordinate and participate in a variety of human resources activities such as coordinating and initiating recruitment efforts.

Additional responsibilities include managing the hiring process for all faculty (full time, adjunct and visiting scholars), temporary staff and students, including on-boarding to the department, supporting and addressing faculty classroom needs, acquisition of textbooks and compiling course materials, and liaising with and assisting faculty with academic and administrative matters such as administrative aspects of course and curricula preparation. This role makes decisions related to academic support and serves as the administrative subject matter expert for the department. This position participates in monthly school-wide meetings for administrative managers, and may supervise a small staff of non-exempt employees and/or students.

The George Washington University, Forensic Psychology department is seeking an Academic Department Administrator. The responsibilities of this position include the following:

- Manages all logistical aspects of the Forensic Psychology department, including evaluations, space, food and beverages, print and digital program materials, graduate student recruitment, speaker travel, retreats, and other tasks.
- Stays current on faculty affairs: including contracts, special agreements, startup funds, etc.
- Develops and monitors budgets and prepares and process all financial related matters, including purchase orders, supplemental compensation, invoices, honorarium, stipends, volunteer appreciation recognition, expense reimbursements, and expenses. Maintains department P-card. Ensures budget compliance with institutional policies and procedures.
- Supports the administrative operations of the department, to include: developing and maintaining databases; scheduling, supporting/attending, producing agendas and minutes; preparing correspondence designed to effect action or publicize department activities; and compiling/distributing various assessments
- Regularly updates departmental web platform
- Liaison between departments and offices within the CCAS and GW

Performs other duties as assigned. The omission of specific duties does not preclude the supervisor from assigning duties that are logistically related to the position.

title: Senior Scientific Director - Publications (Heme-Onc)
description:
This position can be based remotely (working from home) or at our headquarters in Stamford, CT.

About Lockwood: Lockwood collaborates with clients in the pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device industries to identify effective, holistic, science-based strategies to address their objectives through medical communications. Our clients count on us to challenge their assumptions and help them creatively navigate around obstacles. From strategy through execution, we focus on accuracy, transparency, and scientific value to create programs that are evidence-based, clinically relevant, and contribute to the development of our clients’ brands. Over a third of our staff hold advanced scientific or medical degrees, and most work from where they live. Because our flexible structure provides better work-life balance, we attract the best talent, facilitate their best work, and as a result, are more responsive to our clients, wherever and whenever they do business.

Summary: In this role, the Senior Scientific Director is responsible for the planning, development, and oversight of scientific content for an assigned account or accounts across various therapeutic areas addressing different target audiences.

Responsibilities: Responsibilities include working with the Group Scientific Director to provide clients with strategic medical communication recommendations that support the achievement of brand goals, independently leading execution of content development activities, supervising Associate Scientific Directors, and liaising with other in-house or freelance staff to manage writing and other content-related tasks such as conducting background research, data-checking, and reference annotation.

Education: An advanced degree in science (ie. PhD, PharmD, or MD) is required. CMPP preferred.

Professional Skills and Requirements:

  • Candidates must have 5 or more years of relevant job experience with medical publications, including manuscripts, posters, abstracts, podium presentations, scientific platforms, and publication extenders.
  • This role requires demonstrated organizational, analytical, and interpersonal communication skills, as well as the ability to analyze and interpret scientific data, multitask, work independently, and manage projects within tight deadlines.
  • Experience with established professional medical editorial processes (ie. AMA style) and ethical guideline working knowledge (ie. ICMJE, GPP2022) is also required.
  • Experience with Heme/Oncology is required.

description:
Regional Vice President of Sales

Our client, a highly respected fee-only portfolio management and fiduciary firm with over $200 billion in assets under management, is looking for qualified financial professionals to join their firm as a Regional Vice President of Sales. title: Director, Sanctions Program Owner and Advisor
description:
Employee Applicant Privacy Notice

Who we are:

Shape a brighter financial future with us.

Together with our members, we’re changing the way people think about and interact with personal finance.

We’re a next-generation financial services company and national bank using innovative, mobile-first technology to help our millions of members reach their goals. The industry is going through an unprecedented transformation, and we’re at the forefront. We’re proud to come to work every day knowing that what we do has a direct impact on people’s lives, with our core values guiding us every step of the way. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the financial world.

The role:

As SoFi continues its expansion into digital assets and cutting-edge financial technology, you will play a critical role in ensuring our sanctions compliance program keeps pace. You will oversee the strategy, establishment, and ongoing direction of our Enterprise Sanctions Program. You will support the business in identifying, mitigating, and managing risks related to global sanctions (OFAC, UN, MX, HK, EU, UK), while ensuring the enterprise meets evolving regulatory expectations. We are seeking a Principal Advisor to develop, refine, and lead the Global Sanctions Compliance function across all lines of business, jurisdictions, and operational units. The ideal candidate brings senior-level experience in a government agency, combined with leadership experience at a Tier-1 global financial institution.

What you’ll do:

Be accountable as the Sanctions Program Leader.

Act as Sanctions subject matter expert for the SoFi Enterprise, advising Compliance, product managers, engineers, and SoFi’s business units.

Continuously engage with leaders in the AML department and across SoFi’s cross-functional leadership within the three lines of defense to identify changes impacting Sanctions-related processes and prepare guidance as applicable.

Support the AML Governance team with the annual Sanctions risk assessment and identify strategies to implement effective controls to mitigate identified risks.

Provide proactive guidance to detect and reduce sanctions exposure.

Support with the development and review of Sanctions policies, procedures, and controls for the SoFi Enterprise, ensuring that they align with both regulatory requirements and business objectives. Ensure policies and procedures are properly implemented throughout the product lifecycle.

Partner closely with compliance, business, and engineering teams to identify, assess, and advise on Sanctions issues and controls.

Stay informed of the latest developments in Sanctions regulations, industry trends, and best practices.

Recommend product updates, policies, and processes to strengthen compliance and reduce sanctions risk.

Assist in regulatory exams, internal audits, and third-party risk management reviews and respond to requests from regulatory agencies.

What you’ll need:

  • Minimum 5+ years in a senior policy, enforcement, licensing, or compliance role directly within the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).
  • 10-15+ years of experience in sanctions, with experience in crypto and global sanctions compliance.
  • Comprehensive understanding of BaaS products including payment processing, card issuance, credit and lending, and other traditional banking services.
  • Ability to lead the development and continuous enhancement of core sanctions policies, risk appetites, and governance structures to reflect evolving legal, geopolitical, and regulatory landscapes.
  • Provide direct advisory support to the Compliance and Risk Leadership team on high-risk transactions, strategic market expansions, mergers, and emerging international sanctions regimes.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with all levels of the organization and across different business lines.
  • Demonstrated strong leadership and management skills that build solid working relationships within the organization.
  • Excellent working knowledge of Sanctions Compliance within various international jurisdictions
  • Excellent organizational, verbal, written and interpersonal skills are required.
  • Must be able to multitask, adapt well to changing priorities, and effectively prioritize responsibilities to meet critical deadlines.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, demanding, and changing environment; must work well under pressure.
  • Excellent analytical skills required.
  • Ability to work collaboratively and independently while managing projects and assignments.

Nice to have:

  • Multilingual

_**Job Title: Specialist, Project and Component Engineer**_

_**Job Code: 45506**_

_**Job Location: Canoga Park, CA**_

_**Job Schedule: 9/80 Work 9 out of every 14 days – totaling 80 hours worked – and have every other Friday off**_

**Job Description:**

The Missle Solutions Segment of L3Harris is currently seeking an experienced **Specialist, Project and Component Engineer**. The Project and Component Engineer will assist in executing multiple phases of Pressurant and Propellant components (i.e. tanks, pressure switch, filters, regulators, transducers and valves) within assigned defense programs, as well as supporting advanced propulsion systems. Communicates with contacts within and outside of own department and may occasionally have responsibility for communicating with parties external to the organization (e.g., customers, vendors, etc).  Responsible to identify, define, communicate and address general issues typically encountered within job area or function.  Project and Component engineer will be expected to collaborate with multiple engineering, operational, quality, and supply chain functions to ensure successful component completion.

**Essential Functions:**

- Under general supervision, determine approaches to objectives demonstrating a complete understanding and application of engineering principles, concepts, and practices.
- Production and fabrication support system assemblies in rocket engine components. Translates engineering and scientific concepts from preliminary ideas through product life cycle.
- Ability to obtain and maintain a US security clearance
- Supplier integration with external suppliers ensuing requirements are achieved on time and within budget.
- Interface with other members of project or program teams, management, and technical staff to provide coordination of technical, schedule, and cost solutions to team objectives.
- Analyze and verify product design and performance for adequacy and reliability. Support investigation and resolution of hardware and process anomalies and issues identified by preventative action/corrective action boards or safety initiative activities.
- Coordinate with subject matter experts and multiple engineering disciplines to author and refine specifications, trade studies, design concepts, systems integration and component-level test plans.
- Work consists of making moderate enhancements or improvements to systems and processes to solve problems or improve effectiveness of job area.
- Up to 10% business travel to suppliers and other production sites.
- Position may require extended hours, as needed, to meet business objectives.

**Qualifications:**

- Bachelor’s Degree and minimum 4 years of prior relevant engineering experience.  Graduate Degree and a minimum of 2 years of prior related engineering experience.  In lieu of a degree, minimum of 8 years of prior related engineering experience.

**Preferred Additional Skills:**

- Bachelor’s Degree in Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering.
- Experience with Microsoft Office products (Project, Excel, Powerpoint, Word).
- Experienced in interpreting engineering technical drawings and experienced in GD&T symbology and application.
- Strong ability to understand technical drawings and specifications as well as working knowledge of general production systems/methods and lean manufacturing principles.
- Comprehensive knowledge of Project Engineering.
- Experience working in the defense industry with an existing clearance is a plus
- Experience with CAD software tools (CREO), and PLM Systems (Windchill) is a plus
- Experienced in the design, manufacturing, or testing involved in the production of valves, pressure regulators, pressure switches, tanks, or transducers is highly desired.
- Experienced in large component assemblies, including integration of multiple critical subassemblies pertaining to rocket propulsion components is highly desired.

title: Administrative Services Director (EMS Band 4)
description:
Description




Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen



The Department of Ecology is hiring an Administrative Services Director (EMS Band 4) within the Executive Leadership Team.


Location:

  • Headquarters Office in Lacey, WA.

  • Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule:

  • This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.

  • A minimum of three days per week is required in the office.

  • Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline:

  • Apply by October 21, 2026

  • Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

We are looking for a leader ready to partner with a dedicated group of professionals in leading and creating transformational change across a multi-disciplinary team here at Washington Ecology.

In this role, you will serve as the Director of Ecology’s Administrative Services Division director overseeing key cross-agency operations including information and real property management, facilities operations and sustainability, risk and emergency management, records management, public disclosure, fleet and transportation services, continuity of operations, and agency security. You will translate organizational vision into effective, efficient, and optimized enterprise services that support the long-term strategic direction of the organization. You will provide strategic decision-making and deliver policies with broad agency-wide impacts that shape how Ecology manages its resources, assets, and information.

Responsibilities include:

  • Planning, leading, organizing, and directing Ecology’s statewide administrative services, including facilities and real property management, risk management, emergency management and business continuity, fleet operations, security, records management, public disclosure, and cross-organizational administrative support functions.
  • Developing long-term strategies and biennial facilities plans in coordination with the Office of Financial Management and the Department of Enterprise Services to ensure sustainable, compliant, and mission-aligned facility operations across all Ecology locations.
  • Establishing and updating policies, procedures, and standards for administrative and operational services, including serving as the signatory authority for Ecology’s Policy Manual Chapter 14, Facilities and Vehicles.
  • Managing and optimizing Ecology’s statewide real property portfolio, including approximately 500,000 square feet of owned and leased facilities and tenant services for state and federal entities.
  • Overseeing agency security policies, practices, monitoring, and preparedness while chairing Ecology’s Security Committee and ensuring physical safety across facilities.
  • Leading agency-wide emergency management and business continuity planning, including representing Ecology’s Director in statewide and enterprise-level emergency management, homeland security, continuity of operations, and disaster recovery efforts.
  • Implementing and overseeing enterprise Electronic Content Management systems in partnership with Ecology’s Information Technology and Services Office to strengthen information governance and records integrity.
  • Overseeing fleet operations as a shared service with the Department of Enterprise Services, ensuring vehicle safety, operational reliability, and accurate reporting of energy use, greenhouse gas emissions, and zero-emission vehicle utilization.
  • Serving as Ecology’s Risk Manager, including developing and maintaining risk policies, conducting agency-wide compliance monitoring, guiding risk financing decisions, and ensuring alignment with statewide risk requirements.
  • Directing administrative services budgets, facility investments, procurement activities, and contracts—approving expenditures, leases, purchases, and personnel actions consistent with Ecology’s Signature and Authority Matrix.
  • Hiring, mentoring, and developing administrative services leaders and staff while fostering a collaborative, inclusive, accountable, and high-performing division.
  • Representing Ecology on statewide administrative, facility, fleet, emergency management, and risk management issues with OFM, DES, other state agencies, federal partners, and local jurisdictions.
  • Serving as Executive Sponsor for the Fleet Management Advisory Committee and the Modern Work Environment Steering Committee.

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for an experienced executive who can partner and collaborate effectively within complex governance structures and with scientific, regulatory, technical, and operational teams across the agency.

You will need to be able to:

  • Conceptualize and implement long-range administrative strategy, anticipate emerging facility and operational needs, and guide Ecology through complex organizational and infrastructure planning.
  • Communicate effectively with diverse partners across government, including OFM, DES, federal entities, local jurisdictions, and internal staff on high-impact administrative and facility issues.
  • Demonstrate a clear understanding of real property management, construction project practices, facility operations, procurement requirements, statewide administrative governance, risk finance principles, records and disclosure laws, and public-sector operational constraints.
  • Recognize how facilities, security, risk management, records, transportation, and operational systems influence environmental programs, staff effectiveness, public service delivery, and the communities where Ecology owns or leases facilities—and identify what is needed to deliver durable, mission-aligned outcomes.
  • Apply advanced management principles to balance complex priorities, optimize resources, develop staff, ensure compliance, and advance agency-wide operational readiness.

A Key Member of Ecology’s Executive Leadership Team

This position serves as a key member of Ecology’s Executive Leadership Team and plays a critical role in advancing the agency’s mission to protect, preserve, and enhance Washington’s environment for current and future generations.

It is essential that you consistently demonstrate the highest standards of personal, professional, and ethical conduct in support of transparent, accountable, and effective government.

This is a highly visible executive position with statewide impact. You will guide agency-wide administrative policy, represent Ecology on issues related to facilities, real property, fleet, emergency management, security, records governance, and operational resilience, and support executive decision-making through forward-looking administrative leadership. You will balance complex operational demands with long-term vision to build secure, resilient, efficient administrative systems that support staff and strengthen Ecology’s statewide mission.

As a key member of Ecology's Executive Leadership Team, you will:

  • Serve as a trusted leader and advisor on cross-agency management and operational strategy, including but not limited to asset and real property management, emergency preparedness, risk management practices, security policy, and records governance.
  • Advise the Director and Deputy Directors on administrative strategy and investments, policy development, enterprise risk, and operational readiness.
  • Collaborate across programs to align administrative priorities with Ecology’s environmental mission, scientific needs, regulatory responsibilities, and operational goals.
  • Represent the Director and agency on statewide administrative, facility, security, and risk management issues.
  • Foster a diverse, equitable, inclusive, respectful, and high-performing workplace that supports learning, accountability, transparency, and staff engagement.


This position is an Exempt Management Service (EMS) Band IV position. The minimum and maximum salary for EMS Band IV positions is $100,692 - $173,472.


Qualifications


For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website.


Required Qualifications:


Demonstrated expertise in business administration, workforce administration, facilities, records, security, risk and emergency readiness, natural science, environmental studies, engineering, public administration, planning public policy, political science, law, or other related qualifying discipline. This expertise can be demonstrated through professional degrees and/or professional and lived experience, as listed below.

  • Demonstrated professional level management experience which includes:
    • Strategic Planning and Direction Setting – Proven track record conceptualizing and articulating long-range organizational direction and developing and implementing annual and biennial strategic plans that strengthen agency operations and guide future administrative priorities.
    • Judgment and Decision Making – Demonstrated competence making high-impact operational and policy decisions to promote agency effectiveness, legal compliance, and operational continuity.
    • Communication and Collaboration –Proven experience conveying complex administrative, policy, or facilities matters to audiences from various backgrounds to ensure shared understanding and informed decisions.
    • Inter-Governmental and Legislative Engagement – Demonstrated ability to interpret and respond to legislative and inter-governmental processes to ensure administrative strategies align with external requirements and governmental expectations.
    • Negotiation and Consensus Building – Proven track record facilitating agreement among groups from various backgrounds, who may have differing or competing interests, to reach workable administrative, operational, or policy outcomes that support organizational goals.
    • Risk and Emergency Management – Demonstrated ability to develop and implement comprehensive risk management, emergency preparedness, and business continuity frameworks to safeguard agency operations and assets.
    • Administrative Policy and Program Oversight – Demonstrated proficiency in establishing, implementing, and evaluating administrative policies, procedures, and services to promote operational efficiency and organizational accountability.
    • Budget Development and Fiscal Administration – Proven track record with developing and administering complex budgets to support strategic priorities and ensure effective financial stewardship.
    • Records, Disclosure, and Content Management Systems – Demonstrated ability to oversee records governance and management, public disclosure processes, and enterprise electronic content management systems to ensure legal compliance, information integrity, and efficient enterprise-wide data practices to strengthen compliance and service delivery.
    • Fleet, Facilities, and Environmental Operations Management – Demonstrated proficiency with overseeing agency vehicle fleet operations, construction and facility maintenance activities, and environmental reporting systems to ensure safe, compliant, cost-effective facility performance and accurate documentation that supports responsible resource stewardship.



Desired Qualifications:

  • Desired Education:
    • Involving a major study in public affairs or administration, business administration, environmental management, natural sciences, natural resources, environmental sciences, physical sciences, engineering, planning, or other related field.
  • Desired Experience:
    • Successful record of accomplishment working with state, city, county and federal government agencies.
    • Serving as a supervisor.
    • Leading or managing in a large organization or significant public resources.
    • Working in, or collaborating with, state government.
    • Managing high-risk or high-impact administrative functions.
    • Working with or applying policy decisions and advising senior leaders on resource allocation and operational issues.
    • Experience with regulatory or compliance issues such as torts or other legal frameworks.
  • Desired Competencies:
    • Strategic Change Management – Ability to guide complex organizational change to improve systems, processes, and agency-wide operations.
    • Innovation and Process Improvement – Skilled with identifying opportunities to modernize administrative services and implement more efficient, cost-effective, or sustainable practices.
    • Complex Project and Program Management – Ability to oversee major, multi-phase administrative or facilities projects to ensure they are delivered on time, within scope, and within budget.
    • Data-Driven Management – Skilled with using operational data, metrics, and analytical tools to inform administrative decisions and resource planning.
    • Legislative and Regulatory Awareness – Skilled with interpreting evolving rules, legislation, and requirements to anticipate impacts on administrative services and adjust agency practices accordingly.


If you are excited about this role and meet the required qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Desired qualifications reflect additional knowledge, skills, or experience that are nice to have but not required. Studies have shown that some applicants, especially women and people of color, are less likely to apply unless they meet every listed qualification. At the Department of Ecology, we are dedicated to building a diverse and authentic workplace centered in belonging, and we welcome applicants with varied backgrounds and unique perspectives.


Supplemental Information

Ecology does not use the E-Verify system; therefore, we are not eligible to extend STEM Optional Practical Training (OPT). For more information, please visit .


Our Commitment to DEIR

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Respect (DEIR) are core values central to Ecology's work. We strive to be a workplace where we are esteemed for sharing our authentic identities, while advancing our individual professional goals and collaborating to protect, preserve, and enhance the environment for current and future generations.


Diversity: We celebrate and appreciate diversity; our unique perspectives and abilities enrich us all and lead to innovative approaches and solutions.


Equity: We champion equity, recognizing that each of us need different things to thrive.


Inclusion: We intentionally create and hold space so that we all have meaningful opportunities to participate and contribute to Ecology’s work.


Respect: We treat each other with respect and dignity, acknowledging the inherent worth of our diverse perspectives and lived experiences, even in times of uncertainty and disagreement.


We believe that DEIR is both a goal and an action. We are on a journey, honoring our shared humanity and taking steps to demonstrate our commitment to a vision where each of us is heard, seen, and valued.

Ecology seeks diverse applicants: We view diversity, equity, inclusion, and respect through a broad lens including race, ethnicity, class, age, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, immigration status, military background, language, education, life experience, physical disability, neurodiversity, and intersectional identities. Qualified job seekers from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

title: Director, Guest Experience and Volunteer Programs
description:
Who We Are

Founded in 1926, the Colonial Williamsburg Foundation is a private, not-for-profit educational, historic, and cultural institution that owns and operates one of the largest and best-known museum complexes in the world. Our mission is “that the future may learn from the past” through preserving and restoring 18th-century Williamsburg, Virginia’s colonial capital. We engage, inform, and inspire people to learn about this historic capital, the events that occurred here, and the diverse peoples who helped shape a new nation.

Today, Colonial Williamsburg is the largest living history museum in the U.S. The Historic Area is the 301-acre restored colonial capital with 89 original buildings and 525 buildings reconstructed to how they appeared in the 18th century through extensive archaeological, architectural, and documentary research. The Historic Area is staffed by highly trained, historically dressed interpreters and expert tradespeople who bring the 18th century to life. The Foundation also owns and operates two world-class museums, the DeWitt Wallace Decorative Arts Museum, and the Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Folk Art Museum, The Bob and Marion Wilson Teacher Institute, and a renowned research library, the John D Rockefeller Jr Library.

Additionally, Colonial Williamsburg is home to five world class accommodations at the Williamsburg Inn, Williamsburg Lodge Autograph Collection, the Griffin Hotel, the Williamsburg Woodlands Hotels and Suites and the unique Colonial Houses in the Historical Area. Visitors may also indulge in food and drink at our many on site restaurants and taverns that blend a historically inspired dining experience with today’s evolved tastes. Each year over five million people visit Williamsburg and another 20 million engage with us digitally.

***This position is an onsite position and candidates must reside in or be ready to relocate to Virginia at time of hire***

About the Position

Main Duties:

1. Guest Experience Strategy and Service Framework
Develop and maintain an enterprise-wide guest experience strategy that defines how Colonial Williamsburg's Common Purpose (mission), Service Standards, Service Behaviors, and Leader Behaviors should be reflected at every touchpoint across the guest journey. Establish a practical framework that operating areas can use to adapt and translate service expectations into day-to-day guest interactions, decisions, and improvement priorities.

2. Volunteer Programs Leadership and Oversight
Provide strategic and operational oversight for Colonial Williamsburg Volunteer Programs across all areas of the organization. Directly supervise the Manager, Volunteer Programs and provide leadership oversight for multiple Supervisors, Volunteer Programs. Establish clear priorities, accountability, staffing structures, and consistent enterprise practices for recruiting, selecting, placing, onboarding, training, scheduling, supervising, evaluating, recognizing, and retaining more than 800 volunteers.

3. Volunteer Program Growth, Wayfinding, and Liberty Lounge Operations
Lead the planned expansion of Colonial Williamsburg Volunteer Programs by 200-300 individuals. Oversee the design, build-out, launch, and continuing operation of the Wayfinding volunteer program, including role design, recruitment, training, deployment, service expectations, and coordination with operating areas. Maintain leadership accountability for the Liberty Lounge operation, including supervisory coverage, volunteer preparedness, consistent service, operating coordination, and a welcoming experience for active-duty, veteran, and retired military members and their families.

4. Guest Experience Analytics Leadership and Analyst Supervision
Directly supervise the full-time Analyst, Guest Experience and Volunteer Programs, and establish priorities for enterprise guest experience measurement and analysis. Ensure the Analyst maintains reliable guest experience metrics, develops recurring and ad hoc summaries for operating areas and leadership audiences, and presents information in forms appropriate to each audience. Guide the Analyst in identifying trends, recurring concerns, emerging service issues, and data signals that may warrant service recovery, escalation, or additional operational review. Ensure that analytical work supports timely decisions, cross-functional improvement, and clear accountability while distinguishing what the data establish from what requires further investigation.

5. Common Purpose, Service Standards, and Service Behaviors
Serve as the primary organizational steward for the guest-facing application of Colonial Williamsburg's Common Purpose, Service Standards, and Service Behaviors. Partner with Hospitality, Historic Area, Museums, Operations, and other guest-facing functions to keep standards clear, relevant, observable, coachable, and measurable. Recommend revisions when evidence shows that standards or behaviors need clarification or adjustment.

6. Guest Journey and Experience Mapping
Lead enterprise experience mapping to understand the guest journey across pre-arrival, arrival, on-site experiences, transitions between locations, departure, and post-visit contact. Identify important handoffs, friction points, inconsistent experiences, and opportunities to improve clarity, ease, hospitality, and continuity across departments and locations. Use experience maps to support specific cross-functional improvement work rather than as stand-alone planning documents.

7. Voice of the Guest and Feedback Systems
Support and coordinate guest feedback systems across Colonial Williamsburg, including surveys, direct comments, digital feedback, online reviews, correspondence, and other appropriate listening channels. Establish consistent practices for collecting, categorizing, routing, and reviewing guest feedback so that information is timely, usable, and connected to the operating area able to respond or improve.

8. Guest Experience Performance Dashboard
Direct and oversee development and maintenance of an enterprise Guest Experience Performance Dashboard that provides a clear view of guest experience performance across Colonial Williamsburg. Through the Analyst, Guest Experience and Volunteer Programs, integrate guest satisfaction, NPS, service recovery activity, guest feedback themes, recurring concerns, and other appropriate measures. Ensure information is presented at an enterprise level while allowing leaders to understand meaningful variation by location, function, touchpoint, or time period where the data support that level of analysis.

9. Guest Metrics and Trend Analysis
Oversee the analysis of guest satisfaction results, NPS, feedback themes, service recovery data, and other available indicators to identify patterns and emerging issues. Direct the Analyst, Guest Experience and Volunteer Programs in maintaining routine metric reviews, preparing summaries, distinguishing one-time incidents from recurring conditions, and identifying data signals that may require service recovery or further investigation. Work with leaders and managers to determine where corrective action or additional review is warranted, and track trends over time to determine whether improvement efforts are producing the intended result.

10. Service Recovery Framework
Establish and maintain an enterprise service recovery framework that defines how employees and leaders should respond when the guest experience falls short. Set clear expectations for acknowledgment, ownership, response, follow-through, documentation, and appropriate recovery while allowing operating areas sufficient discretion to address the circumstances of an individual guest. Reinforce the principle that effective recovery should resolve the immediate concern and help prevent recurrence.

11. Escalation and Resolution Standards
Define practical standards for guest issue escalation and resolution, including when concerns should remain with the operating area and when they should move to higher levels of review. Clarify responsibility, expected response times, documentation, follow-up, and closure. Review significant or recurring escalations to identify process gaps, unclear ownership, or operational conditions that require broader attention.

12. Cross-Functional Guest Experience Improvement
Facilitate cross-functional improvement efforts when guest experience issues extend across departments, locations, systems, or stages of the guest journey. Bring together the appropriate leaders, define the problem using available evidence, identify the responsible owners, establish actions and timelines, and monitor progress. Focus improvement work on specific guest consequences and measurable operating conditions.

13. Field Observation and Experience Consistency
Maintain a regular presence across guest-facing areas to observe the experience as it is delivered and to understand how service expectations operate in different settings. Use structured observation, guest comments, leader input, and available performance information to identify inconsistent practices or conditions. Share findings with responsible leaders and support practical improvements while respecting operational ownership.

14. Service Training Partnership
Partner with the Director, Learning and Development to design, maintain, and reinforce guest-facing service training. Ensure training reflects Colonial Williamsburg's Common Purpose, Service Standards, Service Behaviors, service recovery expectations, communication practices, and the realities of different guest-facing roles. Use guest feedback and observed service patterns to identify training needs and evaluate whether training is improving behavior and guest outcomes.

15. Leader and Employee Service Reinforcement
Working with the Manager, Employee Engagement, provide leaders with practical tools and guidance for reinforcing guest experience expectations in daily operations. Support leaders in observing service behaviors, providing timely feedback, coaching employees, discussing guest feedback, and using service standards to guide decisions. Work with Learning and Development and Employee Engagement to strengthen consistent reinforcement rather than relying only on formal training events.

16. Employee and Guest Experience Connection
Work closely with the Manager, Employee Engagement to reinforce the relationship between employee experience and guest experience. Share guest feedback and service examples that can support recognition of employees and volunteers who demonstrate outstanding service. Identify, where evidence permits, employee experience conditions that may be associated with recurring guest experience patterns and bring those findings to the appropriate leaders.

17. Positive Guest Feedback and Recognition Partnership
Create a reliable process for identifying positive guest comments that recognize exceptional service by employees or volunteers. Coordinate with the Manager, Employee Engagement so that guest recognition is validated, shared promptly with the employee or volunteer and leader, and connected to Colonial Williamsburg's Common Purpose, Service Standards, and Service Behaviors when appropriate.

18. Internal Communication and Guest Experience Alignment
Partner with Internal Communications to ensure employees receive clear and useful information about guest experience priorities, recurring guest needs, service expectations, and significant changes that affect the guest journey. Where appropriate, work with Internal Communications to examine communication reach, readership, engagement, message clarity, and employee understanding when those measures may help explain service consistency or guest experience results.

19. Integrated Experience Analytics and Correlation
Work with Internal Communications, operating leaders, and other data owners to examine relationships among employee experience, communication effectiveness, guest experience, and operational performance. Use correlation and comparative analysis cautiously, distinguish association from causation, and clearly identify data limitations. Use findings to generate questions, target further review, or support improvement decisions rather than making claims the data cannot support.

20. Guest Accessibility and Inclusive Experience
Review guest experience practices with attention to accessibility, clarity, differing abilities, age, language needs, and other factors that can affect a guest's ability to navigate and enjoy Colonial Williamsburg. Partner with the appropriate subject matter experts and operating teams to identify barriers, improve communication and service practices, and help ensure that service standards are applied consistently to a diverse guest population.

21. Guest Experience Technology and Data Stewardship
Evaluate and support technology used for guest feedback, survey administration, service recovery tracking, experience reporting, and related guest experience functions. Establish sound practices for data quality, access, categorization, documentation, and retention in coordination with technology, privacy, legal, and operational partners. Ensure systems produce reliable information for timely action and longitudinal analysis.

22. Reporting and Executive Insights
Direct preparation of regular guest experience reports and concise decision-ready insights for the Vice President, Organizational Culture, executive leadership, and relevant leadership and culture teams. Use the Analyst, Guest Experience and Volunteer Programs to develop audience-appropriate summaries, dashboards, and supporting analysis for enterprise and operating-area needs. Explain what the data show, what they suggest, what cannot yet be determined, and where action is recommended. Highlight significant trends, recurring guest concerns, service recovery performance, cross-functional issues, and progress on agreed improvement actions.

23. Guest Experience Governance and Continuous Improvement
Establish practical governance for enterprise guest experience work, including definitions, reporting standards, ownership, review cadence, documentation, and improvement follow-through. Maintain a disciplined process for reviewing performance, selecting priorities, assigning accountability, and evaluating results. Help create a culture in which guest feedback is used constructively, service expectations are reinforced consistently, and recurring problems lead to specific improvement work.

This job description reflects the general responsibilities of the position and is not intended to be an exhaustive list. Duties and responsibilities may evolve over time based on operational needs.

title: Structural Steel Detailer
description:
Key Responsibilities

  • Model and detail structural steel in SDS/2 (SDS2025 or SDS2026), producing complete and accurate shop drawings, erection drawings, and associated deliverables.
  • Perform checker duties on projects detailed by others: verify dimensions, connections, member sizes, quantities, bolt schedules, hole types, weld symbols, and compliance with project specifications and standards.
  • Export, organize, and transmit CNC files to the shop floor, including (as applicable) NC1/DSTV, DXF, EJE, and other machine-specific formats.
  • Generate and maintain job-ready reports and supporting documents (bolt lists, part/assembly lists, cut lists, shipping tickets, revision logs, RFIs, transmittals).
  • Coordinate with project managers, engineers, and the shop to clarify design intent, resolve clashes, and address RFIs and redlines in a timely manner.
  • Apply revision control: update models, drawings, and CNC outputs; clearly cloud and record changes; reissue affected deliverables.
  • Prepare CNC programs and nests for the 10'×20' plasma plate table using Steel Solutions; prepare production files and manage runs for the Voortman V807 beam profiler using VACAM (training provided).
  • Adhere to internal quality standards, project schedules, naming conventions, and folder structures to ensure reliable handoff to fabrication and erection.
  • Support fabrication by responding to shop questions, verifying fit-up and sequence, and providing supplemental sketches when necessary.

Tools & Software You Will Use

  • SDS/2 (SDS2025 or SDS2026) for steel modeling, connections, detailing, reporting, and CNC exports.
  • Steel Solutions (for the 10'×20' plasma plate table).
  • Voortman VACAM for the V807 beam profiler.
  • Microsoft 365: Excel (lists, takeoffs, logs), Word (submittals, transmittals), Outlook/Teams (coordination).

Schedule & Employment

  • Full Time- 40 hours per week.
  • Work type: Onsite at Top Coat — Jones Creek, TX.
  • Work hours are flexible within typical shop hours.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience detailing structural steel using SDS/2 (required)
  • Ability to read and interpret architectural/structural drawings, specifications, and connection design requirements.
  • Working knowledge of AISC standards, welding symbols, bolting (AISC), hole types, and shop/field practices.
  • Experience producing shop and erection drawings, bills of material, and CNC exports from a 3D model.
  • Familiarity with common CNC export formats (e.g., NC1/DSTV, DXF; familiarity with EJE or similar job exports).
  • Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and methodical checking habits.
  • Proficient with Windows-based file management and Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Teams, Excel, Word).

Preferred Qualifications

  • 2+ years of structural steel detailing or checking experience in a fabrication environment.
  • Familiarity with Voortman V807 workflows using VACAM and with plate nesting workflows in Steel Solutions (training provided).
  • Experience coordinating with engineers of record, connection design partners, and general contractors.
  • Knowledge of model-based clash detection and QA processes; comfort working with reference models (IFC/STEP/DWG) is a plus.
  • Understanding of shop sequencing, kitting, and shipping documentation.

Additional Requirements

  • Work authorization in the United States.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality of project data and customer information.
  • Commitment to a safe, drug-free workplace and adherence to company policies and procedures.

Physical & Work Environment Requirements

  • Ability to sit at a computer for extended periods while modeling/checking.
  • Occasional shop floor walk-throughs; ability to use PPE and navigate an active fabrication environment.
  • Ability to lift up to 25–30 lbs. occasionally for samples or documents.

• Develop detailed project plans, schedules, resource allocation, and risk assessments.

• Lead cross-functional teams through the project lifecycle.

• Communicate clearly with clients and internal teams regarding progress, issues, and changes.

• Manage budgets, track expenditures, and provide status reports to senior leadership.

• Ensure compliance with company policies, standards, and regulatory requirements.

• Conduct project performance reviews using defined metrics and key performance indicators, driving continuous improvement post-completion.

• Teach and model project management and process improvement skills & methods to others in the organization.

Education and Experience:

• Competency and ability to guide others in using Lean process improvement and human-centered design methodologies.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

• Strong organizational, time-management, and communication skills.

• Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and work under pressure.

• Knowledge and effective use of change management methodology and principles.

• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, both verbal and written.

• Strong customer service orientation.

title: Population Health Specialist
description:
Akido builds AI-powered doctors. Akido is the first AI-native care provider, combining cutting-edge technology with a nationwide medical network to address America’s physician shortage and make exceptional healthcare universal. Its AI empowers doctors to deliver faster, more accurate, and more compassionate care.

Position Summary

The Population Health Specialist supports Akido's value-based care strategy by identifying, engaging, and coordinating care for patient populations requiring preventive services, chronic disease management, and care gap closure. This role collaborates with providers, clinic teams, health plans, and patients to improve quality outcomes, patient engagement, continuity of care, and access to services.

The Population Health Specialist utilizes population health tools, patient registries, quality reports, and outreach workflows to support HEDIS, STAR, risk adjustment, Annual Wellness Visits, and other quality initiatives while contributing to organizational performance and patient health outcomes.

Essential Functions

  • Conduct patient outreach and engagement activities to close preventive and chronic care gaps.
  • Coordinate appointments, screenings, referrals, and follow-up services.
  • Support organizational quality improvement and value-based care initiatives.
  • Maintain accurate patient documentation and outreach records.
  • Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to address barriers to care.
  • Monitor and track performance metrics related to population health outcomes.
  • Support patient retention, engagement, and continuity of care efforts.

Key Responsibilities

Population Health & Care Gap Management

  • Identify patients with open quality, preventive, and chronic care gaps through approved reports, registries, and work queues.
  • Conduct outreach through phone calls, text messaging, patient portals, and other approved communication channels.
  • Coordinate Annual Wellness Visits, preventive screenings, immunizations, specialty referrals, chronic disease follow-up, and diagnostic testing.
  • Document outreach efforts, patient responses, barriers, and intervention outcomes accurately and timely.
  • Prioritize patient outreach based on clinical risk, health plan requirements, and organizational goals.

Patient Engagement & Care Coordination

  • Serve as a primary point of contact for assigned patient populations.

  • Assist with chart review, data validation, documentation improvement, and quality audits.

  • Follow standardized workflows to ensure accurate quality reporting and compliance.

Data Management & Reporting

title: Copy of Assistant Project Manager
description:

description:

Job Summary: The CCS Mental Health Worker (MHW) provides direct services to adults in crisis at the CCS. The Mental Health Worker will carry a case load based on daily census and will provide direct care supports including admission, treatment planning, running groups, case management, and discharge. The Mental Health Worker ensures safety of all clients through provision of as needed 1:1 supervision, conducting and documenting checks, proactively addressing escalating behaviors. The MHW also provides for operation of the CCS in terms of meal set-up and clean-up; room maintenance; keeping the unit clean; and doing laundry. This is a non-exempt position. Essential Functions of Position:

Completes and documents admissions, treatment plans, client daily documentation, and discharge summaries in accordance with BCHS, DMH and applicable payer and regulatory standards.

Ensure that the unit follows the daily schedule of program activities, client meetings, and groups. Oversight of therapeutic groups as leader, co-leader, and observer.

Ensures for the cleanliness and upkeep of the unit, assists in meal preparation and cleanup, completes bed set up and gathers linens.

Maintains effective working relationships with insurers, DMH, local community resources, and treatment/rehabilitation programs throughout the Cape Cod community.

Participation in daily rounds with multidisciplinary team and follows up on identified issues for the unit and for the individual clients.

Ensures that safety protocols are routinely reviewed and followed consistently by all staff (such as emergency systems; identification and remedy of facility safety hazards; security systems; lock up of sharps and any potential toxins; hazardous waste management; checks protocols, checking vitals protocols, etc).

Support referrals and warm handoffs to Cape Cod CBHC outpatient, urgent, crisis, care coordination, peer, and recovery-support services under the direction of the clinical team.

Complete timely documentation in eHana and communicate information needed for CCS/CBHC admission, discharge, follow-up, and continuity-of-care workflows.

Participate in CCS/CBHC training, team consultation, and quality-improvement activities as assigned.

Performs all other duties and projects as assigned by supervisor.

Schedule/shift: Monday-Friday 7am-3pm

Full-time, part-time/per-diem schedule for each opening.

Minimally 3 years’ experience working in a mental health setting.

Excellent writing and oral communication skills.

Demonstrated skills in working as an effective team player in a fast-paced unit

Ability to work collaboratively as a member of multi-disciplinary and cross-functional teams.

Demonstrated ability to work in a pressured situation and maintain clarity, focus, judgment, and compassion

Ability to provide leadership

Ability to identify problems and initiate solutions to problems

Ability to work with people in crisis in a hopeful and compassionate manner and model this for others

Ability to work independently
