DLR Group’s Los Angeles studio has an opening for a Mechanical Engineering Summer Intern.

  • Los Angeles, CA

We have multiple positions and locations available; please refer to all openings posted and apply to the locations that are most suitable for your living situation during the course of your internship. This is not a remote position.

About EPX at DLR Group

As an intern at DLR Group, you’ll be part of our Emerging Professional Experience (EPX) Program, designed to give you a meaningful introduction to life within an integrated design firm and a strong foundation for your career in the AEC industry.

Each person at DLR Group has a design voice, and EPX gives you opportunities to develop and share yours. Through hands-on project work, mentorship, and learning experiences, you’ll gain exposure to the people, disciplines, and ideas that shape the built environment. You may participate in design discussions, project meetings, site visits, business development efforts, office activities, and other experiences that broaden your understanding of the design profession.

The program combines three core components: mentorship, project work, and weekly learning sessions. Topics may include design culture, sustainability, design technology, communication, marketing and business development, project and resource management, research, equity, career development, and more. Along the way, you’ll hear from leaders and integrated designers across DLR Group and build connections with fellow emerging professionals.

Position Summary

As a Mechanical Engineering Intern at DLR Group, you will be an important part of our integrated design team, contributing to the design of mechanical systems for buildings of various types, sizes, and complexities. Working alongside mechanical engineers and professionals across architecture, engineering, interiors, and other disciplines, you will gain hands-on experience with the design process from early concepts and system development through documentation and construction administration.

Our Summer Internship Program is a paid, full-time opportunity running May 18 through August 6, 2027, and interns are expected to participate for the duration of the program. This is an opportunity to apply what you’ve learned in the classroom, build your technical and professional skills, and contribute your perspective to design solutions that support our brand promise of Elevating the Human Experience through design.

What you will do

  • Work with a licensed engineer designing mechanical systems for new construction and/or building renovation projects
  • Attend design team meetings with a mechanical engineer and observe the coordination that occurs among the team members of a multi-disciplinary design team
  • Assist a mechanical engineer with the design and development of construction documents primarily using Revit
  • Visit an active construction site (contingent on the status of local construction projects)
  • Develop HVAC, plumbing, and fire protection designs from concept through completion

Required Qualifications:

  • Completed at least one year at an ABET-accredited Mechanical Engineering or Architectural Engineering program
  • Experience or interest in BIM (e.g. Autodesk Revit MEP) workflow

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam
  • Interest in architectural building design
  • A third-year student in an accredited engineering program

Our comprehensive Benefits at DLR Group include medical, dental, vision, disability, wellness programs, flex spending, paid holidays, and paid time off. Hourly Rate
$20—$26 USD

DLR Group is an integrated design firm delivering architecture, engineering, interiors, planning, and building optimization for new builds, renovations, and adaptive reuse projects.

Salary Type: Hourly

About the Role

Uber Freight is looking for Logistics Specialists to support dedicated customer accounts within our Managed Transportation organization. In this role, you will play a critical part in day-to-day transportation execution, helping ensure freight moves efficiently, service expectations are met, and customers receive a high level of operational support.

This role is ideal for individuals who enjoy problem-solving, multitasking, working cross-functionally, and building strong relationships with carriers and customers. You will gain exposure to transportation management systems, shipment execution, carrier operations, and customer communication while working alongside a highly collaborative team.

This position follows a hybrid work schedule (3 days in-office, 2 days remote) and is based out of our Rogers, AR office.

What The Candidate Will Do

  • Manage daily transportation execution activities for assigned customer accounts
  • Utilize Uber Freight’s Transportation Management System (TMS) to support the full shipment lifecycle, including load building, tendering, tracking, and updates
  • Coordinate with carriers, shippers, and receivers to ensure on-time pickup and delivery performance
  • Monitor shipment activity and proactively resolve operational issues, delays, or service disruptions
  • Support appointment scheduling and shipment visibility updates
  • Communicate professionally with customers and internal stakeholders regarding shipment status and operational impacts
  • Analyze shipment and carrier performance trends to identify opportunities for service improvement
  • Leverage routing guides and spot market options to support effective freight coverage and transportation solutions
  • Assist with resolving shipment data discrepancies and invoice-related issues within the TMS
  • Document and follow customer-specific operational procedures and workflows
  • Partner cross-functionally with internal operations, carrier management, and customer support teams to drive successful outcomes

Basic Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED equivalent

title: Professional Mentor - San Diego
description:
Friends of the Children is a nonprofit that is impacting generational change by empowering youth through relationships with professional mentors. We do this by providing children facing the most obstacles with a long-term, paid, professional mentor, who we call a “Friend,” from kindergarten through high school graduation, 12+ years – no matter what. We are currently seeking an extraordinary professional to embark on a new career journey as a Friend at our new San Diego location.

At Friends of the Children, we put children first and use our values to change the way the world treats and views youth facing great barriers. As a Friend you will nurture long-term relationships from a foundation of love, acceptance, and practices. Do you want to help urban, rural, and Indigenous youth discover their limitless potential, by fostering their internal resiliency? Are you ready to help build relationships within the communities of our youth and families to strengthen social networks and provide bridges to new opportunities? If so, the impactful role of a Friend might be for you.

Basic Function / Position Objective:

We are currently seeking a mentor to serve as a positive adult role model to eight elementary children (kindergarten to 5th Grade) and develop loving, caring, and sustained relationships with each child. For each child, a Friend will set positive expectations; nurture and promote each child’s strength, talents, and abilities; help ensure physical and emotional well-being; teach life and academic skills; provide enrichment activities; and model responsible behavior. A Friend will fully document activities and participate in the ongoing evaluation process. Friends will work primarily one-on-one with the children they serve, while also building trusting supportive relationships with parents/caregivers. A Friend must know, understand, honor, and support the organization’s mission, vision, values, and principles, and be able to clearly articulate the organization’s function.

Essential Functions and Responsibilities:

  • Develop and sustain a long-term, caring, protective, and loving relationship with each child.
  • Spend time with children, one-on-one.
  • Partner with parents/caregivers to provide concrete and social emotional supports for the family.
  • Set realistic expectations and goals based on each child’s strengths, talents, abilities, and needs.
  • Teach life skills and help develop a talent/skill/area of interest with each child.
  • Deepen connections for youth through incorporating specific cultural knowledge in programming.
  • Provide enrichment resources and activities that include opportunities for cultural identity development.
  • Develop positive relationships with families, teachers, and others involved in each child’s life.
  • Reinforce basic academic skills.
  • Maintain a 40-hour work schedule that includes afternoons, evenings, and weekends (normal working days are Tuesday through Saturday with Sundays and Mondays off).
  • Maintain spending within budgetary guidelines.
  • Complete, distribute, and collect time summaries, activity journals, short-term plans, expense reports, and evaluations materials accurately and in a timely manner.
  • Attend and actively participate in team meeting and staff functions.
  • Maintain First Aid/CPR certification.
  • Transport children in personal vehicle as required for mentoring activities.
  • Provide information and support to the development and executive team on related activities.
  • Fulfill other responsibilities as requested.

The ideal candidate will have the following Education, Experience, and Abilities:

  • 2 or 4-year degree
    • Alternatively, at least seven years’ progressive experience working with children and families will be considered in lieu of a college degree
  • Willingness to commit for a minimum of three years.
  • Advocate to secure additional resources, opportunities, and services for youth as appropriate
  • Assist with systems navigation in schools to secure conditions for optimal academic success
  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Demonstrated ability to work with children in varied capacities and settings
  • Ability to develop trusting relationships with children, families, teachers, and others involved in each child’s life
  • Ability to work independently and as a team player
  • Ability to manage several concurrent issues and solve problems effectively
  • Strong written and verbal communications skills
  • Strong organizational and time management skills
  • A sense of humor is a plus

Benefits

  • 3 weeks paid vacation. Comprehensive health, dental, vision, and long-term disability, 401k with 3% match.

Compensation:

  • $50,000 ‒ $60,000 Annually

Reports To:

  • Program Director

Location:

  • San Diego, California

Cover Letter: Applications without cover letters will not be considered; please use this as an opportunity to convey why you want to be a Professional Mentor at Friends of the Children – San Diego!

Friends of the Children is growing rapidly as communities across the country are experiencing the power of how “One” changes a child's story: One Friend. One Child. 12+ years. No matter what. #ThePowerOfOne

title: Training Specialist
description:

title: Market Engagement Representative
description:
Join Our Team at IVX Health!

IVX Health is seeking a Market Engagement Representative (MER) to identify, qualify, and advance referral opportunities across assigned markets. This marketing-aligned, field-enablement role supports Business Development Managers by generating leads, gathering market intelligence, and ensuring opportunities are well-documented and ready for productive field engagement. This role is ideal for a highly organized professional who enjoys research, relationship-building, and supporting growth through informed market execution.

What You'll Do

  • Generate & Qualify Opportunities: Identify referral opportunities at the location level and research key market insights, including prescribing patterns, therapy mix, site-of-care preferences, referral workflows, clinic schedules, and key contacts.
  • Support Business Development Managers: Partner closely with assigned BDMs to prioritize and advance opportunities. Provide relevant background and market intelligence to help field teams conduct informed, high-value conversations.
  • Support Marketing Campaigns: Follow up on engagement signals generated through corporate marketing initiatives and help convert interest into qualified opportunities. Serve as a bridge between corporate marketing and local market execution.
  • Maintain CRM Excellence: Accurately document research, outreach activity, lead status, meetings, and outcomes in Sugar or other CRM systems. Maintain timely, accurate records to support reporting, forecasting, and pipeline visibility.
  • Strengthen Market Engagement: Ensure outreach is professional, consistent, and aligned with IVX Health messaging and brand standards. Collaborate with marketing and sales leadership to refine lead criteria and engagement strategies.
  • Maintain Performance & Accountability: Meet defined activity, quality, and documentation expectations while maintaining responsiveness to field partners and marketing leadership in a remote environment.

Essential Competencies & Skills

  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to research, synthesize, and clearly document market intelligence.
  • Comfort working in CRM systems; experience with Sugar preferred.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple markets, priorities, and stakeholders.
  • Collaborative, service-oriented approach to supporting field teams.
  • Understanding of referral workflows, provider office operations, or site-of-care dynamics.

Required Education & Experience

title: Youth Advocate
description:
Job Title:

Youth Advocate

Department:

SOC/Youth United

Reports to:

Regional Youth Coordinator

FLSA:

Non-Exempt

Division

Community Partnerships & Projects

Location

Hybrid

Business Unit

Community Partnerships & Projects

Grade level

5

This position offers a starting hourly range of $16.98 - $20.38 per year, depending on experience and qualifications.

Children’s Center of Wayne County (TCC) The Children’s Center, founded in 1929, provides evidence-based clinical therapy to children who deal with mental, behavioral, emotional, intellectual, and developmental health and educational challenges or may have experienced trauma.

School + Community-Based Partnerships: We partner with K-12 schools and community organizations that serve children to provide clinical therapy, counseling, psychological services, and psychiatric evaluations, treatment & interventions.

Child Welfare: In addition to the clinical therapy programs offered, The Children’s Center places children in licensed foster homes, and supports them throughout their time in the child welfare system.

Child Well-being + Family Success: We operate an onsite family success center that promotes child-wellbeing and offers children and youth from all walks of life to access relevant mental health crisis prevention and child abuse and neglect prevention services.

Advocacy: We champion child and youth well-being for those experiencing poverty-related issues, those within the child welfare system, and those in need of evidence-based, clinical therapy.

TCC’s mission is to help children and families shape their own futures. If as many children as possible, and their families can easily access comprehensive, evidence-based, clinical therapy that is integrated into and supports their everyday lives then, children will experience an improved quality of life where they have a true sense of agency and empowerment in their lives.

We embrace and demonstrate a set of Core Values as the foundation of our culture. They define how we do what we do, and what we value in our work with each other and our community. Daily demonstration of these values, in mindset and behavior, is required to be successful as a TCC team member.

  • Dedicated-We are devoted, dedicated and always willing to pitch to accomplish our mission.
  • Passionate-We are passionate about what we do and helping the people we serve.
  • Accountable-We do what we say and accomplish all aspects of our responsibilities.
  • Can Do Attitude- We approach our responsibilities with a positive attitude.
  • Respectful- We always treat co-workers, donors, children and families with the utmost respect, courtesy, and patience.

Job Summary

Youth Advocates, employed by The Children’s Center, serve as representatives of the Youth United Initiative led by the Detroit Wayne Integrated Health Network. Youth United is a youth-led initiative that promotes youth voice, youth involvement, and positive youth development throughout Wayne County’s System of Care. Youth Advocates promote and advocate on behalf of youth ages 14-25 who are actively involved in the mental health, child welfare, special education, foster care, and/or juvenile justice systems. Youth United advocates by providing positive youth involvement activities and workshops to youth in Wayne County in the areas/regions of leadership, stigma reduction and advocacy.

Job Requirements

  • Must be between the ages of 17-23 years old.
  • Current or prior involvement with mental health, child welfare, special education, and/or the juvenile justice system is required. Second-hand experience is acceptable as well (i.e. having a family member involved in the mental health system).
  • High School Diploma or Equivalent
  • Basic knowledge of the Wayne County system of care (mental health, child welfare, special education, foster care and/or juvenile justice services) and community resources for youth.
  • Knowledge of issues and needs that today’s youth are experiencing
  • Have past leadership, work, or volunteer experience
  • Ability to demonstrate basic computer skills including familiarity with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Teams, PPT), Canva and/or graphic design tools, and general office equipment.
  • Knowledge of social media, including how to create posts, share information, and align with current social media trends and topics
  • Ability to effectively manage time, information, and meet deadlines
  • Ability to work in a team environment and independently
  • Strong communication, critical thinking, and creativity skills
  • Event planning experience is a plus
  • Must be able to work some evenings and weekends
  • Must be able to provide clearance that there is no record and/or convictions as a perpetrator of child abuse and/or neglect in the State of Michigan Child Abuse/Neglect Central Registry and other states of residency over the past 5 years.
  • Must have reliable transportation to and from work sites. If driving, you must be able to provide proof of having a current valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and current automobile insurance.

Essential Functions

  • Use of personal expertise to advocate for Wayne County Connections (System of Care) and provide training to staff and other stakeholders regarding youth involvement, positive youth development, and youth-led programming and participation.
  • Work directly with Regional Youth Coordinator/Supervisor to identify and support youth involvement activities and programming.
  • Participate in the System of Care Advisory Council, which will advise Connections Cross System Transformation team on youth related programming and policies.
  • Participate in activities as requested by The Children’s Center, Detroit Wayne Integrated Health Network, and other local, state, or national stakeholders.
  • Participate in the planning of various events and workshops geared towards youth and community engagement.
  • Participate in evaluating existing programs for youth.
  • Be able to work flexible hours, including weekends and evenings.
  • Recruit youth participants through written, phone, and face to face outreach.
  • Help plan and facilitate morale boosting and team building activities.
  • Assist in identifying youth-led activities related to assigned focus area (stigma, advocacy, training).
  • Develop Performance Goals and Expectations with immediate supervisor annually.
  • Support the values of The Children's Center's mission and the commitment to the ongoing safety and family stability.
  • Collaborate and maintain professional standards at all times while conducting agency business.
  • Assist with coordinating Youth United’s Youth MOVE Detroit Advisory Council.
  • Create and identify content for Youth United and Youth MOVE Detroit’s social media pages.
  • Be able to conduct public speaking and group facilitation at youth related events.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • 100% completion of the annual Wayne County Youth United Workplan Initiatives for Central Region
  • Plan and implement two advocacy events, per year
  • Maintain a minimum of five active youth members on the Youth MOVE Detroit Advisory Council
  • Participate in 6 community events per year to raise awareness of youth related issues

Additional Functions

  • Contribute to a positive workplace culture that demonstrates evidence of high accountability, inclusivity, and collaboration.
  • Demonstrate a commitment to anti-racist practices, diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.
  • Actively support and encourage creating a safe, welcoming, and inclusive administrative and service delivery environment.
  • Adhere to best practices, ethical standards, and compliance with relevant laws and regulations.
  • Physical Requirements
  • Hybrid work environment, with a required 2 days in the office per week
  • Must be able to attend in person events when scheduled
  • Ability to lift up to 10 lbs.
  • Ability to sit for extended periods of times.
  • Ability to stand for extended periods of times.

Other

  • Youth Advocates will assist the Youth United team members at Black Family Development Inc., Detroit Wayne Integrated Health Network, and MiSide, with various youth related tasks.

title: Software Engineer II
description:
Yugabyte is the company behind YugabyteDB, the AI-ready, multi-modal, distributed PostgreSQL database for cloud-native apps. Trusted by industry leaders including Shopify, Paramount+, GM, Kroger, Fiserv, and NPCI, YugabyteDB has been deployed in over 100 countries and powers more than 5 million clusters worldwide.

Together, our hard-working team of experts and our industry-leading technology are uniquely positioned to meet the demands of modern workloads: geo-distributed, ultra-resilient, and built to scale without limits.

Our Yugabeings (distributed, like our database) span 12+ countries and multiple time zones, sharing expertise from diverse backgrounds and industries.

Software Engineer – Core Database

Location: Sunnyvale, United States
Team: Core Database
Position Level: Software Engineer

About Yugabyte

At Yugabyte, we are on a mission to become the default transactional database for enterprises building cloud-native applications. YugabyteDB is our PostgreSQL compatible distributed database for cloud-native apps. Resilient, scalable, and flexible, it runs on any cloud and enables developers to become instantly productive using well-known APIs.We are looking for talented and driven people to join us on our ambitious mission and help us build a lasting and impactful company. The transactional database market is estimated to grow to $150B by 2030. YugabyteDB is cloud-native by design, has on-demand horizontal scalability, and supports geographical distribution of data using built-in replication. This means that we are well-positioned to meet market demand for geo-distributed, high-scale, high-performance workloads.

Yugabyte offers a culture of innovation, ownership, and technical excellence, with opportunities to impact a cutting-edge distributed SQL database used by global enterprises.

Role Overview

As a Software Engineer on the Core Database Engineering team, you will have an opportunity to work across the SQL layer, query execution, storage, replication, and transactional subsystems of YugabyteDB. You will collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to solve complex problems, ensuring YugabyteDB remains robust, reliable, and performance at scale.

This role is designed for engineers who are excited about databases, distributed systems, and systems programming, and want hands-on experience building a large-scale, production-grade distributed database.

Key Responsibilities

  • Write high-quality C/C++ code (and contribute in other languages as needed) with comprehensive automated tests; participate actively in code reviews.
  • Add unit tests, integration tests, and regression tests to ensure correctness and stability
  • Improve database scalability and throughput as cluster sizes and transaction volumes grow.
  • Contribute to the open source YugabyteDB project and help strengthen our distributed SQL capabilities across releases.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve correctness, stability, and performance issues in complex distributed query planning and execution paths.
  • Design, implement, and test features in YugabyteDB under the guidance of senior engineers
  • Collaborate with engineers across query, storage, and platform teams

Required Qualifications

  • 1–4 years in software engineering, with a strong foundation in compiled languages such as C/C++.
  • Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Computer Science (or related field), or equivalent practical experience.
  • Understanding of systems engineering fundamentals, including operating systems, distributed systems, and databases.
  • Strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and operating systems
  • Experience programming in C/C++, Java, or similar systems-level languages
  • Basic understanding of concurrency, threading, or distributed systems concepts
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to operate effectively in a collaborative, distributed team environment

Preferred Skills

  • Coursework or hands-on experience in distributed systems or storage systems
  • Exposure to databases, SQL, or PostgreSQL (academic or professional)
  • Familiarity with PostgreSQL internals or other relational database engines.
  • Familiarity with concepts such as replication, transactions, or fault tolerance
  • Contributions to open source database or systems projects.

We work in a hybrid model, with the team together in our Sunnyvale office 2–3 days per week.

Work Authorization

This position is based in the U.S. Candidates must have authorization to work in the United States. Sponsorship may be considered only under specific circumstances aligned with current regulatory requirements.

We feel strongly about equal pay for equal work, and transparency in compensation is one way to help achieve that. The cash compensation for this role is market competitive, with a range of USD 150,000-USD 170,000, inclusive of variable/incentive for some roles. As well as equity (when applicable), and benefits including health plans, retirement plans, and unlimited paid time off (PTO). The pay range for this position is a general guideline only and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. The actual pay will vary based on factors including experience, qualifications, and skill level.

title: Sr. Software Development Engineer, EC2 Blackfoot Peering Team
description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Do you want to solve real customer problems through innovative technology? Do you enjoy working on scalable services in a collaborative team environment? Do you want to see your code directly impact millions of customers worldwide?

Amazon EC2 Blackfoot Peering team is looking for a Software Development Engineer to lead a team contributing towards building a forwarding and encapsulation services in EC2 to support large scale networking and new features within AWS Private Gateway Networking Org.

We are growing fast, and are looking for kernel/embedded C programmers who can deliver ultra-high performance - our goal is to be processing many millions of packets per second on embedded CPU cores. This requires both being able to implement highly optimized data structures, but also low level tuning to our hardware. If you have good experience in C/C++, and a passion for systems software engineering such as kernel or embedded development, then this is a unique opportunity to join us in building the platform which is the basis for all new EC2 VPC features in the years to come.

Dataplane engineers work on a lower level of the software stack that directly interacts with hardware, and therefore need knowledge of the hardware also. They aren’t pure software developers that can program to any platform where the underlying hardware is abstracted from them. They require knowledge of the programming languages optimized for lower level programming such as C, C++, Rust, Assembly Language. We require them to be able to read a hardware specification for a Network Card and be able to optimize their code to run on it.

You can have an immediate impact for all of our customers including internal customers such as AWS Lambda, and external customers that run on Amazon EC2 as we deploy new features and updates regularly and often.

With the extensive network and access to Principal, Sr. Principal and Distinguished Engineers across EC2, AWS and Amazon, there are many stretch opportunities to grow your skills and knowledge.


Key job responsibilities
- Being an engineer on a small team, mentoring junior engineers, ensuring the right development practices are followed.
- Be very hands-on; work with the engineering team to manage the day-to-day development activities by leading architecture decisions, participating in designs, design review, code review, and implementation.
- Maintain current technical knowledge to support rapidly changing technology, always on a look out for new technologies and work with management and development team in bringing new technologies.
- Communicating with users, other technical teams, and senior management to collect requirements, describe software product features, technical designs, and product strategy

A day in the life
Our team also puts a high value on work-life balance. Striking a healthy balance between your personal and professional life is crucial to your happiness and success here, which is why we aren’t focused on how many hours you spend at work or online. Instead, we’re happy to offer a flexible schedule so you can have a more productive and well-balanced life—both in and outside of work.

About the team
Blackfoot Peering team is dedicated to supporting new team members. Our team has a broad mix of experience levels and Amazon tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. Our senior/experienced engineers truly enjoy mentoring more junior engineers and engineers from non-traditional backgrounds through one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews. We care about your career growth. We try to assign projects and tasks based on what will help each team member develop into a better-rounded engineer and enable them to take on more complex tasks in the future.

title: Corporate Credit Funds - Director (Chicago)
description:
Position Title: Corporate Credit Funds - Director (Chicago)

Entity: Kroll Bond Rating Agency, LLC

Employment Type: Full-time

Location: Chicago, IL

Summary/Overview:

KBRA (Kroll Bond Rating Agency, LLC) is seeking a Director to join our growing Corporate Credit Funds team in the Chicago office. The Corporate Credit Funds team assigns and monitors credit ratings on various debt instruments backed by portfolios of middle market corporate loans, including senior secured direct lending investments, along with other corporate loans, notes, and bonds.

The team focuses on private credit and direct lending transactions, including feeder fund rated notes, master fund credit facilities, middle market CLOs, corporate loan and bond portfolios, and select synthetic risk transfer structures. The team evaluates financing solutions that enable capital formation, fund investment, and liquidity management for private credit managers and institutional investors.

A strong candidate will have significant experience in corporate credit, private credit, direct lending, or structured credit, with a deep understanding of portfolio construction, asset performance, structural protections, and cash flow dynamics. The primary focus of this role is fund debt transactions supported by portfolios of middle market direct lending investments, primarily senior secured corporate loans, as well as other corporate credit instruments; however, experience in CLOs or structured credit is highly relevant, as the analytical skills, including collateral pool assessment, tranche risk analysis, cash flow modeling, and structural review, are transferable.

About the Job:

  • Lead the new issuance rating process, including evaluation of transaction capital structures, legal protections, collateral quality, portfolio composition, asset performance, and cash flow dynamics.
  • Analyze portfolios of corporate loans, bonds, and other credit instruments, including middle market and sponsor-backed exposures.
  • Conduct due diligence meetings with asset managers, direct lenders, arrangers, and issuers to assess underwriting standards, portfolio management practices, risk management frameworks, and performance history.
  • Prepare rating memoranda and new issuance reports, and present recommendations to rating committees.
  • Lead ongoing monitoring and surveillance of outstanding transactions, tracking portfolio performance, credit migration, and concentration trends.
  • Develop and maintain complex financial models to assess collateral performance, cash flow coverage, stress scenarios, and structural resilience.
  • Collaborate with KBRA experts across structured credit, corporate finance, financial institutions, and ABS to evaluate cross-sector and hybrid portfolio transactions.
  • Supervise and mentor junior team members, fostering strong analytical development and professional growth.
  • Lead or assist in developing analytical tools and standardized frameworks to enhance consistency, transparency, and efficiency in new issuance and surveillance processes.
  • Represent KBRA at industry conferences, panels, and investor meetings, sharing insights on private credit, direct lending, and portfolio finance trends.
  • Contribute to credit research and publications related to corporate portfolio finance, direct lending, and structured credit markets.

You will be successful in this role if you have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business, Economics or Math related fields.
  • Eight (8) or more years of work experience in corporate credit analysis, private credit, direct lending, fund investing, CLO analysis, or structured finance.
  • Experience reviewing legal documents and strong understanding of liability structures, LTV/advance rates, payment priorities, and structural protections.
  • Advanced proficiency in Excel is required to build and analyze excel based financial models to assess asset cash flow projections, and debt repayment under stress scenarios
  • Ability to assess creditworthiness of funds, assets, and counterparties; understanding how this applies to rating methodologies.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills to prepare clear, concise, and well-reasoned credit memos and reports and present them to committees in an efficient manner.
  • Strong interpersonal skills to work as an integral part of a highly collaborative team and across disciplines in a challenging and dynamic environment and effectively manage internal and external relationships.
  • CFA or MBA is a plus
  • Ability to manage time and resources in fast-growing company.
  • Familiarity with Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT for research, data insights, and general productivity is a plus.

Salary Range:

The anticipated annual base salary range for this full-time position is $150,000 to $175,000. Offer amounts are determined by factors such as experience, skills, geography, and other job-related factors.

Benefits:

  • A hybrid work schedule (Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursdays in the office)
  • Competitive benefits and paid time off
  • Paid family and disability leave
  • 401(k) plan, including employer match (100% vested)
  • Educational and professional development financial assistance
  • Employee referral bonus program

About Us

Kroll Bond Rating Agency, LLC (KBRA) is a full-service credit rating agency registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission as an NRSRO. Kroll Bond Rating Agency Europe Limited is registered as a CRA with the European Securities and Markets Authority. Kroll Bond Rating Agency UK Limited is registered as a CRA with the UK Financial Conduct Authority pursuant to the Temporary Registration Regime. In addition, KBRA is designated as a designated rating organization by the Ontario Securities Commission for issuers of asset-backed securities to file a short form prospectus or shelf prospectus. KBRA is also recognized by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners as a Credit Rating Provider.

title: Director of Product Operations
description:
Position Summary:

Build the operating engine behind products that make healthcare data work harder. HHIT is looking for a Director of Product Operations who can turn strategy into momentum across our product portfolio. You will design and lead the governance, processes, metrics, release disciplines, and cross-functional programs that move ideas from discovery to launch, and from launch to lasting adoption, with clarity, consistency, and accountability. You will also lead product distribution and enablement, making it easier for employees, customers, and partners to understand, demonstrate, implement, support, and confidently use our solutions. By transforming complex capabilities into scalable training, documentation, communications, and adoption resources, you will create more space for Product Management to focus on strategy, discovery, customer engagement, and roadmap execution. This highly visible role connects teams across HHIT and will evolve alongside our products, customers, regulations, technology, and priorities.


This position is an in-office or hybrid role (three days in-office, two days remote) if local to South Bend.


Primary Responsibilities:

Product Operations & Governance

  • Design the playbook: Define and execute the Product Operations strategy, operating model, standards, and governance practices that translate company and product priorities into coordinated action.
  • Create clarity from idea to impact: Establish lifecycle and stage-gate frameworks that make decision rights, deliverables, dependencies, approvals, and accountability unmistakable from discovery through post-launch adoption.
  • Set the operating rhythm: Lead annual and periodic roadmap planning, portfolio cadences, operational-readiness reviews, Product team onboarding, and process education.
  • Make priorities visible: Partner with Product leadership to strengthen prioritization, capacity insight, portfolio transparency, and consistent execution across teams.
  • Vendor engagement and management: Lead and manage third-party vendor relationships for Product Management as it pertains to software tooling enablement and EHR partnerships.

Release Management

  • Orchestrate the release runway: Establish enterprise release-management standards and maintain one integrated release schedule.
  • Make readiness measurable: Define and monitor criteria, risks, dependencies, communications, training, documentation, support preparation, and customer-impact plans.
  • Guide confident decisions: Facilitate readiness reviews and go/no-go decisions, drive gap closure, and deliver timely, audience-appropriate release information.
  • Lead change without disruption: Coordinate end-user platform, application, feature, data, and customer migrations or transitions with accountable delivery teams.

Productization & Launch Program Management

  • Turn capability into a compelling offering: Lead cross-functional productization programs that create repeatable, market-ready solutions with clear packaging, operational support, implementation readiness, and adoption plans.
  • Keep launches moving: Build and manage launch plans, readiness scorecards, milestones, decision logs, risks, dependencies, and executive status reporting.
  • Prepare the whole organization to win: Ensure every affected function is ready to sell, market, contract, implement, support, operate, and measure new products, modules, enhancements, and releases alongside Product Managers and Product Marketing.
  • Connect commercial and operational details: Coordinate packaging, pricing tools, discovery forms, contracts, and customer migration requirements with Product Management and business partners.

Product Enablement, Training & Adoption

  • Make expertise scalable: Set the product enablement strategy and create role-based curriculums, learning paths, certifications, skills assessments, demonstrations, and readiness programs for employees, customers, and partners.
  • Equip every audience: Develop and maintain launch kits, training materials, product presentations, internal communications, product playbooks, and department-specific readiness resources with Product Management, Product Marketing, Development, and enablement teams.
  • Accelerate confident adoption: Partner with Customer Success, Support, Implementation, Sales, and Marketing to improve onboarding, product proficiency, usage, message consistency, and self-service while reducing avoidable support demand.
  • Prove what works: Connect enablement activity to proficiency, feature usage, launch outcomes, customer experience, and support trends through meaningful learning and adoption measures.

Knowledge, Documentation & Digital Content

  • Create one trusted source of product truth: Own governance for centralized knowledge repositories, internal and customer-facing knowledge bases, training assets, product documentation, and playbooks.
  • Keep content useful and current: Establish standards, templates, ownership, review cadences, version control, archival practices, and quality controls that make information accurate, discoverable, and consistent.
  • Translate complexity into clarity: Oversee release notes, product and feature overviews, user and administrator guidance, training modules, technical specifications, and launch communications.
  • Reimagine how people learn: Lead the product video and digital-learning strategy, standards, product walkthroughs, AI-assisted content, and on-demand learning libraries.

Metrics, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

  • Turn performance into a clear story: Own Product organization KPIs and executive reporting across roadmap delivery, release performance, feature adoption, product health, development throughput, customer feedback, readiness, and enablement effectiveness.
  • Move insight into action: Lead recurring operational reviews that reveal trends, surface risks, clarify decisions, and drive accountable follow-through.
  • Remove friction: Identify bottlenecks and administrative burden, standardize best practices, and pursue responsible automation through enterprise software and approved tools.
  • Build a better system every cycle: Use data and stakeholder feedback to improve lifecycle governance, launch quality, operating efficiency, and organizational throughput.

Leadership & Collaboration

  • Be the connector: Serve as a trusted operating partner to Product leadership and link Product, Engineering, Implementation, Support, Operations, IT, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and other stakeholders.
  • Create alignment without relying on authority: Resolve cross-functional ambiguity, establish ownership, and communicate decisions, risks, and tradeoffs effectively from working teams to executives.
  • Build capability that grows with us: Develop scalable Product Operations and Enablement functions, manage and coach team members, and help shape future roles as product and organizational needs evolve.
  • Champion momentum with discipline: Lead change with transparency, continuous improvement, customer focus, and measurable outcomes.
What You’ll Bring:
  • 7+ years of progressive experience in product operations, program management, product management, product enablement, or a closely related discipline within a healthcare software product organization.
  • A track record of designing and implementing product operating models, lifecycle governance, cross-functional programs, and release or launch processes.
  • Strong program leadership skills across planning, dependency and risk management, facilitation, and executive reporting.
  • An analytical, highly organized approach—and experience defining KPIs that turn data into decisions and operational improvements.
  • Exceptional written, verbal, presentation, and leadership skills, including the ability to make complex product concepts resonate with varied audiences.
  • Experience in creating scalable documentation, training, communications, or adoption resources for enterprise software.
Even Better If You Bring:
  • SaaS or enterprise software experience, including Agile/Scrum delivery and product lifecycle management.
  • Expertise in launch management, technical documentation, learning management systems, product marketing, or multimedia content production.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft and Atlassian products, AI-enablement tools, knowledge-management platforms, and AI-assisted content-development tools.
How You’ll Lead:
  • Think strategically and pragmatically • Communicate with executive clarity • Influence without authority • Lead change • Govern the product lifecycle • Drive complex programs • Design scalable processes • Improve continuously • Build meaningful KPIs • Turn portfolio data into insight • Create learning experiences • Write product and technical content with clarity • Facilitate and enable teams • Tell compelling product stories
General:

  • Responsible for protecting data entrusted to HHIT by customers or other parties, strictly adhering to HHIT’s data security and privacy policies and procedures, HIPAA, PIPEDA and all other applicable laws.
  • Speaking and writing English is a requirement for this position
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States and travel 15-20%
Physical Requirements:
  • Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer
  • Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times

title: Staff/Software Software Engineer
description:
About the role

We're hiring an experienced full-stack engineer to help shape the architecture and technical direction of Pear Suite's platform. This posting spans two levels on our engineering ladder (Senior Software Engineer and Staff Software Engineer) because we're hiring for the scope of work below, not a fixed title. We'll assess your experience through the interview process and offer the level, title, and compensation that fit: Senior or Staff.


A note on leveling. Engineers at both levels do similar kinds of work, architecture, hands-on development, and technical direction. What changes is scope and independence. A Senior Software Engineer typically owns the design and architecture of a system with some oversight from engineering leadership. A Staff Software Engineer typically owns architecture for a major system or cross-cutting concern used across the whole engineering org, sets technical direction with minimal oversight, and leads complex multi-engineer initiatives end to end. The requirements below are a spectrum and where you land within that spectrum will be determined during the interview process.


What you'll do

  • Design and architect scalable, reusable software across the full stack: frontend (React/TypeScript), backend (GraphQL), and cloud infrastructure (GCP).
  • Lead technical initiatives from proposal through delivery, balancing hands-on development with strategic design.
  • Set technical standards and raise the bar on quality, performance, and maintainability.
  • Document technical decisions and designs clearly, for both engineering and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Thoroughly test individual pieces of code and the system as a whole; champion software engineering best practices.
  • Mentor other engineers, formally or informally.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering leadership on technical priorities and trade-offs.

At the Staff level, you'll additionally

  • Own architecture and technical direction for a major system or cross-cutting concern used across the entire engineering org (e.g., data platform, integrations, security).
  • Lead complex, multi-engineer initiatives with minimal oversight.

Qualifications

The required list below is the floor for this posting. The more of the “typically Staff” list that matches your background, the more likely you'll be leveled as Staff rather than Senior.

Required

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, including full-stack development.
  • Deep expertise in React, GraphQL, and TypeScript.
  • Proven experience designing and maintaining cloud architectures (GCP).
  • Strong architecture and system-design judgment, with a track record of decisions that held up in production.
  • Demonstrated ability to balance hands-on development with strategic design.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication; ability to convey technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

Typically Points to a Staff-Level Offer

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant ownership of complex, cross-cutting systems.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership across multiple projects, systems, or teams.
  • A track record of setting technical direction with minimal oversight, and owning a system or platform area used by the entire engineering org.
  • Experience mentoring engineers across levels without formal management authority.

How Success Is Measured

  • Senior: quality and durability of the systems you design, depth of hands-on contribution, and growing cross-team influence.
  • Staff: scope and impact of the systems you own, quality of technical decisions at an org level, and contribution to engineering-wide practices and the hiring bar.


Benefits and Perks

  • A mission driven culture that values innovation, collaboration and growth
  • Equity: participation in an early-stage company
  • Fully Remote
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Comprehensive Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • Health and Wellness Stipend
  • Tech Stipend
  • Co-working Stipend
  • Education and professional development allowance ($1,500 annually)
  • Home office setup stipend

Compensation

  • Senior Software Engineer: $120,000 – $150,000 base salary.
  • Staff Software Engineer: $150,000 – $170,000 base salary.

Compensation Range Disclosure

Pear Suite posts broad salary bands to support pay transparency.


While the full band is shown, actual offers within this band are based on a candidate's experience, skills, and internal pay equity. Only a small number of candidates, typically those with highly specialized and directly relevant experience, are placed near the top of the range. Pear Suite is a fully remote organization so compensation may be adjusted upward for candidates residing in higher-cost labor markets. These geographic adjustments are not reflected in the posted range.

title: Access Control Technician
description:
Build the Future with Us — EquipmentShare is Hiring a Traveling Access Control Technician (low voltage)

At EquipmentShare, we're not just filling a role — we're assembling the best team on the planet to build something that's never been built before. We're on a mission to transform an industry that's been stuck in the past by empowering contractors and communities through innovative technology, real-time support, and a team that truly cares.

We're hiring a Traveling Access Control Technician (low voltage) based out of Dallas, TX, and we're looking for someone who's ready to grow with us, bring energy and drive to their work, and provide installation, maintenance, and repair services for electronic access control systems. You will install, troubleshoot, repair, and maintain badge readers, keypad entry systems, turnstiles, electronic door hardware, gate access systems, and related low-voltage equipment at customer job sites across the country, helping us build the future of construction.

Schedule: Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with overtime pay after working 40 hours. (This role is subject to on-call scheduling with additional compensation provided.)

Travel: 70–85%

Primary Responsibilities

As a Traveling Low Voltage Access Control Technician, you'll use our technology to create, assign, and monitor work orders, track equipment maintenance, order replacement parts, and diagnose system issues. With real-time information at your fingertips, you can work smarter, not harder.

  • Practice safe work habits while installing, servicing, and repairing access control systems.
  • Install, troubleshoot, repair, and maintain key card readers, badge scanners, keypad entry systems, turnstiles, electronic door locks, gate operators, and other access control equipment.
  • Perform preventative maintenance and scheduled inspections to ensure access control systems remain fully operational.
  • Diagnose electrical, mechanical, wiring, networking, and hardware issues using appropriate testing equipment and manufacturer documentation.
  • Run, terminate, label, and troubleshoot low-voltage cabling associated with access control installations.
  • Install and replace controllers, readers, power supplies, locks, request-to-exit devices, sensors, and communication hardware.
  • Configure and test field devices to ensure proper communication with access control software.
  • Read and interpret wiring diagrams, installation drawings, blueprints, and technical documentation.
  • Use laptops, tablets, and mobile devices to configure equipment, complete work orders, and document completed work.
  • Maintain accurate electronic documentation of work performed in a complete and timely manner.
  • Maintain knowledge of OSHA requirements and jobsite safety practices.
  • Participate in year-round company-provided OEM and manufacturer training.

Why EquipmentShare?

Because we do things differently. We're a people-first company powered by cutting-edge technology. Our proprietary T3 platform makes your job easier, safer, and more connected. Whether you're installing new systems or troubleshooting existing equipment, technology supports you, and you drive us forward.

Perks & Benefits

  • Monthly Family Dinner Night — We treat you and your family to dinner every month.
  • Competitive compensation and tool/boot reimbursements.
  • Full medical, dental, and vision coverage.
  • 401(k) with company match.
  • 16 hours of paid volunteer time per year.

About You

We're looking for people who see challenges as opportunities and bring grit, heart, and humility to their work.

Required Skills & Abilities

  • Mechanical and electrical aptitude with experience installing, troubleshooting, and repairing low-voltage electronic systems.
  • Working knowledge of access control hardware including badge readers, keypad entry systems, electronic locks, turnstiles, gate operators, and related devices.
  • Experience running, terminating, testing, and troubleshooting low-voltage wiring.
  • Ability to read wiring diagrams, blueprints, installation drawings, and technical documentation.
  • Experience with industry-leading access control platforms such as Lenel, Brivo, Avigilon Alta (Openpath), HID, Gallagher, AMAG, Genetec, Honeywell Pro-Watch, RS2, or similar systems is highly preferred.
  • Familiarity with IP networking, TCP/IP communications, PoE devices, and basic network troubleshooting is a plus.
  • Comfortable using laptops, tablets, and mobile applications to configure equipment and manage work orders.
  • Strong troubleshooting, communication, and customer service skills.
  • Construction experience or background preferred.

Education & Experience

  • High School diploma or equivalent required.
  • Active applicable state driver's license required.
  • Experience installing or servicing access control, electronic security, low-voltage, or related systems preferred.
  • Construction experience preferred.

Physical Requirements

  • Must be able to move, stand, stoop, kneel, and bend freely.
  • Must be able to climb ladders and work both indoors and outdoors in varying weather conditions.
  • Must be comfortable working on active construction sites.
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.
  • This is a safety-sensitive position, and any offer of employment will be contingent upon passing a 10-panel drug screen.

A Workplace For All

At EquipmentShare, we believe the best solutions come from a team that reflects the world around us. Our initiative — A Workplace For All — is rooted in the belief that we must work together to solve some of the toughest problems in construction. That means attracting, developing, and retaining great people from all walks of life.

We value different backgrounds, talents, and perspectives. We want you to feel like you belong here — because you do.

EquipmentShare is an EOE M/F/D/V.

Employment is contingent on passing a background check. Additionally, some roles require passing a drug test, depending on the job responsibilities.

title: Management Analyst 4
description:
Description

Management Analyst 4
Monday - Friday | 8AM - 5PM | HYBRID


The Department of Enterprise Services (DES) provides centralized business services to state government agencies; to other public entities such as cities, counties and tribes; and to Washington residents. DES’ mission is to strengthen the business of government for a sustainable and just future. Learn more about DES.

The Contracts & Procurement (C&P) Division provides centralized procurement leadership, solutions, and services in support of all state agencies and other government entities’ operations.

About the Opportunity:
The position supports the Business Operation team in Contracts and Procurement Division (CPD) by providing data analysis, research, and reporting. The role helps ensure contract information is accurate and builds reports and dashboards for the division and agency leadership. This position also serves as the business expert for CPD’s contracting systems, working with IT and teams to maintain information and successfully launching enhancements. The position supports and leads process improvement efforts to help CPD work more efficiently.

To learn more about this position, please email the recruiter: Rachel Vaughan via rachel.vaughan@des.wa.gov and request the full job description.

Duties

Duties associated with this position include:
Contracts and Procurement Support:

  • Independently manages the Economic Price Adjustment (EPA) process, completes, and performs research that uses the appropriate industry indices, market conditions, labor rates, producer price index elements and economic factors to provide reference and verification data for contract cost validation and analysis.
  • Research industry indices and standard references to ensure accurate and verifiable contract cost data.
  • Perform complex market analysis, expenditure analysis, spend under management analysis, data graphical representation, trend analysis, and cost/benefit analysis as needed.
  • Performs bid tab services by independently consulting with all levels of contracts and management on low, medium, and high-level contracts evaluation criteria to reduce the number of protests requested and upheld based on calculations in data.
Customer Support:
  • Primary support for the team inbox, reviewing messages, prioritizing requests, and routing items to the appropriate staff. Responds to requests from program managements, senior analysts, and customers within 24 hours.
Analysis and Reports:
  • Supports DES and enterprise-wide diversity spend tracking and analysis.
  • Works directly with executive management to provide data requests.
  • Facilitate and support management fee sales and revenue process. Maintains the Revenue Dashboard to review financial health metrics around contracts sales, staffing, and revenue of the division.
  • Regularly conducts on and off contract spend analysis. Provide financial tracking and projection worksheets, charts and other tools to assist with forecasting projections.
  • Provide direct support to executive management, agency leadership and contract consultants to identify long-range efficiency strategies and standards around CPD services.
Legislative Support:
  • Completes division fiscal notes for CPD.
  • Support the team in all efforts to meet division legislative and policy requirements.
  • Leads and coordinates efforts to write, update, and complete legislatively required reports.
Major Duty:
  • Provides business expertise, leads, or supports enterprise-wide contracting applications, including Purchasing Contracts Management System (PCMS), Washington’s Electronic Business Solution (WEBS), Enterprise Contracts Management System (ECMS), Workload Tool, Cars, and any future systems and data.
  • Business expert for the Purchasing and Contracts Management System (PCMS) to include the Office of Minority and Women Business Enterprise (OMWBE) and Department of Veteran’s Affairs (DVA) data and reporting on Statewide Contracts.
  • Business support for (ECMS).
  • Business support for WEBS.
  • Work in collaboration with IT to make improvements to the systems.
  • Business expert, facilitator, and lead in system user groups.
  • Contributor from DES on enterprise-wide contracting systems in preparation for OneWa.
  • Facilitates CPD process improvement activities using problem solving tools and techniques.
  • Consults with leadership and program management on data-driven process improvement efforts.
  • Creates and maintains process improvement documentation.
  • Maps current and future state workflows.
  • Identifies opportunities to reduce waste and improve operational efficiency.

Qualifications

Required Qualification/Experience/Education/ Competencies
To qualify for this position, you must have a total of eight (8) years of any combination of qualifying education or relevant qualifying experience. Experience may substitute year for year of higher education.

Relevant experience includes conducting research and analyzing policies, laws, rules, or regulations.
Relevant education includes business administration, public administration, law, public health, health administration, or related field.

In addition to meeting with the above requirements, applicants will also need to possess:

  • Four (4) years of experience using Microsoft Excel to compile, analyze and report data. This experience should include the use of:
    • Pivot tables
    • Visual/graphic data modeling
    • Data import/export using SQL
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting findings and recommendations to leadership.
Preferred/Desired Qualifications:
  • Advanced Excel skills, including complex formulas, data modeling, and working with large datasets.
  • Intermediate to advanced Power BI skills, including building and maintaining dashboards and reports.
  • Intermediate to advanced SharePoint skills, including building and maintaining team sites and pages.
  • Experience with procurement or contract management systems such as WEBS, PCMS, or ECMS.
  • Experience with the Agency Finance Reporting System (AFRS).
  • Basic SQL knowledge.
Statewide Equity Competencies:
Incumbents to this position must possess and demonstrate the following competencies:
  • Take action to learn and grow: Demonstrate a willingness to learn from new experiences, seek feedback, consider different perspectives, and continuously improve knowledge, skills, communication, and approaches to work.
  • Take action to meet the needs of others: Seek to understand the needs and experiences of customers, coworkers, and communities. Identify barriers to access and participation and address them before they become obstacles for the people we serve, providing support that is respectful, timely, and effective.

Supplemental Information

How to Apply:
Interested? We would love to hear from you! Click “Apply” at the top of this page to start your application. You can save the application and come back to it, if needed. Be sure to complete the application fully to include a full work history and responses to the supplemental questions.

Please provide the following documents in order to be considered; failure to do so may result in you not being considered for the position:

  • A letter of interest that describes why you are the successful candidate and how you meet the specific qualifications for this position
  • A current resume, detailing experience, and education
  • A current list of at least three (3) professional references with current contact information
Do not attach any documents that include photos or private information (social security number, year of birth, etc.).

Please Note: By submitting these materials, you are indicating that all information is true and correct. The state may verify information. Any untruthful or misleading information is cause for removal from the applicant pool or dismissal if employed. A resume will not be substitute for completing the “duties summary” section of the online application. Please do not refer to the resume for detail or your application may be disqualified.

Washington Fair Chance Act:
We are committed to providing equitable access to employment opportunities. If a criminal background check is required for employment at an agency, it will occur only after a conditional offer of employment has been made and accepted. Applicants are not required to disclose criminal history during the hiring process prior to a conditional offer. Criminal history will not automatically exclude an applicant from consideration and will be reviewed on an individual basis consistent with applicable law and the requirements of the position.

Learn more about the Washington Fair Chance Act: Washington Fair Chance act guide.

Background Check Notice: Prior to any new appointment into the Department of Enterprise Services, a background check including criminal record history will be conducted as a condition of employment. Information from the background check will not necessarily preclude employment but will be considered in determining the applicant's suitability and competence to perform in the position.

Union Inclusion: This position is in a bargaining unit and falls under the Collective Bargaining Agreement between the state of Washington and the Washington Federation of State Employees.

Opportunity for All:
The Department of Enterprise Services celebrates our differences and we are committed to a workplace that supports equal opportunity employment and inclusion regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity diversity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local laws.

You are welcome to include the name and pronoun you would like to be referred to in your materials and we will honor this as you interact with our organization.

Contact Information:
For questions about this recruitment or to request a reasonable accommodation in the application process, contact Rachel Vaughan via email at jobs@des.wa.gov. Applicants who are deaf or hard of hearing may call through the Washington Relay Service by dialing 7-1-1 or 1-800-833-6388.

title: Clinical Supervisor
description:
Company Summary:
Beacon is a successful and national behavioral health company providing residential-based services and supports to children and adults with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities, Severe Mental Illness, Autism, and high-acuity behaviors..

Position Summary:
The Clinical Supervisor is responsible for overseeing the delivery and implementation of clinical services within their market or region. This includes ensuring adherence to core standards of care, providing crisis intervention support, supervising and training clinical staff, monitoring compliance, and collaborating with both internal teams and external stakeholders. This position ensures that services provided to individuals meet regulatory requirements, are trauma-informed, evidence-based, person-centered, and align with best practices. The Clinical Supervisor plays a key role in ensuring that individuals served receive high-quality care in compliance with Medicaid, state, and federal regulations.

Supervisory Responsibilities:
Supervises Clinicians, Behavior Specialists, and Practicum or Internship Students

Primary Responsibilities:

Ensure full compliance with organizational policies and all applicable state and federal regulations.
Promotes day-to-day clinical integrity by coaching and supporting staff and/or students to provide effective, ethical, and consistent care in alignment with best practices and organizational standards.
Works closely with clinical staff and/or students to build confidence, expand clinical knowledge, and develop skills that improve the quality of care and service delivery.
Provides direct supervision and guidance to assigned clinical staff and/or students, including regular supervision meetings, performance feedback, and support in implementing evidence-based practices and treatment plans.
Oversees the tracking and monitoring of High-Risk Case Reviews, clinical incidents, and related follow-up actions to ensure appropriate documentation, accountability, and resolution in alignment with agency policies and clinical standards.
Collaborate with the Clinical Director to implement a best-in-class, evidence-based behavioral health model across assigned programs or regions.

Foster a collaborative, “One Team” environment by supporting integration between clinical, medical, and operational teams to promote high-quality, coordinated care.
Participate in leadership meetings and contribute to clinical decision-making processes.
Oversee clinical services to ensure they are aligned with clinical best practices, trauma-informed care principles, and appropriate to the individual's level of acuity.
Monitor caseloads, acuity levels, and staffing patterns to ensure service intensity and frequency meet both clinical needs and regulatory expectations.
Support continuity and consistency of services across programs and homes, including coordination of external behavioral health providers when necessary.
Maintain regular, open, and consistent communication across clinical teams and with other departments.
Carry a limited caseload of clients, as needed, to support high-acuity cases or program needs.
Assist in developing and implementing individualized crisis stabilization plans and provide direct crisis intervention and risk assessments when required.
Lead or coordinate clinical in-service trainings, orientation for new clinical staff and/or students, and ongoing skill development for clinical staff and/or students.
Attend program and team meetings, trainings, and supervisory sessions as required
Performs ongoing reviews and audits of clinical charts to verify compliance with documentation standards, clinical best practices, and federal billing requirements
Oversee internal audits and assist in implementing continuous quality improvement initiatives related to clinical services.
Ensure behavior plans and crisis documentation meet standards for federal reimbursement and clinical effectiveness.
Support and maintain positive working relationships with external agencies and providers to ensure optimal outcomes for the individuals served.
Ensure that Individualized Support Plans (ISPs) are personalized, data-informed, and address precursors and triggers for high-acuity behaviors.
Review and assist in the development of clinical tools, procedures, and policies when needed.

Education and Qualifications:

Master’s degree in Psychology, Social Work, Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), Sociology, Human Services, or a closely related field from an accredited college or university is preferred.

In lieu of a graduate degree, substantial experience in a supervisory role may be considered. In such cases, a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, Social Work, Human Services, or a related discipline from an accredited institution is required.
Must hold a valid license in a behavioral healthcare discipline (LLBSW, LBSW, LLP, LLPC, LLMSW, LMSW, BCBA); full licensure is preferred.
A minimum of one (1) year of prior experience providing clinical supervision is preferred.
Responsible for maintaining all mandatory training and certification requirements.
Must pass criminal background checks, central registry check (in applicable states) and child abuse registry (in applicable states).
Must complete and pass a drug test, in applicable states.
Must possess a valid Driver’s License and have reliable transportation.
Proficient in speaking, reading and writing the English language.
Approved by state, federal and government entities to work within BSLS programs.
Ability to use office equipment, including BSLS information technology systems.

Skills and Abilities:

Must be able to communicate and function in an interdisciplinary team.
Strong computer skills utilizing various software programs and applications.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Ability to create professional employee communication materials.
Capable of working well with all levels of the organization.
A professional demeanor.
Demonstrated ability to multi-task.
Ability to work with little daily supervision.

Work Environment:
Most of your job duties will be performed from an office but travel to Beacon locations is required.

Travel:
Occasional travel 25-30% or as otherwise determined by the needs of the market to support BSLS locations in Missouri.

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work:
This is a full-time position. Hybrid work environment with corporate office presence and regional travel. Days and hours of work are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Occasional evenings and weekend work may be required as job duties demand.
